# Vue Checkbox Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Checkbox component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CCheckbox

```jsx
import { CCheckbox } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | - | The id attribute of the input. Generated automatically when a label is set. |
| `indeterminate` | `boolean` | - | Display the checkbox in an indeterminate state - there is no HTML attribute for it, only this property. |
| `label` | `string` | - | The label rendered after the input, already wired to it with `for`. |
| `modelValue` | `boolean` | `undefined` | The checked state, used with v-model. |
| `size` | `string` | - | Size the checkbox small or large. |
| `theme` | `Color` | - | Sets the color context of the checked state to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the checked state emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `change` | Event occurs when the checked value has been changed. |
| `update:modelValue` | Emit the new checked state whenever there’s a change event. |
| `update:validationState` | Event occurs with `undefined` when the user changes the checked state, or the form is reset, while `validationState` is set. A given state is a verdict on the choice it was given for; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it and let the browser's own validation show again. |

## CFormCheck

```jsx
import { CFormCheck } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `button` | `object` | - | Create button-like checkboxes and radio buttons. |
| `falseValue` | `string` | - | Use in conjunction with the v-model directive to specify the value that should be assigned to the bound variable when the checkbox is in the `false` state. |
| `feedback` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable feedback. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable feedback. |
| `feedbackValid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable invalid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied two CSS pseudo-classes, `:invalid` and `:valid`. |
| `id` | `string` | - | The id global attribute defines an identifier (ID) that must be unique in the whole document. |
| `indeterminate` | `boolean` | - | Input Checkbox indeterminate Property |
| `inline` | `boolean` | - | Group checkboxes or radios on the same horizontal row by adding. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control invalid. |
| `label` | `string` | - | The element represents a caption for a component. |
| `modelValue` | `array\|boolean\|string` | - | The default name for a value passed using v-model. |
| `reverse` | `boolean` | - | Put checkboxes or radios on the opposite side. |
| `theme` | `Color` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `trueValue` | `string` | - | Use in conjunction with the v-model directive to specify the value that should be assigned to the bound variable when the checkbox is in the `true` state. |
| `type` | `string` | `'checkbox'` | Specifies the type of component. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control valid. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the checked state emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`. |
| `value` | `string` | - | The value attribute of component. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `change` | Event occurs when the checked value has been changed. |
| `update:modelValue` | Emit the new value whenever there’s a change event. |
| `update:validationState` | Event occurs with `undefined` when the user changes the checked state, or the form is reset, while `validationState` (or the deprecated `invalid`) is set. A given state is a verdict on the choice it was given for; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it and let the browser's own validation show again. |

# Vue Checkbox Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Checkbox component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

Vue Checkbox reads its own custom properties, so restyling it does not touch radios or switches. Set them on the control itself — an ancestor cannot override a token the element declares for itself.

```scss
$check-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-check-size: var(--cui-control-size),
    --cui-check-bg: var(--cui-btn-input-bg),
    --cui-check-border: var(--cui-border-width) solid var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-check-border-radius: .25em,
    --cui-check-mark-color: var(--cui-primary-contrast),
    --cui-check-mark-checked: #{escape-svg(url("data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 20 20'><path fill='none' stroke='black' stroke-linecap='round' stroke-linejoin='round' stroke-width='3' d='m6 10 3 3 6-6'/></svg>"))},
    --cui-check-mark-indeterminate: #{escape-svg(url("data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 20 20'><path fill='none' stroke='black' stroke-linecap='round' stroke-linejoin='round' stroke-width='3' d='M6 10h8'/></svg>"))},
    --cui-check-checked-bg: var(--cui-control-checked-bg),
    --cui-check-checked-border-color: var(--cui-control-checked-border-color),
    --cui-check-indeterminate-bg: var(--cui-control-indeterminate-bg),
    --cui-check-indeterminate-border-color: var(--cui-control-indeterminate-border-color),
    --cui-check-disabled-opacity: var(--cui-control-disabled-opacity),
    --cui-check-margin-top: calc((var(--cui-body-line-height) * 1em - var(--cui-check-size)) * .5),
    --cui-check-active-filter: var(--cui-control-active-filter),
    --cui-check-label-disabled-opacity: var(--cui-control-label-disabled-opacity),
  ),
  $check-tokens
);
```

#### How to use CSS variables

```vue
<CCheckbox :style="{ '--cui-check-size': '1.25em', '--cui-check-checked-bg': '#198754' }" />
```

### Shared variables

The checkbox, the radio and the switch share their size and their focus, active and disabled states. Those live on `:root` as `--cui-control-*`, so one declaration retunes all three at runtime:

```scss
--cui-control-size: 1em,
--cui-control-checked-bg: var(--cui-primary-base),
--cui-control-checked-border-color: var(--cui-primary-base),
--cui-control-indeterminate-bg: var(--cui-primary-base),
--cui-control-indeterminate-border-color: var(--cui-primary-base),
--cui-control-active-filter: brightness(90%),
--cui-control-focus-border-color: var(--cui-btn-input-focus-border-color),
--cui-control-disabled-bg: var(--cui-bg-3),
--cui-control-disabled-opacity: .5,
--cui-control-label-disabled-opacity: .5,
--cui-control-transition-duration: .15s,
--cui-control-transition-timing: cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1),
```

### Sass maps

Each entry is one size class, and the same map drives both `.check-{size}` and `.radio-{size}` — add a key to define a size, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$check-sizes: defaults(
  (
    sm: (size: .875rem, margin-top: .21875rem, font-size: var(--cui-font-size-sm)),
    lg: (size: 1.25rem, margin-top: .3125rem, font-size: var(--cui-font-size-lg))
  ),
  $check-sizes
);
```

# Vue Bootstrap Checkbox Component

> Learn how to build accessible and consistent Bootstrap-style checkboxes in Vue using CoreUI components.

## How to use Vue Bootstrap Checkbox component

Use CoreUI’s `<CCheckbox>` to create cross-browser, accessible, and Bootstrap-styled checkboxes in Vue. Checkboxes are ideal for selecting one or more options from a list and can be styled, stacked, or grouped using layout utilities.

### Basic example

Use the `<CCheckbox>` component to render a standard Bootstrap-style checkbox.

```html
<template>
```

```html
<template>

  </CFormField>

<script setup>
import { CCheckbox, CFormField } from '@coreui/vue'
```

```html
<template>
```

# Vue Chip Input Component

> Vue Chip Input component for CoreUI helps you create tag-like multi-value inputs for skills, categories, or recipients with keyboard support, selection, and form integration.

## Overview

The CoreUI **Vue Chip Input component** lets users enter multiple values as chips inside a single field. Use it as a tag input, multi-value selector, or token field for skills, categories, email recipients, and more. The chip input component supports keyboard-friendly entry, chip removal, and optional selection for bulk actions.

- Type values and press **Enter** or a separator to create chips
- Chips can be removable and selectable
- The input stays inline and grows as you type
- Form integration through a hidden field the browser validates, submitted when `name` is provided
- Full v-model support for reactive data binding

## When to use Chip Input

Use the Vue Chip Input component when you need:

- A **tag input** or **token field** for free-form multi-value entry
- An **email or recipient input** where users add multiple addresses
- A **skills or category selector** in forms
- A **filterable multi-select** that integrates with standard HTML forms

## Basic example

Use `CChipInput` to render a multi-value field with predefined chips and inline input.

```html
<template>
  <CChipInput v-model="tags" placeholder="Type and press Enter..." />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/vue'

const tags = ref(['Vue.js', 'TypeScript', 'CoreUI'])
</script>
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CChipInput
      id="techStackField"
      label="Tech stack"
      :model-value="['Vue', 'Vite']"
      name="techStack"
      placeholder="Add package..."
    />
    <CFormText>Press Enter or comma to add a value.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CChipInput, CFormField, CFormText } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## With label

Use the `label` prop for accessibility and better UX.

```html
<template>
  <CChipInput id="skills-input" v-model="skills" label="Skills" placeholder="Add skill..." />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/vue'

const skills = ref(['Problem Solving', 'Teamwork', 'Communication'])
</script>
```

## Sizes

Use `size="sm"` and `size="lg"` to match surrounding form controls.

```html
<template>
  <div>
    <div class="mb-4">
      <CChipInput
        id="skillsInputSm"
        v-model="smallTags"
        label="Small"
        size="sm"
        placeholder="Add a small chip"
      />
    </div>

    <div class="mb-4">
      <CChipInput
        id="skillsInputDefault"
        v-model="defaultTags"
        label="Default"
        placeholder="Add a default chip"
      />
    </div>

    <div>

        id="skillsInputLg"
        v-model="largeTags"
        label="Large"
        size="lg"
        placeholder="Add a large chip"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/vue'

const smallTags = ref(['Small chip'])
const defaultTags = ref(['Default chip'])
const largeTags = ref(['Large chip'])
</script>
```

## Validation

`CChipInput` carries its chips in a hidden `<textarea>` the browser validates, so `required` stops the submit of an empty field and the browser shows its message over the component. The state shows on the frame and on the text input, and the message after the frame is linked to the text input. The messages come from the `feedback`, `feedback-invalid` and `feedback-valid` props, and the last two also from the slots of the same names.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row g-4" novalidate validate>
    <div class="col-md-6">
      <CChipInput
        id="validationTopics"
        feedback-invalid="Add at least one topic."
        label="Topics"
        name="topics"
        placeholder="Add a topic..."
        required
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-md-6">
      <CChipInput
        id="validationRecipients"
        v-model:validation-state="recipientsState"
        feedback="bob@example is not a full address."
        label="Recipients"
        name="recipients"
      >
        <CChip>ana@example.com</CChip>
        <CChip>bob@example</CChip>
      </CChipInput>
    </div>
    <div class="col-12">
      <CButton color="primary" type="submit">Submit</CButton>
    </div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CChip, CChipInput, CForm } from '@coreui/vue'

const recipientsState = ref('invalid')
</script>
```

The state comes from three places, in this order:

- `validationState`: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`. While it is set, the component draws it instead of what the browser reports. While it is `'invalid'`, the hidden field blocks the submit with the text of the linked message, or `Invalid value.` when there is none, unless the component is `disabled` or `readOnly`.
- A validation that reports the hidden field invalid: a submit, `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()`, which [`CForm`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/validation/) and the stepper call as well. From then on the frame and the text input show it invalid whenever the value is invalid, until the form is reset, and the message after the frame shows.
- In a form with `validate`, the `:user-invalid` state of the hidden field, and with `validate="valid"` also its `:user-valid` state.

A state you give is a verdict on the chips it was given for. When the user adds or removes a chip, or the form is reset, the component emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop the state, as the second field above does. A change your code makes through `v-model` keeps it, and so does an action that changes nothing, such as entering a value the field already holds. A reset emits once it has run, so a state you set from a `reset` listener on the form gets the same event, and your handler decides whether to drop it. A native reset of the form puts back the chips given by the `CChip` children, and leaves a bound `v-model` to you.

## Selectable chips

Enable chip selection with the `selectable` prop. Use the `@select` event to track selected chips.

```html
<template>
  <div>
    <CChipInput
      v-model="items"
      selectable
      placeholder="Click chips to select them..."
      @select="handleSelect"
    />

    <p v-if="selectedItems.length" class="mt-4 fg-2 small">
      Selected: {{ selectedItems.join(', ') }}
    </p>
    <p v-else class="mt-4 fg-2 small">No chips selected</p>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/vue'

const items = ref(['Apple', 'Banana', 'Cherry', 'Date', 'Elderberry'])
const selectedItems = ref([])

const handleSelect = (selected) => {
  selectedItems.value = selected
}
</script>
```

## Form integration

The chips travel in a hidden `<textarea>`, separated by commas, which takes part in standard form submission once `name` is provided.

```html
<template>
  <CForm @submit.prevent="handleSubmit">
    <CChipInput v-model="tags" name="tags" label="Tags" placeholder="Add tags..." />
    <CButton type="submit" theme="primary" class="mt-3">Submit</CButton>
    <div v-if="submitted" class="mt-3 fg-success">
      <small>Form submitted with tags: {{ submittedTags }}</small>
    </div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CChipInput, CForm, CButton } from '@coreui/vue'

const tags = ref(['Tag1', 'Tag2'])
const submitted = ref(false)
const submittedTags = ref('')

const handleSubmit = () => {
  submitted.value = true
  submittedTags.value = tags.value.join(', ')
  setTimeout(() => {
    submitted.value = false
  }, 3000)
}
</script>
```

## Events

The component emits several events for tracking changes:

- `@update:modelValue` - Main v-model event with updated values array
- `@change` - Fires when values change
- `@add` - Fires when a chip is added (receives the new value)
- `@remove` - Fires when a chip is removed (receives the removed value)
- `@input` - Fires when the text input value changes
- `@select` - Fires when selected chips change (when `selectable` is true)
- `@update:validationState` - Fires when the validation state drops, for `v-model:validation-state`

```html
<template>
  <div>
    <CChipInput
      v-model="tags"
      placeholder="Type to trigger events..."
      @add="onAdd"
      @remove="onRemove"
    />

    <div v-if="events.length" class="mt-4 p-4 bg-light rounded">
      <h6>Event Log:</h6>
      <ul class="list-unstyled small mb-0">
        <li v-for="(event, index) in events.slice(-5)" :key="index">
          <span class="badge bg-secondary me-3">{{ event.type }}</span>
          {{ event.value }}
        </li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/vue'

const tags = ref(['Demo', 'Events'])
const events = ref([])

const onAdd = (value) => {
  events.value.push({ type: 'add', value })
}

const onRemove = (value) => {
  events.value.push({ type: 'remove', value })
}
</script>
```

## Keyboard behavior

The Chip Input component supports comprehensive keyboard interaction:

### In the text input

- **Enter**: Create a chip from the current input value
- **Backspace** (when input is empty): Focus the last chip
- **Delete** (when input is empty): Focus the last chip
- **ArrowLeft** (at start of input): Focus the last chip
- **Escape**: Clear the input and blur

### On a focused chip

- **Backspace** / **Delete**: Remove the chip
- **ArrowLeft** / **ArrowRight**: Navigate between chips
- **Home** / **End**: Jump to first/last chip
- **Enter** / **Space** (if selectable): Toggle chip selection
- **Shift** + **ArrowLeft** / **ArrowRight** (if selectable, multiple): Move focus and add the chip it lands on to the selection
- **Shift** + **Home** / **End** (if selectable, multiple): Extend the selection to the first or last chip
- **Ctrl** / **Cmd** + **A** (if selectable, multiple): Select every chip

## Usage with v-model

For reactive data binding, use `v-model`. A native reset of the form puts back the chips given by an initial `model-value` or, without one, by the `CChip` children: with no `model-value` at all, it sets those chips and emits `change`; with one, it asks for the value it started with through `update:modelValue` and `change` and shows your chips until you take it:

```html
<template>
  <div>
    <CChipInput v-model="tags" placeholder="Type and press Enter..." />
    <div class="mt-4 fg-2">Current values: {{ tags.join(', ') || '(empty)' }}</div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/vue'

const tags = ref(['Vue', 'React', 'Angular'])
</script>
```

### Default values

For initial values without a reactive binding, pass `model-value` one-way:

```html
<template>
  <div>
    <CChipInput
      :model-value="['HTML', 'CSS', 'JavaScript']"
      placeholder="Add more..."
      @change="handleChange"
    />
    <div class="mt-4 fg-2">Last change: {{ lastChange || 'No changes yet' }}</div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/vue'

const lastChange = ref('')

const handleChange = (values) => {
  lastChange.value = values.join(', ')
}
</script>
```

# Vue Chip Input Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Chip Input component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CChipInput

```jsx
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaAddedAnnouncement` | `string \| ((values: string[]) => string)` | `'added'` | Sets the wording announced when chips are added: a word that follows their values, joined with commas, or a function that receives the values and returns the whole message. |
| `ariaRemovedAnnouncement` | `string \| ((values: string[]) => string)` | `'removed'` | Sets the wording announced when chips are removed: a word that follows their values, joined with commas, or a function that receives the values and returns the whole message. |
| `ariaRemoveLabel` | `string \| ((label: string) => string)` | `'Remove'` | Names each chip's remove button with the chip's value: a string has `{label}` replaced by it, or gets it appended when there is no `{label}` (`Remove Vue`); a function receives the value and returns the whole name. |
| `chipClassName` | `ChipClassName` | `undefined` | Adds custom classes to chips rendered by the component. Accepts a static className or a resolver function based on chip value. |
| `createOnBlur` | `boolean` | `true` | Creates a new chip when the component loses focus with a pending value. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `feedback` | `string` | - | Feedback for the current `validationState` — rendered only while the state is set, and styled after it. For the client-side mode, where the browser owns the state, use `feedbackValid` and `feedbackInvalid` instead. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `string` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is invalid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `feedbackValid` | `string` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is valid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `filter` | `boolean` | - | Renders the chips as filter chips, each showing a leading check icon while selected. Implies `selectable`. |
| `id` | `string` | - | Sets the `id` of the internal text input rendered by the component. |
| `label` | `string\|object` | - | Renders an inline label inside the component container. |
| `maxChips` | `number` | `null` | Sets the maximum number of chips that can be created in the component. |
| `modelValue` | `string[]` | `undefined` | The default name for a value passed using v-model. |
| `name` | `string` | - | Name of the hidden field the chips are submitted under, separated by commas. Without it the chips are not submitted with the form. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | Sets placeholder text for the internal input of the component. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the readonly state for the component. |
| `removable` | `boolean` | `true` | Displays remove buttons on chips managed by the component. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | Makes the hidden field that carries the chips required, so an empty component blocks the submit, and marks the text input `aria-required`. |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | - | Enables chip selection behavior in the component. |
| `selectionMode` | `string` | `'multiple'` | Sets how many chips can be selected at once. |
| `separator` | `string` | `','` | Sets the separator character used to create chips while typing or pasting in the component. |
| `size` | `string` | - | Size the component small or large. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class on the frame; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` on the text input and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the chips emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `add` | Event occurs when the component adds a new chip. |
| `change` | Event occurs when the value list changes. |
| `input` | Event occurs when the internal text input value changes. |
| `remove` | Event occurs when the component removes a chip. |
| `select` | Event occurs when the selected chip values change. |
| `update:modelValue` | Emit the new value whenever there's a change. |
| `update:validationState` | Event occurs with `undefined` when the user adds or removes a chip, or the form is reset, while `validationState` is set. A given state is a verdict on the chips it was given for; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it and let the browser's own validation show again. |

# Vue Chip Input Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Chip Input component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

A chip input is a [`.form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/form-control-group/styling/#css-variables), so it reads the group's `--cui-control-*` tokens; `.chip-input` only re-points the ones it sets differently — padding, border colour and radius, and the gap between chips. `class` and `style` on `<CChipInput>` land on that element, so override any group token there to restyle a single chip input.

```scss
$chip-input-tokens: () !default;
$chip-input-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-control-padding-y: .25rem,
    --cui-control-padding-x: .75rem,
    --cui-control-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-control-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-4),
    --cui-control-group-gap: .375rem,
  ),
  $chip-input-tokens
);
```

#### How to use CSS variables

```vue
<template>
  <CChipInput :style="vars">...</CChipInput>
</template>

<script setup>
const vars = {
  '--cui-control-bg': '#f8f9fa',
  '--cui-control-group-gap': '.5rem',
}
</script>
```

# Vue Chip Input Component Accessibility

> Detailed overview of the accessibility features implemented in CoreUI Vue Chip Input, ensuring compliance with WAI-ARIA guidelines.

## Accessibility

The Vue Chip Input component follows WAI-ARIA patterns to ensure the chip input is fully usable with keyboards and assistive technologies.

- Associate a `<label>` with the ghost input for screen readers.
- Chips are focusable and keyboard navigable.
- Each remove button the component creates is named with `ariaRemoveLabel` and the chip's value, `Remove <value>` by default. Put `{label}` where the value goes, or pass a function of the value for another word order.
- Adding and removing chips is announced through [`announce()`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/accessibility/screen-readers/#announcing-messages) in the live region of the page, or of the modal dialog around the set, one message per update: the values the set did not hold before, or else the values it no longer holds, joined with commas as in `Vue, Svelte added`, and nothing while the set is hidden; customize the wording with the `ariaAddedAnnouncement` and `ariaRemovedAnnouncement` props. A function in place of the word receives the values and returns the whole message, so a page can put the word first, agree it with the number of chips or give a count for a long list, as in `(values) => values.length > 3 ? values.length + ' chips added' : values.join(', ') + ' added'`.
- The container is a generic element, so `disabled` and `readOnly` are carried by the inner input rather than stamped on it.
- Use a descriptive `aria-label` or `<label>` on the chip input container to communicate its purpose (e.g., "Add skills" or "Recipients").

# Vue Bootstrap Chip Input Component

> Learn how to use CoreUI’s Vue Chip Input component with Bootstrap styles for flexible, framework-consistent UI.

## Overview

The CoreUI **Vue Chip Input component** lets users enter multiple values as chips inside a single field. Use it as a tag input, multi-value selector, or token field for skills, categories, email recipients, and more. The chip input component supports keyboard-friendly entry, chip removal, and optional selection for bulk actions.

- Type values and press **Enter** or a separator to create chips
- Chips can be removable and selectable
- The input stays inline and grows as you type
- Form integration is supported with a hidden input when `name` is provided
- Full v-model support for reactive data binding

## When to use Chip Input

Use the Vue Chip Input component when you need:

- A **tag input** or **token field** for free-form multi-value entry
- An **email or recipient input** where users add multiple addresses
- A **skills or category selector** in forms
- A **filterable multi-select** that integrates with standard HTML forms

## Basic example

Use `CChipInput` to render a multi-value field with predefined chips and inline input.

```html
</template>

</script>
```

```html
<template>
```

```html
    <CChipInput v-model="tags" :separator="null" placeholder="Type and press Enter..." />
    <p class="mt-3 fg-2">
      <small>Separator disabled - use Enter key to create chips</small>
    </p>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/vue'

const tags = ref(['Press Enter'])
</script>
```

## Maximum chips

Limit the number of chips with `maxChips`.

```html
<template>
  <div>
    <CChipInput v-model="tags" :max-chips="5" placeholder="Max 5 chips" />
    <p class="mt-3 fg-2">
      <small>{{ tags.length }}/5 chips - {{ 5 - tags.length }} remaining</small>
    </p>
  </div>
</template>

const tags = ref(['One', 'Two', 'Three'])
</script>
```

## Create on blur

By default, typing a value and blurring the input creates a chip. Disable this with `createOnBlur`.

```html
<template>
  <div>
    <CChipInput v-model="tags" :create-on-blur="false" placeholder="Must press Enter" />
    <p class="mt-3 fg-2">
      <small>Blurring won't create a chip - you must press Enter</small>
    </p>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/vue'

const tags = ref(["Blur won't create"])
```
```html
</script>
```

## Selectable chips

Enable chip selection with the `selectable` prop. Use the `@select` event to track selected chips.

```html
<template>
  <div>
    <CChipInput
      v-model="items"
      selectable
      placeholder="Click chips to select them..."
      @select="handleSelect"
    />

    <p v-if="selectedItems.length" class="mt-4 fg-2 small">
      Selected: {{ selectedItems.join(', ') }}
    </p>
    <p v-else class="mt-4 fg-2 small">No chips selected</p>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/vue'

const items = ref(['Apple', 'Banana', 'Cherry', 'Date', 'Elderberry'])
const selectedItems = ref([])

const handleSelect = (selected) => {
  selectedItems.value = selected
}
</script>
```

## Form integration

When `name` is provided, a hidden input is rendered for standard form submission.

```html
<template>
  <CForm @submit.prevent="handleSubmit">
    <CChipInput v-model="tags" name="tags" label="Tags" placeholder="Add tags..." />
    <CButton type="submit" theme="primary" class="mt-3">Submit</CButton>
    <div v-if="submitted" class="mt-3 fg-success">
      <small>Form submitted with tags: {{ submittedTags }}</small>
    </div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CChipInput, CForm, CButton } from '@coreui/vue'

const tags = ref(['Tag1', 'Tag2'])
const submitted = ref(false)
const submittedTags = ref('')

const handleSubmit = () => {
  submitted.value = true
  submittedTags.value = tags.value.join(', ')
  setTimeout(() => {
    submitted.value = false
  }, 3000)
}
</script>
```

## Events

The component emits several events for tracking changes:

- `@update:modelValue` - Main v-model event with updated values array
- `@change` - Fires when values change
- `@add` - Fires when a chip is added (receives the new value)
- `@remove` - Fires when a chip is removed (receives the removed value)
- `@input` - Fires when the text input value changes
- `@select` - Fires when selected chips change (when `selectable` is true)

```html
<template>
  <div>
    <CChipInput
      v-model="tags"
      placeholder="Type to trigger events..."
      @add="onAdd"
      @remove="onRemove"
    />

    <div v-if="events.length" class="mt-4 p-4 bg-light rounded">
      <h6>Event Log:</h6>
      <ul class="list-unstyled small mb-0">
        <li v-for="(event, index) in events.slice(-5)" :key="index">
          <span class="badge bg-secondary me-3">{{ event.type }}</span>
          {{ event.value }}
        </li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/vue'

const tags = ref(['Demo', 'Events'])
const events = ref([])

const onAdd = (value) => {
  events.value.push({ type: 'add', value })
}

const onRemove = (value) => {
  events.value.push({ type: 'remove', value })
}
</script>
```

## Keyboard behavior

The Chip Input component supports comprehensive keyboard interaction:

### In the text input

- **Enter**: Create a chip from the current input value
- **Backspace** (when input is empty): Focus the last chip
- **Delete** (when input is empty): Focus the last chip
- **ArrowLeft** (at start of input): Focus the last chip
- **Escape**: Clear the input and blur

### On a focused chip

- **Backspace** / **Delete**: Remove the chip
- **ArrowLeft** / **ArrowRight**: Navigate between chips
- **Home** / **End**: Jump to first/last chip
- **Enter** / **Space** (if selectable): Toggle chip selection

## Usage with v-model

For reactive data binding, use `v-model`:

```html
<template>
  <div>
    <CChipInput v-model="tags" placeholder="Type and press Enter..." />
    <div class="mt-4 fg-2">Current values: {{ tags.join(', ') || '(empty)' }}</div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/vue'

const tags = ref(['Vue', 'React', 'Angular'])
</script>
```

### Default values

For initial values without a reactive binding, pass `model-value` one-way:

```html
<template>
  <div>
    <CChipInput
      :model-value="['HTML', 'CSS', 'JavaScript']"
      placeholder="Add more..."
      @change="handleChange"
    />
    <div class="mt-4 fg-2">Last change: {{ lastChange || 'No changes yet' }}</div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/vue'

const lastChange = ref('')

const handleChange = (values) => {
  lastChange.value = values.join(', ')
}
</script>
```

# Vue Combobox Component

> A select-like control written as components: a form-control toggle next to a popup list box. CCombobox runs the open state, the selection, the keyboard and form submission, and leaves the content of every option to you.

## Overview

_Added in 6.0.0._

A combobox is a `.form-control` toggle button followed by a popup holding a [List box](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/list-box/). The toggle shows the current value and the list holds the choices; `<CCombobox>` keeps the two in step — it opens and closes the panel, positions it against the toggle, tracks the selection, runs the keyboard through `aria-activedescendant`, and submits the value through a hidden `<select>` the browser validates.

Everything inside the panel is List box markup, so an option is whatever you put in it: plain text, an icon, a two-line label with a description. The component never rewrites an option's content.

```html
<template>
  <CCombobox name="option" placeholder="Select an item…" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption value="1">Option one</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="2">Option two</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="3">Option three</CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### When to use

<div class="table-responsive">

| Component | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| Combobox | Picking from a list you wrote as components, with full control over what an option looks like. |
| [Autocomplete](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/autocomplete/) | Typing to narrow a list, with hints and a free-text value. |
| [Multi Select](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/multi-select/) | A native `<select>` enhanced in place, with chips, select-all and groups. |
| [List box](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/list-box/) | The list on its own, without a toggle or a panel. |

</div>

## Example

The options are `<CListBoxOption>` children, exactly as in a List box; every option carries its value in `value` and an option without one is worth its text. The component fills in the parts around them: the `.combobox-value` text, the caret, `type="button"`, `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded`.

### Placeholders

`placeholder` is the text the toggle shows while nothing is selected. It carries `.combobox-placeholder` while it stands for an empty value, so it can be dimmed without being confused for a choice.

```html
<template>
  <CCombobox name="country" placeholder="Pick a country…" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption value="us">United States</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="uk">United Kingdom</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="ca">Canada</CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### Pre-selected value

`defaultValue` seeds the uncontrolled selection — the toggle reads its label from the first render. `value` does the same and keeps the selection yours: the component then renders what you pass and reports the user's picks through `change`, which `v-model:value` binds for you. Both take an array in `multiple` mode.

```html
<template>
  <CCombobox
    default-value="editor"
    name="role"
    placeholder="Choose a role…"
    style="max-width: 20rem"
  >
    <CListBoxOption value="admin">Admin</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="editor">Editor</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="viewer">Viewer</CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### Options from data

Pass `items` instead of children and every entry renders as a `<CListBoxOption>` showing its `label`. The default slot then becomes the option template, called once per entry with `item` and `index`.

```html
<template>
  <CCombobox :items="items" placeholder="Pick a country…" style="max-width: 20rem" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CCombobox } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const items = [
  { label: 'United States', value: 'us' },
  { label: 'United Kingdom', value: 'uk' },
  { label: 'Canada', value: 'ca' },
]
</script>
```

### With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CFormLabel for="exampleCombobox">Country</CFormLabel>
    <CCombobox id="exampleCombobox" name="country" placeholder="Pick a country…">
      <CListBoxOption value="us">United States</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="uk">United Kingdom</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="ca">Canada</CListBoxOption>
    </CCombobox>
    <CFormText>We ship to these three for now.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CCombobox, CFormField, CFormLabel, CFormText, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Custom content

An option is an ordinary element, so it takes whatever markup belongs there. The toggle shows its text: the `.list-box-option-label` when there is one, the option's own text otherwise — so an option with an icon and a description still reads as one word in the closed control.

### Icons

```html
<template>
  <CCombobox name="language" placeholder="Choose a language…" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption v-for="language in languages" :key="language.value" :value="language.value">
      <CIcon :icon="language.icon" />
      <span class="list-box-option-label">{{ language.label }}</span>
    </CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { cibJavascript, cibPython, cibRuby } from '@coreui/icons-pro'
import { CIcon } from '@coreui/icons-vue'
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const languages = [
  { icon: cibJavascript, label: 'JavaScript', value: 'js' },
  { icon: cibPython, label: 'Python', value: 'python' },
  { icon: cibRuby, label: 'Ruby', value: 'ruby' },
]
</script>
```

### Descriptions

`description` puts a second line under the label. The toggle shows the label alone.

```html
<template>
  <CCombobox name="plan" placeholder="Choose a plan…" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption description="Everything you need to start" value="starter">
      Starter
    </CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption description="For growing teams" value="team">Team</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption description="Dedicated support and SLA" value="enterprise">
      Enterprise
    </CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### Checkbox indicator

`indicator="checkbox"` draws a decorative checkbox in front of every option, so a multiple selection reads as a list of checkboxes.

```html
<template>
  <CCombobox
    indicator="checkbox"
    multiple
    name="skills"
    placeholder="Select skills…"
    style="max-width: 20rem"
  >
    <CListBoxOption value="html">HTML</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="css">CSS</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="js">JavaScript</CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### All together

```html
<template>
  <CCombobox
    indicator="checkbox"
    multiple
    name="teammates"
    placeholder="Invite teammates…"
    style="max-width: 20rem"
  >
    <CListBoxOption
      v-for="member in members"
      :key="member.value"
      :description="member.description"
      :value="member.value"
    >
      <CIcon :icon="cilUser" />

    </CListBoxOption>

import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const members = [
  { description: 'Design', label: 'Ada Lovelace', value: 'ada' },
  { description: 'Engineering', label: 'Alan Turing', value: 'alan' },
  { description: 'Support', label: 'Grace Hopper', value: 'grace' },
]
</script>
```

## Search

`search` puts the List box's own search field at the top of the panel and hides what does not match. Because a hidden option leaves the navigation, everything downstream follows: the arrows skip it and `<CListBoxEmpty>` takes over when nothing is left. The focus moves into the field when the panel opens, and `aria-activedescendant` moves there with it, so typing and choosing happen in one place.

`searchPlaceholder` fills the field's placeholder and `ariaSearchLabel` its accessible name.

```html
<template>
  <CCombobox name="country" placeholder="Select a country…" search style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption value="us">United States</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="uk">United Kingdom</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="ca">Canada</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="au">Australia</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="de">Germany</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="fr">France</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="jp">Japan</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="br">Brazil</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxEmpty>No results found</CListBoxEmpty>
  </CCombobox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CCombobox, CListBoxEmpty, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### Matching past the accents

`searchNormalize` compares both sides without their diacritics, so `zoe` finds `Zoë` and `oe` finds both. It normalizes to `NFD` and drops the combining diacritics, which leaves the labels themselves untouched — only the comparison changes.

```html
<template>
  <CCombobox placeholder="Find a name…" search search-normalize style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption value="zoe">Zoë</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="renee">Renée</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="joao">João</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="ana">Ana</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxEmpty>No results found</CListBoxEmpty>
  </CCombobox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CCombobox, CListBoxEmpty, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### External search

`search="external"` builds the same field and filters nothing. Every keystroke fires `search` with the query, and you answer with a new `items` array — the list shows what you hand it, so the query is yours to interpret.

```html
<template>
  <CCombobox
    :items="items"
    placeholder="Search users…"
    search="external"
    search-placeholder="Search users"
    style="max-width: 20rem"
    @search="onSearch"
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CCombobox } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const items = ref([])

let timer

const loadUsers = async (query) => {
  const response = await fetch(`https://apitest.coreui.io/demos/users?first_name=${query}&limit=10`)
  const users = await response.json()

  items.value = users.records.map((user) => ({
    label: `${user.first_name} ${user.last_name}`,
    value: String(user.id),
  }))
}

const onSearch = (query) => {
  clearTimeout(timer)
  timer = setTimeout(() => loadUsers(query), 300)
}

loadUsers('')
</script>
```

## Groups

Group options in a `<CListBoxSection>` and name it with `label`. The section carries `role="group"` and is announced with its name. A section whose options are all filtered out is hidden with its label.

```html
<template>
  <CCombobox name="language" placeholder="Select a language…" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxSection label="Frontend">
      <CListBoxOption value="html">HTML</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="css">CSS</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="js">JavaScript</CListBoxOption>
    </CListBoxSection>
    <CListBoxSection label="Backend">
      <CListBoxOption value="python">Python</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="ruby">Ruby</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="go">Go</CListBoxOption>
    </CListBoxSection>
  </CCombobox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption, CListBoxSection } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Multiple select

`multiple` toggles options instead of replacing the selection, and the panel stays open so several picks cost one opening. The toggle shows the one label while a single option is selected and `selectedLabel` past that — a function of the count and the number of options, or a string in which `{count}` and `{total}` are replaced. `selectionLimit` caps how many can be taken at once, and the `selectionLimit` event reports the limit together with the value it turned down.

```html
<template>
  <CCombobox
    indicator="checkbox"
    multiple
    name="skills"
    placeholder="Select skills…"
    selected-label="{count} selected"
    style="max-width: 20rem"
  >
    <CListBoxOption value="html">HTML</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="css">CSS</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="js">JavaScript</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="python">Python</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="ruby">Ruby</CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Sizing

The toggle carries `.form-control`, so `size` reaches it unchanged and it stands exactly as tall as a text input of the same size.

```html
<template>
  <CCombobox class="mb-4" placeholder="Small select…" size="sm" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption value="1">Option one</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="2">Option two</CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
  <CCombobox class="mb-4" placeholder="Default select…" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption value="1">Option one</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="2">Option two</CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
  <CCombobox placeholder="Large select…" size="lg" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption value="1">Option one</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="2">Option two</CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Disabled

`disabled` turns the whole control off — the panel never opens and the list box is disabled with it. A single option opts out with `disabled` on `<CListBoxOption>`, which takes it out of the keyboard order and out of every selection the user makes, and `disabled` on `<CListBoxSection>` does that for every option in it. A `value` or `defaultValue` naming a disabled option still selects it, as a native select does.

```html
<template>
  <CCombobox class="mb-4" disabled placeholder="Cannot interact…" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption value="1">Option one</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="2">Option two</CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
  <CCombobox placeholder="Select an option…" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption value="1">Available</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption disabled value="2">Unavailable</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="3">Available</CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Controlled value

`v-model:value` hands the selection to you: the component renders what you pass and reports every pick through `change`. `v-model:show` does the same for the panel. A native reset of the form puts back the value the combobox started with; a controlled one asks for its first `value` through `change` and keeps showing your `value` until you take it.

```html
<template>
  <CCombobox v-model:value="value" placeholder="Pick a country…" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption value="us">United States</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="uk">United Kingdom</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="ca">Canada</CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
  <div class="mt-4">Selected: {{ value ?? 'nothing' }}</div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const value = ref(null)
</script>
```

## Form submission

The component renders a hidden `<select class="combobox-select">` right after the toggle and keeps its selected options in step with the selection, so a combobox posts like a `<select>`, and like a `<select multiple>` in `multiple` mode: one key per value, `country=us&country=ca`. Set `name` to submit it; without a name the combobox is not submitted with the form. With nothing selected a single combobox posts `country=` and a `multiple` one posts nothing, as the native selects do. The select carries `.input-group-ignore`, so a toggle in an input group keeps its corners. A disabled combobox is not submitted, like any disabled field.

```html
<!-- What you write -->
<CCombobox name="country">…</CCombobox>

<!-- What the component renders after the toggle -->
<select class="combobox-select input-group-ignore" name="country" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true">
  <option value="us" selected>us</option>
</select>
```

## Validation

The hidden `<select>` takes part in the browser's validation, so `required` blocks the submit while nothing is selected. When a validation reports it, the component lays it along the start of the toggle, so the browser shows its message under the combobox, and the focus it gets goes to the toggle. The state shows on the toggle as the `.is-*` class, and the message after it is added to the toggle's `aria-describedby`. The messages come from the `feedback`, `feedback-invalid` and `feedback-valid` props, and the last two also from the slots of the same names.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row g-4" novalidate validate>
    <div class="col-md-6">
      <CFormLabel for="validationCountry">Country (required)</CFormLabel>
      <CCombobox
        id="validationCountry"
        feedback-invalid="Pick a country."
        name="country"
        placeholder="Pick a country…"
        required
      >
        <CListBoxOption value="us">United States</CListBoxOption>
        <CListBoxOption value="uk">United Kingdom</CListBoxOption>
        <CListBoxOption value="ca">Canada</CListBoxOption>
      </CCombobox>
    </div>
    <div class="col-md-6">
      <CFormLabel for="validationRole">Role</CFormLabel>
      <CCombobox
        id="validationRole"
        v-model:validation-state="roleState"
        default-value="admin"
        feedback="This project already has an admin."
        name="role"
      >
        <CListBoxOption value="admin">Admin</CListBoxOption>
        <CListBoxOption value="editor">Editor</CListBoxOption>
      </CCombobox>
    </div>
    <div class="col-12">
      <CButton color="primary" type="submit">Submit</CButton>
    </div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CCombobox, CForm, CFormLabel, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const roleState = ref('invalid')
</script>
```

The state comes from three places, in this order:

- `validationState`: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`. While it is set, the component draws it instead of what the browser reports. While it is `'invalid'`, the hidden select blocks the submit with the text of the linked message, or `Invalid value.` when there is none, unless the component is `disabled`.
- A validation that reports the hidden select invalid: a submit, `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()`, which [`CForm`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/validation/) and the stepper call as well. From then on the toggle shows it invalid whenever the value is invalid, until the form is reset, and the message after the toggle shows.
- In a form with `validate`, the `:user-invalid` state of the hidden select, and with `validate="valid"` also its `:user-valid` state.

A state you give is a verdict on the value it was given for. When the user picks a different value, or the form is reset, the component emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop the state, as the second field above does. A change your code makes through `v-model:value` keeps it, and so does picking the value the combobox already holds. A reset emits once it has run, so a state you set from a `reset` listener on the form gets the same event, and your handler decides whether to drop it. A native reset of the form puts back the value given by `default-value`, and leaves a bound `v-model:value` to you.

The toggle is a `<button>`, a role that has neither an invalid nor a required state, so it carries neither `aria-invalid` nor `aria-required`: a screen reader learns what is wrong from the message in its description, and that the field is required only from its label, so say it there, as the first field above does.

## Accessibility

The toggle is a real `<button>` carrying `aria-haspopup="listbox"` and `aria-expanded`; name it with a `<CFormLabel for>` or an `aria-label`. The panel is a [List box](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/list-box/), so `role="listbox"` sits on the options element and `role="option"` on every option, with `aria-selected` kept in step with the selection.

The focus never enters the list. It stays on the toggle, or on the search field when there is one, and the highlighted option is reported through `aria-activedescendant` on whichever of the two holds it.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `↓` / `↑` | Open the panel; once it is open, move the highlight to the next/previous option |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Open the panel; once it is open, select the highlighted option |
| `Home` / `End` | Move the highlight to the first/last option; the search field keeps them for the caret |
| `A` – `Z` | Move the highlight to the next option whose label starts with what you typed |
| `Escape` | Close the panel and return the focus to the toggle |
| `Tab` | Close the panel and move on |

## Customizing

### CSS variables

The toggle declares its own properties on `.combobox-toggle`:

```css
--cui-combobox-toggle-caret-color
--cui-combobox-toggle-caret-size
--cui-combobox-toggle-caret-transition-duration
--cui-combobox-toggle-caret-transition-timing
--cui-combobox-toggle-gap
--cui-combobox-toggle-placeholder-color
--cui-combobox-toggle-show-bg
```

The panel is the shared combobox surface, which only sizes itself:

```css
--cui-combobox-popup-min-width
```

Everything inside it — options, section labels and the checkbox indicator — is a [List box](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/list-box/) and takes its `--cui-list-box-*` variables. `.list-box` declares them itself, so a value set on `.combobox-popup` or on `:root` does not reach it: set them with a rule on `.combobox-popup .list-box`, which covers the panels of Combobox, Autocomplete and Multi Select alike. The frame of the toggle is a [`.form-control`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/form-control/) and takes the `--cui-control-*` properties.

## API

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

- [&lt;CCombobox /&gt;](./api/#ccombobox)
- [&lt;CListBoxEmpty /&gt;](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/list-box/api/#clistboxempty)
- [&lt;CListBoxOption /&gt;](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/list-box/api/#clistboxoption)
- [&lt;CListBoxSection /&gt;](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/list-box/api/#clistboxsection)

# Vue Combobox Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Combobox component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CCombobox

```jsx
import { CCombobox } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaSearchLabel` | `string` | `'Search options'` | A string that provides an accessible name for the search field. |
| `caretIcon` | `boolean \| VNode \| string` | `undefined` | The caret drawn at the end of the toggle. Pass `false` to draw none. |
| `container` | `HTMLElement \| (() => HTMLElement) \| string` | `'body'` | The element the panel is rendered into instead of `document.body`. Implies `portal`. Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert. |
| `defaultShow` | `boolean` | - | The initial visibility of the panel, when it is not controlled through `show`. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| string[] \| null` | - | The initially selected values, when the selection is not controlled through `value`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Turns the control off: the panel never opens and the list box is disabled with it. |
| `feedback` | `string` | - | Feedback for the current `validationState` — rendered only while the state is set, and styled after it. For the client-side mode, where the browser owns the state, use `feedbackValid` and `feedbackInvalid` instead. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `string` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is invalid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `feedbackValid` | `string` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is valid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `indicator` | `ListBoxIndicator` | `'none'` | Renders a checkbox in every option, so a multiple selection reads as a list of checkboxes. |
| `items` | `ListBoxOption[]` | - | The options to render. Each entry is passed to the default slot as `item`, so the slot works as the option template; without a slot every entry renders as a `<CListBoxOption>` showing its `label`. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | - | Toggles options instead of replacing the selection, and keeps the panel open. |
| `name` | `string` | - | Name of the hidden select the value is submitted under. With `multiple` it posts one key per value, as a `<select multiple>` does: `tags=a&tags=b&tags=c`. Without a name the combobox is not submitted with the form. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | Text shown in the toggle while nothing is selected. It carries `.combobox-placeholder` while it stands for an empty value. |
| `portal` | `boolean` | - | Renders the panel through a portal: into the open `<dialog>` the field sits in, otherwise into `document.body`. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | Makes the hidden select that carries the value required, so an empty combobox blocks the submit. |
| `search` | `ListBoxSearch` | `false` | Puts a search field at the top of the panel. `true` filters the list itself; `'external'` filters nothing and reports every keystroke through the `search` event instead. |
| `searchNormalize` | `boolean` | - | Compares both sides of the filter without their diacritics, so `zoe` matches `Zoë`. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | `'Search'` | Placeholder of the search field. |
| `selectedLabel` | `CountLabel` | `() => defaultSelectedLabel` | What the toggle shows past one selected option in the `multiple` mode. A function `(count, total) => string`, or a string in which `{count}` and `{total}` are replaced. |
| `selectionLimit` | `number` | - | The number of options the selection stops at, in the `multiple` mode. |
| `show` | `boolean` | `undefined` | The visibility of the panel. Supports the `v-model:show` binding. |
| `size` | `string` | - | Size the toggle the way a text input of the same size is sized. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `typeahead` | `boolean` | `true` | Move the highlight to the option matching what the user types. The buffer resets after 500 ms. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class on the toggle, with the feedback message in its `aria-describedby`; `'invalid'` also blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next pick of a different value emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`. |
| `value` | `string \| string[] \| null` | `undefined` | The selected values. When set, the component renders that selection and only reports the user's changes through the `change` event. Supports the `v-model:value` binding. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `change` | Callback fired when the selection changes. The value is an array in the `multiple` mode, a string or `null` otherwise. |
| `hide` | Callback fired when the panel has been closed. |
| `search` | Callback fired when the search field changes. In the `'external'` search mode it is the only report the component makes — nothing is filtered here. |
| `selectionLimit` | Callback fired when `selectionLimit` refuses a pick, with the limit and the value that did not fit. |
| `show` | Callback fired when the panel has been opened. |
| `update:show` | Emit the visibility of the panel to support the `v-model:show` binding. |
| `update:validationState` | Event occurs with `undefined` when the user picks a different value, or the form is reset, while `validationState` is set. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it and let the browser's own validation show again. |
| `update:value` | Emit the selected value to support the `v-model:value` binding. |
