# Vue Date Input Component

> Create Vue date fields with a section-based input mask. Users type the day, month, and year in separate sections with automatic navigation and validation — like the native date input, but with full control over the format.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Example

_Added in 5.22.0._

The Vue Date Input component renders a masked date field. The mask is split into day, month, and year sections — click or focus a section and type, use arrow keys to adjust values, and the caret moves to the next section automatically.

By default, the section order and separators are derived from the user's locale, so `12/31/2026` in `en-US` becomes `31.12.2026` in `de-DE` without any configuration.

Pass `date` one-way and it seeds the field, which keeps managing itself from there; bind it with `v-model:date` and the field follows your state — a committed change the parent doesn't accept is reverted — while `date-change` alone only reports what the field does. `date` is compared by timestamp, so an inline `new Date(...)` re-created on every render doesn't disturb typing. A native reset of the form asks a bound field for the `date` it started with through `update:date` and `date-change`.

A field holds what its format shows. The time of day of a `date` given to a field without a time is not kept: the first change the user makes reaches `date-change` at midnight, and a format with a time set later shows 00:00. Use `type="datetime"` or a format with a time when the time matters.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CDateInput label="Delivery date" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDateInput date="2022-08-17" label="Delivery date" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Date and time

Set `type="datetime"` and the field carries the time as well. The hour cycle follows the locale, so a 12-hour locale gets an AM/PM section and a 24-hour one does not. Everything else on this page applies unchanged: the same typing, the same arrow keys, the same `date-change`.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CDateInput label="Appointment" locale="en-US" type="datetime" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDateInput date="2026-07-14 14:30" label="Appointment" locale="en-US" type="datetime" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

Add `seconds` for a seconds section:

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDateInput label="Timestamp" seconds type="datetime" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

`type="time"` keeps only the time sections. That is the field [`<CTimeInput>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/time-input/) renders, with `v-model:time` and `@time-change` in place of `v-model:date` and `@date-change`.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDateInput label="Opening hour" type="time" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

A `format` overrides the type, because it names the sections itself. [`<CDateRangeInput>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/date-range-input/) takes both props too, so a range with time is the same two props on the range component.

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <span class="form-label">Delivery date</span>
    <CDateInput locale="en-US" name="deliveryDate" />
    <CFormText>We deliver on working days only.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CFormText } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Formats

Set an explicit format with the `format` property. The parser accepts both dayjs/moment-style tokens (`DD`, `MM`, `YYYY`, `YY`) and date-fns/Unicode-style tokens (`dd`, `MM`, `yyyy`, `yy`), so you can reuse the format strings from the date library you already use. Any other character becomes a literal separator.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-4 mb-4 mb-lg-0">
      <CDateInput format="dd.MM.yyyy" label="dd.MM.yyyy" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-4 mb-4 mb-lg-0">
      <CDateInput format="YYYY-MM-DD" label="YYYY-MM-DD" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CDateInput format="MM/DD/YY" label="MM/DD/YY" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

Two-digit year sections expand with smart century assignment — values up to 50 years in the future resolve to the current century, older ones to the previous century.

The format doesn't have to include every section — a month-and-year mask works like the native `month` input and reports the first day of the month:

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CDateInput format="MM.yyyy" label="MM.yyyy" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDateInput format="MMMM yyyy" label="MMMM yyyy" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

For picking whole weeks, use the [date picker](../date-picker/) with `selectionType="week"` — a masked week-number field has no native or MUI equivalent and isn't supported.

## Month names

Use the `MMM` or `MMMM` tokens for text month sections with localized short or full month names. Type letters to match a month by prefix — `m` selects <strong>M</strong>arch, continuing with `may` switches to <strong>May</strong> — and the caret moves on as soon as the prefix is unambiguous. Digits and arrow keys keep working too.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CDateInput format="DD MMMM YYYY" label="DD MMMM YYYY" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDateInput format="MMM D, YYYY" label="MMM D, YYYY" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

Month names default to the grammatical form used inside a full date — e.g. Polish shows the genitive `14 lipca 2026`, not the standalone `lipiec`. To use a different form (or your own localization), pass all twelve names through the `monthNames` property; they are used for display, letter matching, and paste alike.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDateInput
        format="DD MMMM YYYY"
        label="Standalone Polish month names"
        locale="pl-PL"
        :month-names="monthNames"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const monthNames = [
  'styczeń',
  'luty',
  'marzec',
  'kwiecień',
  'maj',
  'czerwiec',
  'lipiec',
  'sierpień',
  'wrzesień',
  'październik',
  'listopad',
  'grudzień',
]
</script>
```

## Locale

Without an explicit format, the mask follows the locale set via the `locale` property.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-4 mb-4 mb-lg-0">
      <CDateInput label="en-US" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-4 mb-4 mb-lg-0">
      <CDateInput label="pl-PL" locale="pl-PL" year-placeholder="RRRR" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CDateInput label="ja-JP" locale="ja-JP" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Min and max dates

Constrain the selectable range with `minDate` and `maxDate`. A completed date outside the range gets the `.is-invalid` class and the component reports `null` until the value is corrected. A date field compares the limits by the day. A field with a time compares them to the smallest unit it shows, and there a `maxDate` without a time of day covers its whole day.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDateInput
        format="dd.MM.yyyy"
        label="Date in July 2026"
        max-date="2026-07-31"
        min-date="2026-07-01"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Disabled dates

Beyond a simple range, the `disabledDates` property excludes specific dates — single `Date`s, `[start, end]` ranges, or a matcher function. Unlike in the [date picker](../date-picker/#disabled-dates), there is no calendar to gray out: a completed date that hits a disabled entry gets the `.is-invalid` class and the component reports `null` until the value is corrected.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CDateInput
        :date="new Date(2026, 6, 10)"
        :disabled-dates="disabledDates"
        format="dd.MM.yyyy"
        label="Delivery date"
        :max-date="new Date(2026, 6, 31)"
        :min-date="new Date(2026, 6, 1)"
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDateInput
        :disabled-dates="(date) => date.getDay() === 0 || date.getDay() === 6"
        format="dd.MM.yyyy"
        label="Business day"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const disabledDates = [[new Date(2026, 6, 4), new Date(2026, 6, 7)], new Date(2026, 6, 16)]
</script>
```

## Custom formats

The built-in token parser covers dayjs, moment, date-fns, and luxon format strings for date masks, so you can reuse the format string from the date library you already work with — the library itself isn't required to render or edit the mask. Pair it with `inputDateParse` when you want that library to also parse text pasted into the field, here with `date-fns`:

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDateInput
        :date="new Date(2022, 8, 3)"
        format="MMMM DD, YYYY"
        :input-date-parse="(value) => parse(value, 'MMMM dd, yyyy', new Date())"
        label="date-fns format"
        locale="en-US"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
import { parse } from 'date-fns'
</script>
```

## Validation

The field shows its validation state on the element and on its sections, and links the message that follows it, the way [`<CForm>`](../validation/) does for a native field. It keeps its value in a `<textarea>` laid invisibly over the field, which takes part in native constraint validation: a `required` field that is empty, incomplete or holds a rejected date blocks the submit, and the browser, or `<CForm>`, puts focus on its first empty section, the browser with its own message over the field. A field that is not required does not block, and submits no date while it rejects one.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row g-4" novalidate validate>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDateInput
        feedback-invalid="Please provide a delivery date."
        format="dd.MM.yyyy"
        label="Delivery date (required)"
        name="delivery"
        required
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDateInput
        v-model:validation-state="pickupState"
        date="2026-07-20"
        feedback="We have no pickup slots left on this date."
        format="dd.MM.yyyy"
        label="Pickup date"
        name="pickup"
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-12">
      <CButton color="primary" type="submit">Submit</CButton>
    </div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDateInput, CForm } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const pickupState = ref('invalid')
</script>
```

The state comes from four places, in this order:

- The limits: a completed date outside `minDate`/`maxDate`/`disabledDates` makes the field invalid until it is corrected, whatever else is set, whether the user typed it or the field got it through its value, and again when the limits change. Until then the value field submits no date, also in a read-only field. A date before year 1 counts as before `minDate` even without that prop; when the field loses the focus, its year becomes 1.
- `validationState`: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`, for example after a server has checked the date.
- A validation that reports the field invalid: a submit, `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()`, which `<CForm>` and the [stepper](../stepper/) call as well. From then on the field shows it invalid whenever its date is invalid, until a native reset of the form.
- In a form with the `validate` property of `<CForm>` (the `data-coreui-validate` attribute), the `:user-invalid` and `:user-valid` states of the value field, the same states the stylesheet reads on a native field. A field becomes `.is-valid` only when the form opts into success styling with `validate="valid"`.

A state you give is a verdict on the date it was given for. When the user changes the date, with a typed digit or letter, an arrow, <kbd>Backspace</kbd> or <kbd>Delete</kbd>, a paste or a cut, or the form is reset, the component emits `update:validationState` with `undefined` before `date-change`; bind the state with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it, as the second field above does. A key that leaves the field as it is emits nothing, and neither does a change your code makes through `date`. While the given state is `'invalid'`, the field blocks the submit like any invalid field, with the text of the linked message, or `Invalid value.` when there is none; a custom validity you set on the value field yourself stays as it is, and a disabled or read-only field does not block. An `aria-invalid` you pass is not read as a state. A native form reset returns the field to the date it started with; a `reset` listener that calls `preventDefault()` cancels the whole reset. A field your page controls, with `v-model:date` or the `date-change` event, keeps the value your page gives it.

While the field is invalid, its `feedbackInvalid` text and an `.invalid-feedback` or `.invalid-tooltip` you render after the field yourself describe every section, so a screen reader reads the error with the field. A message rendered later, while the field stays invalid, is picked up when the field next updates, or right after the `error` event when you render it in reply to that event.

To react to validation transitions programmatically, use the `error` event: it receives `'incomplete'`, `'minDate'`, `'maxDate'`, `'disabledDate'`, or `null` when the value is valid or the field is empty.

## Floating labels

Use the `floatingLabel` property. When the field is empty and not focused, the mask placeholders are hidden so the label can rest inside the field; focusing the field floats the label and reveals the mask.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDateInput id="floatingDateInput" floating-label="Delivery date" format="dd.MM.yyyy" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

Set `floatingLabelAlways` to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the mask showing.

## Sizing

The field renders as a `.form-control`, so the standard sizing works — set the `size` property to `lg` or `sm`.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-4 mb-4 mb-lg-0">
      <CDateInput format="dd.MM.yyyy" label="Large" size="lg" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-4 mb-4 mb-lg-0">
      <CDateInput format="dd.MM.yyyy" label="Default" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CDateInput format="dd.MM.yyyy" label="Small" size="sm" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Disabled and readonly

Set the `disabled` property to disable the field, or `readOnly` to make it focusable but non-editable.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CDateInput date="2026-07-14" disabled format="dd.MM.yyyy" label="Disabled" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDateInput date="2026-07-14" format="dd.MM.yyyy" label="Readonly" read-only />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Accessibility

The date input implements the [spinbutton pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/spinbutton/) per section, mirroring the internal structure of the native date input:

- **Role attributes**: the container has `role="group"`, every section is a `role="spinbutton"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow`, and `aria-valuetext` (month sections announce the localized month name).
- **Roving tabindex**: the whole field is a single tab stop; arrow keys move between sections.
- **Labels**: `label` and `floatingLabel` name the group through `aria-labelledby`, and an `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label` you pass wins over both; without an `aria-label`, or with an empty one, the group also carries `aria-label="Date input"` (`Date and time input` with `type="datetime"`, `Time input` with `type="time"`), the name it is announced by when nothing else names it. Sections receive `aria-label`s (`Day`, `Month`, `Year`), each replaceable on its own — `ariaDayLabel`, `ariaMonthLabel`, `ariaYearLabel` — for localization.
- **Label click**: clicking the `label`, a `<label>` or `.form-label` an `aria-labelledby` you pass points at, or a `<label for>` pointing at the field's `id` moves focus to the first empty section, as clicking the label of an input focuses it.
- **Validity**: while the field is invalid (a date outside `minDate` / `maxDate` or in `disabledDates`, typed, pasted or given as the value, a date before year 1, `validationState="invalid"`, or a `required` field a validation has reported and that is still empty), every section carries `aria-invalid="true"`; the group, which takes no focus, carries none, and an `aria-invalid` you set on the field is not read. A disabled or read-only field is never reported as missing. With `required`, every section carries `aria-required="true"`.
- **Description**: the field is described by the `aria-describedby` you set, then its `text`, then the feedback that matches its state; that description reaches the first section, and every section while the field is invalid, together with an error message you render after the field, so the error is read wherever the focus sits.
- **Mobile input**: sections use `inputmode="numeric"`, so touch devices show the numeric keyboard.

### Keyboard support

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>0</kbd>–<kbd>9</kbd> | Type into the focused section; the caret advances when the section is complete |
| <kbd>A</kbd>–<kbd>Z</kbd> | In text month sections, match a month name by prefix; the caret advances when the prefix is unambiguous |
| <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> | Increment / decrement the focused section, wrapping day and month around their bounds; an empty year starts at the current year |
| <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> | Move focus to the next / previous section; in a right-to-left layout the two keys swap |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | Move focus to the first / last section |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd> | Clear the focused section; move to the previous section when already empty |
| <kbd>Delete</kbd> | Clear the focused section |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> | Select the whole value; <kbd>Backspace</kbd> then clears all sections, typing restarts from the first section |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> | Copy the selection — the whole formatted value after <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> | Paste a date and fill all sections |

Apart from the shortcuts in the table, a key pressed with <kbd>Alt</kbd>, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> changes nothing in the field and is not cancelled: arrows, <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> move no focus and change no section, and a digit or letter is not entered. The key stays free for the browser, assistive technology and the picker around the field, where <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> opens the calendar. A character that <kbd>AltGr</kbd> or <kbd>Option</kbd> composes is still entered.

# Vue Date Input Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Date Input component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## CDateInput

```jsx
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaDayLabel` | `string` | `'Day'` | The `aria-label` of the day section. |
| `ariaHourLabel` | `string` | `'Hour'` | The `aria-label` of the hour section. |
| `ariaMeridiemLabel` | `string` | `'AM/PM'` | The `aria-label` of the meridiem section. |
| `ariaMinuteLabel` | `string` | `'Minute'` | The `aria-label` of the minute section. |
| `ariaMonthLabel` | `string` | `'Month'` | The `aria-label` of the month section. |
| `ariaQuarterLabel` | `string` | `'Quarter'` | The `aria-label` of the quarter section. |
| `ariaSecondLabel` | `string` | `'Second'` | The `aria-label` of the second section. |
| `ariaWeekLabel` | `string` | `'Week'` | The `aria-label` of the week section. |
| `ariaYearLabel` | `string` | `'Year'` | The `aria-label` of the year section. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | - | Focus the first section right after mounting, like the native `autofocus` attribute. |
| `date` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | The date — a `Date` or a date string like `'2026-07-14'`, one with a time part like `'2026-07-14 14:30'` on `type="datetime"`, or a time string like `'14:30'` on `type="time"`. Passed one-way it seeds the field, which keeps managing itself; bound with `v-model:date` it follows your state. |
| `dayPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `DD` the day section shows while it is empty. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `disabledDates` | `DisabledDate \| DisabledDate[]` | `undefined` | Specify the list of dates that cannot be selected. It can be a single `Date`, an `[start, end]` range, a matcher function, or an array of these. |
| `feedback` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable feedback to your users with HTML5 form validation feedback. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable invalid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied `validationState="invalid"`. |
| `feedbackValid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable valid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied `validationState="valid"`. |
| `floatingClassName` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the floating label wrapper. |
| `floatingLabel` | `string` | - | Wrap the field in a floating label. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `format` | `string \| ((locale: string) => DateSection[])` | `undefined` | The mask layout. A string is parsed as dayjs/moment or date-fns/luxon format tokens, a function receives the locale and returns the section layout, and `undefined` derives the layout from the locale. |
| `hourPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `HH` (`hh` on a 12-hour clock) the hour section shows while it is empty. |
| `id` | `string` | - | The id attribute of the field. |
| `inputDateParse` | `(value: string) => Date \| null` | `undefined` | Custom function to parse text pasted into the field into a `Date` object, e.g. with an external date library. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `locale` | `string` | `'default'` | Sets the default locale for the component. If not set, it is inherited from the browser. |
| `maxDate` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | Max selectable date. |
| `meridiemPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `AM` the meridiem section shows while it is empty. |
| `minDate` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | Min selectable date. |
| `minutePlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `mm` the minute section shows while it is empty. |
| `monthNames` | `string[]` | `undefined` | Twelve custom month names for text month sections (`MMM`/`MMMM`), overriding the locale-derived, date-context grammatical form. |
| `monthPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `MM` the month section shows while it is empty. |
| `name` | `string` | - | Name of the value input the value is submitted under. Without it the field is not submitted with the form. |
| `quarterPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `Q` the quarter section shows while it is empty. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the readonly state for the component. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | When present, it specifies that the field must be filled out before submitting the form. |
| `secondPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `ss` the second section shows while it is empty. |
| `seconds` | `boolean` | - | Include a seconds section in the locale-derived time layout. |
| `size` | `string` | `undefined` | Size the component small or large. |
| `text` | `string` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `type` | `string` | `'date'` | Which sections the locale-derived layout carries. A `format` names the sections itself and overrides this. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` on every section and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. A field of a date range whose end is before its start draws no other state. The user's next change of the value emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`. |
| `weekPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `WW` the week section shows while it is empty. |
| `yearPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `YYYY` the year section shows while it is empty. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `date-change` | Callback fired when the date changes; receives the `Date` (or `null` while incomplete or invalid) and the formatted value. |
| `error` | Callback fired when the validation state changes; receives `'incomplete'`, `'minDate'`, `'maxDate'`, `'disabledDate'`, or `null` when the value is valid or the field is empty. When one change moves both the value and the validation state, it fires after `date-change`, so a value set from it replaces the one just reported. |
| `update:date` | Emit the new date to support the `v-model:date` binding. |
| `update:validationState` | Event occurs with `undefined` when the user changes the date, or the form is reset, while `validationState` is set. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it and let the browser's own validation show again. |

# Vue Date Input Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Date Input component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

### CSS variables

The date, time, and date-time inputs share one set of styles under the `form-date-time` name. The field is a [`.form-control`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/input/styling/#css-variables), so its frame comes from the `--cui-control-*` tokens; the ones below style the sections inside it. Both sets sit on the field, where `class` and `style` on `<CDateInput>` land, and can be set on a single element.

```scss
// Redeclaring a --cui-control-* token here would shadow `.form-control`
// on the same element, and with it the validation states.
$form-date-time-tokens: () !default;
$form-date-time-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-date-time-placeholder-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-form-date-time-section-border-radius: .25rem,
    --cui-form-date-time-section-focus-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg-subtle),
  ),
  $form-date-time-tokens
);
```

# Vue Date Picker Component

> The Vue Date Picker Component is an essential tool for any Vue-based application that requires date selection functionality.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## About

This component, provided by CoreUI for Vue.js, offers a user-friendly interface and various customization options to ensure an excellent user experience.

With its responsive design and support for all modern browsers, the Vue Date Picker Component can be easily integrated into any application. The component comes with an array of styling options, including color, size, and shape, that can be easily adjusted to fit the application's design.

The Vue Date Picker Component is also fully customizable, allowing developers to tailor the component to their specific needs. With its set of APIs, developers can control the default value, visibility, and date range of the component.

One of the standout features of the Vue Date Picker Component is its accessibility. CoreUI has ensured that the component is fully compliant with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), making it accessible to all users. The component supports keyboard navigation and screen readers, ensuring that users with disabilities can also benefit from its functionality.

## Example

Below is an example of a basic Vue DatePicker.

### Days

Basic examples demonstrating how to pick dates using the Vue Date Picker Component.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CDatePicker label="Date" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDatePicker date="2022/2/16" label="Date" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

#### With footer

The `footer` slot projects your own content below the calendar. Its slot props carry the picker's context — `setDate`, `today`, `clear`, `reset`, `close`, `isDateSelectable`, `date` and `disabled` — so a projected button acts on the picker and reads its state. That is also how a "Today" button disables itself when today falls outside `minDate`, `maxDate` or `disabledDates`; the example checks when the panel renders and again on click, so a date that crosses a limit while the panel is open is not written.

Any descendant can reach the same context with the `useDatePicker()` composable.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CDatePicker locale="en-US">
        <template #footer="{ clear, close, isDateSelectable, today }">
          <CButton
            class="me-auto"
            theme="danger"
            :disabled="!isDateSelectable(new Date())"
            size="sm"
            variant="ghost"
            @click="isDateSelectable(new Date()) && today()"
          >
            Today
          </CButton>
          <CButton theme="primary" size="sm" variant="ghost" @click="clear">Clear</CButton>
          <CButton theme="primary" size="sm" @click="close">OK</CButton>
        </template>
      </CDatePicker>
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDatePicker date="2022/2/16" locale="en-US">
        <template #footer="{ close, reset }">
          <CButton class="me-auto" theme="primary" size="sm" variant="ghost" @click="reset">
            Reset
          </CButton>
          <CButton theme="primary" size="sm" @click="close">OK</CButton>
        </template>
      </CDatePicker>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CButton, CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### With v-model

The `v-model:date` binding keeps the selected date in sync with your component's state.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row mb-4">
    <div class="col-lg-6">
      <CDatePicker v-model:date="vDate" label="Date" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
  </div>
  <div>{{ vDate && vDate.toLocaleDateString([], options) }}</div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
import { ref } from 'vue'
const vDate = ref(new Date(2022, 2, 1))
const options = {
  year: 'numeric',
  month: 'long',
  day: 'numeric',
  weekday: 'long',
}
</script>
```

## With time

Set `timepicker` to add the time half. The field switches to a date and time mask, the panel grows a row of time selects under the calendar, and picking a day no longer closes the panel — the two halves own different parts of one value, so the interaction is not over until the user says so. While no time is picked, or the field holds a time a list does not offer, each select stands on a `--` placeholder, so every enabled option, the first allowed one included, sets the time.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CDatePicker label="Appointment" locale="en-US" timepicker />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDatePicker date="2026/07/14 14:30:00" label="Appointment" locale="en-US" timepicker />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

`minDate` and `maxDate` can carry a time of day. Their day stays selectable in the calendar and the time selects disable the hours, minutes and seconds before `minDate` or after `maxDate` on that day. A time the panel sets beyond a limit, such as the current time when the day of `minDate` is picked, moves to the limit; a typed time beyond it marks the field invalid. Until a date is picked, the time selects work on today moved into the limits. A limit without a time of day covers its whole day.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDatePicker
        label="Appointment"
        locale="en-US"
        :max-date="new Date(2026, 9, 30, 17)"
        :min-date="new Date(2026, 9, 15, 9, 30)"
        timepicker
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

`seconds`, `minutes` and `hours` narrow what the time half offers, and are ignored without `timepicker`. Hours are 0 to 23 in every locale; on a 12-hour clock an hour that only one period allows sets that period.

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

A native reset of the form returns the picker to the date it started with and drops the state a submit set; a picker bound with `v-model:date` asks for the date it started with through `update:date` and `date-change` and shows the date your page gives until the page takes it.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <span class="form-label">Delivery date</span>
    <CDatePicker locale="en-US" name="deliveryDate" />
    <CFormText>We deliver on working days only.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CFormText } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Cleaner and picker button

The field ends with two buttons: one clears the value, the other opens the calendar. The `cleanerIcon` and `pickerIcon` slots swap their artwork for your own, `:cleaner="false"` leaves the cleaner out, and `:picker-icon="false"` leaves out the button that opens the calendar. Without that button the popup has no pointer opener and nothing reports the expanded state, though the field keeps the keyboard openers listed under [Keyboard support](#keyboard-support).

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDatePicker date="2022/08/17" locale="en-US">
        <template #cleanerIcon>
          <CIcon :icon="cilXCircle" />
        </template>
        <template #pickerIcon>
          <CIcon :icon="cilCalendarCheck" />
        </template>
      </CDatePicker>
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDatePicker :cleaner="false" date="2022/08/17" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
import { CIcon } from '@coreui/icons-vue'
import { cilCalendarCheck, cilXCircle } from '@coreui/icons'
</script>
```

## Floating labels

Set `floatingLabel` and the component wraps its input in `.form-floating` and renders the label itself — the text also becomes the field's accessible name. No wrapper markup is needed, and the mask placeholders stay hidden while the label rests inside the field.

```html
<template>
  <CDatePicker floating-label="Delivery date" locale="en-US" />
</template>
```

Set `floatingLabelAlways` to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the mask showing.

## Sizing

Set heights using `size` property like `size="lg"` and `size="sm"`.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row mb-5">
    <div class="col-lg-6">
      <CDatePicker locale="en-US" size="lg" />
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CDatePicker locale="en-US" size="sm" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Disabled dates

CoreUI Vue DatePicker component includes a feature that allows you to disable certain dates, such as weekends or holidays. This can be accomplished by passing an array to `disabledDate` prop to the component, which determines which dates should be disabled based on custom logic.

In week, month, quarter and year selection the calendar and the field judge the whole period: it is refused only when it lies wholly before `minDate` or after `maxDate`, or `disabledDates` covers every day of it that the limits leave. In week selection the limits count as whole weeks, so for a week that is all seven days.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CDatePicker
        :calendar-date="calendarDate"
        :disabled-dates="disabledDates"
        locale="en-US"
        :max-date="maxDate"
        :min-date="minDate"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const calendarDate = new Date(2022, 2, 1)
const disabledDates = [
  [new Date(2022, 2, 4), new Date(2022, 2, 7)],
  new Date(2022, 2, 16),
  new Date(2022, 3, 16),
  [new Date(2022, 4, 2), new Date(2022, 4, 8)],
]
const maxDate = new Date(2022, 5, 0)
const minDate = new Date(2022, 1, 1)
</script>
```

### Disabling weekends

You can disable weekends by passing a function to the `disabledDates` prop. Here's how to do it:

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDatePicker :disabled-dates="disableWeekends" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const disableWeekends = (date) => {
  const day = date.getDay()
  return day === 0 || day === 6 // Disable Sundays (0) and Saturdays (6)
}
</script>
```

## Validation

The picker shows its validation state on the frame and on the sections of its field, which the message after the picker describes, the way [`<CForm>`](../validation/) does for a native field. The field keeps its value in a `<textarea>` laid invisibly over it, so a `required` picker that is empty, incomplete or holds a rejected date blocks the submit, as the [date input](../date-input/#validation) does. The picker also sets the state itself: a date the limits reject marks it invalid, for as long as it stands.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row g-4" novalidate validate>
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDatePicker
        feedback-invalid="Please provide a start date."
        label="Start date (required)"
        locale="en-US"
        name="start"
        required
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDatePicker
        v-model:validation-state="deliveryState"
        date="2026-07-14"
        feedback="We have no delivery slots left on this date."
        label="Delivery date"
        locale="en-US"
        name="delivery"
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-12">
      <CButton color="primary" type="submit">Submit</CButton>
    </div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDatePicker, CForm } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const deliveryState = ref('invalid')
</script>
```

`validationState` gives a state: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`, with `invalid` and `valid` as deprecated aliases that ask to be dropped the same way, though only a `validation-state` bound with `v-model:validation-state` is cleared by it. A given state is a verdict on the date it was given for. When the user changes the date, with a day picked in the calendar, a time picked with `timepicker`, the cleaner, a footer button that changes the date through the context, or typing in the field, or the form is reset, the picker emits `update:validationState` with `undefined` before `date-change`; bind the state with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it, as the second picker above does. An action that leaves the date as it is emits nothing, and neither does a change your code makes through `date`. While the given state is `'invalid'`, the picker blocks the submit with the text of the message after it, or `Invalid value.` when there is none.

## Locale

CoreUI Vue Date Picker allows users to display dates and times in a non-English locale. This is useful for applications that have international users or need to support multiple languages.

### Auto

By default, the DatePicker component uses the default browser locale, but it can be easily configured to use a different locale supported by the JavaScript Internationalization API. To set the locale, you can simply pass the desired language code as a prop to the DatePicker component. This feature enables to create more inclusive and accessible applications that cater to a diverse audience.

With server-side rendering, pass `locale` explicitly: by default the server writes the text in its own locale and the browser in the reader's, and Vue reports a hydration mismatch when the two differ.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CDatePicker />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Custom container

By default the calendar is rendered in `document.body`. Pass an HTML element, or a function that returns one, to the `container` property to render it somewhere else — for example inside a scrollable panel or a modal, so that it scrolls together with the rest of the content.

```html
<template>
  <div ref="container">
    <CDatePicker v-if="container" :container="container" locale="en-US" />
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const container = ref(null)
</script>
```

To render the calendar in place, right after the input group, set `portal` to `false` instead.

## Custom formats

The `format` property is a mask: it spells out the sections the field renders. Tokens are `dd` for the day, `ww` for the ISO week, `MM` (`MMM`, `MMMM` for names) for the month, `QQQ` for the quarter, `yyyy` for the year, and text in single quotes is a literal, even when it contains token letters — `'Week' ww, yyyy` renders `Week 29, 2026`. Without it the field follows the locale's own date format.

`inputDateParse` still applies to pasted text, turning a custom string into a `Date`.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CDatePicker
        date="2022/08/17"
        format="MMMM dd, yyyy"
        label="Date picker"
        locale="en-US"
        :input-date-parse="(date) => parse(date, 'MMMM dd, yyyy', new Date())"
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CDatePicker
        date="2022/08/17"
        format="yyyy MMMM dd"
        label="Selector de fechas"
        locale="es-ES"
        :input-date-parse="(date) => parse(date, 'yyyy MMMM dd', new Date(), { locale: es })"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
import { parse } from 'date-fns'
import { es } from 'date-fns/locale'
</script>
```

### Weeks

Setting `selectionType` to `'week'` narrows the field to the locale's week presentation — `Week 29, 2026`. Override it with a mask of your own: `yyyy-'W'ww` for the ISO form, or a localized label. The `showWeekNumber` property adds the week numbers to the calendar.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CDatePicker
        date="2022W10"
        format="yyyy-'W'ww"
        label="Date picker"
        locale="en-US"
        selection-type="week"
        show-week-number
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CDatePicker
        date="2022W10"
        format="'Semana' ww, yyyy"
        label="Selector de fechas"
        locale="es-ES"
        selection-type="week"
        show-week-number
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### Months

Setting `selectionType` to `'month'` narrows the field to `MM/yyyy`. Give `format` a mask of your own — `MMM yyyy` renders the month name instead of its number.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CDatePicker
        date="2022-08"
        format="MMM yyyy"
        label="Date picker"

      />
    </div>

        format="MMM yyyy"
        label="Selector de fechas"
        locale="es-ES"
        selection-type="month"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Open state

_Added in 6.0.0._

Bind `v-model:show` and the calendar renders what you pass — dismiss gestures only emit `update:show`, so the binding feeds the change back. Here a checkbox pins the calendar open, and a dismiss gesture unchecks it.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField class="mb-4">
    <CCheckbox id="datePickerControlledShow" v-model="show" label="Keep the calendar open" />
  </CFormField>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDatePicker v-model:show="show" label="Date Picker" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CCheckbox, CDatePicker, CFormField } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

Use it when the open state belongs to something else — a route, a tour step, or a control outside the picker like the checkbox above.

### Initial open state

Without a binding the picker manages its own calendar. Pass `show` to seed it open on mount.

```vue
<CDatePicker show />
```

The `update:show` event fires either way whenever the calendar requests an open-state change — a dismiss gesture (Escape, a click outside) or any internal toggle — so you can watch the state without taking it over. The deprecated `visible` prop keeps its old behavior and is ignored when `show` is set.

## Accessibility

The field is a group of spinbutton sections, so its own arrow keys belong to the value and the popup opens on the native control's dropdown keys instead. The field takes its name from an `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label` you pass to the picker, otherwise from `floatingLabel` or, without one, from `label`, and it is described by an `aria-describedby` you pass to the picker, then by `text` and the feedback that matches its state. Clicking the label that names the field moves focus to its first empty section. Focus enters the calendar on the selected date, else on today or on the `minDate` / `maxDate` today falls outside of, also when that date cannot be picked: it is announced as unavailable and the arrows move on from it. In week selection it enters on the row of that week.

The toggle button carries the panel's state — `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-controls` pointing at the popup while it is open, and `aria-expanded` — so a screen reader announces what the button does and whether the panel is showing. The panel itself is a `dialog` with `aria-modal`, so focus moves into it on open, stays there while it is open, and returns to the element that opened it, the toggle or the field, when it closes.

The toggle's name ends with the date the picker holds, written in full (`Toggle calendar, Friday, August 14, 2026`, with the time after it with `timepicker`), so a screen reader reads the picked date when the popup closes and focus goes back to the toggle. A live message would be lost at that moment, so the calendar does not announce a pick that closes the popup onto that toggle. With `timepicker` the popup stays open, and the calendar announces the pick through `ariaSelectedDateAnnouncement`; it does the same without a toggle (`pickerIcon` set to `false`).

### Keyboard support

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd> (<kbd>Option</kbd> on macOS) + <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> / <kbd>F4</kbd> | Open the popup and move focus into it |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close the popup and return focus to the field or the toggle that opened it |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> / <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move within the open panel; the field is outside the dialog and stays out of the cycle |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Select the focused value |

Inside the grid, navigation follows the calendar keyboard model: arrows move by day and week, <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> move to the first and last day of the week inside `minDate` / `maxDate` (the first and last week of the month with `selectionType="week"`), and <kbd>Page Down</kbd> / <kbd>Page Up</kbd> (with <kbd>Shift</kbd> for years) move between months and years. A date that cannot be picked takes the focus like any other, and <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Space</kbd> do nothing there. A key pressed there with <kbd>Alt</kbd>, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> is neither handled nor cancelled, so it stays free for the browser and assistive technology.

# Vue Date Picker Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Date Picker component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## CDatePicker

```jsx
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaCleanerLabel` | `string` | `'Clear date'` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that clears the value. |
| `ariaDayLabel` | `string` | `'Day'` | The `aria-label` of the day section. |
| `ariaHourLabel` | `string` | `'Hour'` | The `aria-label` of the hour section. |
| `ariaMeridiemLabel` | `string` | `'AM/PM'` | The `aria-label` of the meridiem section. |
| `ariaMinuteLabel` | `string` | `'Minute'` | The `aria-label` of the minute section. |
| `ariaMonthLabel` | `string` | `'Month'` | The `aria-label` of the month section. |
| `ariaNavNextMonthLabel` | `string` | `'Next month'` | A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the next month in the calendar. |
| `ariaNavNextYearLabel` | `string` | `'Next year'` | A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the next year in the calendar. |
| `ariaNavNextYearsLabel` | `string` | `'Next 12 years'` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that turns the years view to the next page of years. |
| `ariaNavPrevMonthLabel` | `string` | `'Previous month'` | A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the previous month in the calendar. |
| `ariaNavPrevYearLabel` | `string` | `'Previous year'` | A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the previous year in the calendar. |
| `ariaNavPrevYearsLabel` | `string` | `'Previous 12 years'` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that turns the years view to the previous page of years. |
| `ariaNothingToPickLabel` | `string` | `'Nothing on this page can be picked'` | Sets the description (`aria-describedby`) of a grid in which nothing can be picked, such as a page wholly outside `minDate` / `maxDate` or one that `disabledDates` covers, also announced when the calendar turns to such a page. An empty string leaves the grid without a description. |
| `ariaPickerLabel` | `string` | `'Toggle calendar'` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that opens the calendar, followed by the date the picker holds. |
| `ariaPopupLabel` | `string` | `'Calendar'` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the calendar panel, which opens as a `role="dialog"`. |
| `ariaQuarterLabel` | `string` | `'Quarter'` | The `aria-label` of the quarter section. |
| `ariaSecondLabel` | `string` | `'Second'` | The `aria-label` of the second section. |
| `ariaSelectedDateAnnouncement` | `string` | `'Selected date: {date}'` | Sets the message announced when a click or Enter / Space picks a date in a panel that stays open, with `timepicker` or without the toggle. A pick that closes the panel names the toggle with the date instead. `{date}` is replaced by the full name of what was picked, such as `Wednesday, August 12, 2026`. An empty string announces nothing. |
| `ariaSelectHoursLabel` | `string` | `'Select hours'` | Sets the accessible label of the hours select of the time half. |
| `ariaSelectMeridiemLabel` | `string` | `'Select AM/PM'` | Sets the accessible label of the AM/PM select of the time half. |
| `ariaSelectMinutesLabel` | `string` | `'Select minutes'` | Sets the accessible label of the minutes select of the time half. |
| `ariaSelectSecondsLabel` | `string` | `'Select seconds'` | Sets the accessible label of the seconds select of the time half. |
| `ariaWeekLabel` | `string` | `'Week'` | The `aria-label` of the week section. |
| `ariaWeekNumberLabel` | `(weekNumber: number) => string \| undefined` | - | Names each week number for screen readers: a function that takes the week number and returns its name. Without it the name is the locale's word for week and the number, such as `Week 36`. Keep the number in the name, so a voice-control user can say what they see. |
| `ariaYearLabel` | `string` | `'Year'` | The `aria-label` of the year section. |
| `calendarDate` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | The date the calendar opens on while nothing is selected. |
| `cleaner` | `boolean` | `true` | Renders the button that clears the value. |
| `container` | `HTMLElement \| (() => HTMLElement) \| string` | `'body'` | The element the calendar is rendered into instead of `document.body`. Implies `portal`. Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert. |
| `date` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | The date — a `Date` or a date string like `'2026-07-14'`. Passed one-way it seeds the field, which keeps managing itself; bound with `v-model:date` it follows your state. |
| `dayFormat` | `func\|string` | `'numeric'` | Set the format of day name. |
| `dayPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `DD` the day section shows while it is empty. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggles the disabled state. |
| `disabledDates` | `DisabledDate \| DisabledDate[]` | `undefined` | Specify the list of dates that cannot be selected. It can be a single `Date`, an `[start, end]` range, a matcher function, or an array of these. In week, month, quarter and year selection a period is disabled when every day of it is. |
| `feedback` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable feedback to your users with HTML5 form validation feedback. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable invalid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied `invalid` prop. |
| `feedbackValid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable valid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied `valid` prop. |
| `firstDayOfWeek` | `number` | `1` | Sets the day of start week. - 0 - Sunday, - 1 - Monday, - 2 - Tuesday, - 3 - Wednesday, - 4 - Thursday, - 5 - Friday, - 6 - Saturday, |
| `floatingLabel` | `string` | - | Renders a floating label inside the field — the component wraps its input in `.form-floating` and the text also becomes the field's accessible name. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `format` | `string \| ((locale: string) => DateSection[])` | `undefined` | The mask layout of the field. A string is parsed as dayjs/moment or date-fns/luxon format tokens, a function receives the locale and returns the section layout, and `undefined` derives the layout from the locale and the selection type. |
| `hourPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `HH` (`hh` on a 12-hour clock) the hour section shows while it is empty. |
| `hours` | `number[] \| ((hour: number) => boolean)` | `undefined` | Narrows the hours of the time half to a list, or to the ones a predicate accepts. Hours are 0 to 23 in every locale; on a 12-hour clock an hour that only one day period allows sets that period when picked. |
| `inputDateParse` | `(value: string) => Date \| null` | `undefined` | Custom function to parse text pasted into the field into a `Date` object, e.g. with an external date library. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control invalid. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `locale` | `string` | `'default'` | Sets the default locale for the component. If not set, it is inherited from the browser. |
| `maxDate` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | Max selectable date. The days after its day are disabled, and a time of day it carries leaves its own day selectable. In week selection its whole week stays selectable. |
| `meridiemPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `AM` the meridiem section shows while it is empty. |
| `minDate` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | Min selectable date. The days before its day are disabled, and a time of day it carries leaves its own day selectable. In week selection its whole week stays selectable. |
| `minutePlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `mm` the minute section shows while it is empty. |
| `minutes` | `boolean \| number[] \| ((minute: number) => boolean)` | `true` | Renders the minutes part of the time half, optionally narrowed the way `hours` is. |
| `monthFormat` | `string` | `'short'` | Sets the format for month names. |
| `monthNames` | `string[]` | `undefined` | Twelve custom month names for text month sections (`MMM`/`MMMM`), overriding the locale-derived, date-context grammatical form. |
| `monthPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `MM` the month section shows while it is empty. |
| `name` | `string` | - | Name of the value input the value is submitted under. Without it the field is not submitted with the form. |
| `pickerIcon` | `boolean` | `true` | The button that opens the panel. Set to `false` to render no button; replace the artwork through the `pickerIcon` slot. |
| `portal` | `boolean` | `true` | Renders the calendar through a portal: into the open `<dialog>` the field sits in, otherwise into `document.body`. |
| `quarterPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `Q` the quarter section shows while it is empty. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the readonly state for the component. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | When present, it specifies that the field must be filled out before submitting the form. |
| `secondPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `ss` the second section shows while it is empty. |
| `seconds` | `boolean \| number[] \| ((second: number) => boolean)` | `true` | Renders the seconds part of the time half and the field's second section, optionally narrowed the way `hours` is. |
| `selectAdjacentDays` | `boolean` | - | Set whether days in adjacent months shown before or after the current month are selectable. This only applies if the `showAdjacentDays` option is set to true. A picked day of an adjacent month keeps the month on screen and shows as selected with an outline on a subtle background instead of the solid fill. |
| `selectionType` | `string` | `'day'` | Specify the type of date selection as day, week, month, quarter, or year. |
| `show` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Control the open state via `v-model:show`. When set, the calendar renders what `show` says and dismiss gestures only emit `update:show` — nothing closes until the parent flips the prop. |
| `showAdjacentDays` | `boolean` | `true` | Set whether to display dates in adjacent months (non-selectable) at the start and end of the current month. |
| `showWeekNumber` | `boolean` | - | Set whether to display week numbers in the calendar. |
| `size` | `string` | `undefined` | Sizes the control, the way `.form-control-sm` and `.form-control-lg` size a form control. |
| `text` | `string` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `timepicker` | `boolean` | - | Add a time half to the panel: a row of hour, minute and second selects under the calendar, and a date and time mask in the field. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control valid. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` on every section of the field and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the date emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Controls the visibility of the calendar. |
| `weekdayFormat` | `func\|number\|string` | `2` | Set length or format of day name. |
| `weekNumbersLabel` | `string` | - | Label displayed over week numbers in the calendar. Without it the column is named for screen readers with the locale's word for week. |
| `weekPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `WW` the week section shows while it is empty. |
| `yearFormat` | `string` | `'numeric'` | Sets how the year cells of the years view write the year: `'numeric'` (2026) or `'2-digit'` (26). The navigation always writes the full year. |
| `yearPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `YYYY` the year section shows while it is empty. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `calendar-date-change` | Callback fired when the calendar date changed. |
| `date-change` | Callback fired once when the value changes, whether from the field, the calendar or the context methods; receives the `Date` the field holds (or `null` while the field is empty, incomplete or out of range) and the formatted value. |
| `error` | Callback fired when the validation state changes; receives `'incomplete'`, `'minDate'`, `'maxDate'`, `'disabledDate'`, or `null` when the value is valid or the field is empty. When one change moves both the value and the validation state, it fires after `date-change`, so a value set from it replaces the one just reported. |
| `hide` | Callback fired when the calendar is hidden. |
| `show` | Callback fired when the calendar is shown. |
| `update:date` | Emit the new date to support the `v-model:date` binding. |
| `update:show` | Emit the requested open state to support the `v-model:show` binding — a dismiss gesture (Escape, a click outside) or any internal toggle. |
| `update:validationState` | Event occurs with `undefined` when the user changes the date, or the form is reset, while `validationState` (or the deprecated `invalid`/`valid`) is set. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it and let the browser's own validation show again. |
| `view-change` | Callback fired when the calendar's view changes between days, months, quarters or years, and with the starting view each time the calendar opens. |

# Vue Date Picker Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Date Picker component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

### CSS variables

The field is a [`.form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/form-control-group/styling/#css-variables) on the picker element itself, so its frame, the cleaner and the toggle read the `--cui-control-*` and `--cui-control-group-*` tokens. `class` and `style` on `<CDatePicker>` land on that element; set the tokens there to restyle one field.

The picker declares its local CSS variables on its panel, `.date-picker-popup`, and the calendar inside it declares its own on `.calendar`. Values are set via Sass, so Sass customization is supported too.

```scss
$date-picker-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-gap: .25rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-date-picker-timepickers-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-timepickers-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-date-picker-footer-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-footer-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
  ),
  $date-picker-tokens
);
```

The time half declares its own on `.date-picker-time-body`, so it can be restyled without touching the panel around it.

```scss
$date-picker-time-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-date-picker-time-body-padding-y: var(--cui-spacer-3),
    --cui-date-picker-time-body-padding-x: var(--cui-spacer-3),

    --cui-date-picker-time-icon-size: 1rem,

    --cui-date-picker-time-select-padding-y: var(--cui-btn-input-sm-padding-y),

```

The panel is a `.popup`: its surface, border, shadow, stacking and fade come from the tokens every popup panel shares with the other pickers, the combobox, autocomplete and multi select.

#### How to use CSS variables

Each part of the panel declares its tokens itself, and the panel is rendered into `document.body` unless `portal` is `false`, so a variable set on `CDatePicker` through `style` styles the field but reaches none of them. Set them with a rule on the part that declares them:

```css
.date-picker-popup {
  --cui-popup-bg: #f8f9fa;
}

.date-picker-popup .calendar {
  --cui-calendar-cell-hover-bg: #e9ecef;
}
```
