# Vue Date Range Input Component

> Create a Vue start and end date field in one frame. Both ends use the section-based mask of the date input, and the range is validated as a whole.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Example

_Added in 6.0.0._

The Vue Date Range Input component is two [date input](../date-input/) fields and a separator in one frame, held together by the range it owns: both ends share the mask and the limits, and an end before the start marks the whole field invalid.

Pass `start-date` and `end-date` one-way and they seed the fields, which keep managing themselves from there; bind them with `v-model:start-date` / `v-model:end-date` and the fields follow your state; the `start-date-change` / `end-date-change` events alone only report what the fields do. A native reset of the form puts back the date each end started with, and a bound end only asks for it.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CDateRangeInput label="Stay" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDateRangeInput end-date="2026-07-20" label="Stay" locale="en-US" start-date="2026-07-14" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Date and time

Set `type="datetime"` and both ends carry the time. The hour cycle follows the locale, and `seconds` adds a seconds section to each field. The range compares its two ends by instant, so an end earlier in the day than the start on the same date marks the field invalid.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-7">
      <CDateRangeInput
        end-name="shift-end"
        label="Shift"
        locale="en-US"
        start-name="shift-start"
        type="datetime"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-6">
      <CFormField>
        <CFormLabel id="dateRangeInputStayLabel">Stay</CFormLabel>
        <CDateRangeInput
          aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputStayLabel"
          end-name="stayEnd"
          locale="en-US"
          start-name="stayStart"
        />
        <CFormText>Check-out has to be on or after check-in.</CFormText>
      </CFormField>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CFormLabel, CFormText } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Formats

Set an explicit mask for both ends with the `format` property. The parser is the [date input's](../date-input/#formats), so dayjs/moment tokens (`DD`, `MM`, `YYYY`) and date-fns/Unicode tokens (`dd`, `MM`, `yyyy`) both work, and any other character becomes a literal separator.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CDateRangeInput format="dd.MM.yyyy" label="dd.MM.yyyy" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDateRangeInput format="YYYY-MM-DD" label="YYYY-MM-DD" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

A mask that leaves out sections works here too — a month-and-year range reports the first day of each month:

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDateRangeInput format="MM.yyyy" label="Reporting period" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

For picking a whole range on a calendar, use the [date range picker](../date-range-picker/).

## Month names

Use the `MMM` or `MMMM` tokens for text month sections in both ends; typing letters matches a month by prefix. Pass all twelve names through the `month-names` property to override the locale-derived, date-context grammatical form.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CDateRangeInput format="DD MMMM YYYY" label="DD MMMM YYYY" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDateRangeInput
        format="DD MMMM YYYY"
        label="Standalone Polish month names"
        locale="pl-PL"
        :month-names="monthNames"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const monthNames = [
  'styczeń',
  'luty',
  'marzec',
  'kwiecień',
  'maj',
  'czerwiec',
  'lipiec',
  'sierpień',
  'wrzesień',
  'październik',
  'listopad',
  'grudzień',
]
</script>
```

## Locale

Without an explicit format, both masks follow the locale set via the `locale` property.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CDateRangeInput label="en-US" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDateRangeInput label="ja-JP" locale="ja-JP" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Min and max dates

`min-date` and `max-date` constrain both ends. A completed date outside the range gets the `.is-invalid` class on its own field and that end reports `null` until the value is corrected.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDateRangeInput
        format="dd.MM.yyyy"
        label="Dates in July 2026"
        locale="en-US"
        :max-date="maxDate"
        :min-date="minDate"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const minDate = new Date(2026, 6, 1)
const maxDate = new Date(2026, 6, 31)
</script>
```

## Disabled dates

Beyond a simple range, the `disabled-dates` property excludes specific dates from both ends — single `Date`s, `[start, end]` ranges, or a matcher function.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CDateRangeInput
        :disabled-dates="disabledDates"
        format="dd.MM.yyyy"
        label="Stay"
        locale="en-US"
        :max-date="maxDate"
        :min-date="minDate"
        :start-date="startDate"
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDateRangeInput
        :disabled-dates="disableWeekends"
        format="dd.MM.yyyy"
        label="Business days"
        locale="en-US"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const startDate = new Date(2026, 6, 10)
const minDate = new Date(2026, 6, 1)
const maxDate = new Date(2026, 6, 31)
const disabledDates = [[new Date(2026, 6, 4), new Date(2026, 6, 7)], new Date(2026, 6, 16)]
const disableWeekends = (date) => date.getDay() === 0 || date.getDay() === 6
</script>
```

## Custom formats

The built-in token parser covers dayjs, moment, date-fns, and luxon format strings, so you can reuse the format string from the date library you already work with — the library itself isn't required to render or edit the masks. Pair it with `input-date-parse` when you want that library to also parse text pasted into either end, here with `date-fns`:

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-6">
      <CDateRangeInput
        :end-date="endDate"
        format="MMMM DD, YYYY"
        :input-date-parse="inputDateParse"
        label="date-fns format"
        locale="en-US"
        :start-date="startDate"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { parse } from 'date-fns'
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const startDate = new Date(2026, 6, 14)
const endDate = new Date(2026, 6, 20)
const inputDateParse = (value) => parse(value, 'MMMM dd, yyyy', new Date())
</script>
```

## Validation

The frame shows the state of the range and each field shows its own, the way [`<CForm>`](../validation/) does for a native field. Each end keeps its value in a `<textarea>` laid invisibly over its field, which takes part in native constraint validation: a `required` end that is empty, incomplete or holds a rejected date blocks the submit, and the browser, or `<CForm>`, puts focus on its first empty section.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row g-4" novalidate validate>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDateRangeInput
        :end-date="endBeforeStart"
        end-name="check-out"
        feedback-invalid="Check-out has to be on or after check-in."
        format="dd.MM.yyyy"
        label="Out of order"
        locale="en-US"
        :start-date="start"
        start-name="check-in"
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDateRangeInput
        v-model:validation-state="stayState"
        :end-date="end"
        end-name="to"
        feedback="Those dates are already booked."
        format="dd.MM.yyyy"
        label="Stay"
        locale="en-US"
        :start-date="start"
        start-name="from"
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-12">
      <CButton color="primary" type="submit">Submit</CButton>
    </div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDateRangeInput, CForm } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const start = new Date(2026, 6, 20)
const end = new Date(2026, 6, 21)
const endBeforeStart = new Date(2026, 6, 14)
const stayState = ref('invalid')
</script>
```

The state comes from these places, in this order:

- The order: an end before the start is a state of the range, not of either date, and only dates the limits accept take part in it, so `.is-invalid` lands on the frame and both fields stay editable. Every section of both fields carries `aria-invalid="true"` until the order is fixed, and neither field is drawn valid meanwhile, whatever else is set.
- The limits: a completed date outside `min-date`/`max-date`/`disabled-dates` makes its own field invalid, which the frame picks up, and that field's value field submits no date until it is corrected. A date before year 1 counts as before `min-date` even without that prop; when the field loses the focus, its year becomes 1.
- `validation-state`: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`, a verdict on the whole range that lands on the frame and on both ends.
- A validation that reports a field (a submit, `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()`, which `<CForm>` and the [stepper](../stepper/) call as well), and in a form with the `validate` property of `<CForm>` the `:user-invalid` state of each value field, with `validate="valid"` also its `:user-valid` state, as for the [date input](../date-input/#validation).

A state you give is a verdict on the range it was given for. When the user changes either end, or the form is reset, the component emits `update:validationState` with `undefined` before it reports the change; bind the state with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it from both ends and the frame, as the second range above does. A change your code makes through `start-date` or `end-date` emits nothing. While the given state is `'invalid'`, both ends block the submit with the text of the message after the frame, or `Invalid value.` when there is none, unless the range is disabled or read-only. A native form reset returns both ends to the dates they started with; a `reset` listener that calls `preventDefault()` cancels the whole reset. An end bound with `v-model:start-date`/`v-model:end-date` only asks for the date it started with and keeps the value your page gives it until the page takes it; an end that only reports through its change event goes back to that date itself.

While an end is invalid, an `.invalid-feedback` or `.invalid-tooltip` you render after the range describes each of its sections.

### Blocking the submit

A `required` end that is empty, incomplete or rejected by the limits blocks the submit by itself. An end before the start does not, since both ends hold dates the browser accepts, and neither does an optional end that is empty, incomplete or rejected, which submits no date. Check the dates before you send them; the `start-date-change` and `end-date-change` events report `null` for an end that is empty, incomplete or rejected, so one condition covers both:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const start = ref<Date | null>(null)
const end = ref<Date | null>(null)

const onSubmit = (event: Event) => {
  if (!start.value || !end.value || end.value < start.value) {
    event.preventDefault()
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <CForm @submit="onSubmit">
    <CDateRangeInput @end-date-change="end = $event" @start-date-change="start = $event" />
    <CButton type="submit">Book</CButton>
  </CForm>
</template>
```

## Floating labels

Each end can carry its own [floating label](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/floating-labels/) through `start-floating-label` and `end-floating-label`; the text is also that end's accessible name.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-6">
      <CDateRangeInput
        end-floating-label="Check-out"
        locale="en-US"
        start-floating-label="Check-in"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

Set `floatingLabelAlways` to keep both labels [always floating](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the masks showing.

## Separator

The `separator` slot replaces the arrow between the two ends with a word, an icon of your own, or anything else you render. It is hidden from assistive technology either way. Left out, the default arrow renders and flips for right-to-left.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-6">
      <CDateRangeInput label="Stay" locale="en-US">
        <template #separator>
          <span class="fg-2">to</span>
        </template>
      </CDateRangeInput>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Sizing

The frame is a `.form-control-group`, so the standard sizing works — set the `size` property to `lg` or `sm` and both ends follow.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-6 mb-4">
      <CDateRangeInput label="Large" locale="en-US" size="lg" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-6">
      <CDateRangeInput label="Small" locale="en-US" size="sm" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>

</script>
```

## Disabled and readonly

Set the `disabled` property to disable both ends, or `read-only` to make them focusable but non-editable.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CDateRangeInput
        disabled
        :end-date="endDate"
        format="dd.MM.yyyy"
        label="Disabled"
        locale="en-US"
        :start-date="startDate"
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CDateRangeInput
        :end-date="endDate"
        format="dd.MM.yyyy"
        label="Readonly"
        locale="en-US"
        read-only
        :start-date="startDate"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const startDate = new Date(2026, 6, 14)
const endDate = new Date(2026, 6, 20)
</script>
```

## Accessibility

Each end is a [date input](../date-input/#accessibility) with the spinbutton pattern per section, so the range is two labelled groups rather than one opaque control:

- **Role attributes**: each end has `role="group"`, every section is a `role="spinbutton"` with its value attributes.
- **Names**: `label` names the pair, because the frame around both ends is a `role="group"` pointing at it; the start and end are named separately — `aria-start-label` and `aria-end-label` by default, or the floating label text when one is set. Each end is described by an `aria-describedby` you pass, then by `text` and the feedback that matches the state of the range.
- **Label click**: clicking the label that names the pair moves focus to the first empty section of the start date, as clicking the label of an input focuses it.
- **Separator**: hidden from assistive technology, whatever you render into it.
- **Roving tabindex**: each end is a single tab stop; <kbd>Tab</kbd> moves from the start to the end.

### Keyboard support

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>0</kbd>–<kbd>9</kbd> | Type into the focused section; the caret advances when the section is complete |
| <kbd>A</kbd>–<kbd>Z</kbd> | In text month sections, match a month name by prefix |
| <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> | Increment / decrement the focused section |
| <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> | Move focus to the next / previous section, crossing the separator from the last section of the start date into the end date and back; in a right-to-left layout the two keys swap |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | Move focus to the first / last section of the focused end |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd> | Clear the focused section; move to the previous section when already empty |
| <kbd>Delete</kbd> | Clear the focused section |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move from the start date to the end date |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> | Select the whole value of the focused end |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> | Paste a date into the focused end |

Apart from the shortcuts in the table, a key pressed with <kbd>Alt</kbd>, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> changes nothing in the field and is not cancelled: arrows, <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> move no focus and change no section, and a digit or letter is not entered. The key stays free for the browser, assistive technology and the picker around the field, where <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> opens the calendar. A character that <kbd>AltGr</kbd> or <kbd>Option</kbd> composes is still entered.

# Vue Date Range Input Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Date Range Input component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## CDateRangeInput

```jsx
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaDayLabel` | `string` | `'Day'` | The `aria-label` of the day section. |
| `ariaEndLabel` | `string` | `'End date'` | The accessible name of the end field, used when it has no floating label. |
| `ariaHourLabel` | `string` | `'Hour'` | The `aria-label` of the hour section. |
| `ariaMeridiemLabel` | `string` | `'AM/PM'` | The `aria-label` of the meridiem section. |
| `ariaMinuteLabel` | `string` | `'Minute'` | The `aria-label` of the minute section. |
| `ariaMonthLabel` | `string` | `'Month'` | The `aria-label` of the month section. |
| `ariaQuarterLabel` | `string` | `'Quarter'` | The `aria-label` of the quarter section. |
| `ariaSecondLabel` | `string` | `'Second'` | The `aria-label` of the second section. |
| `ariaStartLabel` | `string` | `'Start date'` | The accessible name of the start field, used when it has no floating label. |
| `ariaWeekLabel` | `string` | `'Week'` | The `aria-label` of the week section. |
| `ariaYearLabel` | `string` | `'Year'` | The `aria-label` of the year section. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | - | Focus the first section of the start date right after mounting. |
| `dayPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `DD` the day section shows while it is empty. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for both ends. |
| `disabledDates` | `DisabledDate \| DisabledDate[]` | `undefined` | Specify the list of dates that cannot be selected in either end. It can be a single `Date`, an `[start, end]` range, a matcher function, or an array of these. |
| `endDate` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | The end date — a `Date` or a date string. Passed one-way it seeds the field; bound with `v-model:end-date` it follows your state. |
| `endFloatingLabel` | `string` | - | The floating label of the end field. The text is also that field's accessible name. |
| `endName` | `string` | - | Name of the value input carrying the end date. Without it the end date is not submitted with the form. |
| `feedback` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable feedback to your users with HTML5 form validation feedback. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable invalid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied `validationState="invalid"`. |
| `feedbackValid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable valid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied `validationState="valid"`. |
| `floatingClassName` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the floating label wrapper. |
| `floatingLabel` | `string` | - | Wrap the whole range in a floating label. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `format` | `string \| ((locale: string) => DateSection[])` | `undefined` | The mask layout for both ends. A string is parsed as dayjs/moment or date-fns/luxon format tokens, a function receives the locale and returns the section layout, and `undefined` derives the layout from the locale. |
| `hourPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `HH` (`hh` on a 12-hour clock) the hour section shows while it is empty. |
| `id` | `string` | - | The id attribute of the frame. |
| `inputDateParse` | `(value: string) => Date \| null` | `undefined` | Custom function to parse text pasted into either end into a `Date` object, e.g. with an external date library. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `locale` | `string` | `'default'` | Sets the default locale for both ends. If not set, it is inherited from the browser. |
| `maxDate` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | Latest date either end can hold. |
| `meridiemPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `AM` the meridiem section shows while it is empty. |
| `minDate` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | Earliest date either end can hold. |
| `minutePlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `mm` the minute section shows while it is empty. |
| `monthNames` | `string[]` | `undefined` | Twelve custom month names for text month sections (`MMM`/`MMMM`), overriding the locale-derived, date-context grammatical form. |
| `monthPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `MM` the month section shows while it is empty. |
| `quarterPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `Q` the quarter section shows while it is empty. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | - | Make both ends focusable but non-editable. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | When present, it specifies that both ends must be filled out before submitting the form. |
| `secondPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `ss` the second section shows while it is empty. |
| `seconds` | `boolean` | - | Include a seconds section in the locale-derived layout of `type="datetime"`. Both ends follow. |
| `size` | `string` | `undefined` | Size the component small or large - both ends follow. |
| `startDate` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | The start date — a `Date` or a date string. Passed one-way it seeds the field; bound with `v-model:start-date` it follows your state. |
| `startFloatingLabel` | `string` | - | The floating label of the start field. The text is also that field's accessible name. |
| `startName` | `string` | - | Name of the value input carrying the start date. Without it the start date is not submitted with the form. |
| `text` | `string` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `type` | `string` | `'date'` | Which sections the locale-derived layout carries. A `format` names the sections itself and overrides this. Both ends follow. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class on the frame; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` on the sections of both ends and blocks the submit. An end before the start and an end the limits reject mark the frame invalid on their own. The user's next change of either end emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`. |
| `weekPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `WW` the week section shows while it is empty. |
| `yearPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `YYYY` the year section shows while it is empty. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `end-date-change` | Callback fired when the end date changes. |
| `start-date-change` | Callback fired when the start date changes. |
| `update:endDate` | Emit the new end date to support the `v-model:end-date` binding. |
| `update:startDate` | Emit the new start date to support the `v-model:start-date` binding. |
| `update:validationState` | Event occurs with `undefined` when the user changes either end, or the form is reset, while `validationState` is set. A given state is a verdict on the range it was given for; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it and let the browser's own validation show again. |

# Vue Date Range Input Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Date Range Input component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

### CSS variables

The two ends are date inputs, so they carry the `form-date-time` tokens, and the frame around them carries the [form control group](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/form-control-group/) ones. The range adds no tokens of its own.

```scss
// Redeclaring a --cui-control-* token here would shadow `.form-control`
// on the same element, and with it the validation states.
$form-date-time-tokens: () !default;
$form-date-time-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-date-time-placeholder-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-form-date-time-section-border-radius: .25rem,
    --cui-form-date-time-section-focus-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg-subtle),
  ),
  $form-date-time-tokens
);
```

# Vue Date Range Picker Component

> The Vue Date Range Picker Component is an essential tool for any Vue-based application that requires date range selection functionality.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Example

Explore basic usage of the Date Range Picker through sample code snippets that demonstrate its core functionality.

### Days

Select date ranges by day, from a basic picker to one with projected footer actions.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CDateRangePicker label="Date range" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6">
      <CDateRangePicker
        start-date="2022/08/03"
        end-date="2022/08/17"
        label="Date range"
        locale="en-US"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

#### With footer

The `footer` slot projects your own content below the calendars. Its slot props carry the picker's context — `setRange`, `clear`, `reset`, `close`, `isDateSelectable`, `startDate`, `endDate` and `disabled` — so a projected button acts on the picker and reads its state. While a footer is present the panel stays open after the second date, because the footer's actions are what closes it.

Any descendant can reach the same context with the `useDateRangePicker()` composable.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CDateRangePicker locale="en-US">
        <template #footer="{ clear, close }">
          <CButton class="me-auto" theme="primary" size="sm" variant="ghost" @click="clear">
            Clear
          </CButton>
          <CButton theme="primary" size="sm" @click="close">OK</CButton>
        </template>
      </CDateRangePicker>
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6">
      <CDateRangePicker end-date="2022/08/17" locale="en-US" start-date="2022/08/03">
        <template #footer="{ close, reset }">
          <CButton class="me-auto" theme="primary" size="sm" variant="ghost" @click="reset">
            Reset
          </CButton>
          <CButton theme="primary" size="sm" @click="close">OK</CButton>
        </template>
      </CDateRangePicker>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CButton, CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### With v-model

The `v-model:start-date` and `v-model:end-date` bindings keep the selected range in sync with your component's state.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row mb-4">
    <div class="col-lg-6">
      <CDateRangePicker
        v-model:start-date="vStartDate"
        v-model:end-date="vEndDate"
        label="Date range"
        locale="en-US"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
  <div>
    {{ vStartDate && vStartDate.toLocaleDateString([], options) }} -
    {{ vEndDate && vEndDate.toLocaleDateString([], options) }}
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
import { ref } from 'vue'
const vStartDate = ref(new Date(2022, 2, 1))
const vEndDate = ref(new Date(2022, 2, 7))
const options = {
  year: 'numeric',
  month: 'long',
  day: 'numeric',
  weekday: 'long',
}
</script>
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

A native reset of the form returns the picker to the range it started with and drops the state a submit set; an end bound with `v-model:start-date`/`v-model:end-date` asks for the date it started with through its update and change events and shows the date your page gives until the page takes it.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <span class="form-label">Reporting period</span>
    <CDateRangePicker end-name="periodEnd" locale="en-US" start-name="periodStart" />
    <CFormText>Both dates are included in the report.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CFormText } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Cleaner and picker button

The field ends with two buttons: one clears the range, the other opens the calendar. The `cleanerIcon` and `pickerIcon` slots swap their artwork for your own, `:cleaner="false"` leaves the cleaner out, and `:picker-icon="false"` leaves out the button that opens the calendar.

## Floating labels

Set `floatingLabels` and each field carries its own floating label, floating independently — the label text also becomes that field's accessible name. No wrapper markup is needed, and the mask placeholders stay hidden while the label rests inside the field.

```html
<template>
  <CDateRangePicker :floating-labels="['Check-in', 'Check-out']" locale="en-US" />
</template>
```

Set `floatingLabelAlways` to keep both labels [always floating](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the masks showing.

## Sizing

Set heights using `size` property like `size="lg"` and `size="sm"`.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row mb-5">
    <div class="col-lg-6">
      <CDateRangePicker locale="en-US" size="lg" />
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDateRangePicker locale="en-US" size="sm" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Disabled dates

CoreUI Vue Date Range Picker component includes a feature that allows you to disable certain dates, such as weekends or holidays. This can be accomplished by passing an array to the `disabledDates` prop to the component, which determines which dates should be disabled based on custom logic.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDateRangePicker
        :calendar-date="calendarDate"
        :disabled-dates="disabledDates"
        locale="en-US"
        :max-date="maxDate"
        :min-date="minDate"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const calendarDate = new Date(2022, 2, 1)
const disabledDates = [
  [new Date(2022, 2, 4), new Date(2022, 2, 7)],
  new Date(2022, 2, 16),
  new Date(2022, 3, 16),
  [new Date(2022, 4, 2), new Date(2022, 4, 8)],
]
const maxDate = new Date(2022, 5, 0)
const minDate = new Date(2022, 1, 1)
</script>
```

### Disabling weekends

You can disable weekends by passing a function to the `disabledDates` prop. Here's how to do it:

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDateRangePicker :disabled-dates="disableWeekends" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const disableWeekends = (date) => {
  const day = date.getDay()
  return day === 0 || day === 6 // Disable Sundays (0) and Saturdays (6)
}
</script>
```

## Validation

The picker shows its validation state on the frame and on the sections of both fields, which the message after the picker describes, the way [`<CForm>`](../validation/) does for a native field. Each field keeps its value in a `<textarea>` laid invisibly over it, so a `required` end that is empty, incomplete or holds a rejected date blocks the submit, as in the [date range input](../date-range-input/#validation). The picker also sets the state itself: a date the limits reject marks the range invalid, and so does an end before the start, for as long as it stands.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row g-4" novalidate validate>
    <div class="col-lg-7">
      <CDateRangePicker
        v-model:validation-state="stayState"
        end-date="2026-08-17"
        end-name="to"
        feedback="Those dates are already booked."
        locale="en-US"
        start-date="2026-08-10"
        start-name="from"
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-12">
      <CButton color="primary" type="submit">Submit</CButton>
    </div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDateRangePicker, CForm } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const stayState = ref('invalid')
</script>
```

`validation-state` gives a state of the range: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`, with `invalid` and `valid` as deprecated aliases that ask to be dropped the same way, though only a `validation-state` bound with `v-model:validation-state` is cleared by it. `feedback-invalid` or `feedback-valid` is the message shown while that state holds, describing both fields, and `tooltip-feedback` shows it as a tooltip instead. A given state is a verdict on the range it was given for. When the user changes the range, with a day picked in the calendar, the cleaner, a preset or a footer button that changes it through the context, or typing in a field, or the form is reset, the picker emits `update:validationState` with `undefined` before it reports the change; bind the state with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it, as the example does. An action that leaves the range as it is emits nothing, and neither does a change your code makes through `start-date` and `end-date`. While the given state is `'invalid'`, both ends block the submit with the text of the message after the picker, or `Invalid value.` when there is none.

### Blocking the submit

A `required` end that is empty, incomplete or rejected by the limits blocks the submit by itself. An end before the start does not, since both ends hold dates the browser accepts, and neither does an optional end that is empty, incomplete or rejected, which submits no date. Check the dates before you send them; the `start-date-change` and `end-date-change` events report `null` for an end that is empty, incomplete or rejected, so one condition covers both:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const start = ref<Date | null>(null)
const end = ref<Date | null>(null)

const onSubmit = (event: Event) => {
  if (!start.value || !end.value || end.value < start.value) {
    event.preventDefault()
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <CForm @submit="onSubmit">
    <CDateRangePicker @end-date-change="end = $event" @start-date-change="start = $event" />
    <CButton type="submit">Book</CButton>
  </CForm>
</template>
```

## Custom ranges

The `ranges` slot projects content beside the calendars — that is where range presets live. Its slot props carry the picker's context; a preset button calls `setRange` with its own two dates.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-5">
      <CDateRangePicker locale="en-US">
        <template #ranges="{ setRange }">
          <CButton
            v-for="[label, [start, end]] in presets"
            :key="label"
            theme="primary"
            size="sm"
            variant="ghost"
            @click="setRange(start, end)"
          >
            {{ label }}
          </CButton>
        </template>
      </CDateRangePicker>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CButton, CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const today = new Date()
const daysAgo = (days) => new Date(new Date().setDate(today.getDate() - days))

const presets = [
  ['Today', [today, today]],
  ['Yesterday', [daysAgo(1), daysAgo(1)]],
  ['Last 7 days', [daysAgo(6), today]],
  ['Last 30 days', [daysAgo(29), today]],
  ['This month', [new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), 1), today]],
  [
    'Last month',
    [
      new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth() - 1, 1),
      new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), 0),
    ],
  ],
]
</script>
```

## Locale

CoreUI Vue Date Range Picker allows users to display dates and times in a non-English locale. This is useful for applications that have international users or need to support multiple languages.

### Auto

By default, the DateRangePicker component uses the default browser locale, but it can be easily configured to use a different locale supported by the JavaScript Internationalization API. To set the locale, you can simply pass the desired language code as a prop to the DateRangePicker component. This feature enables to create more inclusive and accessible applications that cater to a diverse audience.

With server-side rendering, pass `locale` explicitly: by default the server writes the text in its own locale and the browser in the reader's, and Vue reports a hydration mismatch when the two differ.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDateRangePicker />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Custom formats

The `format` property is a mask: it spells out the sections both fields render. Tokens are `dd` for the day, `ww` for the ISO week, `MM` (`MMM`, `MMMM` for names) for the month, `QQQ` for the quarter, `yyyy` for the year, and text in single quotes is a literal, even when it contains token letters. Without it the fields follow the locale's own date format.

`inputDateParse` still applies to pasted text, turning a custom string into a `Date`.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-6">
      <CDateRangePicker
        end-date="2022/08/17"
        format="MMMM dd, yyyy"
        locale="en-US"
        start-date="2022/08/03"
        :input-date-parse="(date) => parse(date, 'MMMM dd, yyyy', new Date())"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
import { parse } from 'date-fns'
</script>
```

### Weeks

Setting `selectionType` to `'week'` narrows both fields to the locale's week presentation. Override it with a mask of your own: `yyyy-'W'ww` for the ISO form, or a localized label. The `showWeekNumber` property adds the week numbers to the calendars.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDateRangePicker
        end-date="2022W12"
        format="yyyy-'W'ww"
        label="Date range"
        locale="en-US"
        selection-type="week"
        show-week-number
        start-date="2022W10"
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CDateRangePicker
        end-date="2022W12"
        format="'Semana' ww, yyyy"
        label="Selector de rango de fechas"
        locale="es-ES"
        selection-type="week"
        show-week-number
        start-date="2022W10"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Open state

_Added in 6.0.0._

Bind `v-model:show` and the calendar renders what you pass — dismiss gestures only emit `update:show`, so the binding feeds the change back. Here a checkbox pins the calendar open, and a dismiss gesture unchecks it.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField class="mb-4">
    <CCheckbox id="dateRangePickerControlledShow" v-model="show" label="Keep the calendar open" />
  </CFormField>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-7">
      <CDateRangePicker v-model:show="show" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CCheckbox, CDateRangePicker, CFormField } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

Use it when the open state belongs to something else — a route, a tour step, or a control outside the picker like the checkbox above.

### Initial open state

Without a binding the picker manages its own calendar. Pass `show` to seed it open on mount.

```vue
<CDateRangePicker show />
```

The `update:show` event fires either way whenever the calendar requests an open-state change — a dismiss gesture (Escape, a click outside) or any internal toggle — so you can watch the state without taking it over. The deprecated `visible` prop keeps its old behavior and is ignored when `show` is set.

## Accessibility

Both fields are groups of spinbutton sections, so their own arrow keys belong to the value and the popup opens on the native control's dropdown keys instead. Each field is named by its floating label, or by `aria-start-label` and `aria-end-label` ("Start date" and "End date" by default), so a screen reader tells the two apart. They sit inside one `role="group"` named by `label`, and clicking that label moves focus to the first empty section of the start date. Each is described by an `aria-describedby` you pass to the picker, then by `text` and the feedback that matches its state.

The toggle button carries the panel's state — `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-controls` pointing at the popup while it is open, and `aria-expanded` — so a screen reader announces what the button does and whether the panel is showing. The panel itself is a `dialog` with `aria-modal`, so focus moves into it on open, stays there while it is open, and returns to the element that opened it, the toggle or the field, when it closes.

The toggle's name ends with the range the picker holds, written by the locale (`Toggle calendar, Thursday, August 20 – Sunday, August 23, 2026`), so a screen reader reads the picked range when the popup closes and focus goes back to the toggle. A live message would be lost at that moment, so the calendar does not announce the pick of the end that closes the popup. A pick that leaves the popup open, such as a new start that keeps the end or any pick with a `footer` slot, is announced through `ariaSelectedRangeAnnouncement`, and so is every pick without a toggle (`pickerIcon` set to `false`).

### Keyboard support

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd> (<kbd>Option</kbd> on macOS) + <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> / <kbd>F4</kbd> | Open the popup and move focus into it |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close the popup and return focus to the field or the toggle that opened it |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> / <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move within the open panel; the field is outside the dialog and stays out of the cycle |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Select the focused value |

Inside the grid, navigation follows the calendar keyboard model: arrows move by day and week, <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> move to the first and last day of the week inside `minDate` / `maxDate` (the first and last week of the month with `selectionType="week"`), and <kbd>Page Down</kbd> / <kbd>Page Up</kbd> (with <kbd>Shift</kbd> for years) move between months and years. A date that cannot be picked takes the focus like any other, and <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Space</kbd> do nothing there.

import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `ariaDayLabel` | `string` | `'Day'` | The `aria-label` of the day section. |
| `ariaEndLabel` | `string` | `'End date'` | The accessible name of the end field, used when it has no floating label. |
| `ariaHourLabel` | `string` | `'Hour'` | The `aria-label` of the hour section. |
| `ariaMeridiemLabel` | `string` | `'AM/PM'` | The `aria-label` of the meridiem section. |
| `ariaMinuteLabel` | `string` | `'Minute'` | The `aria-label` of the minute section. |
| `ariaMonthLabel` | `string` | `'Month'` | The `aria-label` of the month section. |
| `ariaNavNextMonthLabel` | `string` | `'Next month'` | A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the next month in the calendar. |
| `ariaNavNextYearLabel` | `string` | `'Next year'` | A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the next year in the calendar. |
| `ariaNavNextYearsLabel` | `string` | `'Next 12 years'` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that turns the years view to the next page of years. |
| `ariaNavPrevMonthLabel` | `string` | `'Previous month'` | A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the previous month in the calendar. |
| `ariaNavPrevYearLabel` | `string` | `'Previous year'` | A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the previous year in the calendar. |
| `ariaNavPrevYearsLabel` | `string` | `'Previous 12 years'` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that turns the years view to the previous page of years. |
| `ariaNothingToPickLabel` | `string` | `'Nothing on this page can be picked'` | Sets the description (`aria-describedby`) of a grid in which nothing can be picked, such as a page wholly outside `minDate` / `maxDate` or one that `disabledDates` covers, also announced when the calendar turns to such a page. An empty string leaves the grid without a description. |
| `ariaPickerLabel` | `string` | `'Toggle calendar'` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that opens the calendar, followed by the range the picker holds. |
| `ariaPopupLabel` | `string` | `'Calendar'` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the calendar panel, which opens as a `role="dialog"`. |
| `ariaQuarterLabel` | `string` | `'Quarter'` | The `aria-label` of the quarter section. |
| `ariaSecondLabel` | `string` | `'Second'` | The `aria-label` of the second section. |
| `ariaSelectedDateAnnouncement` | `string` | `'Selected date: {date}'` | Sets the message announced when a pick leaves both ends on the same day, unless the pick closes the panel, which names the toggle with the range instead. `{date}` is replaced by the full name of that day, week, month, quarter or year. An empty string announces nothing. |
| `ariaSelectedRangeAnnouncement` | `string` | `'Selected range: {start} to {end}'` | Sets the message announced when a pick leaves both ends set, unless the pick closes the panel, which names the toggle with the range instead. `{start}` and `{end}` are replaced by the full names of its ends. An empty string announces nothing. |
| `ariaStartLabel` | `string` | `'Start date'` | The accessible name of the start field, used when it has no floating label. |
| `ariaWeekLabel` | `string` | `'Week'` | The `aria-label` of the week section. |
| `ariaWeekNumberLabel` | `(weekNumber: number) => string \| undefined` | - | Names each week number for screen readers: a function that takes the week number and returns its name. Without it the name is the locale's word for week and the number, such as `Week 36`. Keep the number in the name, so a voice-control user can say what they see. |
| `ariaYearLabel` | `string` | `'Year'` | The `aria-label` of the year section. |
| `calendarDate` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | The date the calendar opens on while nothing is selected. |
| `calendars` | `number` | `2` | The number of calendars shown side by side. |
| `cleaner` | `boolean` | `true` | Renders the button that clears the value. |
| `container` | `HTMLElement \| (() => HTMLElement) \| string` | `'body'` | The element the calendar is rendered into instead of `document.body`. Implies `portal`. Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert. |
| `dayFormat` | `func\|string` | `'numeric'` | Set the format of day name. |
| `dayPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `DD` the day section shows while it is empty. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggles the disabled state. |
| `disabledDates` | `DisabledDate \| DisabledDate[]` | `undefined` | Specify the list of dates that cannot be selected. It can be a single `Date`, an `[start, end]` range, a matcher function, or an array of these. In week, month, quarter and year selection a period is disabled when every day of it is. |
| `endDate` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | The end of the range. Passed one-way it seeds the range, which keeps managing itself; bound with `v-model:end-date` it follows your state. |
| `endName` | `string` | - | Name of the end value input. Without it the end date is not submitted with the form. |
| `feedback` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable feedback to your users with HTML5 form validation feedback. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable invalid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied `invalid` prop. |
| `feedbackValid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable valid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied `valid` prop. |
| `firstDayOfWeek` | `number` | `1` | Sets the day of start week. - 0 - Sunday, - 1 - Monday, - 2 - Tuesday, - 3 - Wednesday, - 4 - Thursday, - 5 - Friday, - 6 - Saturday, |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `floatingLabels` | `string[]` | - | Renders a floating label over each field — `['Check-in', 'Check-out']` — which also becomes that field's accessible name. |
| `format` | `string \| ((locale: string) => DateSection[])` | `undefined` | The mask layout of the field. A string is parsed as dayjs/moment or date-fns/luxon format tokens, a function receives the locale and returns the section layout, and `undefined` derives the layout from the locale and the selection type. |
| `hourPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `HH` (`hh` on a 12-hour clock) the hour section shows while it is empty. |
| `inputDateParse` | `(value: string) => Date \| null` | `undefined` | Custom function to parse text pasted into the field into a `Date` object, e.g. with an external date library. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control invalid. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `locale` | `string` | `'default'` | Sets the default locale for the component. If not set, it is inherited from the browser. |
| `maxDate` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | Max selectable date. The days after its day are disabled, and a time of day it carries leaves its own day selectable. In week selection its whole week stays selectable. |
| `meridiemPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `AM` the meridiem section shows while it is empty. |
| `minDate` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | Min selectable date. The days before its day are disabled, and a time of day it carries leaves its own day selectable. In week selection its whole week stays selectable. |
| `minutePlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `mm` the minute section shows while it is empty. |
| `monthFormat` | `string` | `'short'` | Sets the format for month names. |
| `monthNames` | `string[]` | `undefined` | Twelve custom month names for text month sections (`MMM`/`MMMM`), overriding the locale-derived, date-context grammatical form. |
| `monthPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `MM` the month section shows while it is empty. |
| `pickerIcon` | `boolean` | `true` | The button that opens the panel. Set to `false` to render no button; replace the artwork through the `pickerIcon` slot. |
| `portal` | `boolean` | `true` | Renders the calendar through a portal: into the open `<dialog>` the field sits in, otherwise into `document.body`. |
| `quarterPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `Q` the quarter section shows while it is empty. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the readonly state for the component. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | When present, it specifies that the field must be filled out before submitting the form. |
| `secondPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `ss` the second section shows while it is empty. |
| `selectAdjacentDays` | `boolean` | - | Set whether days in adjacent months shown before or after the current month are selectable. This only applies if the `showAdjacentDays` option is set to true. A picked day of an adjacent month keeps the month on screen and shows as selected with an outline on a subtle background instead of the solid fill. |
| `selectionType` | `string` | `'day'` | Specify the type of date selection as day, week, month, quarter, or year. |
| `show` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Control the open state via `v-model:show`. When set, the calendar renders what `show` says and dismiss gestures only emit `update:show` — nothing closes until the parent flips the prop. |
| `showAdjacentDays` | `boolean` | `true` | Set whether to display dates in adjacent months (non-selectable) at the start and end of the current month. |
| `showWeekNumber` | `boolean` | - | Set whether to display week numbers in the calendar. |
| `size` | `string` | `undefined` | Sizes the control, the way `.form-control-sm` and `.form-control-lg` size a form control. |
| `startDate` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | The start of the range. Passed one-way it seeds the range, which keeps managing itself; bound with `v-model:start-date` it follows your state. |
| `startName` | `string` | - | Name of the start value input. Without it the start date is not submitted with the form. |
| `text` | `string` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control valid. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` on the sections of both fields and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the range emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Controls the visibility of the calendar. |
| `weekdayFormat` | `func\|number\|string` | `2` | Set length or format of day name. |
| `weekNumbersLabel` | `string` | - | Label displayed over week numbers in the calendar. Without it the column is named for screen readers with the locale's word for week. |
| `weekPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `WW` the week section shows while it is empty. |
| `yearFormat` | `string` | `'numeric'` | Sets how the year cells of the years view write the year: `'numeric'` (2026) or `'2-digit'` (26). The navigation always writes the full year. |
| `yearPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `YYYY` the year section shows while it is empty. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `calendar-date-change` | Callback fired when the calendar date changed. |
| `end-date-change` | Callback fired once when the end of the range changes, whether from its field, the calendar or the context methods; receives the `Date` the field holds (or `null` while it is empty, incomplete or out of range) and the formatted value. |
| `error` | Callback fired when the validation state changes; receives `'incomplete'`, `'minDate'`, `'maxDate'`, `'disabledDate'`, or `null` when the value is valid or the field is empty. When one change moves both the value and the validation state, it fires after `start-date-change` and `end-date-change`, so a value set from it replaces the one just reported. |
| `hide` | Callback fired when the calendar is hidden. |
| `show` | Callback fired when the calendar is shown. |
| `start-date-change` | Callback fired once when the start of the range changes, whether from its field, the calendar or the context methods; receives the `Date` the field holds (or `null` while it is empty, incomplete or out of range) and the formatted value. |
| `update:end-date` | Emit the new end of the range to support the `v-model:end-date` binding. |
| `update:show` | Emit the requested open state to support the `v-model:show` binding — a dismiss gesture (Escape, a click outside) or any internal toggle. |
| `update:start-date` | Emit the new start of the range to support the `v-model:start-date` binding. |
| `update:validationState` | Event occurs with `undefined` when the user changes either end, or the form is reset, while `validationState` (or the deprecated `invalid`/`valid`) is set. A given state is a verdict on the range it was given for; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it and let the browser's own validation show again. |
| `view-change` | Callback fired when the calendar's view changes between days, months, quarters or years, and with the starting view each time the calendar opens. |

# Vue Date Range Picker Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Date Range Picker component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

### CSS variables

The field is a [`.form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/form-control-group/styling/#css-variables) on the picker element itself, so its frame, the separator, the cleaner and the toggle read the `--cui-control-*` and `--cui-control-group-*` tokens. `class` and `style` on `<CDateRangePicker>` land on that element; set the tokens there to restyle one field. The two ends are [date inputs](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/date-input/styling/#css-variables) and carry the `form-date-time` tokens.

The range picker shares the date picker's panel, `.date-picker-popup`, and declares its local CSS variables there; the calendar inside it declares its own on `.calendar`. Values are set via Sass, so Sass customization is supported too.

```scss
$date-picker-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-gap: .25rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-date-picker-timepickers-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-timepickers-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-date-picker-footer-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-footer-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
  ),
  $date-picker-tokens
);
```

```scss
$calendar-tokens: defaults(

```

The panel is a `.popup`: its surface, border, shadow, stacking and fade come from the tokens every popup panel shares with the other pickers, the combobox, autocomplete and multi select.

```scss
$popup-tokens: () !default;
$popup-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-popup-zindex: var(--cui-z-dropdown),
    --cui-popup-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-popup-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-popup-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-popup-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-popup-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow),
    --cui-popup-transition-duration: .15s,
    --cui-popup-transition-timing: var(--cui-transition-timing-overlay),
  ),
  $popup-tokens
);
```

#### How to use CSS variables

Each part of the panel declares its tokens itself, and the panel is rendered into `document.body` unless `portal` is `false`, so a variable set on `CDateRangePicker` through `style` styles the field but reaches none of them. Set them with a rule on the part that declares them:

```css
.date-picker-popup {
  --cui-popup-bg: #f8f9fa;
}

.date-picker-popup .calendar {
  --cui-calendar-cell-hover-bg: #e9ecef;
}
```

# Vue Form Field

> A layout wrapper for a form control, its label, description and validation feedback, built on CSS grid.

`<CFormField>` renders the `.form-field` wrapper, which gives a control the layout and spacing it needs alongside its label, description and validation feedback — so a form is spaced by the field itself rather than by margin utilities sprinkled over its parts.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CFormLabel for="fieldText">Email address</CFormLabel>
    <CFormInput id="fieldText" type="email" placeholder="name@example.com" />
    <CFormText>We'll never share your email with anyone else.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CFormInput, CFormLabel, CFormText } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## How it works

- **Default layout** is a single-column grid: everything stacks vertically with one gap. Use it for text inputs, selects, textareas, ranges, input groups and any of the [PRO field components](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/form-control-group/).
- **Two-column layout** switches on through `:has()` when the input `<CCheckbox>`, `<CRadio>` or `<CSwitch>` renders (`.check`, `.radio`, `.switch`) is a direct child — the control pins to the first column, the label and description stack in the second. The deprecated `.form-check-input` triggers it too, so the markup the legacy `<CFormCheck>` and `<CFormSwitch>` render lays out the same way.
- **A field label** (`<CFormLabel>`, rendering `.form-label`) spans both columns and sits above the control row.
- **Grouped controls** — nest a `<CFormField>` per control inside an outer one to put several radios or checkboxes under a shared label with a shared description.

## Examples

### Select

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CFormLabel for="fieldSelect">Country</CFormLabel>
    <CFormSelect
      id="fieldSelect"
      :options="[
        { label: 'Choose one…' },
        { label: 'United States', value: '1' },
        { label: 'Canada', value: '2' },
        { label: 'United Kingdom', value: '3' },
      ]"
    />
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CFormLabel, CFormSelect } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

### Textarea

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CFormLabel for="fieldTextarea">Message</CFormLabel>
    <CFormTextarea id="fieldTextarea" :rows="3" />
    <CFormText>Be sure to include the relevant details.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CFormLabel, CFormText, CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

### Checkbox

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CCheckbox id="fieldCheck" label="Subscribe to the newsletter" />
    <CFormText>We send one email a month, and never share your address.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CCheckbox, CFormField, CFormText } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

### Grouped

Nest one `<CFormField>` per control inside an outer one, and give the group its own `.form-label`.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <span class="form-label">Delivery</span>
    <CFormField>
      <CRadio id="fieldRadio1" name="fieldRadio" label="Standard" checked />
      <CFormText>Three to five working days.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
    <CFormField>
      <CRadio id="fieldRadio2" name="fieldRadio" label="Express" />
      <CFormText>Next working day, where available.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CFormText, CRadio } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

### Switch

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CSwitch id="fieldSwitch" label="Email notifications" />
    <CFormText>Turn this off and we will only contact you about your account.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CFormText, CSwitch } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Overhead label

When a check, radio, or switch needs a field title above it, add a `.form-label`. It sits on its own row above the control, while the control's own label and description keep their places:

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <span class="form-label">Terms and conditions</span>
    <CCheckbox id="fieldOverheadCheck" label="I agree to the terms" />
    <CFormText>Please read them before agreeing.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CCheckbox, CFormField, CFormText } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Validation

Feedback elements are children of the field like any other, so they inherit its gap and land under the control. Set `validation-state` on the form component and pass the message through `feedback-valid` / `feedback-invalid`.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CFormLabel for="fieldValidation">Username</CFormLabel>
    <CFormInput
      id="fieldValidation"
      type="text"
      model-value="jan kowalski"
      validation-state="invalid"
      feedback-invalid="A username cannot contain spaces."
    />
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CFormInput, CFormLabel } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

See [validation](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/validation/) for the full picture, including the server-side and browser-native flavours.

# Vue Form Field Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Form Field component with CSS variables and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

Vue Form Field uses local CSS variables for enhanced real-time customization. Set them on the field itself, or on an ancestor for a whole form.

```scss
$form-field-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-field-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-form-field-column-gap: .5rem,
  ),
  $form-field-tokens
);
```

`.form-field-card` and `.form-group` carry their own sets:

```scss
$form-field-card-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-field-card-padding-y: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * .75),
    --cui-form-field-card-padding-x: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * .75),
    --cui-form-field-card-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-form-field-card-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-form-field-card-checked-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-form-field-card-checked-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
  ),
  $form-field-card-tokens
);
```

```scss
$form-group-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-group-gap: .5rem,
  ),
  $form-group-tokens
);
```

#### How to use CSS variables

```vue
<CFormField :style="{ '--cui-form-field-gap': '0.75rem' }">...</CFormField>
```

# Vue Floating labels

> Vue floating label component. Create beautifully simple form labels that float over your input fields.

## Example
Use `floatingLabel` property on `<CFormInput>`, `<CFormSelect>` or `<CFormTextarea>` to enable floating labels with textual form fields. A `placeholder` is required on each `<CFormInput>`, `<CFormSelect>` and `<CFormTextarea>` as our method of CSS-only floating labels uses the `:placeholder-shown` pseudo-element. The placeholder stays hidden while the label rests in the field, and shows under the floated label once the field has focus.

```html
<template>
  <CFormInput
    id="floatingInput"
    class="mb-4"
    type="email"
    floating-label="Email address"
    placeholder="name@example.com"
  />
  <CFormInput
    id="floatingPassword"
    type="password"
    floating-label="Password"
    placeholder="••••••••"
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

You can create the same form control by wrapping a pair of `<CFormInput>` and `<CFormLabel>` elements in `<CFormFloating>` to enable floating labels with textual form fields. A `placeholder` is required on each `<CFormInput>` as our method of CSS-only floating labels uses the `:placeholder-shown` pseudo-element. Write the `<CFormLabel>` first, so a screen reader announces it before the field's value. The control-first order keeps working.

```vue
<CFormFloating class="mb-4">
  <CFormLabel for="floatingInput">Email address</CFormLabel>
  <CFormInput type="email" id="floatingInput" placeholder="name@example.com" />
</CFormFloating>
<CFormFloating>
  <CFormLabel for="floatingPassword">Password</CFormLabel>
  <CFormInput type="password" id="floatingPassword" placeholder="••••••••" />
</CFormFloating>
```

When there's a `value` already defined, `<CFormLabel>`s will automatically adjust to their floated position.

```html
<template>
  <CFormFloating>
    <CFormInput
      id="floatingInputValue"
      type="email"
      floating-label="Input with value"
      placeholder="name@example.com"
      value="test@example.com"
    />
  </CFormFloating>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormFloating, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

Form validation styles also work as expected.

```html
<template>
  <CFormInput
    id="floatingInputInvalid"
    class="mb-4"
    type="email"
    floating-label="Email addresss"
    placeholder="name@example.com"
    validation-state="valid"
    value="test@example.com"
  />
  <CFormInput
    id="floatingInputInvalid"
    type="email"
    validation-state="invalid"
    floating-label="Email addresss"
    placeholder="name@example.com"
    value="test@example.com"
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Textareas

By default, `<CFormTextarea>`s will be the same height as `<CFormInput>`s.

```html
<template>
  <CFormFloating>
    <CFormTextarea
      id="floatingTextarea"
      floating-label="Comments"
      placeholder="Leave a comment here"
    ></CFormTextarea>
  </CFormFloating>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormFloating, CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

To set a custom height on your `<CFormTextarea>`, do not use the `rows` attribute. Instead, set an explicit `height` (either inline or via custom CSS).

```html
<template>
  <CFormFloating>
    <CFormTextarea
      id="floatingTextarea2"
      placeholder="Leave a comment here"
      floating-label="Comments"
      style="height: 100px"
    ></CFormTextarea>
  </CFormFloating>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormFloating, CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Selects

Other than `<CFormInput>`, floating labels are only available on `<CFormSelect>`s. They work in the same way, but unlike `<CFormInput>`s, they'll always show the `<CFormLabel>` in its floated state. **Selects with `size` and `multiple` are not supported.**

```html
<template>
  <CFormFloating>
    <CFormSelect
      id="floatingSelect"
      floating-label="Works with selects"
      aria-label="Floating label select example"
    >
      <option>Open this select menu</option>
      <option value="1">One</option>
      <option value="2">Two</option>
      <option value="3">Three</option>
    </CFormSelect>
  </CFormFloating>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormFloating, CFormSelect } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Date and time

Date, time, datetime-local, month, and week inputs also always show the label in its floated state. These controls do not support placeholders the way textual inputs do, so a `placeholder` is not required (and is ignored by most browsers on these types). For a field that formats its value by locale, use the [Date Picker](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/date-picker/#floating-labels) or the [Time Picker](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/time-picker/#floating-labels) with the `floatingLabel` property.

```html
<template>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <CFormInput id="floatingDate" type="date" floating-label="Date" />
  </div>
  <CFormInput id="floatingTime" type="time" floating-label="Time" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Always floating

Set `floatingLabelAlways` on the form control, or `always` on `<CFormFloating>`, to keep the label floated and show the placeholder.

```html
<template>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <CFormInput
      id="alwaysFloatingInput"
      type="email"
      floating-label="Email address"
      floating-label-always
      placeholder="name@example.com"
    />
  </div>
  <CFormFloating always>
    <CFormLabel for="alwaysFloatingPassword">Password</CFormLabel>
    <CFormInput id="alwaysFloatingPassword" type="password" placeholder="••••••••" />
  </CFormFloating>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormFloating, CFormInput, CFormLabel } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

The date and time pickers take `floatingLabelAlways` as well.

```html
<template>
  <CDatePicker floating-label="Delivery date" floating-label-always locale="en-US" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

By default, placeholders stay transparent until the control is focused. With `floatingLabelAlways`, the placeholder stays visible in both states, so keep it short on a textarea, where the floated label covers its first line.

## Layout

When working with the CoreUI for Vue grid system, be sure to place form elements within column classes.

```html
<template>
  <CRow :xs="{ gutter: 3 }">
    <CCol md>
      <CFormFloating>
        <CFormInput
          id="floatingInputGrid"
          type="email"
          floating-label="Email address"
          placeholder="name@example.com"
          value="email@example.com"
        />
      </CFormFloating>
    </CCol>
    <CCol md>
      <CFormFloating>
        <CFormSelect
          id="floatingSelectGrid"
          floating-label="Works with selects"
          aria-label="Floating label select example"
        >
          <option>Open this select menu</option>
          <option value="1">One</option>
          <option value="2">Two</option>
          <option value="3">Three</option>
        </CFormSelect>
      </CFormFloating>
    </CCol>
  </CRow>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CRow, CCol, CFormFloating, CFormInput, CFormSelect } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

- [&lt;CFormFloating /&gt;](./api/#cformfloating)

# Vue Form Floating Labels Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Form Floating Labels component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CFormFloating

```jsx
import { CFormFloating } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `always` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
