# Vue Bootstrap Floating labels Component

> Learn how to use CoreUI’s Vue Floating labels component with Bootstrap styles for flexible, framework-consistent UI.

## Example
Use `floatingLabel` property on `<CFormInput>`, `<CFormSelect>` or `<CFormTextarea>` to enable floating labels with textual form fields. A `placeholder` is required on each `<CFormInput>`, `<CFormSelect>` and `<CFormTextarea>` as our method of CSS-only floating labels uses the `:placeholder-shown` pseudo-element. The placeholder stays hidden while the label rests in the field, and shows under the floated label once the field has focus.

```html
<template>
  <CFormInput
    id="floatingInput"
    class="mb-4"
    type="email"
    floating-label="Email address"
    placeholder="name@example.com"
  />
  <CFormInput
    id="floatingPassword"
    type="password"
    floating-label="Password"
    placeholder="••••••••"
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

You can create the same form control by wrapping a pair of `<CFormInput>` and `<CFormLabel>` elements in `<CFormFloating>` to enable floating labels with textual form fields. A `placeholder` is required on each `<CFormInput>` as our method of CSS-only floating labels uses the `:placeholder-shown` pseudo-element. Write the `<CFormLabel>` first, so a screen reader announces it before the field's value. The control-first order keeps working.

```vue
<CFormFloating class="mb-4">
  <CFormLabel for="floatingInput">Email address</CFormLabel>
  <CFormInput type="email" id="floatingInput" placeholder="name@example.com" />
</CFormFloating>
<CFormFloating>
  <CFormLabel for="floatingPassword">Password</CFormLabel>
  <CFormInput type="password" id="floatingPassword" placeholder="••••••••" />
</CFormFloating>
```

When there's a `value` already defined, `<CFormLabel>`s will automatically adjust to their floated position.

```html
<template>
  <CFormFloating>
    <CFormInput
      id="floatingInputValue"
      type="email"
      floating-label="Input with value"
      placeholder="name@example.com"
      value="test@example.com"
    />
  </CFormFloating>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormFloating, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

Form validation styles also work as expected.

```html
<template>
  <CFormInput
    id="floatingInputInvalid"
    class="mb-4"
    type="email"
    floating-label="Email addresss"
    placeholder="name@example.com"
    validation-state="valid"
    value="test@example.com"
  />
  <CFormInput
    id="floatingInputInvalid"
    type="email"
    validation-state="invalid"
    floating-label="Email addresss"
    placeholder="name@example.com"
    value="test@example.com"
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Textareas

By default, `<CFormTextarea>`s will be the same height as `<CFormInput>`s.

```html
<template>
  <CFormFloating>
    <CFormTextarea
      id="floatingTextarea"
      floating-label="Comments"
      placeholder="Leave a comment here"
    ></CFormTextarea>
  </CFormFloating>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormFloating, CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

To set a custom height on your `<CFormTextarea>`, do not use the `rows` attribute. Instead, set an explicit `height` (either inline or via custom CSS).

```html
<template>
  <CFormFloating>
    <CFormTextarea
      id="floatingTextarea2"
      placeholder="Leave a comment here"
      floating-label="Comments"
      style="height: 100px"
    ></CFormTextarea>
  </CFormFloating>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormFloating, CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Selects

Other than `<CFormInput>`, floating labels are only available on `<CFormSelect>`s. They work in the same way, but unlike `<CFormInput>`s, they'll always show the `<CFormLabel>` in its floated state. **Selects with `size` and `multiple` are not supported.**

```html
<template>
  <CFormFloating>
    <CFormSelect
      id="floatingSelect"
      floating-label="Works with selects"
      aria-label="Floating label select example"
    >
      <option>Open this select menu</option>
      <option value="1">One</option>
      <option value="2">Two</option>
      <option value="3">Three</option>
    </CFormSelect>
  </CFormFloating>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormFloating, CFormSelect } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Date and time

Date, time, datetime-local, month, and week inputs also always show the label in its floated state. These controls do not support placeholders the way textual inputs do, so a `placeholder` is not required (and is ignored by most browsers on these types). For a field that formats its value by locale, use the [Date Picker](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/date-picker/#floating-labels) or the [Time Picker](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/time-picker/#floating-labels) with the `floatingLabel` property.

```html
<template>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <CFormInput id="floatingDate" type="date" floating-label="Date" />
  </div>
  <CFormInput id="floatingTime" type="time" floating-label="Time" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Always floating

Set `floatingLabelAlways` on the form control, or `always` on `<CFormFloating>`, to keep the label floated and show the placeholder.

```html
<template>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <CFormInput
      id="alwaysFloatingInput"
      type="email"
      floating-label="Email address"
      floating-label-always
      placeholder="name@example.com"
    />
  </div>
  <CFormFloating always>
    <CFormLabel for="alwaysFloatingPassword">Password</CFormLabel>
    <CFormInput id="alwaysFloatingPassword" type="password" placeholder="••••••••" />
  </CFormFloating>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormFloating, CFormInput, CFormLabel } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

The date and time pickers take `floatingLabelAlways` as well.

```html
<template>
  <CDatePicker floating-label="Delivery date" floating-label-always locale="en-US" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

By default, placeholders stay transparent until the control is focused. With `floatingLabelAlways`, the placeholder stays visible in both states, so keep it short on a textarea, where the floated label covers its first line.

## Layout

When working with the CoreUI for Vue grid system, be sure to place form elements within column classes.

```html
<template>
  <CRow :xs="{ gutter: 3 }">
    <CCol md>
      <CFormFloating>
        <CFormInput
          id="floatingInputGrid"
          type="email"
          floating-label="Email address"
          placeholder="name@example.com"
          value="email@example.com"
        />
      </CFormFloating>
    </CCol>
    <CCol md>
      <CFormFloating>
        <CFormSelect
          id="floatingSelectGrid"
          floating-label="Works with selects"
          aria-label="Floating label select example"
        >
          <option>Open this select menu</option>
          <option value="1">One</option>
          <option value="2">Two</option>
          <option value="3">Three</option>
        </CFormSelect>
      </CFormFloating>
    </CCol>
  </CRow>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CRow, CCol, CFormFloating, CFormInput, CFormSelect } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

# Vue Form Control Group

> Assemble an input, icons and action buttons into one control that looks and behaves like a single form field — the frame every CoreUI field component is built on.

## Example

_Added in 6.0.0._

A control is often more than an input: it carries an icon, a clear button, a
toggle. `.form-control-group` draws **one** frame around all of it, so the
result reads as a single field rather than a row of parts. The PRO field
components — [autocomplete](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/autocomplete/), [chip input](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/chip-input/),
[date picker](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/date-picker/), [date range picker](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/date-range-picker/),
[multi select](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/multi-select/), [password input](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/password-input/) and
[time picker](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/time-picker/) —
emit this markup internally, which is why they all size, focus and validate the
same way. Reach for the classes directly when you are assembling a field of
your own.

```html
<template>
  <CFormControlGroup>
    <CFormControlIcon>
      <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 512 512" fill="currentColor">
        <path
          d="M479.6 399.716l-81.084-81.084-62.368-25.767A175.014 175.014 0 0 0 368 192c0-97.047-78.953-176-176-176S16 94.953 16 192s78.953 176 176 176a175.034 175.034 0 0 0 101.619-32.377l25.7 62.2L400.4 479.6a56 56 0 1 0 79.2-79.884ZM48 192c0-79.4 64.6-144 144-144s144 64.6 144 144-64.6 144-144 144S48 271.4 48 192Zm408.971 264.284a24.028 24.028 0 0 1-33.942 0l-76.572-76.572-23.894-57.835 57.835 23.894 76.573 76.572a24.028 24.028 0 0 1 0 33.941Z"
        />
      </svg>
    </CFormControlIcon>
    <CFormInput type="search" placeholder="Search…" aria-label="Search" />
  </CFormControlGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormControlGroup, CFormControlIcon, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## How it works

- **The group is the frame.** `.form-control-group` looks exactly like
  `.form-control` — same padding, typography, colours, border and transition,
  from the same `--cui-control-*` custom properties — and lays its
  children out in a row. Theme `.form-control` and the group follows.
- **The control inside keeps its own class.** Put `<CFormInput>` in the group:
  inside it the `.form-control` gives up its border, padding and background, so
  only the group's frame is drawn. There is no separate "ghost" class to remember.
- **Focus is answered by the group.** A `<div>` never fires `:focus`, so the
  frame lights up on `:focus-within`.

## Parts

| Component | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `<CFormControlGroup>` | The frame. Size every part at once with `size="sm"` or `size="lg"`. |
| `<CFormInput>` | The editable inside it. |
| `<CFormControlIcon>` | Decoration — an icon and nothing more. It ignores pointer events, and can sit in the group on its own or inside an action. |
| `<CFormControlText>` | Static text in the frame — a prefix or suffix like `https://`, `@` or `.00`. Inert and unselectable, so a click lands in the input and a drag over the field does not pick it up. |
| `<CFormControlAction>` | An interactive adornment: a real `<button>`. Give it an `aria-label`; it may hold a `<CFormControlIcon>`. |
| `<CFormControlCleaner>` | The action that clears the value — a real `<button>` with the clearing glyph built in (`ariaLabel` defaults to "Clear"). The field components render theirs automatically; in a custom group showing and hiding it is your job, since only you know whether the control holds a value. |

Icons take their size from the group, so they follow `size="sm"` and
`size="lg"` without being told. An icon inside an action follows the
button's colour, which is how a validation state reaches it.

```html
<template>
  <CFormControlGroup>
    <CFormInput type="text" value="Ada Lovelace" aria-label="Name" />
    <CFormControlAction aria-label="Clear">
      <CFormControlIcon>
        <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="currentColor">
          <path
            d="M.293.293a1 1 0 011.414 0L8 6.586 14.293.293a1 1 0 111.414 1.414L9.414 8l6.293 6.293a1 1 0 01-1.414 1.414L8 9.414l-6.293 6.293a1 1 0 01-1.414-1.414L6.586 8 .293 1.707a1 1 0 010-1.414z"
          />
        </svg>
      </CFormControlIcon>
    </CFormControlAction>
  </CFormControlGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CFormControlAction,
  CFormControlGroup,
  CFormControlIcon,
  CFormInput,
} from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Clearing the value

`<CFormControlCleaner>` is the clearing action with the glyph built in. Render it only while the control holds a value:

```html
<template>
  <CFormControlGroup>
    <CFormInput v-model="value" type="text" aria-label="Name" />
    <CFormControlCleaner v-if="value.length > 0" @click="value = ''" />
  </CFormControlGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CFormControlCleaner, CFormControlGroup, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const value = ref('Ada Lovelace')
</script>
```

## Static text

_Added in 6.0.0._

Use `.form-control-text` for a fixed prefix or suffix that labels the value
rather than changing it — a scheme, a unit, a currency. It is inert: pointer
events pass through to the input, and the text cannot be selected, so
double-clicking to select the value never catches the adornment instead.

Which side it lands on is decided by where you put it, because the group is a
flex row and follows DOM order. Write it before the input for a prefix, after
for a suffix — there is no separate class for the end.

```html
<template>
  <CFormControlGroup class="mb-4">
    <CFormControlText>https://</CFormControlText>
    <CFormInput type="text" placeholder="example.com" aria-label="Website address" />
  </CFormControlGroup>
  <CFormControlGroup class="mb-4">
    <CFormControlText>@</CFormControlText>
    <CFormInput type="text" placeholder="username" aria-label="Username" />
  </CFormControlGroup>
  <CFormControlGroup>
    <CFormControlText>$</CFormControlText>
    <CFormInput type="text" placeholder="0" aria-label="Amount" />
    <CFormControlText>.00</CFormControlText>
  </CFormControlGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormControlGroup, CFormControlText, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

It combines with the other parts, and dims with the group when the field is
disabled:

```html
<template>
  <CFormControlGroup>
    <CFormControlIcon>
      <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="currentColor">
        <path d="M8 0a8 8 0 100 16A8 8 0 008 0zM1.5 8a6.5 6.5 0 1113 0 6.5 6.5 0 01-13 0z" />
      </svg>
    </CFormControlIcon>
    <CFormControlText>USD</CFormControlText>
    <CFormInput type="text" value="1250" disabled aria-label="Amount" />
  </CFormControlGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormControlGroup, CFormControlIcon, CFormControlText, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Sizing

Add `.form-control-sm` or `.form-control-lg` to the group — the standard
control sizing classes, no per-component variants.

```html
<template>
  <CFormControlGroup size="sm" class="mb-4">
    <CFormInput type="text" placeholder="Small" aria-label="Small" />
  </CFormControlGroup>
  <CFormControlGroup class="mb-4">
    <CFormInput type="text" placeholder="Default" aria-label="Default" />
  </CFormControlGroup>
  <CFormControlGroup size="lg">
    <CFormInput type="text" placeholder="Large" aria-label="Large" />
  </CFormControlGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormControlGroup, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Validation

Put `.is-invalid` or `.is-valid` on the group. The state also reaches the frame
from the control inside it, so a component that validates its own field lights
the frame up without any extra wiring. The validation icon is suppressed inside
a group — an action usually occupies that corner — and the actions carry the
state colour instead.

```html
<template>
  <CFormControlGroup class="is-invalid">
    <CFormInput type="text" value="Not quite" aria-label="Invalid example" />
    <CFormControlAction aria-label="Clear">
      <CFormControlIcon>
        <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="currentColor">
          <path
            d="M.293.293a1 1 0 011.414 0L8 6.586 14.293.293a1 1 0 111.414 1.414L9.414 8l6.293 6.293a1 1 0 01-1.414 1.414L8 9.414l-6.293 6.293a1 1 0 01-1.414-1.414L6.586 8 .293 1.707a1 1 0 010-1.414z"
          />
        </svg>
      </CFormControlIcon>
    </CFormControlAction>
  </CFormControlGroup>
  <div class="invalid-feedback d-block">Please pick a different value.</div>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CFormControlAction,
  CFormControlGroup,
  CFormControlIcon,
  CFormInput,
} from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Disabled

Disable the control inside the group and the frame follows; use `.disabled` on
the group when there is no single control to disable.

```html
<template>
  <CFormControlGroup>
    <CFormInput type="text" value="Read only" aria-label="Disabled example" disabled />
    <CFormControlAction aria-label="Clear" disabled>
      <CFormControlIcon>
        <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="currentColor">
          <path
            d="M.293.293a1 1 0 011.414 0L8 6.586 14.293.293a1 1 0 111.414 1.414L9.414 8l6.293 6.293a1 1 0 01-1.414 1.414L8 9.414l-6.293 6.293a1 1 0 01-1.414-1.414L6.586 8 .293 1.707a1 1 0 010-1.414z"
          />
        </svg>
      </CFormControlIcon>
    </CFormControlAction>
  </CFormControlGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CFormControlAction,
  CFormControlGroup,
  CFormControlIcon,
  CFormInput,
} from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

> **Not to be confused with [input group](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/input-group/).** An input group
> joins *separate* controls and add-ons side by side — each keeps its own frame,
> and the seams between them are visible. A form control group is *one* control
> assembled from parts inside a single frame.

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CFormLabel for="formControlGroupField">Search</CFormLabel>
    <CFormControlGroup>
      <CFormControlIcon>
        <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 512 512" fill="currentColor">
          <path
            d="M479.6 399.716l-81.084-81.084-62.368-25.767A175.014 175.014 0 0 0 368 192c0-97.047-78.953-176-176-176S16 94.953 16 192s78.953 176 176 176a175.034 175.034 0 0 0 101.619-32.377l25.7 62.2L400.4 479.6a56 56 0 1 0 79.2-79.884ZM48 192c0-79.4 64.6-144 144-144s144 64.6 144 144-64.6 144-144 144S48 271.4 48 192Zm408.971 264.284a24.028 24.028 0 0 1-33.942 0l-76.572-76.572-23.894-57.835 57.835 23.894 76.573 76.572a24.028 24.028 0 0 1 0 33.941Z"
          />
        </svg>
      </CFormControlIcon>
      <CFormInput id="formControlGroupField" type="search" placeholder="Search…" />
    </CFormControlGroup>
    <CFormText>Searches titles and body text.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CFormInput, CFormLabel, CFormText } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CFormControlGroup, CFormControlIcon } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

# Vue Form Control Group Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Form Control Group with CSS variables and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

The frame runs on the shared `--cui-control-*` custom properties, so it
is themed together with `.form-control`. The parts the group owns have their
own:

```scss
$form-control-group-tokens: () !default;
$form-control-group-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-control-group-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-control-group-icon-size: 1rem,
    --cui-control-group-icon-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-text-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-action-size: 1.5rem,
    --cui-control-group-action-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-action-hover-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-control-group-action-bg: transparent,
    --cui-control-group-action-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-control-group-action-border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-sm-border-radius),
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-property: #{var(--cui-btn-input-action-transition-property), transform},
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-duration: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-duration),
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-timing: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-timing),
    --cui-control-group-disabled-opacity: var(--cui-btn-input-disabled-opacity),
  ),
  $form-control-group-tokens
);
```

# Vue Bootstrap Form Control Group Component

> Learn how to compose Bootstrap-styled inputs with icons, static text and actions inside one shared frame using CoreUI's form control group.

## How to use Vue Bootstrap Form Control Group component

The `form-control-group` primitive puts an input together with icons, static text and actions inside one Bootstrap-styled frame — the same markup the PRO field components render internally.

```html
<template>
  <CFormControlGroup>
    <CFormControlIcon>
      <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 512 512" fill="currentColor">
        <path
          d="M479.6 399.716l-81.084-81.084-62.368-25.767A175.014 175.014 0 0 0 368 192c0-97.047-78.953-176-176-176S16 94.953 16 192s78.953 176 176 176a175.034 175.034 0 0 0 101.619-32.377l25.7 62.2L400.4 479.6a56 56 0 1 0 79.2-79.884ZM48 192c0-79.4 64.6-144 144-144s144 64.6 144 144-64.6 144-144 144S48 271.4 48 192Zm408.971 264.284a24.028 24.028 0 0 1-33.942 0l-76.572-76.572-23.894-57.835 57.835 23.894 76.573 76.572a24.028 24.028 0 0 1 0 33.941Z"
        />
      </svg>
    </CFormControlIcon>
    <CFormInput type="search" placeholder="Search…" aria-label="Search" />
  </CFormControlGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormControlGroup, CFormControlIcon, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### Parts

# Vue Form Input

> Vue input components. Give textual form `<input>`s an upgrade with custom styles, sizing, focus states, validation, and more.

## Example

```html
<template>
  <CForm>
    <CFormInput
      id="exampleFormControlInput1"
      type="email"
      label="Email address"
      placeholder="name@example.com"
      text="Must be 8-20 characters long."
    />
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CForm, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

If you need to add custom classs to form's components, or need to add some custom elements you can add each form component separately. Please check the example below.

```vue
<CForm>
  <CFormLabel for="exampleFormControlInput1">Email address</CFormLabel>
  <CFormInput type="email" id="exampleFormControlInput1" placeholder="name@example.com" aria-describedby="exampleFormControlInputHelpInline" />
  <CFormText as="span" id="exampleFormControlInputHelpInline">
    Must be 8-20 characters long.
  </CFormText>
</CForm>
```

You can also use slots.

```vue
<CFormInput
  type="email"
  id="exampleFormControlInput1"
  placeholder="name@example.com"
>
  <template #label>Email address</template>
  <template #text>Must be 8-20 characters long.</template>
</CFormInput>
```

## Sizing

Set heights using `size` property like `size="lg"` and `size="sm"`.

```html
    type="text"
    class="mb-4"
    placeholder="Default input"
    aria-label="default input example"
  />
  <CFormInput
    type="text"
    class="mb-4"
    size="sm"
    placeholder="Small input"
    aria-label="sm input example"
  />

</script>
```

```html
</script>
```

# Vue Form input Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Form input component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CFormInput

```jsx
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `feedback` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable feedback. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable feedback. |
| `feedbackValid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable invalid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied two CSS pseudo-classes, `:invalid` and `:valid`. |
| `floatingLabel` | `string` | - | Provide a floating label for the component — the text rests inside the field and floats once it has focus or a value. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `id` | `string` | - | The id global attribute defines an identifier (ID) that must be unique in the whole document. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control invalid. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `modelValue` | `File\|number\|string` | - | The default name for a value passed using v-model. |
| `plainText` | `boolean` | - | Render the component styled as plain text. Removes the default form field styling and preserve the correct margin and padding. Recommend to use only along side `readonly`. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the readonly state for the component. |
| `size` | `string` | - | Size the component small or large. |
| `text` | `string` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `type` | `string` | `'text'` | Specifies the type of component. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control valid. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the value emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `change` | Event occurs when the element loses focus, after the content has been changed. |
| `input` | Event occurs immediately after the value of a component has changed. |
| `update:modelValue` | Emit the new value whenever there’s an input or change event. |
| `update:validationState` | Event occurs with `undefined` when the user changes the value, or the form is reset, while `validationState` (or the deprecated `invalid`) is set. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it and let the browser's own validation show again. |

## CFormFeedback

```jsx
import { CFormFeedback } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `string` | `'div'` | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Style the feedback as the invalid message. |
| `tooltip` | `boolean` | - | If your form layout allows it, you can display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Style the feedback as the valid message. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state this feedback belongs to, rendered as the `{state}-feedback` (or `{state}-tooltip`) class. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. |

## CFormLabel

```jsx
import { CFormLabel } from '@coreui/vue'
```


### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `string` | `'div'` | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |

# Vue Form input Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Form input component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

`.form-control` and `.form-select` declare the `--cui-control-*` tokens on themselves, and so does every field built on them: the [form control group](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/form-control-group/styling/#css-variables) and every component that renders one — Autocomplete, Chip Input, Multi Select, the pickers, the password and number inputs — and the cells of the OTP input. Set a token on the field to restyle that field; a value set on an ancestor or on `:root` stops there. `class` and `style` on `<CFormInput>` land on the `<input>` itself. To restyle the frame of every field at once, change the [`--cui-btn-input-*` tokens](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/overview/#css-variables) it points to; buttons share their sizes, so they move too. The placeholder, disabled background and file button colours point at the palette instead and are set per field. The `sm` and `lg` sizes, `.form-control-sm` and `.form-control-lg`, are themselves token overrides.

The checkbox, radio and switch are not fields: the few `--cui-control-*` tokens they share sit on `:root` and are listed with the [checkbox](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/checkbox/styling/#shared-variables).

```scss
$form-control-tokens: () !default;
$form-control-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-control-min-height: var(--cui-btn-input-min-height),
    --cui-control-padding-y: var(--cui-btn-input-padding-y),
    --cui-control-padding-x: var(--cui-btn-input-padding-x),
    --cui-control-font-size: var(--cui-btn-input-font-size),
    --cui-control-font-weight: var(--cui-btn-input-font-weight),
    --cui-control-line-height: var(--cui-btn-input-line-height),
    --cui-control-fg: var(--cui-btn-input-fg),
    --cui-control-bg: var(--cui-btn-input-bg),
    --cui-control-border-width: var(--cui-btn-input-border-width),
    --cui-control-border-color: var(--cui-btn-input-border-color),
    --cui-control-border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-border-radius),
    --cui-control-box-shadow: var(--cui-btn-input-box-shadow),
    --cui-control-transition-property: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-property),
    --cui-control-transition-duration: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-duration),
    --cui-control-transition-timing: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-timing),
    --cui-control-placeholder-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-focus-color: var(--cui-btn-input-focus-color),
    --cui-control-focus-bg: var(--cui-btn-input-focus-bg),
    --cui-control-focus-border-color: var(--cui-btn-input-focus-border-color),
    --cui-control-disabled-color: var(--cui-control-fg),
    --cui-control-disabled-bg: var(--cui-bg-2),
    --cui-control-disabled-border-color: var(--cui-control-border-color),
    --cui-control-action-color: var(--cui-btn-input-fg),
    --cui-control-action-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-control-action-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-2),
    --cui-control-action-transition-property: var(--cui-btn-input-action-transition-property),
    --cui-control-action-transition-duration: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-duration),
    --cui-control-action-transition-timing: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-timing),
  ),
  $form-control-tokens
);
```

Two tokens are declared by the class that uses them rather than on every control: `--cui-control-plaintext-color` on `.form-control-plaintext`, and `--cui-control-color-width` on `.form-control-color`.

`.form-label` and `.col-form-label` carry the `--cui-label-*` tokens. Set them on a single label to restyle just that one, or on an ancestor to cover a whole form. The size classes are themselves token overrides: `.col-form-label-lg` sets `--cui-label-padding-y` and `--cui-label-font-size`.

```scss
$form-label-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-label-margin-bottom: .5rem,
    --cui-label-font-size: null,
    --cui-label-font-style: null,
    --cui-label-font-weight: var(--cui-font-weight-medium),
    --cui-label-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
  ),
  $form-label-tokens
);
```

`.form-text` carries the `--cui-form-text-*` tokens.

```scss
$form-text-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-text-margin-top: .25rem,
    --cui-form-text-font-size: var(--cui-small-font-size),
    --cui-form-text-font-style: null,
    --cui-form-text-font-weight: null,
    --cui-form-text-color: var(--cui-fg-2),
  ),
  $form-text-tokens
);
```

### Sass maps

Each entry generates one `.form-control-{size}` and `.form-select-{size}` class, pointing the control at the matching `--cui-btn-input-{size}-*` values. Add a key to define a size, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
$form-control-sizes: defaults(
  ("sm", "lg"),
  $form-control-sizes
);
```

# Vue Input Group Component

> Easily extend form controls by adding text, buttons, or button groups on either side of textual inputs, custom selects, and custom file inputs.

## Basic example

Place one add-on or button on either side of an input. You may also place one on both sides of an input. Remember to place `<CFormLabel>`s outside the input group.

```html
<template>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CInputGroupText id="basic-addon1">@</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput placeholder="Username" aria-label="Username" aria-describedby="basic-addon1" />
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CFormInput
      placeholder="Recipient's username"
      aria-label="Recipient's username"
      aria-describedby="basic-addon2"
    />
    <CInputGroupText id="basic-addon2">@example.com</CInputGroupText>
  </CInputGroup>
  <CFormLabel for="basic-url">Your vanity URL</CFormLabel>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CInputGroupText id="basic-addon3">https://example.com/users/</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput id="basic-url" aria-describedby="basic-addon3" />
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CInputGroupText>$</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput aria-label="Amount (to the nearest dollar)" />
    <CInputGroupText>.00</CInputGroupText>
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CFormInput placeholder="Username" aria-label="Username" />
    <CInputGroupText>@</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput placeholder="Server" aria-label="Server" />
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup>
    <CInputGroupText>With textarea</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormTextarea aria-label="With textarea"></CFormTextarea>
  </CInputGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CInputGroup, CInputGroupText, CFormInput, CFormLabel, CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CFormLabel for="inputGroupField">Your vanity URL</CFormLabel>
    <CInputGroup>
      <CInputGroupText>https://example.com/users/</CInputGroupText>
      <CFormInput id="inputGroupField" />
    </CInputGroup>
    <CFormText>Choose a unique name for your profile.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CFormText,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
} from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Wrapping

Input groups wrap by default via `flex-wrap: wrap` in order to accommodate custom form field validation within an input group. You may disable this with `.flex-nowrap`.

```html
<template>
  <CInputGroup class="flex-nowrap">
    <CInputGroupText id="addon-wrapping">@</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput placeholder="Username" aria-label="Username" aria-describedby="addon-wrapping" />
  </CInputGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CInputGroup, CInputGroupText, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Sizing

Add the relative form sizing classes to the `<CInputGroup>` itself and contents within will automatically resize—no need for repeating the form control size classes on each element.

**Sizing on the individual input group elements isn't supported.**

```html
<template>
  <CInputGroup size="sm" class="mb-4">
    <CInputGroupText id="inputGroup-sizing-sm">Small</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput aria-label="Sizing example input" aria-describedby="inputGroup-sizing-sm" />
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CInputGroupText id="inputGroup-sizing-default">Default</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput aria-label="Sizing example input" aria-describedby="inputGroup-sizing-default" />
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup size="lg">
    <CInputGroupText id="inputGroup-sizing-lg">Large</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput aria-label="Sizing example input" aria-describedby="inputGroup-sizing-lg" />
  </CInputGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CInputGroup, CInputGroupText, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Checkboxes and radios

Place any checkbox or radio option within an input group's addon instead of text.

```html
<template>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CInputGroupText>
      <CCheckbox value="" aria-label="Checkbox for following text input" />
    </CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput aria-label="Text input with checkbox" />
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup>
    <CInputGroupText>
      <CRadio value="" aria-label="Radio button for following text input" />
    </CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput aria-label="Text input with radio button" />
  </CInputGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CCheckbox, CFormInput, CInputGroup, CInputGroupText, CRadio } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Multiple inputs

While multiple `<CFormInput>`s are supported visually, validation styles are only available for input groups with a single `<CFormInput>`.

```html
<template>
  <CInputGroup>
    <CInputGroupText>First and last name</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput aria-label="First name" />
    <CFormInput aria-label="Last name" />
  </CInputGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CInputGroup, CInputGroupText, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Multiple addons

Multiple add-ons are supported and can be mixed with checkbox and radio input versions.

```html
<template>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CInputGroupText>$</CInputGroupText>
    <CInputGroupText>0.00</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput aria-label="Dollar amount (with dot and two decimal places)" />
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup>
    <CFormInput aria-label="Dollar amount (with dot and two decimal places)" />
    <CInputGroupText>$</CInputGroupText>
    <CInputGroupText>0.00</CInputGroupText>
  </CInputGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CInputGroup, CInputGroupText, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Custom forms

Input groups include support for custom selects and custom file inputs. Browser default versions of these are not supported.

### Custom select

```html
<template>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CInputGroupText as="label" for="inputGroupSelect01">Options</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormSelect id="inputGroupSelect01">
      <option>Choose...</option>
      <option value="1">One</option>
      <option value="2">Two</option>
      <option value="3">Three</option>
    </CFormSelect>
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CFormSelect id="inputGroupSelect02">
      <option>Choose...</option>
      <option value="1">One</option>
      <option value="2">Two</option>
      <option value="3">Three</option>
    </CFormSelect>
    <CInputGroupText as="label" for="inputGroupSelect02">Options</CInputGroupText>
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CButton type="button" theme="secondary" variant="outline">Button</CButton>
    <CFormSelect id="inputGroupSelect03" aria-label="Example select with button addon">
      <option>Choose...</option>
      <option value="1">One</option>
      <option value="2">Two</option>
      <option value="3">Three</option>
    </CFormSelect>
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup>
    <CFormSelect id="inputGroupSelect04" aria-label="Example select with button addon">
      <option>Choose...</option>
      <option value="1">One</option>
      <option value="2">Two</option>
      <option value="3">Three</option>
    </CFormSelect>
    <CButton type="button" theme="secondary" variant="outline">Button</CButton>
  </CInputGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CInputGroup, CInputGroupText, CFormSelect, CButton } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

### Custom file input

```html
<template>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CInputGroupText as="label" for="inputGroupFile01">Upload</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput id="inputGroupFile01" type="file" />
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CFormInput id="inputGroupFile02" type="file" />
    <CInputGroupText as="label" for="inputGroupFile02">Upload</CInputGroupText>
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CButton id="inputGroupFileAddon03" type="button" theme="secondary" variant="outline"
      >Button</CButton
    >
    <CFormInput
      id="inputGroupFile03"
      type="file"
      aria-describedby="inputGroupFileAddon03"
      aria-label="Upload"
    />
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup>
    <CFormInput
      id="inputGroupFile04"
      type="file"
      aria-describedby="inputGroupFileAddon04"
      aria-label="Upload"
    />
    <CButton id="inputGroupFileAddon04" type="button" theme="secondary" variant="outline"
      >Button</CButton
    >
  </CInputGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CInputGroup, CInputGroupText, CFormInput, CButton } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

```jsx
import { CInputGroup } from '@coreui/vue'
```

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

```jsx
import { CInputGroupText } from '@coreui/vue'
```

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

# Vue Input group Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Input group component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

The addon declares its own tokens on `.input-group-text`, so a single addon can be repainted or resized without a modifier class. The first six are the [`--cui-control-*`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/input/styling/#css-variables) frame tokens, copied onto the addon so it lines up with the control next to it; `size` on `<CInputGroup>` (`.input-group-{size}`) re-points all of them but the border width, on the addon and on the `.form-control` or `.form-select` next to it. `.input-group` itself declares none — it is a layout wrapper, and a token set on it reaches neither the addon nor the control, because each declares its own.

```scss
$input-group-tokens: () !default;
$input-group-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-control-padding-y: var(--cui-btn-input-padding-y),
    --cui-control-padding-x: var(--cui-btn-input-padding-x),
    --cui-control-font-size: var(--cui-btn-input-font-size),
    --cui-control-line-height: var(--cui-btn-input-line-height),
    --cui-control-border-width: var(--cui-btn-input-border-width),
    --cui-control-border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-border-radius),
    --cui-input-group-addon-font-weight: var(--cui-btn-input-font-weight),
    --cui-input-group-addon-color: var(--cui-btn-input-fg),
    --cui-input-group-addon-bg: var(--cui-bg-2),
    --cui-input-group-addon-border-color: var(--cui-btn-input-border-color),
  ),
  $input-group-tokens
);
```

```vue
<CInputGroupText style="--cui-input-group-addon-bg: var(--cui-bg-1)">@</CInputGroupText>
```

### Sass maps

Each entry is one `.input-group-{size}` class, and the map merges with your overrides — add a key to define a size, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$input-group-sizes: defaults(
  ("sm", "lg"),
  $input-group-sizes
);
```


---

# Vue Bootstrap Input group Component

> Learn how to use CoreUI’s Vue Input group component with Bootstrap styles for flexible, framework-consistent UI.

## Basic example

Place one add-on or button on either side of an input. You may also place one on both sides of an input. Remember to place `<CFormLabel>`s outside the input group.

```html
<template>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CInputGroupText id="basic-addon1">@</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput placeholder="Username" aria-label="Username" aria-describedby="basic-addon1" />
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CFormInput
      placeholder="Recipient's username"
      aria-label="Recipient's username"
      aria-describedby="basic-addon2"
    />
    <CInputGroupText id="basic-addon2">@example.com</CInputGroupText>
  </CInputGroup>
  <CFormLabel for="basic-url">Your vanity URL</CFormLabel>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CInputGroupText id="basic-addon3">https://example.com/users/</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput id="basic-url" aria-describedby="basic-addon3" />
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CInputGroupText>$</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput aria-label="Amount (to the nearest dollar)" />
    <CInputGroupText>.00</CInputGroupText>
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CFormInput placeholder="Username" aria-label="Username" />
    <CInputGroupText>@</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput placeholder="Server" aria-label="Server" />
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup>
    <CInputGroupText>With textarea</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormTextarea aria-label="With textarea"></CFormTextarea>
  </CInputGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CInputGroup, CInputGroupText, CFormInput, CFormLabel, CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Wrapping

Input groups wrap by default via `flex-wrap: wrap` in order to accommodate custom form field validation within an input group. You may disable this with `.flex-nowrap`.

```html
<template>
  <CInputGroup class="flex-nowrap">
    <CInputGroupText id="addon-wrapping">@</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput placeholder="Username" aria-label="Username" aria-describedby="addon-wrapping" />
  </CInputGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CInputGroup, CInputGroupText, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Sizing

Add the relative form sizing classes to the `<CInputGroup>` itself and contents within will automatically resize—no need for repeating the form control size classes on each element.

**Sizing on the individual input group elements isn't supported.**

```html

    <CInputGroupText id="inputGroup-sizing-default">Default</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput aria-label="Sizing example input" aria-describedby="inputGroup-sizing-default" />
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup size="lg">
    <CInputGroupText id="inputGroup-sizing-lg">Large</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormInput aria-label="Sizing example input" aria-describedby="inputGroup-sizing-lg" />
  </CInputGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CInputGroup, CInputGroupText, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

```html
</script>
```

## Custom forms

Input groups include support for custom selects and custom file inputs. Browser default versions of these are not supported.

### Custom select

```html
<template>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CInputGroupText as="label" for="inputGroupSelect01">Options</CInputGroupText>
    <CFormSelect id="inputGroupSelect01">
      <option>Choose...</option>
      <option value="1">One</option>
      <option value="2">Two</option>
      <option value="3">Three</option>
    </CFormSelect>
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CFormSelect id="inputGroupSelect02">
      <option>Choose...</option>
      <option value="1">One</option>
      <option value="2">Two</option>
      <option value="3">Three</option>
    </CFormSelect>
    <CInputGroupText as="label" for="inputGroupSelect02">Options</CInputGroupText>
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup class="mb-4">
    <CButton type="button" theme="secondary" variant="outline">Button</CButton>
    <CFormSelect id="inputGroupSelect03" aria-label="Example select with button addon">
      <option>Choose...</option>
      <option value="1">One</option>
      <option value="2">Two</option>
      <option value="3">Three</option>
    </CFormSelect>
  </CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroup>
    <CFormSelect id="inputGroupSelect04" aria-label="Example select with button addon">
      <option>Choose...</option>
      <option value="1">One</option>
      <option value="2">Two</option>
      <option value="3">Three</option>
    </CFormSelect>
    <CButton type="button" theme="secondary" variant="outline">Button</CButton>
  </CInputGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CInputGroup, CInputGroupText, CFormSelect, CButton } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

### Custom file input

```html
<template>

  </CInputGroup>

    <CButton id="inputGroupFileAddon03" type="button" theme="secondary" variant="outline"
      >Button</CButton
    >
    <CFormInput
      id="inputGroupFile03"
      type="file"
      aria-describedby="inputGroupFileAddon03"
      aria-label="Upload"
    />
  </CInputGroup>

    <CFormInput
      id="inputGroupFile04"
      type="file"
      aria-describedby="inputGroupFileAddon04"
      aria-label="Upload"

      >Button</CButton
    >
  </CInputGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CInputGroup, CInputGroupText, CFormInput, CButton } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

# Vue Multi Select

> Customize the native <select>s with a powerful Vue Multi Select component that changes the element’s initial appearance and brings some new functionalities.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Basic example

A clear demonstration of implementing a basic Vue Multi Select dropdown, highlighting essential options and configurations.

```html
<template>
  <CMultiSelect
    label="Framework"
    :options="options"
    text="Please select your framework."
    search
    :default-value="[2, 3, 5]"
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const options = [
  {
    value: 0,
    label: 'Angular',
  },
  {
    value: 1,
    label: 'Bootstrap',
  },
  {
    value: 2,
    label: 'React.js',
  },
  {
    value: 3,
    label: 'Vue.js',
  },
  {
    label: 'backend',
    options: [
      {
        value: 4,
        label: 'Django',
      },
      {
        value: 5,
        label: 'Laravel',
      },
      {
        value: 6,
        label: 'Node.js',
      },
    ],
  },
]
</script>
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CFormLabel for="multiSelectField">Technologies</CFormLabel>
    <CMultiSelect
      id="multiSelectField"
      name="stack"
      :options="[
        { value: 0, label: 'Angular' },
        { value: 1, label: 'Bootstrap' },
        { value: 2, label: 'React.js' },
        { value: 3, label: 'Vue.js' },
      ]"
    />
    <CFormText>Pick every technology you work with.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CFormLabel, CFormText } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Search

You can configure the search functionality within the component. The `search` property determines how the search input element is enabled and behaves. It accepts multiple types to provide flexibility in configuring search behavior. By default is set to `true`.

### Disabled search

To disable the default search input element, please set `search` property to `false` like in the example below:

```html
<template>
  <CMultiSelect :options="options2" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const options2 = [
  {
    value: 0,
    label: 'Angular',
    selected: true,
  },
  {
    value: 1,
    label: 'Bootstrap',
    selected: true,
    disabled: true,
  },
  {
    value: 2,
    label: 'React.js',
  },
  {
    value: 3,
    label: 'Vue.js',
  },
  {
    label: 'backend',
    options: [
      {
        value: 4,
        label: 'Django',
      },
      {
        value: 5,
        label: 'Laravel',
        selected: true,
      },
      {
        value: 6,
        label: 'Node.js',
      },
    ],
  },
]
</script>
```

### Where typing goes

Typing reaches the search box from anywhere in the component — the control, the options panel, the select all button — so it never depends on where the focus happens to be.

Set `:global-search="false"` to keep typing local. The search box then filters only while it has the focus, and a keystroke over the options list jumps to the first option starting with it. With `search="external"` the list holds only the last results, so that keystroke does nothing.

```html
<template>
  <CMultiSelect :options="options" :global-search="false" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const options = [
  {
    value: 0,
    label: 'Angular',
  },
  {
    value: 1,
    label: 'Bootstrap',
  },
  {
    value: 2,
    label: 'React.js',
  },
  {
    value: 3,
    label: 'Vue.js',
  },
  {
    label: 'backend',
    options: [
      {
        value: 4,
        label: 'Django',
      },
      {
        value: 5,
        label: 'Laravel',
      },
      {
        value: 6,
        label: 'Node.js',
      },
    ],
  },
]
</script>
```

### External search

When external search is enabled (`search="external"`), the component delegates search operations to an external API. This setup is ideal for scenarios where third-party services or custom backend implementations power search capabilities. 

```vue
<CMultiSelect :options=[...] search="external" @filter-change="..." />
```

Please check the [External Data](#external-data) section to check a working example of how to handle external data.

## Modes

### Allow create options

Users can create new options as well as choose from a list of pre-existing options by using the `allowCreateOptions` property in the Vue Multi Select component.

If this propety is set to `true`, the user can enter a new option in the multiselect component's search input field, and if it doesn't already exist in the list, it will be created and added there. This can be useful when the list of available options is not comprehensive or when the user needs to select an option that is not already available.

```html
<template>
  <CMultiSelect allow-create-options :options="options" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const options = [
  {
    value: 0,
    label: 'Angular',
  },
  {
    value: 1,
    label: 'Bootstrap',
  },
  {
    value: 2,
    label: 'React.js',
  },
  {
    value: 3,
    label: 'Vue.js',
  },
  {
    label: 'backend',
    options: [
      {
        value: 4,
        label: 'Django',
      },
      {
        value: 5,
        label: 'Laravel',
      },
      {
        value: 6,
        label: 'Node.js',
      },
    ],
  },
]
</script>
```

### Clear search on select

The `clearSearchOnSelect` property is a Boolean attribute that can be used with the MultiSelect component in the CoreUI Vue library.

The MultiSelect component's search input field will be cleared as soon as the user chooses an item from the dropdown list if the property `clearSearchOnSelect` is set to `true`. This indicates that the user can instantly begin a fresh search after the search query is reset.

By default, the search input field will keep the user's search query even after an option has been picked because the value of the `clearSearchOnSelect` property is set to `false`. When a user must choose from a dropdown list several items that all match the same search term, this can be helpful.

You only need to specify the `clearSearchOnSelect` property to 'true' or 'false' as necessary in your code to use the MultiSelect component of the CoreUI Vue package. For example:

```html
<template>
  <CMultiSelect clear-search-on-select :options="options" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const options = [
  {
    value: 0,
    label: 'Angular',
  },
  {
    value: 1,
    label: 'Bootstrap',
  },
  {
    value: 2,
    label: 'React.js',
  },
  {
    value: 3,
    label: 'Vue.js',
  },
  {
    label: 'backend',
    options: [
      {
        value: 4,
        label: 'Django',
      },
      {
        value: 5,
        label: 'Laravel',
      },
      {
        value: 6,
        label: 'Node.js',
      },
    ],
  },
]
</script>
```

In this example, the `clearSearchOnSelect` property is set to `true`, which means that the search input field will be cleared as soon as the user selects an option from the dropdown list.

## Selection types

Users can present selected items in a variety of ways by using the Vue Multi Select component. Selected things can be shown to users as chips, a counter, or a list of values separated by commas.

Use the `selectionType` property to set the presentation type to alter how the selected items are displayed.

### Chips

By default, the `selectionType` property is set to `"chips"`, which renders selected options as removable [chips](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/chip/). Users can remove a selected option with its remove button, named by `ariaChipRemoveLabel`. `"tags"`, the v5 name of this mode, renders the same and is deprecated.

```html
<template>
  <CMultiSelect :options="options2" selection-type="chips" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const options2 = [
  {
    value: 0,
    label: 'Angular',
    selected: true,
  },
  {
    value: 1,
    label: 'Bootstrap',
    selected: true,
    disabled: true,
  },
  {
    value: 2,
    label: 'React.js',
  },
  {
    value: 3,
    label: 'Vue.js',
  },
  {
    label: 'backend',
    options: [
      {
        value: 4,
        label: 'Django',
      },
      {
        value: 5,
        label: 'Laravel',
        selected: true,
      },
      {
        value: 6,
        label: 'Node.js',
      },
    ],
  },
]
</script>
```

### Counter

The items from the list that are chosen for the example below are counted and shown as a counter. Set the `selectionType` property to "counter" in order to use this option.

The `selectedLabel` property builds the counter's whole text: pass a function `(count, total) => string`, or a string in which `{count}` and `{total}` are replaced. `total` is the number of options in the list, disabled ones, the ones inside a group and the ones the user created included, so a disabled option shows that not everything is selected, plus any selected value the options lack, so it never falls below `count`. Pass `total` to put a number of your own in `{total}`, such as the records a search on your server can reach, when the list holds only one page of them.

```html
<template>
  <CMultiSelect :options="options2" selection-type="counter" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const options2 = [
  {
    value: 0,
    label: 'Angular',
    selected: true,
  },
  {
    value: 1,
    label: 'Bootstrap',
    selected: true,
    disabled: true,
  },
  {
    value: 2,
    label: 'React.js',
  },
  {
    value: 3,
    label: 'Vue.js',
  },
  {
    label: 'backend',
    options: [
      {
        value: 4,
        label: 'Django',
      },
      {
        value: 5,
        label: 'Laravel',
        selected: true,
      },
      {
        value: 6,
        label: 'Node.js',
      },
    ],
  },
]
</script>
```

### Text

Set the `selectionType` property to '"text"' to show the list of selected options as comma-separated text values.

```html
<template>

    value: 3,

    label: 'backend',
```

## Select all

_Added in 5.19.0._

When `multiple` is enabled, a **select all** button is rendered in the dropdown header (toggle it with the `selectAll` property, on by default). The button works as a toggle: it selects every option and its label switches to `deselectAllLabel`, then deselects everything on the next click.

With the default `indicator="checkbox"` the button shows a tri-state marker that mirrors the overall selection — `none` when nothing is selected, `all` when everything is, and `indeterminate` in between. `indicator="none"` drops the marker from the whole list, the button included.

```html
<template>
  <CMultiSelect :options="options" search />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const options = [
  {
    value: 0,
    label: 'Angular',
  },
  {
    value: 1,
    label: 'Bootstrap',
  },
  {
    value: 2,
    label: 'React.js',
  },
  {
    value: 3,
    label: 'Vue.js',
  },
  {
    label: 'backend',
    options: [
      {
        value: 4,
        label: 'Django',
      },
      {
        value: 5,
        label: 'Laravel',
      },
      {
        value: 6,
        label: 'Node.js',
      },
    ],
  },
]
</script>
```

### Acting on filtered options

By default (`selectAllMode="all"`) the header button acts on the full list, ignoring the current filter. Set `selectAllMode="filtered"` to scope the button to the options currently matched by the search filter. The button's label and checkbox then answer "are all *filtered* options selected?". With no active filter, every option matches, so this behaves exactly like `"all"`.

To avoid a misleading "Select all" while a filter is active, the label switches to `selectFilteredLabel` / `deselectFilteredLabel` (default `Select filtered` / `Deselect filtered`) whenever the filter actually narrows the list — and falls back to `selectAllLabel` / `deselectAllLabel` when nothing is hidden.

Type into the search box below, then use select all — only the matching options are selected.

```html
<template>
  <CMultiSelect :options="options" search select-all-mode="filtered" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const options = [
  {
    value: 0,
    label: 'Angular',
  },
  {
    value: 1,
    label: 'Bootstrap',
  },
  {
    value: 2,
    label: 'React.js',
  },
  {
    value: 3,
    label: 'Vue.js',
  },
  {
    label: 'backend',
    options: [
      {
        value: 4,
        label: 'Django',
      },
      {
        value: 5,
        label: 'Laravel',
      },
      {
        value: 6,
        label: 'Node.js',
      },
    ],
  },
]
</script>
```

### Hiding select all when search has no results

_Added in 5.20.0._

When `search` is enabled and the user types a query that matches no options, there is nothing left to select — so leaving the **select all** button visible above the empty "No results found" message is misleading. By default (`hideSelectAllOnSearchNoResults` is `true`) the component hides the whole dropdown header in that case, and brings it back as soon as the search matches at least one option again.

Type a query that matches nothing (for example `xyz`) into the example below — the select all button disappears together with the options, then returns when you clear or change the search.

```html
<template>
  <CMultiSelect :options="options" search />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const options = [
  {
    value: 0,
    label: 'Angular',
  },
  {
    value: 1,
    label: 'Bootstrap',
  },
  {
    value: 2,
    label: 'React.js',
  },
  {
    value: 3,
    label: 'Vue.js',
  },
  {
    label: 'backend',
    options: [
      {
        value: 4,
        label: 'Django',
      },
      {
        value: 5,
        label: 'Laravel',
      },
      {
        value: 6,
        label: 'Node.js',
      },
    ],
  },
]
</script>
```

Set `:hide-select-all-on-search-no-results="false"` to keep the header (and the select all button) visible even when the search returns no results.

```html
<template>
  <CMultiSelect :options="options" search :hide-select-all-on-search-no-results="false" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const options = [
  {
    value: 0,
    label: 'Angular',
  },
  {
    value: 1,
    label: 'Bootstrap',
  },
  {
    value: 2,
    label: 'React.js',
  },
  {
    value: 3,
    label: 'Vue.js',
  },
  {
    label: 'backend',
    options: [
      {
        value: 4,
        label: 'Django',
      },
      {
        value: 5,
        label: 'Laravel',
      },
      {
        value: 6,
        label: 'Node.js',
      },
    ],
  },
]
</script>
```

This option only affects the built-in select all button. A [custom dropdown header](#custom-dropdown-header) is always rendered, since it may contain controls unrelated to the options list.

## Selection limit

_Added in 5.19.0._

Use the `selectionLimit` property to limit how many options can be selected. The select all button stays enabled and selects options up to the limit, then toggles to deselect all once the limit is reached. The `selection-limit` event fires when a user tries to select more options than allowed — use it to show feedback.

```html
<template>
  <CAlert
    v-if="limitReached"
    theme="warning"
    dismissible
    @close="
      () => {
        limitReached = false
      }
    "
  >
    You can select up to 3 options.
  </CAlert>
  <CMultiSelect
    :options="options"
    search
    :selection-limit="3"
    @selection-limit="
      () => {
        limitReached = true
      }
    "
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CAlert } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const limitReached = ref(false)

const options = [
  {
    value: 0,
    label: 'Angular',
  },
  {
    value: 1,
    label: 'Bootstrap',
  },
  {
    value: 2,
    label: 'React.js',
  },
  {
    value: 3,
    label: 'Vue.js',
  },
  {
    label: 'backend',
    options: [
      {
        value: 4,
        label: 'Django',
      },
      {
        value: 5,
        label: 'Laravel',
      },
      {
        value: 6,
        label: 'Node.js',
      },
    ],
  },
]
</script>
```

## Selectable groups

_Added in 5.19.0._

Enable `optionsGroupsSelectable` to turn each group label into its own tri-state checkbox that toggles the group's visible options. Because the indicator is rendered with CSS, it supports a third, `indeterminate` state — shown when only some of a group's options are selected — without any real `<input>` element. One property decides the marker for the whole list: `indicator` (`'checkbox'` by default) reaches the options, the group labels and the select-all button alike, and every one of them requires `multiple`.

```html
<template>
  <CMultiSelect :options="options" search options-groups-selectable />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const options = [
  {
    label: 'Frontend',
    options: [
      {
        value: 0,
        label: 'Angular',
      },
      {
        value: 1,
        label: 'Bootstrap',
      },
      {
        value: 2,
        label: 'React.js',
      },
      {
        value: 3,
        label: 'Vue.js',
      },
    ],
  },
  {
    label: 'Backend',
    options: [
      {
        value: 4,
        label: 'Django',
      },
      {
        value: 5,
        label: 'Laravel',
      },
      {
        value: 6,
        label: 'Node.js',
      },
    ],
  },
]
</script>
```

## Custom dropdown header

_Added in 5.19.0._

Use the `header` scoped slot to fully customize the dropdown header — the area above the options list — including rendering several action buttons. It replaces the built-in select all button and renders independently of `selectAll`. The slot exposes a `state` object (`{ selected, total, filtered, filteredSelected }`) and an `actions` object (`{ selectAll, deselectAll, selectFiltered, deselectFiltered }`) with the component's selection methods, so you can wire your own controls. It re-renders on every selection change and search filter, so labels and `disabled` states stay up to date.

```html
<template>
  <CMultiSelect :options="options" placeholder="Select frameworks" search>
    <template #header="{ state, actions }">
      <div class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-3">
        <CButton
          size="sm"
          theme="primary"
          :disabled="state.selected >= state.total"
          @click="actions.selectAll()"
        >
          Select all ({{ state.total }})
        </CButton>
        <CButton
          size="sm"
          theme="secondary"
          :disabled="state.filtered === state.filteredSelected"
          @click="actions.selectFiltered()"
        >
          Select filtered ({{ state.filtered }})
        </CButton>
        <CButton
          size="sm"
          theme="secondary"
          variant="outline"
          :disabled="state.filteredSelected === 0"
          @click="actions.deselectFiltered()"
        >
          Deselect filtered ({{ state.filteredSelected }})
        </CButton>
        <CButton
          size="sm"
          theme="danger"
          variant="outline"
          :disabled="state.selected === 0"
          @click="actions.deselectAll()"
        >
          Deselect all ({{ state.selected }})
        </CButton>
      </div>
    </template>
  </CMultiSelect>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CButton } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const options = [
  {
    value: 'angular',
    label: 'Angular',
  },
  {
    value: 'bootstrap',
    label: 'Bootstrap',
  },
  {
    value: 'react',
    label: 'React.js',
  },
  {
    value: 'vue',
    label: 'Vue.js',
  },
```

## Validation

The component shows its validation state on the frame and on the element that takes the focus, and stops the form from being submitted while it is invalid.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row g-4" novalidate validate>
    <div class="col-md-6">
      <CMultiSelect
        feedback-invalid="Pick at least one framework."
        label="Frameworks"
        :options="options"
        required
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-md-6">
      <CMultiSelect
        v-model:validation-state="planState"
        :default-value="[0]"
        feedback="Angular is not available in this plan."
        label="Plan frameworks"
        :options="options"
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-12">
      <CButton color="primary" type="submit">Submit</CButton>
    </div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CForm, CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const planState = ref('invalid')

const options = [
  { value: 0, label: 'Angular' },
  { value: 1, label: 'Bootstrap' },
  { value: 2, label: 'React.js' },
  { value: 3, label: 'Vue.js' },
]
</script>
```

The state comes from three places, in this order:

- `validationState`: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`; `invalid` and `valid` still work as aliases. While it is set, the component draws it instead of what the browser reports. While it is `'invalid'`, the native select blocks the submit with the text of the linked message, or `Invalid value.` when there is none, unless the component is `disabled`; a custom validity you set on the native select yourself stays as it is.
- A validation that reports the native select invalid: a submit, `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()`, which [`CForm`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/validation/) and the stepper call as well. From then on the frame and the control show it invalid whenever its selection is invalid, until the form is reset, and the message after the frame shows.
- In a form with `validate`, the `:user-invalid` state of the native select, and with `validate="valid"` also its `:user-valid` state.

A state you give is a verdict on the selection it was given for. When the user changes the selection, or the form is reset, the component emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop the state, as the second field above does. A change your code makes through `value` keeps it, and so does an action that leaves the selection as it is. A reset emits once it has run, so a state you set from a `reset` listener on the form gets the same event, and your handler decides whether to drop it. An `aria-invalid` attribute on the component is not read; set the state with `validationState`. A native reset of the form puts back the selection given by `defaultValue` or the options' `selected` and emits `change` when that changes the selection; with `value` it asks through `change` for the `value` the component started with.

## Disabled

Add the `disabled` boolean property to give it a grayed out appearance, remove pointer events, and prevent focusing. A group given with `disabled: true` disables every option in it; a plain string option inside it reaches your slots and events as `{ label, value, disabled: true }`.


## Floating labels

Set `floatingLabel` and the component renders the label itself — no wrapper markup needed — and the text also becomes the field's accessible name; it has no input to report emptiness, so the label floats on focus and on the first selection, and the component's `placeholder` is hidden while the label rests inside the field.

```html
<template>
  <CMultiSelect
    id="floatingMultiSelect"
    floating-label="Frameworks"
    :options="[
      { label: 'Angular', value: 1 },
      { label: 'Bootstrap', value: 2 },
      { label: 'React.js', value: 3 },
      { label: 'Vue.js', value: 4 },
    ]"
  />
</template>
```

Set `floatingLabelAlways` to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the placeholder showing.

## Virtual Scroller (1000 records)

To enhance performance and manage large amounts of data in Vue Multi Select, you can generate a list of options using ``. This component renders only the items currently visible on the screen, and as the user scrolls, new items are dynamically loaded and added to the view. This helps to reduce the data load and processing time, resulting in a more responsive UI.

To enable Virtual Scroller, simply set the `virtualScroller` boolean property to `true`, as shown in the example below.
