## External Data

One of the key features of Vue Multi Select component is the ability to load data from an external source, such as an API or a server-side script. This can be useful if you have a large amount of data that you don't want to load all at once. To load external data into a Vue MultiSelect, you can use the Fetch API to the data source.

Here is an example of how you might use Vue Multi Select with external data:

```html
<template>
  <CMultiSelect
    label="Users"
    :loading="loading"
    :options="users"
    search="external"
    text="Please select your user."
    virtual-scroller
    @show="() => getUsers()"
    @filter-change="(value) => getUsers(value)"
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
import { ref } from 'vue'
const loading = ref(false)
const users = ref([])
const getUsers = async (name = '') => {
  loading.value = true
  fetch(`https://apitest.coreui.io/demos/users?first_name=${name}`)
    .then((response) => response.json())
    .then((result) => {
      loading.value = false
      users.value = result.records.map((record) => ({
        value: record.id,
        label: record.first_name,
      }))
    })
}
</script>
```

## Selection and panel

_Added in 6.0.0._

The selection and the dropdown panel are independent — each has its own starting value, its own way of handing control to the parent, and its own change event.

| | seeds the start | hands control to the parent | change event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Selection | `defaultValue` | `value` | `@change` |
| Panel | `show` | `v-model:show` | `@update:show` |

The events fire either way — `@change` with the selected options, `@update:show` whenever the panel requests an open-state change (a dismiss gesture like Escape or an outside click, or any internal toggle) — so you can watch either state without taking it over. The deprecated `visible` prop keeps its old behavior and is ignored when `show` is set.

### Selection

`defaultValue` seeds the uncontrolled selection — matched against the option values — and the select manages it from there. The per-option `selected` flags are the same seed in another spelling, read from the options the component starts with and ignored entirely when `defaultValue` or `value` is set. Options that arrive later, such as an answer to an external search, never change what the user picked, whatever they are marked; a `defaultValue` value they bring is still taken, and `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange` starts from the marked options when the values change.

```vue
<template>
  <CMultiSelect :default-value="[1, 2]" :options="options" />
</template>
```

Pass `value` and the selection is fully controlled: it renders exactly what you pass, a pick only fires `@change`, and nothing moves until you feed the change back. `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange` and a native reset of the form follow the same contract — in controlled mode they only request the empty selection, or the first `value`, through `@change`. A selection you give never emits `change`: `value`, `defaultValue` and options marked `selected`, also when the options it names arrive later, unless `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange` puts it in place of the selection. Check **Ignore picks** below and select something to watch a dropped change revert.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField class="mb-4">
    <CCheckbox
      id="multiSelectControlledValueIgnore"
      v-model="ignorePicks"
      label="Ignore picks (watch them revert)"
    />
  </CFormField>
  <CMultiSelect label="Frameworks" :options="options" :value="value" @change="handleChange" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const ignorePicks = ref(false)
const value = ref([1, 2])

const options = [
  { value: 0, label: 'Angular' },
  { value: 1, label: 'Bootstrap' },
  { value: 2, label: 'React.js' },
  { value: 3, label: 'Vue.js' },
]

const handleChange = (selected) => {
  if (!ignorePicks.value) {
    value.value = selected.map((option) => option.value)
  }
}
</script>
```

### Panel

Without a binding the select manages the panel itself. Pass `show` to seed it open on mount.

```vue
<template>
  <CMultiSelect show :options="options" />
</template>
```

Pass `show` and the panel renders what you pass — dismiss gestures only emit `@update:show`, so feed the change back, or nothing closes. That includes a pick: in single selection a pick that would normally close the panel only requests the close through `@update:show`. The `v-model:show` binding is that loop in one attribute. Here a checkbox pins the panel open, and a dismiss gesture unchecks it.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField class="mb-4">
    <CCheckbox id="multiSelectControlledShow" v-model="show" label="Keep the panel open" />
  </CFormField>
  <CMultiSelect v-model:show="show" label="Framework" :multiple="false" :options="options" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const show = ref(false)

const options = [
  { value: 0, label: 'Angular' },
  { value: 1, label: 'Bootstrap' },
  { value: 2, label: 'React.js' },
  { value: 3, label: 'Vue.js' },
]
</script>
```

Use it when the open state belongs to something else — a route, a tour step, or a control outside the select like the checkbox above.

## Accessibility

The CoreUI Vue Multi Select component is designed with accessibility in mind and follows WAI-ARIA guidelines to ensure it works well with assistive technologies like screen readers.

### Built-in Accessibility Features

The Multi Select component includes several accessibility features out of the box:

- **ARIA Roles**: A `combobox` control opening a `dialog` panel, with a `listbox` inside it
- **ARIA States**: Dynamic `aria-expanded`, `aria-selected`, and `aria-disabled` attributes
- **Keyboard Navigation**: Full keyboard support with arrow keys, Enter, Space, and Escape
- **Focus Management**: The focus moves into the panel while it is open and returns to the control when it closes
- **Screen Reader Labels**: Descriptive labels for interactive elements

### Customizing Accessibility Labels

You can customize the accessibility labels for better user experience:

```vue
<CMultiSelect
  :options="options"
  aria-cleaner-label="Clear all selected items"
  aria-picker-label="Open options menu"
  placeholder="Choose your options..."
/>
```

### ARIA Attributes

The component automatically handles these ARIA attributes:

- `aria-expanded`: Indicates whether the dropdown is open or closed
- `aria-haspopup="dialog"`: Tells screen readers that the control opens a dialog
- `aria-labelledby`: Names the control and the panel after the label (`label`, `floatingLabel`, or a `<label>` pointing at the component's `id`, read when the component mounts or its `id` changes); an `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label` given to the component takes precedence. A `<label>` wrapping the component is left out, because its text would take in the control's own content and selection. The search box keeps a name of its own, `ariaSearchLabel`
- `aria-required`: Marks the focused control, the search box when `search` is on, as required when `required` is set or an `aria-required` is given to the component
- `aria-multiselectable="true"`: Indicates multiple selections are allowed
- `aria-selected`: Shows which options are currently selected
- `aria-disabled`: Identifies disabled options
- `aria-controls`: Points the control at the dropdown dialog and the search input at the list of options while the dropdown is open

### Keyboard Navigation

The options panel is a dialog named like the control. Opening it moves the focus inside — onto the search box when `search` is on, otherwise onto the option the list points at, which is the selection the user left or the first option. The options are focusable one at a time, so the arrows move the focus itself.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move between the search box, the select all button and the options list; the focus stays in the open panel |
| <kbd>Enter/Space</kbd> | Open the panel from the control, or select the focused option; <kbd>Enter</kbd> in the search box takes the option the list points at |
| <kbd>Arrow Up/Down</kbd> | Move through the options, or enter the list from the search box |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Arrow Up/Down</kbd> | Extend the selection while moving (multiple selection) |
| <kbd>Home/End</kbd> | Focus the first/last option (not while typing in the search box), or the first/last chip from a chip |
| <kbd>Ctrl/Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> | Select every option the list shows, from the options list (multiple selection) |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close the panel and return the focus to the control |
| <kbd>Backspace/Delete</kbd> | In the empty search box, focus the last chip; on a chip, remove it and move the focus to the next chip, else the previous one, else the search box, or the field when there is none. Entering the chips closes an open panel. A single select and the `counter` and `text` selections remove the last selected item at once |
| <kbd>Arrow Left/Arrow Right</kbd> | From the start of the search box, focus the last chip; between the chips, move the focus; past the last chip, return to the search box (mirrored in right-to-left) |

### Best Practices

For optimal accessibility, consider these recommendations:

1. **Always provide a label**: Use the `label` prop or associate with a `<label>` element
2. **Use descriptive placeholder text**: Help users understand what to select
3. **Provide clear option labels**: Ensure option text is descriptive and unique
4. **Consider color contrast**: Ensure sufficient contrast for visual indicators
5. **Test with screen readers**: Verify the component works with assistive technologies

```vue
<CMultiSelect
  label="Select your preferred programming languages"
  placeholder="Choose languages..."
  :options="[
    { value: 'js', label: 'JavaScript' },
    { value: 'ts', label: 'TypeScript' },
    { value: 'py', label: 'Python' }
  ]"
  :validation-state="hasError ? 'invalid' : undefined"
  feedback="Please select at least one language"
/>
```

# Vue Multi Select Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Multi Select component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## CMultiSelect

```jsx
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allowCreateOptions` | `boolean` | - | Allow users to create options if they are not in the list of options. |
| `ariaChipRemoveLabel` | `string \| ((label: string) => string)` | `'Remove'` | Names a chip's remove button with the selected option's label: a string has `{label}` replaced by it, or gets it appended when there is no `{label}` ("Remove Angular"); a function receives the label and returns the whole name. |
| `ariaCleanerLabel` | `string` | `'Clear all selections'` | A string that provides an accessible label for the cleaner button. This label is read by screen readers to describe the action associated with the button. |
| `ariaPickerLabel` | `string` | `'Toggle options list'` | A string that provides an accessible label for the indicator button. This label is read by screen readers to describe the action associated with the button. |
| `ariaRemovedAnnouncement` | `string \| ((values: string[]) => string)` | `'removed'` | Announced after a value is removed through its chip, Backspace or the cleaner. A string follows the removed labels (`Angular removed`); a function receives them and returns the whole message. A pick in the list is not announced, since the option says it is selected. |
| `ariaSearchLabel` | `string` | `'Search'` | Accessible label for the search input (when `search` is enabled). |
| `ariaTagDeleteLabel` | `string` | `undefined` | Accessible label prefix for a chip's remove button. While it is set, it takes precedence over `ariaChipRemoveLabel`. |
| `cleaner` | `boolean` | `true` | Enables selection cleaner element. |
| `clearSearchOnSelect` | `boolean` | - | Clear current search on selecting an item. |
| `container` | `HTMLElement \| (() => HTMLElement) \| string` | `'body'` | Appends the dropdown to a specific element. You can pass an HTML element or function that returns a single element. Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert. |
| `defaultValue` | `number \| string \| (number \| string)[]` | `undefined` | The initial selection for the uncontrolled mode — matched against the option values. Ignored when `value` is set. |
| `deselectAllLabel` | `string` | `'Deselect all'` | Sets the select all button label shown once everything is selected. The button is a toggle: it shows `selectAllLabel` (and selects all) until everything is selected, then shows `deselectAllLabel` (and deselects all). |
| `deselectFilteredLabel` | `string` | `'Deselect filtered'` | Sets the deselect filtered button label (used with `selectAllMode="filtered"`). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `feedback` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable feedback. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable feedback. |
| `feedbackValid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable invalid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied two CSS pseudo-classes, `:invalid` and `:valid`. |
| `floatingLabel` | `string` | - | Renders a floating label inside the field — the component wraps its frame in `.form-floating` and the text also becomes the field's accessible name. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `globalSearch` | `boolean` | `true` | Routes typing to the search box from anywhere in the component, so a keystroke never depends on where the focus sits. Set to `false` to keep it local: the search box then filters only while it has the focus, and typing over the options list jumps to the first option that starts with what was typed, except with `search="external"`, where the list holds only the last results. Needs `search`. |
| `hideSelectAllOnSearchNoResults` | `boolean` | `true` | Hide the dropdown header with the built-in select all button when a search filter leaves no matching options. Set to `false` to keep the select all button visible even when there are no results. |
| `id` | `string` | - | Set the id attribute for the native select element. |
| `indicator` | `string` | `'checkbox'` | Sets option style. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control invalid. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | - | When set, the options list is marked busy and shows a row with a spinner and `loadingLabel` below its options while you fetch them; the options it shows can still be picked. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | `'Loading…'` | Text of the loading row below the options, announced to screen readers when the shown list starts loading or the list shows up loading. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `true` | It specifies that multiple options can be selected at once. |
| `name` | `string` | - | Name of the native select the selection is submitted under. Without it the selection is not submitted with the form. |
| `options` | `(Option \| OptionsGroup)[]` | `() => []` | List of option elements. |
| `optionsGroupsSelectable` | `boolean` | - | Makes each options group label a toggle that selects or deselects the group's visible options. With `indicator="checkbox"` (and `multiple`) the label shows a tri-state checkbox indicator (`none` / `all` / `indeterminate`) reflecting the group's selection. |
| `optionsMaxHeight` | `number\|string` | `'auto'` | Sets maxHeight of options list. |
| `pickerIcon` | `boolean` | `true` | The button that opens the options menu. Set to `false` to render no button; replace the artwork through the `pickerIcon` slot. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `'Select...'` |  |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | When it is present, it indicates that the user must choose a value before submitting the form. |
| `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange` | `boolean` | - | Empties the selection when the options bring different values, then takes the options marked `selected` (or the `defaultValue` values among them), up to `selectionLimit`; with `value` set it only requests the empty selection through the `change` event. For options that depend on another field, so outdated picks do not travel on. |
| `search` | `Search` | `true` | Renders a search box in the control. `true` filters the options as the user types; `'external'` hands the filtering to your code: the component shows the options you pass and reports what the user types through `filter-change`. |
| `searchNoResultsLabel` | `string` | `'No results found'` | Sets the label for no results when filtering. |
| `selectAll` | `boolean` | `true` | Enables select all button. |
| `selectAllLabel` | `string` | `'Select all'` | Sets the select all button label. |
| `selectAllMode` | `string` | `'all'` | Determines what the select all button operates on: all options (`'all'`) or only the currently filtered (search-visible) options (`'filtered'`). |
| `selectedLabel` | `CountLabel` | `() => defaultSelectedLabel` | Sets the counter selection label: a function `(count, total) => string`, or a string in which `{count}` and `{total}` are replaced. `total` is the number of options in the list, disabled ones, the ones inside a group and the ones the user created included, so a disabled option shows that not everything is selected, plus any selected value the options lack, so it never falls below `count`, unless `total` gives a number of its own. |
| `selectFilteredLabel` | `string` | `'Select filtered'` | Sets the select filtered button label (used with `selectAllMode="filtered"`). |
| `selectionLimit` | `number` | `null` | Sets the maximum number of options that can be selected. The select all button stays enabled and selects options up to the limit, then toggles to deselect all once the limit is reached. The `selectionLimit` event fires when a user tries to select more options than allowed. |
| `selectionType` | `string` | `'chips'` | Sets the selection style. `chips` renders the selection as chips; `tags` is a deprecated name for `chips` (since 6.0.0). |
| `show` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Control the open state of the dropdown panel. When set, the panel renders what `show` says and dismiss gestures only emit `update:show` — nothing closes until the parent flips the prop. Supports the `v-model:show` binding. |
| `size` | `string` | `undefined` | Size the component small or large. |
| `teleport` | `boolean` | `false` | Generates dropdown menu using Teleport: into the open `<dialog>` the field sits in, otherwise into `body`. |
| `text` | `string` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `total` | `number` | - | Sets `{total}` of `selectedLabel`. Leave it out to count the options in the list; with external search give the number of records your data source holds, which the component cannot see. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control valid. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid`. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. |
| `value` | `number \| string \| (number \| string)[]` | `undefined` | The controlled selection — matched against the option values. Pair it with the `change` event; for the uncontrolled mode use `defaultValue` instead. |
| `virtualScroller` | `boolean` | - | Enable virtual scroller for the options list. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Toggle the visibility of multi select dropdown. |
| `visibleItems` | `number` | `10` | Amount of visible items when virtualScroller is set to `true`. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `change` | Execute a function when the user or the component changes the selection: a pick, a native reset of the form, or `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange`. A selection you give through `value`, `defaultValue` or options marked `selected` does not fire it, unless `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange` replaced the selection with it. With `value` set it is a request. |
| `filterChange` | Execute a function when the filter value changed. |
| `hide` | The callback is fired when the dropdown requests to be hidden. |
| `selectionLimit` | Execute a function when the user tries to select more options than allowed by `selectionLimit`. |
| `show` | The callback is fired when the dropdown requests to be shown. |
| `update:show` | Emit the requested open state to support the `v-model:show` binding — a dismiss gesture (Escape, outside click) or any internal toggle. |
| `update:validationState` | Emitted with `undefined` when the user changes the selection, or the form is reset, while `validationState` (or `invalid`/`valid`) is set, to support the `v-model:validation-state` binding. A given state is a verdict on the selection it was given for. |

# Vue Multi Select Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Multi Select component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

### CSS variables

The field is a [`.form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/form-control-group/styling/#css-variables), so its frame, the cleaner and the toggle read the `--cui-control-*` and `--cui-control-group-*` tokens. `class` and `style` on `<CMultiSelect>` land on that frame, the `.multi-select` element, so the tokens can be set on a single field. The selected chips add two of their own:

```scss
$multi-select-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-multi-select-selection-chips-gap: .25rem,
    --cui-multi-select-selection-chips-padding-y: .25rem,
  ),
  $multi-select-tokens
);
```

The options panel is the shared combobox surface, which only sizes itself:

```scss
$combobox-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-combobox-popup-min-width: 100%,
  ),
  $combobox-tokens
);
```

Everything inside it — options, section labels, checkbox indicators and the select all button — is a [List box](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/list-box/) and takes its `--cui-list-box-*` variables. `.list-box` declares them itself, so a value set on `.combobox-popup` or on `:root` does not reach it: set them with a rule on `.combobox-popup .list-box`, which covers the panels of Combobox, Autocomplete and Multi Select alike.

#### How to use CSS variables

```vue
<template>
  <CMultiSelect :style="vars">...</CMultiSelect>
</template>

<script setup>
const vars = {
  '--cui-control-bg': '#f8f9fa',
  '--cui-multi-select-selection-chips-gap': '.5rem',
}
</script>
```

# Vue Multi Select Component Accessibility

> Detailed overview of the accessibility features implemented in CoreUI Vue Multi Select, ensuring compliance with WAI-ARIA guidelines.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Accessibility

The Vue Multi Select component is designed with accessibility in mind, implementing WAI-ARIA standards to ensure compatibility with screen readers and assistive technologies.

### ARIA Attributes

The component automatically includes the following ARIA attributes:

- **`role="combobox"`** on the main container to identify it as a combobox control
- **`aria-haspopup="dialog"`** indicates that the control opens a dialog holding the list of options
- **`aria-expanded`** reflects the current state of the dropdown (true when open, false when closed)
- **`aria-controls`** points the control at the dropdown dialog and the search input at the listbox while the dropdown is open
- **`role="listbox"`** on the list of options inside the dropdown
- **`aria-labelledby`** names the control and the dropdown after the label: `label`, `floatingLabel`, or a `<label>` pointing at the component's `id`, read when the component mounts or its `id` changes; an `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label` given to the component takes precedence. A `<label>` wrapping the component is left out, because its text would take in the control's own content and selection. The search box keeps a name of its own, `ariaSearchLabel`
- **`aria-required`** on the focused control, the search box when `search` is on, when `required` is set or an `aria-required` is given to the component
- **`aria-hidden="true"`** on the native `<select>` that carries the value into the form, so assistive technology meets only the combobox
- **Focus that reaches the native `<select>`**, from the browser's validation or from the label, goes on to the control (the search box when `search` is on), which carries `aria-invalid` and the `feedback-invalid` description. A change of selection fires `input` and `change` on the select, as a native list does
- **`aria-multiselectable`** indicates whether multiple selections are allowed
- **`role="option"`** on each selectable option
- **`aria-selected`** on options to indicate their selection state

### Keyboard Navigation

The component supports full keyboard navigation:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Navigate to/from the component |
| <kbd>Enter/Space</kbd> | Open dropdown or select focused option |
| <kbd>Arrow Up/Down</kbd> | Navigate through options |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> | Focus the first option |
| <kbd>End</kbd> | Focus the last option |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close the dropdown |
| <kbd>Backspace/Delete</kbd> | In the empty search box, focus the last chip; on a chip, remove it and move the focus to the next chip, else the previous one, else the search box, or the field when there is none. Entering the chips closes an open panel. A single select and the `counter` and `text` selections remove the last selected item at once |
| <kbd>Arrow Left/Arrow Right</kbd> | From the start of the search box, focus the last chip; between the chips, move the focus; past the last chip, return to the search box (mirrored in right-to-left) |

### Screen Reader Support

- All interactive elements have appropriate accessible names
- Selection changes are announced to screen readers
- Loading states are properly communicated
- Option groups are properly labeled and associated

### Customizable Labels

You can customize the accessible labels for better user experience:

```vue
<CMultiSelect
  :options="options"
  aria-cleaner-label="Remove all selected items"
  aria-picker-label="Open options menu"
/>
```

### Best Practices

- Always provide a meaningful `label` prop for the component
- Use descriptive option labels that make sense when read by screen readers
- Consider the `placeholder` text as it may be announced by some screen readers
- Test with actual screen readers to ensure the experience meets your users' needs

# Vue Number Input Component

> A Vue number field with accessible increment and decrement buttons, with min, max and step handled by the browser.

## Example

_Added in 5.22.0._

`` is a number field with a stepper you can actually hit. The browser's own spinner is tiny, appears only on hover in some engines and does not exist at all on iOS, so the component replaces it with two buttons sized like every other adornment in a form control group. You write neither the frame, the buttons nor their icons.

The `value` attribute seeds the field like on a native input; bind `v-model` for a controlled value.

```html
<template>
  <CNumberInput aria-label="Quantity" value="3" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CNumberInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CFormLabel for="numberInputField">Quantity</CFormLabel>
    <CNumberInput id="numberInputField" :model-value="3" />
    <CFormText>Up to ten items per order.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CFormLabel, CFormText } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CNumberInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Min, max and step

`min`, `max` and `step` are the native attributes — the component does not reimplement them, it calls the browser's own stepping. **A button that cannot move the value any further is disabled**, so the bound is visible rather than just unresponsive.

When the field is empty, a button steps from zero, and the result stays within `min` and `max` and on the `step` grid.

```html
<template>
  <CForm>
    <div class="mb-4">
      <CNumberInput label="Quantity" max="10" min="0" value="10" />
    </div>
    <div>
      <CNumberInput label="Amount" step="0.5" value="2" />
    </div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CForm, CNumberInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Sizing

Use the `size` prop to control the height and padding of the field. Sizing belongs to the frame rather than to the control inside it, so the component puts the class on the group it builds.

```html
<template>
  <CForm>
    <div class="mb-4">
      <CNumberInput aria-label="Quantity" size="sm" value="3" />
    </div>
    <div>
      <CNumberInput aria-label="Quantity" size="lg" value="3" />
    </div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CForm, CNumberInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Controlled value

Bind `v-model` to own the value yourself. Stepping reports through the same `input` and `change` events typing does, so there is one path to handle.

```html
<template>
  <CNumberInput v-model="value" label="Quantity" />
  <div class="mt-3 fg-2">Value: {{ value === '' ? '—' : value }}</div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CNumberInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const value = ref('3')
</script>
```

## Disabled and read-only

```html
<template>
  <CForm>
    <div class="mb-4">
      <CNumberInput disabled label="Disabled" value="3" />
    </div>
    <div>
      <CNumberInput label="Read-only" readonly value="3" />
    </div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CForm, CNumberInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

Both buttons are disabled while the field is disabled or read-only.

## Holding a button

Holding a button repeats the step after a short delay, and releasing it does not add a step. Set `:repeat="false"` to require a click per step.

## Floating labels

Set `floatingLabel` and the component renders the label itself — no wrapper markup needed — and the text also becomes the field's accessible name; the stepper buttons ride along with the field.

```html
<template>
  <CNumberInput id="floatingNumberInput" floating-label="Quantity" :value="42" />
</template>
```

Set `floatingLabelAlways` to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating).

## Accessibility

The buttons carry labels (`Increase` / `Decrease` by default, both configurable through `ariaIncrementLabel` and `ariaDecrementLabel`) but are **kept out of the tab order**: a number field already steps with <kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd>, so putting them in would add two tab stops per field for something the keyboard already reaches. A mouse press on a button, enabled or not, puts the focus in the field rather than on the button, so typing and the arrow keys act on the field you just stepped. Give the field a `label` or an `aria-label` as you would any other control.

> **Decimal separators.** `` accepts the dot as the decimal separator regardless of locale, and a value the browser rejects is reported as an empty string — the field cannot tell you what was typed. If you need locale-aware separators, currency or grouping, that is a formatted-input problem rather than a stepper one, and `type="number"` is the wrong base for it.

## API

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

- [&lt;CNumberInput /&gt;](./api/#cnumberinput)


---

# Vue Number Input Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Number Input component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CNumberInput

```jsx
import { CNumberInput } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaDecrementLabel` | `string` | `'Decrease'` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that decreases the value. |
| `ariaIncrementLabel` | `string` | `'Increase'` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that increases the value. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `feedback` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable feedback to your users with HTML5 form validation feedback. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable invalid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied `validationState="invalid"`. |
| `feedbackValid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable valid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied `validationState="valid"`. |
| `floatingClassName` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the floating label wrapper. |
| `floatingLabel` | `string` | - | Wrap the control in a floating label. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `id` | `string` | - | The id attribute of the native input, also used by the label. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `modelValue` | `number \| string` | `undefined` | The value of the component. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the readonly state for the component. |
| `repeat` | `boolean` | `true` | Repeats the step while a button is held. Set to `false` to require a click per step. |
| `size` | `string` | `undefined` | Sizes the control, the way `.form-control-sm` and `.form-control-lg` size a form control. |
| `text` | `string` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the value emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `change` | Event occurs when the element loses focus, after the content has been changed. |
| `input` | Event occurs immediately after the value of a component has changed. |
| `update:modelValue` | Emit the new value whenever there’s an input or change event. |
| `update:validationState` | Event occurs with `undefined` when the user changes the value, or the form is reset, while `validationState` is set. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it and let the browser's own validation show again. |

# Vue Number Input Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Number Input component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

The frame, the buttons and their sizing are the group's, and read the shared `--cui-control-*` properties. Set them on the `.form-control-group` the component renders around the input: `class` on `<CNumberInput>` lands there, but `style` lands on the `<input>` and does not reach the frame:

```scss
$form-control-group-tokens: () !default;
$form-control-group-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-control-group-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-control-group-icon-size: 1rem,
    --cui-control-group-icon-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-text-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-action-size: 1.5rem,
    --cui-control-group-action-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-action-hover-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-control-group-action-bg: transparent,
    --cui-control-group-action-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-control-group-action-border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-sm-border-radius),
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-property: #{var(--cui-btn-input-action-transition-property), transform},
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-duration: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-duration),
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-timing: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-timing),
    --cui-control-group-disabled-opacity: var(--cui-btn-input-disabled-opacity),
  ),
  $form-control-group-tokens
);
```

### Sass maps

The group takes its own icon and action sizes per size class, and the map merges with your overrides — add a key to define a size, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$form-control-group-sizes: defaults(
  (
    "sm": (icon-size: .875rem, action-size: 1.25rem),
    "lg": (icon-size: 1.25rem, action-size: 1.75rem),
  ),
  $form-control-group-sizes
);
```

# Vue One-Time Password (OTP) Input Component

> Create secure and user-friendly Vue.js one-time password input fields with automatic navigation, paste support, validation, and customizable options for modern authentication flows.

## Overview

The Vue One-Time Password (OTP) Component is a powerful, user-friendly solution for implementing secure authentication flows in your Vue.js applications. Whether you're building two-factor authentication, email verification, or SMS confirmation systems, this OTP component provides an intuitive interface with advanced features like auto-navigation between fields, intelligent paste handling, and comprehensive keyboard support.

Key features of this Vue OTP component include:
- Auto-navigation between input fields
- Smart paste support with auto-fill
- Number and text input validation
- Linear and non-linear input modes
- Auto-submit functionality
- Keyboard navigation with RTL support
- Full accessibility compliance
- Bootstrap-based styling with size variants

## Basic Example

A straightforward demonstration of how to implement a basic OTP input field with 6 digits.

```html
<template>
  <CForm>
    <div class="mb-4">
      <COneTimePassword id="basicOTP" v-model="value" label="Enter OTP Code" name="otp">
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
      </COneTimePassword>
    </div>
    <div v-if="value" class="fg-2 small">Current value: {{ value }}</div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CForm } from '@coreui/vue'
import { COneTimePassword, COneTimePasswordInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const value = ref('')
</script>
```

The basic implementation requires wrapping `COneTimePasswordInput` components within a `COneTimePassword` container. Each input field automatically handles single character input and navigation.

## Pre-filled values

Pass `value` one-way to seed the code — the input manages it from there — or bind `v-model` to keep it in step with your state:

```html
<template>
  <CForm>
    <div class="mb-4">
      <COneTimePassword
        id="prefilledOTPModel"
        v-model="value"
        label="OTP with pre-filled value (v-model)"
        name="otp1"
      >
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
      </COneTimePassword>
    </div>
    <div class="mb-4">
      <COneTimePassword
        id="prefilledOTPValue"
        label="OTP with pre-filled value (value prop)"
        name="otp2"
        :value="valueWithProp"
        @change="handleChange"
      >
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
      </COneTimePassword>
    </div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CForm } from '@coreui/vue'
import { COneTimePassword, COneTimePasswordInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const value = ref('123456')
const valueWithProp = ref('654321')

const handleChange = (newValue) => {
  valueWithProp.value = newValue
}
</script>
```

## Usage with v-model

Bind `v-model` and the code follows your state — typing only emits `@update:modelValue` (and `@change` with the same code), so the binding feeds it back, and `@complete` fires once every slot is filled. Passed one-way, `model-value` or `value` seeds the code, and the input manages it from there. A native reset of the form puts back the code the input started with, emitting `change` only when that changes the code; a bound input asks for its first code through `update:modelValue` and shows yours until you take it.

```vue
<COneTimePassword v-model="code">
```

## Auto-submit

Automatically submit the form when all OTP fields are completed:

```html
<template>
  <form @submit.prevent="handleSubmit">
    <COneTimePassword
      v-model="otpValue"
      label="Auto-submit OTP (fill all 6 digits)"
      :auto-submit="true"
      @complete="onComplete"
    >
      <COneTimePasswordInput />
      <COneTimePasswordInput />
      <COneTimePasswordInput />
      <COneTimePasswordInput />
      <COneTimePasswordInput />
      <COneTimePasswordInput />
    </COneTimePassword>
    <div class="mt-3">
      <small v-if="submitted" class="fg-success">Form submitted with code: {{ otpValue }}</small>
      <small v-else class="fg-2">Fill all fields to auto-submit</small>
    </div>
  </form>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { COneTimePassword, COneTimePasswordInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const otpValue = ref('')
const submitted = ref(false)

const onComplete = (value) => {
  console.log('OTP completed:', value)
}

const handleSubmit = (event) => {
  event.preventDefault()
  submitted.value = true
  setTimeout(() => {
    submitted.value = false
  }, 3000)
}
</script>
```

The `auto-submit` prop triggers form submission when all fields are filled. The `@complete` event fires when the OTP is fully entered.

## Validation

The code is validated as one value, kept in an input laid invisibly over the group. With `required` an empty or incomplete code blocks the submit, and an incomplete code blocks it even when the field is not required; the browser puts focus on the first empty slot and shows its own message over the group. The state shows on the group as the `.is-*` class, and while it is `'invalid'` every slot carries `aria-invalid="true"` and is described by the message after the group: the `feedback-invalid` text, the `feedback` text while you give a state, or an `.invalid-feedback` you render after the field yourself. The hidden input holds the new code by the time `change` and `complete` are emitted, and sends `input` and `change` once the code has rendered, also when your code changes it through `v-model` or `value`.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row g-4" novalidate validate>
    <div class="col-md-6">
      <COneTimePassword
        feedback-invalid="Enter the six digits we sent you."
        label="Verification code"
        name="code"
        required
      >
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
      </COneTimePassword>
    </div>
    <div class="col-md-6">
      <COneTimePassword
        v-model:validation-state="backupCodeState"
        feedback="This backup code has already been used."
        label="Backup code"
        name="backupCode"
        value="482913"
      >
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
      </COneTimePassword>
    </div>
    <div class="col-12">
      <CButton color="primary" type="submit">Verify</CButton>
    </div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CForm } from '@coreui/vue'
import { COneTimePassword, COneTimePasswordInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const backupCodeState = ref('invalid')
</script>
```

The state comes from three places, in this order:

- `validationState`: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`; `invalid` and `valid` still work as aliases. While it is set, the component draws it instead of what the browser reports. While it is `'invalid'`, the code blocks the submit with the text of the linked message, or `Invalid value.` when there is none, unless the component is `disabled`.
- A validation that reports the code invalid: a submit, `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()`, which [`CForm`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/validation/) and the stepper call as well. From then on the group and the slots show it invalid whenever the code is invalid, until the form is reset, and the message after the group shows.
- In a form with `validate`, the `:user-invalid` state of the hidden input, and with `validate="valid"` also its `:user-valid` state.

A state you give is a verdict on the code it was given for. When the user types, deletes, pastes or autofills a different code, or the form is reset, the component emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop the state, as the second field above does. A change your code makes through `v-model` or `value` keeps it, and so does a keystroke that leaves the code as it is. A reset emits once it has run, so a state you set from a `reset` listener on the form gets the same event, and your handler decides whether to drop it. A native reset of the form puts back the code given by `value`, and leaves a bound `v-model` to you. An `aria-invalid` attribute on the component or on a slot is not read; set the state with `validation-state`.

## Accessibility

The one-time password input component is designed with accessibility in mind and follows WCAG guidelines for form inputs.

- **ARIA Labels**: Each input field automatically receives descriptive `aria-label` attributes
- **Role Attribute**: The container has `role="group"` to indicate related form controls, named by `label`
- **Label click**: clicking the label that names the group moves focus to the first empty slot, as clicking the label of an input focuses it
- **Required**: with `required`, every slot carries `aria-required="true"`, since the value input that holds `required` is hidden from assistive technologies
- **Keyboard Navigation**: Full keyboard support with arrow keys, tab, and backspace
- **Screen Reader Support**: Clear announcements when values change; while the code is reported invalid, every slot carries `aria-invalid="true"` and the error message
- **Focus Management**: Automatic focus handling for seamless navigation
- **Autofill**: only the first field advertises `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so SMS autofill and password managers target a single field; a code delivered that way is spread across the slots automatically, exactly like a paste

### Customizing accessibility

You can customize the aria-label generation function to provide more specific descriptions:

```vue
<COneTimePassword
  :aria-label="(index, total) => `Enter digit ${index + 1} of your ${total}-digit verification code`"
/>
```

### Keyboard support

The one-time password input component provides comprehensive keyboard navigation support:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> | Move focus to next input field |
| <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> | Move focus to previous input field |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd> | Delete current character and move to previous field (if empty) |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move to next focusable element (respects linear mode) |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move to previous focusable element |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> | Paste clipboard content and auto-fill fields |

# Vue One-Time Password Input Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue One-Time Password Input component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## COneTimePassword

```jsx
import { COneTimePassword } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `func` | `(index: number, total: number) => `Digit ${index + 1} of ${total}`` | Function to generate aria-label for each input field. Receives current index (0-based) and total number of inputs. |
| `autoSubmit` | `boolean` | `false` | Automatically submit the form when all one time password fields are filled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable all one time password (OTP) input fields. |
| `feedback` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable feedback. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable feedback. |
| `feedbackValid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable invalid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied two CSS pseudo-classes, `:invalid` and `:valid`. |
| `floatingClassName` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the floating label wrapper. |
| `floatingLabel` | `string` | - | Provide a floating label for the component — the text rests inside the field and floats once it has focus or a value. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `id` | `string` | - | ID attribute for the value input. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control invalid. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `linear` | `boolean` | `true` | Enforce sequential input (users must fill fields in order). |
| `masked` | `boolean` | `false` | Show input as password (masked characters). |
| `modelValue` | `string\|number` | - | The default name for a value passed using v-model. |
| `name` | `string` | - | Name of the value input the code is submitted under. Without it the code is not submitted with the form. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | - | Placeholder text for input fields. Single character applies to all fields, longer strings apply character-by-character. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Makes the code required: an empty or incomplete code blocks the submit. |
| `size` | `string` | - | Sets the visual size of the Vue.js one time password (OTP) input. Use 'sm' for small or 'lg' for large input fields. |
| `text` | `string` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `type` | `string` | `'number'` | Input validation type: 'number' for digits only, or 'text' for free text. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control valid. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class on the group; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` on every slot and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the code emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`. |
| `value` | `string\|number` | - | The current value of the one time password input. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | Callback triggered when the Vue.js one time password (OTP) value changes. |
| `change` | Callback triggered when the Vue.js one time password (OTP) value changes. |
| `complete` | Callback triggered when all Vue.js one time password (OTP) fields are filled. |
| `update:validationState` | Event occurs with `undefined` when the user changes the code, or the form is reset, while `validationState` (or `invalid`/`valid`) is set. A given state is a verdict on the code it was given for; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it and let the browser's own validation show again. |

# Vue Password Input Component

> A fully featured Vue password input component with Bootstrap styling. Includes show/hide visibility toggle, validation states, sizing, and full accessibility support.

## Example

The `` is a fully customizable **Vue password input field** designed for security-focused forms. It includes a **toggle to show or hide password visibility**, Bootstrap-based **sizing options**, and full support for `v-model`, validation, `readonly`, and `disabled` states. Ideal for login forms, registration pages, and secure input screens in Vue 3 apps.

```html
<template>
  <CForm>
    <div class="mb-4">
      <CPasswordInput label="Password" placeholder="Enter your password" />
    </div>
    <div class="mb-4">
      <CPasswordInput
        label="Password with value"
        placeholder="Enter your password"
        value="Top secret"
      />
    </div>
    <div>
      <CPasswordInput
        v-model="password"
        label="Password with v-model value"
        placeholder="Enter your password"
      />
    </div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CForm } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CPasswordInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
import { ref } from 'vue'
const password = ref('Top secret')
</script>
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CFormLabel for="passwordInputField">Password</CFormLabel>
    <CPasswordInput id="passwordInputField" placeholder="Enter your password" />
    <CFormText>At least 12 characters.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CFormLabel, CFormText } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CPasswordInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Floating labels

Set `floatingLabel` and the component renders the label itself — no wrapper markup needed — and the text also becomes the field's accessible name; the toggle button rides along with the field, and the placeholder stays hidden until the label floats.

```html
<template>
  <CPasswordInput id="floatingPasswordInput" floating-label="Password" />
</template>
```

Set `floatingLabelAlways` to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the placeholder showing.

## Sizing

Use the `size` prop to adjust the height and padding of the password input. Supports Bootstrap’s sizing classes:

* `size="sm"` – small input
* `size="lg"` – large input

```html
<template>
  <CPasswordInput size="lg" placeholder="Large password input" aria-label="Large input" />
  <CPasswordInput placeholder="Default password input" aria-label="Default input" />
  <CPasswordInput size="sm" placeholder="Small password input" aria-label="Small input" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CPasswordInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Disabled

To disable editing, add the `disabled` prop. The field becomes inactive and is visually dimmed. The visibility toggle is disabled with it and leaves the tab order, so it can't change what a disabled field shows: a password revealed before stays visible, and can be hidden once the field is enabled again.

```html
<template>
  <CPasswordInput placeholder="Disabled input" aria-label="Disabled input example" disabled />
  <CPasswordInput
    placeholder="Disabled readonly input"
    aria-label="Disabled readonly input example"
    disabled
    read-only
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CPasswordInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Readonly

Use the `readOnly` prop to make the password field non-editable, while still allowing users to select and copy the value.

```html
<template>
  <CPasswordInput
    placeholder="Readonly input"
    aria-label="Readonly input example"
    value="You can copy this"
    read-only
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CPasswordInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Usage with v-model

_Added in 6.0.0._

Bind `v-model:show-password` and the visibility toggle keeps the value in step with your state — the toggle button only emits `@update:show-password`, so the binding feeds the change back. Passed one-way, `show-password` seeds the toggle, and the input manages it from there.

```vue
<CPasswordInput v-model:show-password="visible" label="Password" />
<CPasswordInput show-password label="Password, revealed on mount" />
```

## Icons

The component renders the toggle icon and swaps it when the password becomes visible. Replace either state's artwork with the `showIcon` and `hideIcon` slots:

```vue
<CPasswordInput label="Password">
  <template #showIcon><CIcon icon="cilLowVision" /></template>
  <template #hideIcon><CIcon icon="cilEye" /></template>
</CPasswordInput>
```

# Vue Password Input Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Password Input component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CPasswordInput

```jsx
import { CPasswordInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaToggleLabel` | `string` | `'Toggle password visibility'` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) for the toggle password visibility button. This improves accessibility for screen readers and should describe the action, e.g. `"Show password"` or `"Hide password"`. |
| `delay` | `boolean\|number` | `false` | Delay emitting `change` and `update:modelValue` events. `true` = 500ms delay, or specify custom delay in ms. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Disables the password input field. When `true`, the user cannot interact with the field, and the visibility toggle is disabled with it. |
| `feedback` | `string` | - | General feedback text shown below the input. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `string` | - | Feedback text shown when input is invalid. |
| `feedbackValid` | `string` | - | Feedback text shown when input is valid. |
| `floatingClassName` | `string` | - | Class for the floating label wrapper. |
| `floatingLabel` | `string` | - | Floating label text. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `id` | `string` | - | ID of the input element. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Marks the input as invalid. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Main label for the input. |
| `modelValue` | `string` | - | The current value of the password input, used with v-model. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | - | Makes the input read-only, allowing text selection only. |
| `showPassword` | `boolean` | `undefined` | The visibility of the password — `true` renders the input as type `"text"` instead of `"password"`. Bind it with `v-model:show-password` to hand control to the parent; passed one-way it seeds the starting state and the input keeps managing itself. |
| `size` | `String as () => 'sm' \| 'lg' \| undefined` | `undefined` | Sets the visual size of the input. Accepts `'sm'`, `'lg'`, or undefined. |
| `text` | `string` | - | Helper or hint text displayed below the input. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Enables tooltip-style validation feedback messages. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Marks the input as valid. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the value emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`. |
| `value` | `string` | - | Alternative to `modelValue`, mostly for manual `:value` binding. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `change` |  |
| `update:modelValue` |  |
| `update:showPassword` | Callback fired when the visibility toggle requests a new state, receiving the requested visibility. |
| `update:validationState` | Event occurs with `undefined` when the user changes the value, or the form is reset, while `validationState` (or the deprecated `invalid`) is set. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it and let the browser's own validation show again. |

# Vue Password Input Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Password Input component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

The frame — padding, colours, border and the size of the toggle button, including the icon inside it — is the group's, and it reads the shared `--cui-control-*` properties. Set them on the `.form-control-group` the component renders around the input to restyle one field: `class` on `<CPasswordInput>` lands there, but `style` lands on the `<input>` and does not reach the frame. The group declares them itself, so a value on `:root` stops there — to restyle every field at once, change the shared [`--cui-btn-input-*` frame](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/overview/#css-variables). The focus ring is the library's own, coloured by `--cui-focus-ring-color` or the theme:

```scss
$form-control-group-tokens: () !default;
$form-control-group-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-control-group-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-control-group-icon-size: 1rem,
    --cui-control-group-icon-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-text-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-action-size: 1.5rem,
    --cui-control-group-action-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-action-hover-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-control-group-action-bg: transparent,
    --cui-control-group-action-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-control-group-action-border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-sm-border-radius),
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-property: #{var(--cui-btn-input-action-transition-property), transform},
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-duration: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-duration),
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-timing: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-timing),
    --cui-control-group-disabled-opacity: var(--cui-btn-input-disabled-opacity),
  ),
  $form-control-group-tokens
);
```

# Vue Password Strength Component

> Show how strong a password is as it is typed — a segmented meter, a label, and a pluggable scorer that can be asynchronous so a real strength estimator or a breach check can drive it.

## Example

_Added in 6.0.0._

Pass the password to `<CPasswordStrength>` and it renders the meter, the label and the feedback itself — pair it with [Password Input](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/password-input/), which owns the field's frame and visibility toggle.

```html
<template>
  <CFormLabel for="strengthDemo">Password</CFormLabel>
  <CPasswordInput
    id="strengthDemo"
    v-model="password"
    class="mb-3"
    placeholder="Type a password…"
  />
  <CPasswordStrength :value="password" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CFormLabel } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CPasswordInput, CPasswordStrength } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const password = ref('')
</script>
```

## How it works

- **The field stays yours.** The meter never wraps, moves or re-types the input — it just receives the password through the `value` property, so it works with any field you control.
- **The meter is built for you.** It renders the segments, the label, and the places a scorer's warning and suggestions go. Segments are one fewer than there are levels, so the top level fills the bar.
- **The score is a number from 0 to 4.** Level `0` is the worst. That is the same scale [zxcvbn](#zxcvbn) returns, so a real estimator drops in without a conversion step.
- **The meter is hidden from assistive technology** (`aria-hidden`) because it only restates the label. The label and its feedback sit in a polite live region, so a screen reader hears the verdict once, not twice.

## What the built-in scorer is worth

> **The built-in scorer is a UX hint, not a security control.** It counts length and character classes — lowercase, uppercase, digits, symbols. That measures *composition*, not how guessable a password actually is. `P@ssw0rd1` clears every rule it checks and is among the first passwords any attacker tries.
> 
> [NIST SP 800-63B](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html) recommends **against** composition rules of exactly this kind, and **for** checking the password against lists of known-breached secrets. Do that on the server, where it cannot be skipped. Treat this meter as encouragement while typing, and never as the thing that decides whether a password is allowed.

The default scorer stays small and rule-based on purpose: a real estimator ships a dictionary far larger than this entire library. Plug one in with `scorer`.

## Custom scorer

`scorer` replaces the built-in scoring completely. It receives the password and the [user inputs](#user-inputs), and returns either a bare number or an object:

```js
type StrengthResult = number | { score: number, warning?: string, suggestions?: string[] }
```

Return a number when that is all you have — the simple case stays simple:

```html
<template>
  <CPasswordInput v-model="password" class="mb-3" placeholder="Length alone decides…" />
  <CPasswordStrength
    :value="password"
    :scorer="(value) => Math.min(4, Math.floor(value.length / 4))"
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CPasswordInput, CPasswordStrength } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const password = ref('')
</script>
```

Return an object to say *why*. The `warning` and `suggestions` are rendered below the label, and both are inserted as text — markup in them is never parsed. A score outside the range of `levels` is clamped, and a scorer that throws clears the meter rather than leaving a stale verdict on screen.

### Asynchronous scorers

`scorer` may return a promise. This is what makes a serious estimator possible: zxcvbn loads its language packs asynchronously, and a breach check is a network call. Three things the component handles so you do not have to:

- **Debounce.** Input is coalesced (`debounce`, 200 ms by default) so typing a password does not fire a request per keystroke.
- **Out-of-order results.** Every evaluation takes a sequence token. If a slow answer for an old password arrives after a newer one has already resolved, it is discarded. Without this, pausing mid-word and typing on can leave the meter showing the verdict for a prefix.
- **A pending state.** While a promise is outstanding the root gets `.password-strength-busy` and the label shows `busyLabel`. A synchronous scorer never gets this state, so it cannot flicker.

A rejected promise clears the meter, for the same reason a throw does.

> **A scorer that calls the network sends the password off the page.** Anything you `fetch` from inside `scorer` receives the secret the user is in the middle of typing — before they have submitted anything, and on every debounce tick.
> 
> If you check against a breach corpus, use a protocol built for it: the [Pwned Passwords range API](https://haveibeenpwned.com/API/v3#PwnedPasswords) takes the first five characters of the password's SHA-1 hash and returns every matching suffix, so the password itself never leaves the browser. Sending the raw password to a third party is a credential disclosure, whatever the endpoint promises.

### zxcvbn

[zxcvbn](https://github.com/dropbox/zxcvbn) and its maintained successor [zxcvbn-ts](https://github.com/zxcvbn-ts/zxcvbn) estimate how many guesses a password would survive, using dictionaries of common passwords, names, words and keyboard patterns. That is a different question from "does it have a capital letter", and a much more useful one.

We do not ship an adapter — the shapes already line up. zxcvbn returns `{ score, feedback: { warning, suggestions } }`, and `score` is 0–4 on the same scale this component uses. The language packs are large — load them on demand and let the promise support do the waiting:

```vue
<template>
  <CPasswordStrength :value="password" :scorer="scorer" />
</template>

<script setup>
let zxcvbnReady = null

const loadZxcvbn = () => {
  zxcvbnReady ||= Promise.all([
    import('@zxcvbn-ts/core'),
    import('@zxcvbn-ts/language-common'),
    import('@zxcvbn-ts/language-en'),
  ]).then(([core, common, en]) => {
    core.zxcvbnOptions.setOptions({
      dictionary: { ...common.dictionary, ...en.dictionary },
      graphs: common.adjacencyGraphs,
      translations: en.translations,
    })

    return core.zxcvbn
  })

  return zxcvbnReady
}

const scorer = async (password, userInputs) => {
  const zxcvbn = await loadZxcvbn()
  const { score, feedback } = zxcvbn(password, userInputs)

  return { score, warning: feedback.warning, suggestions: feedback.suggestions }
}
</script>
```

Both run entirely in the browser, so neither sends the password anywhere.

## User inputs

A password containing the user's own email, username or site name is weak no matter how it is composed, and no amount of character-class counting notices that. `userInputs` is the list to penalize against.

Pass a function when the values live in fields the user is still filling in — it is called on every evaluation, so it always sees current values. Pass an array when they are fixed.

```html
<template>
  <CFormInput v-model="email" class="mb-3" aria-label="Email" />
  <CPasswordInput v-model="password" class="mb-3" placeholder="Try using the email above…" />
  <CPasswordStrength :value="password" :user-inputs="() => [email]" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CPasswordInput, CPasswordStrength } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const email = ref('ada@example.com')
const password = ref('')
</script>
```

The built-in scorer returns `0` when the password contains any of these values (three characters or more, case-insensitive). A custom scorer receives the same list as its second argument and decides for itself — zxcvbn takes it directly.

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place. The meter is a child of the field like any other, so it picks up the same gap.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CFormLabel for="strengthField">Password</CFormLabel>
    <CPasswordInput id="strengthField" v-model="password" placeholder="Type a password…" />
    <CPasswordStrength :value="password" />
    <CFormText>At least 12 characters.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CFormField, CFormLabel, CFormText } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CPasswordInput, CPasswordStrength } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const password = ref('')
</script>
```

## Accessibility

- The segmented bar is `aria-hidden`, because it carries no information the label does not.
- The label, warning and suggestions share one `role="status"` region with `aria-live="polite"`, so the verdict is announced without interrupting, and as a single message rather than three.
- Debouncing keeps that region from being updated on every keystroke, which is what makes a live region usable here at all.
- The strength label is never the only signal — it is text, not colour alone.

## API

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

- [&lt;CPasswordStrength /&gt;](./api/#cpasswordstrength)

# Vue Password Strength Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Password Strength component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CPasswordStrength

```jsx
import { CPasswordStrength } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `busyLabel` | `string` | `'Checking…'` | Text announced while an asynchronous scorer is pending. |
| `debounce` | `number` | `200` | Milliseconds to wait after the last change before evaluating. |
| `levels` | `string[]` | `() => ['Very weak', 'Weak', 'Fair', 'Good', 'Strong']` | Labels for the strength levels, weakest first. The meter renders one segment fewer than there are levels, and a score above the last label is clamped to it. |
| `minLength` | `number` | `8` | Minimum length the built-in scorer awards points for. |
| `scorer` | `(password: string, userInputs: string[]) => StrengthResult \| Promise<StrengthResult>` | `undefined` | Custom scorer - return a score (or `{ score, warning, suggestions }`), or a promise resolving to one. |
| `thresholds` | `number[]` | `() => [2, 4, 6]` | Point thresholds between the built-in scorer's levels. A threshold left out keeps its default. |
| `userInputs` | `string[] \| (() => string[])` | `() => []` | Words the password must not contain - the user's name, e-mail, the site name. Pass a function to read them lazily. |
| `value` | `string` | `''` | The password to evaluate. |
| `weights` | `Record<string, number>` | `() => ({ minLength: 1, extraLength: 1, longPassword: 1, lowercase: 1, uppercase: 1, numbers: 1, special: 1, multipleSpecial: 1, })` | Points the built-in scorer awards per fulfilled rule. A rule left out keeps its default, so the object is a set of overrides rather than a replacement. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `strength-change` | Callback fired when the computed score changes. The password is masked. |

# Vue Password Strength Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Password Strength component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

Vue Password Strength supports CSS variables for easy customization. These variables are set via Sass but allow direct overrides in your stylesheets or inline styles.

```scss
$password-strength-tokens: () !default;
$password-strength-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-password-strength-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-password-strength-meter-gap: .25rem,
    --cui-password-strength-segment-height: .25rem,
    --cui-password-strength-segment-bg: var(--cui-bg-2),
    --cui-password-strength-segment-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-pill),
    --cui-password-strength-font-size: var(--cui-font-size-sm),
    --cui-password-strength-text-font-weight: 600,
    --cui-password-strength-warning-color: var(--cui-fg-2),
    --cui-password-strength-suggestions-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-password-strength-busy-opacity: .65,
    --cui-password-strength-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
  ),
  $password-strength-tokens
);
```

### Sass maps

Each level pairs a colour with the score it represents; add or override an entry to retint a level:

```scss
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$password-strength-levels: defaults(
  (
    "0": var(--cui-danger-base),
    "1": var(--cui-danger-base),
    "2": var(--cui-warning-base),
    "3": var(--cui-info-base),
    "4": var(--cui-success-base),
  ),
  $password-strength-levels
);
```

### Sass loops

```scss
@each $level, $color in $password-strength-levels {
  &[data-coreui-strength="#{$level}"] {
    --cui-password-strength-color: #{$color};
  }
}
```
