# Vue Stepper Component – Multi-Step Form Wizard for Vue.js

> Build multi-step forms and wizards easily with the Vue Stepper component. Create advanced Vue form flows with custom indicators, validation, and flexible layouts using Vue 3.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

The **Vue Stepper** component helps you build intuitive, multi-step form experiences (Vue Form Wizards) for your Vue.js applications. It supports horizontal and vertical layouts, built-in form validation, customizable indicators, and full slot-based control over step content.

If you're looking for a Vue Form Wizard or a fully flexible Vue Stepper, this component offers a robust and accessible solution.

## Example

This example shows a simple multi-step form wizard built using the Vue Stepper component. Each step defines its content through a slot named `step-<n>` for its 1-based position (`#step-1`, `#step-2`, …), and optionally provides a native `<form>` reference for validation. The `steps` prop defines the sequence, and the `@step-change` event emits the current index. Internal validation is handled automatically via `formRef`.

```html
<script setup>
import { ref, useId } from 'vue'
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CFormSelect,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
  CPasswordInput,
  CStepper,
} from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const stepperRef = ref()
const currentStep = ref(1)
const finish = ref(false)
const uid = useId()

const steps = ['Step 1', 'Step 2', 'Step 3']
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <CStepper
      ref="stepperRef"
      :steps="steps"
      @finish="finish = true"
      @reset="finish = false"
      @step-change="(step) => (currentStep = step)"
    >
      <template #step-1="{ formRef }">
        <form :ref="formRef" class="row g-4">
          <CCol :md="4">
            <CFormInput type="text" value="Łukasz" label="First name" />
          </CCol>
          <CCol :md="4">
            <CFormInput type="text" value="Holeczek" label="Last name" />
          </CCol>
          <CCol :md="4">
            <CFormLabel :for="`validationCustomUsername-${uid}-01`">Username</CFormLabel>
            <CInputGroup>
              <CInputGroupText :id="`inputGroupPrependFeedback-${uid}`">@</CInputGroupText>
              <CFormInput
                :id="`validationCustomUsername-${uid}-01`"
                type="text"
                :aria-describedby="`inputGroupPrependFeedback-${uid}`"
              />
            </CInputGroup>
          </CCol>
        </form>
      </template>

      <template #step-2="{ formRef }">
        <form :ref="formRef" class="row g-4">
          <CCol :md="6">
            <CFormInput type="text" label="City" />
          </CCol>
          <CCol :md="3">
            <CFormSelect label="State">
              <option disabled>Choose...</option>
              <option>...</option>
            </CFormSelect>
          </CCol>
          <CCol :md="3">
            <CFormInput type="text" label="Zip" />
          </CCol>
        </form>
      </template>

      <template #step-3="{ formRef }">
        <form :ref="formRef" class="row g-4">
          <CCol :md="6">
            <CFormInput type="email" label="Email" />
          </CCol>
          <CCol :md="6">
            <CPasswordInput label="Password" />
          </CCol>
          <CCol :xs="12">
            <CCheckbox label="Agree to terms and conditions" />
          </CCol>
        </form>
      </template>
    </CStepper>
    <div v-if="finish">All steps are complete—you're finished.</div>

    <div class="d-flex gap-3 mt-5">
      <CButton v-if="!finish && currentStep > 1" color="secondary" @click="stepperRef?.prev()">
        Previous
      </CButton>
      <CButton
        v-if="!finish && currentStep < steps.length"
        theme="primary"
        @click="stepperRef?.next()"
      >
        Next
      </CButton>
      <CButton
        v-if="!finish && currentStep === steps.length"
        theme="primary"
        @click="stepperRef?.finish()"
      >
        Finish
      </CButton>
      <CButton v-if="finish" theme="danger" @click="stepperRef?.reset()"> Reset </CButton>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Vertical indicator layout

In this example, the step indicators are stacked vertically above the labels using `step-button-layout="vertical"`, while the form content remains horizontally aligned. This option gives a compact and balanced look, especially useful in narrow layouts.

```html
<template>
  <CStepper :steps="['Step 1', 'Step 2', 'Step 3']" step-button-layout="vertical" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CStepper } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Vertical layout

This example demonstrates a fully vertical Vue Form Wizard. By setting `layout="vertical"`, both the step indicators and the form content are stacked vertically, providing a mobile-friendly top-down progression.

```html
<script setup>

import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,

<template>
  <div>
    <CStepper
      ref="stepperRef"
      :steps="steps"

      <template #step-1="{ formRef }">

            <CFormInput type="text" value="Łukasz" label="First name" />

          </CCol>

            <CFormSelect label="State">
              <option disabled>Choose...</option>
              <option>...</option>
            </CFormSelect>
          </CCol>

            <CFormInput type="text" label="Zip" />
          </CCol>
        </form>
      </template>

      <template #step-3="{ formRef }">

        Previous
      </CButton>

        v-if="!finish && currentStep < steps.length"
        theme="primary"
        @click="stepperRef?.next()"
      >
        Next
      </CButton>
      <CButton
        v-if="!finish && currentStep === steps.length"
        theme="primary"
        @click="stepperRef?.finish()"
      >
        Finish
      </CButton>
      <CButton v-if="finish" theme="danger" @click="stepperRef?.reset()"> Reset </CButton>
```

## Linear stepper (Form Wizard)

By default, the Vue Stepper operates in linear mode, requiring each step to be completed before the next becomes available. Set `:linear="true"` to enforce this behavior.

Use a linear Vue Form Wizard when you want structured progression in:

- Checkout flows
- Registration processes
- Multi-step forms with required fields

```html
<template>
  <CStepper :steps="['Step 1', 'Step 2', 'Step 3']" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CStepper } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Non-linear stepper

You can let users open any step directly instead of one at a time by setting `:linear="false"`. This mode is useful when step order is flexible or optional. Moving forward still validates the step being left, as in linear mode; add `:validation="false"` to let users move on with an invalid step.

Example use cases:

- Survey wizards
- Product onboarding
- Complex forms with independent sections

```html
<template>
  <CStepper :linear="false" :steps="['Step 1', 'Step 2', 'Step 3']" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CStepper } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Form validation

The Vue Stepper component provides native step-by-step validation. With `:validation="true"` (enabled by default), users cannot proceed unless each step's form is valid. Use the `formRef` exposed in the step slot to register your native `<form>`.

### Native browser validation

This example demonstrates default HTML5 validation within a Vue Form Wizard.

```html
<script setup>
import { ref, useId } from 'vue'
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CFormSelect,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
  CPasswordInput,
  CStepper,
} from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const stepperRef = ref()
const currentStep = ref(1)
const finish = ref(false)
const uid = useId()

const steps = ['Step 1', 'Step 2', 'Step 3']
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <CStepper
      ref="stepperRef"
      :steps="steps"
      @finish="finish = true"
      @reset="finish = false"
      @step-change="(step) => (currentStep = step)"
    >
      <template #step-1="{ formRef }">
        <form :ref="formRef" class="row g-4">
          <CCol :md="4">
            <CFormInput type="text" value="Łukasz" label="First name" required />
          </CCol>
          <CCol :md="4">
            <CFormInput type="text" value="Holeczek" label="Last name" required />
          </CCol>
          <CCol :md="4">
            <CFormLabel :for="`validationCustomUsername-${uid}-01`">Username</CFormLabel>
            <CInputGroup>
              <CInputGroupText :id="`inputGroupPrependFeedback-${uid}`">@</CInputGroupText>
              <CFormInput
                :id="`validationCustomUsername-${uid}-01`"
                type="text"
                :aria-describedby="`inputGroupPrependFeedback-${uid}`"
                required
              />
            </CInputGroup>
          </CCol>
        </form>
      </template>

      <template #step-2="{ formRef }">
        <form :ref="formRef" class="row g-4">
          <CCol :md="6">
            <CFormInput type="text" label="City" />
          </CCol>
          <CCol :md="3">
            <CFormSelect label="State">
              <option disabled>Choose...</option>
              <option>...</option>
            </CFormSelect>
          </CCol>
          <CCol :md="3">
            <CFormInput type="text" label="Zip" />
          </CCol>
        </form>
      </template>

      <template #step-3="{ formRef }">
        <form :ref="formRef" class="row g-4">
          <CCol :md="6">
            <CFormInput type="email" label="Email" required />
          </CCol>
          <CCol :md="6">
            <CPasswordInput label="Password" required />

      </template>

    <div v-if="finish">All steps are complete—you're finished.</div>

    <div class="d-flex gap-3 mt-5">
      <CButton v-if="!finish && currentStep > 1" color="secondary" @click="stepperRef?.prev()">
        Previous
      </CButton>
      <CButton
        v-if="!finish && currentStep < steps.length"
        theme="primary"
        @click="stepperRef?.next()"
      >
        Next
      </CButton>
      <CButton
        v-if="!finish && currentStep === steps.length"
        theme="primary"
```

### Custom validation

Go beyond native browser validation using `@step-validation-complete`. It is emitted first, before the browser's `invalid` events and before the stepper decides whether the step passes, with `isValid` telling whether every control passed. A validity the handler sets with `setCustomValidity()`, for example when two passwords differ, counts for the step; clear it with `setCustomValidity('')` once the rule holds, or the step stays blocked.

```vue
<CStepper
  :steps="steps"
  @step-validation-complete="
    confirmPassword?.setCustomValidity(
      confirmPassword.value === password?.value ? '' : 'Passwords do not match.'
    )
  "
/>
```

A form with `novalidate` gets the stepper's own feedback instead of the browser's: each time a step is validated, the invalid controls get `.is-invalid` and `aria-invalid` and the controls that pass lose them, focus moves to the first invalid control that can take focus when the step fails, the state then follows the controls as the user changes them until the form or the stepper is reset, and a `CFormInput`, `CFormSelect`, `CFormTextarea`, `CFormCheck`, `CAutocomplete`, `CChipInput`, `CCombobox`, `CMultiSelect`, `CNumberInput`, `COneTimePassword` or `CPasswordInput` with `feedback-invalid` is described by that message, so a screen reader reads it together with the field. A `CAutocomplete`, a `CMultiSelect`, a `CChipInput`, a `CCombobox`, a `COneTimePassword`, the date and time fields, the pickers, a `CRangeSlider` and a `CRating` show that state on their own frame and control, and the stepper leaves the field that carries their value to them. Add `data-coreui-validate="valid"` to the form to also mark the valid controls with `.is-valid`; as on [`CForm`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/validation/), the attribute also shows the state of a control once the user has interacted with it. If a `@step-validation-complete` handler moves focus itself, for example to an error summary, the stepper leaves it there.

```html
<script setup>
import { ref, useId } from 'vue'
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CFormSelect,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
  CPasswordInput,
  CStepper,
} from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const stepperRef = ref()
const currentStep = ref(1)
const finish = ref(false)
const uid = useId()

const steps = ['Step 1', 'Step 2', 'Step 3']
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <CStepper
      ref="stepperRef"
      :steps="steps"
      @finish="finish = true"
      @reset="finish = false"
      @step-change="(step) => (currentStep = step)"
    >
      <template #step-1="{ formRef }">
        <form :ref="formRef" class="row g-4" novalidate>
          <CCol :md="4">
            <CFormInput
              :id="`validationCustomFirstName-${uid}`"
              type="text"
              value="Łukasz"
              feedback-invalid="Please provide your first name."
              label="First name"
              required
            />
          </CCol>
          <CCol :md="4">
            <CFormInput
              :id="`validationCustomLastName-${uid}`"
              type="text"
              value="Holeczek"
              feedback-invalid="Please provide your last name."
              label="Last name"
              required
            />
          </CCol>
          <CCol :md="4">
            <CFormLabel :for="`validationCustomUsername-${uid}-01`">Username</CFormLabel>
            <CInputGroup>
              <CInputGroupText :id="`inputGroupPrependFeedback-${uid}`">@</CInputGroupText>
              <CFormInput
                :id="`validationCustomUsername-${uid}-01`"
                type="text"
                :aria-describedby="`inputGroupPrependFeedback-${uid}`"
                feedback-invalid="Please choose a username."
                required
              />
            </CInputGroup>
          </CCol>
        </form>
      </template>

      <template #step-2="{ formRef }">
        <form :ref="formRef" class="row g-4" novalidate>
          <CCol :md="6">
            <CFormInput :id="`validationCustomCity-${uid}`" type="text" label="City" />
          </CCol>
          <CCol :md="3">
            <CFormSelect :id="`validationCustomState-${uid}`" label="State">
              <option disabled>Choose...</option>
              <option>...</option>
            </CFormSelect>
          </CCol>
          <CCol :md="3">
            <CFormInput :id="`validationCustomZip-${uid}`" type="text" label="Zip" />
          </CCol>
        </form>
      </template>

      <template #step-3="{ formRef }">
        <form :ref="formRef" class="row g-4" novalidate>
          <CCol :md="6">
            <CFormInput
              :id="`validationCustomEmail-${uid}`"
              type="email"
              feedback-invalid="Please provide a valid email."
              label="Email"
              required
            />
          </CCol>
          <CCol :md="6">
            <CPasswordInput
              :id="`validationCustomPassword-${uid}`"
              feedback-invalid="Please provide a password."
              label="Password"
              required
            />
          </CCol>
          <CCol :xs="12">
            <CCheckbox label="Agree to terms and conditions" required />
          </CCol>
        </form>
      </template>
    </CStepper>
    <div v-if="finish">All steps are complete—you're finished.</div>

    <div class="d-flex gap-3 mt-5">
      <CButton v-if="!finish && currentStep > 1" color="secondary" @click="stepperRef?.prev()">
        Previous
      </CButton>
      <CButton
        v-if="!finish && currentStep < steps.length"
        theme="primary"
        @click="stepperRef?.next()"
      >
        Next
      </CButton>
      <CButton
        v-if="!finish && currentStep === steps.length"
        theme="primary"
        @click="stepperRef?.finish()"
      >
        Finish
      </CButton>
      <CButton v-if="finish" theme="danger" @click="stepperRef?.reset()"> Reset </CButton>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
```

### Disable validation

To let users move on with an invalid step, disable validation by adding `:validation="false"`.

```html
<script setup>
import { ref, useId } from 'vue'
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,

<template>
  <div>
    <CStepper
      ref="stepperRef"
      :steps="steps"

      @reset="finish = false"
      @step-change="(step) => (currentStep = step)"
    >
      <template #step-1="{ formRef }">
        <form :ref="formRef" class="row g-4">
          <CCol :md="4">
            <CFormInput type="text" value="Łukasz" label="First name" required />

            <CFormInput type="text" value="Holeczek" label="Last name" required />

          </CCol>
          <CCol :md="3">
            <CFormSelect label="State">
              <option disabled>Choose...</option>
              <option>...</option>
            </CFormSelect>
          </CCol>

            <CFormInput type="text" label="Zip" />
          </CCol>
        </form>
      </template>

      <template #step-3="{ formRef }">
        <form :ref="formRef" class="row g-4">

        Previous

        theme="primary"

      >
        Next
      </CButton>
      <CButton
        v-if="!finish && currentStep === steps.length"
```

## Usage with v-model

Bind `v-model` and the active step follows your state — the step buttons and the built-in navigation only emit `@update:modelValue` (and `@step-change` with the 1-based number), so the binding feeds it back. Without a binding the stepper manages itself; `active-step-number` seeds the starting step.

```html
<template>
  <CStepper v-model="step" :steps="['Account', 'Profile', 'Confirmation']" />
  <div class="d-flex gap-3 mt-4">
    <CButton theme="secondary" :disabled="step === 1" @click="step--">Back</CButton>
    <CButton theme="primary" :disabled="step === 3" @click="step++">Next</CButton>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CStepper } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const step = ref(1)
</script>
```

Use it when the active step belongs to something else: a route, a saved draft, or a wizard you drive from outside the stepper.

## Template ref

Attach a template ref to drive the stepper from your own buttons, outside the built-in navigation: `next()`, `prev()` and `reset()` behave like the matching buttons. `finish()` only does something on the last step, where it completes the wizard; called from an earlier one, it's a no-op. `next()` is the one that falls back to finishing when already on the last step.

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const stepper = ref()
</script>

<template>
  <CStepper ref="stepper" :steps="steps" />
  <CButton @click="stepper.prev()">Previous</CButton>
  <CButton @click="stepper.next()">Next</CButton>
</template>
```

## Accessibility (A11Y)

The CoreUI Stepper Component is built with accessibility in mind:

- **The horizontal layout is a tab set.** `stepper-steps` is the `role="tablist"` the step buttons belong to, each button is a `role="tab"` with `aria-selected`, `aria-controls` and `tabindex`, its `.stepper-step` wrapper is `role="presentation"` so the tabs stay direct children of the list, and the panes are `role="tabpanel"` linked to their buttons.
- **The vertical layout is a list of expandable steps.** Each step holds its own content, and a tablist cannot own the form controls of the open step, so none of the tab roles are written there: the list stays a list, each step stays a list item, and the buttons carry `aria-expanded` rather than `aria-selected`.
- When the step changes while focus is inside the stepper, or the change takes focus away (for example when the **Next** or **Reset** button that triggered it is no longer rendered), focus moves to the button of the new step, so a screen reader reads which step the user is on. A step changed from a control that stays outside the stepper leaves focus where it is.
- When a step whose form has `novalidate` fails validation, the invalid controls get `aria-invalid="true"` and focus moves to the first of them that can take focus, as the browser does for a form without `novalidate`.
- While the stepper marks a control invalid, its invalid feedback is added to its `aria-describedby`, the elements named in `data-coreui-invalid-feedback` or else the `.invalid-feedback` and `.invalid-tooltip` that follow it, which covers `feedback-invalid`, so the validation message is read with the field when focus moves to it. When focus is already on the first invalid control, or no invalid control can take focus, the message is announced through [`announce()`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/accessibility/screen-readers/#announcing-messages) instead, or the browser's validation message when the control has none. The stepper does not rely on `aria-errormessage`, which VoiceOver does not read, and the panes are not live regions, so they do not repeat the message.
- Keyboard navigation is fully supported.

Thanks to these features, your form wizard will be fully compliant with WCAG and modern accessibility standards without additional work.

### Keyboard Support

The Stepper component supports comprehensive keyboard navigation out of the box:

| Key | Function |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> / <kbd>ArrowUp</kbd> | Moves focus to previous step. |
| <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> / <kbd>ArrowDown</kbd> | Moves focus to next step. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | Jumps focus to first or last step |

# Vue Stepper Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Stepper component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

Full API documentation for the CStepper component, including all available props, customization options, and integration tips for building advanced multi-step forms and wizards in Vue.

## CStepper

```jsx
import { CStepper } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `activeStepNumber` | `number` | `1` | The default active step index when not using `v-model`. |
| `id` | `string` | - | Optional unique ID used for accessibility attributes like `aria-labelledby`. |
| `layout` | `String as () => 'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | Sets the layout direction of the Vue Stepper component. - `'horizontal'` – Steps are placed side-by-side. - `'vertical'` – Steps are stacked vertically (ideal for mobile). This makes the Vue Form Wizard adaptable to various screen sizes. |
| `linear` | `boolean` | `true` | Enables linear step progression in the Vue Form Wizard. - `true`: Steps must be completed in order. - `false`: Users can open any step directly. Moving forward still validates the step being left. Useful for enforcing validation and structured data entry in Vue multi-step forms. |
| `modelValue` | `number` | - | The current active step index of the Vue Stepper (used for controlled mode with `v-model`). If this prop is not provided, the Vue Form Wizard will use `activeStepNumber` as its initial value. |
| `stepButtonLayout` | `String as () => 'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | Controls the layout of the step indicator and label. - `'horizontal'`: Icon and label are side-by-side. - `'vertical'`: Label is shown below the icon. Applies only when `layout` is set to `'horizontal'`. |
| `steps` | `Array as () => (StepperStepData \| string)[]` | - | Defines the list of steps in the Vue Stepper. Each step should include: - `label`: The title displayed in the step. - `indicator` (optional): Custom icon, number, or marker. - `formRef` (optional): A reference to the `<form>` used for validation in Vue Form Wizard scenarios. |
| `theme` | `Color` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |
| `validation` | `boolean` | `true` | Enables validation of forms within each step of the Vue Form Wizard. When set to `true`, the user cannot proceed unless the current step's form passes `checkValidity()`. Each step must expose a native form element via the `formRef` slot binding. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `finish` | Emitted when the user successfully finishes all steps in the Vue Form Wizard. |
| `reset` | Emitted when the stepper is reset to its initial state. |
| `stepChange` | Emitted on any manual or programmatic step change. |
| `stepValidationComplete` | Emitted when a step's form is validated (when `validation: true`), before the stepper decides whether the step passes. A validity a handler sets with `setCustomValidity()` counts for the step. |
| `update:modelValue` | Emitted when the current active step changes. Useful for syncing state with `v-model`. |

# Vue Stepper Component Accessibility

> Detailed overview of the accessibility features implemented in CoreUI Vue Stepper, ensuring compliance with WAI-ARIA guidelines.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Accessibility

The Vue Stepper component is fully accessible out of the box:

- Step buttons use `role="tab"` and related ARIA attributes (`aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, `tabindex`)
- Step content areas are labeled with `role="tabpanel"` and properly linked
- When the step changes while focus is inside the stepper, or the change takes focus away, focus moves to the new step's button, so screen readers read which step the user is on
- When a step whose form has `novalidate` fails validation, focus moves to the first invalid control, which is read with its message: the stepper adds the `.invalid-feedback` that follows the control, which covers `feedback-invalid`, or the elements named in `data-coreui-invalid-feedback`, to its `aria-describedby`. The panes are not live regions
- Full keyboard support is included

### Keyboard support

The Stepper component supports comprehensive keyboard navigation out of the box:

| Key | Function |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> / <kbd>ArrowUp</kbd> | Moves focus to previous step. |
| <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> / <kbd>ArrowDown</kbd> | Moves focus to next step. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | Jumps focus to first or last step |

# Vue Switch Components

> Create consistent cross-browser and cross-device switch component.

## Approach

A switch is a [checkbox](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/checkbox/) drawn as a track and a thumb: `<CSwitch>` renders the `<input type="checkbox">` styled that way. The thumb is the input's own `::before`, so its color is a token rather than a fill inside an SVG.

The component renders `role="switch"` to convey the nature of the control to assistive technologies that support the role. Older ones announce it as a plain checkbox, which is a fair fallback. Switches support `disabled` like any checkbox, and the `label` property renders a sibling `<label>` already wired to the input with `for`.

## Basic switch

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CSwitch id="flexSwitchCheckDefault" label="Default switch checkbox input" />
  </CFormField>
  <CFormField>
    <CSwitch id="flexSwitchCheckChecked" label="Checked switch checkbox input" checked />
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CSwitch } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Disabled

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CSwitch id="flexSwitchCheckDisabled" label="Disabled switch checkbox input" disabled />
  </CFormField>
  <CFormField>
    <CSwitch
      id="flexSwitchCheckCheckedDisabled"
      label="Disabled checked switch checkbox input"
      checked
      disabled
    />
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CSwitch } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Sizing

`size="sm"`, `size="lg"` and `size="xl"` size the whole row — the track, its thumb, and the label beside it — the way the [checkbox](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/checkbox/#sizing) and [radio](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/radio/#sizing) sizes do.

Each sets **one** custom property. The track's width follows its height through the aspect ratio, the thumb follows the height minus the padding, and the alignment margin is computed from the line — so nothing needs re-tuning per size.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CSwitch id="flexSwitchCheckSizeSm" size="sm" label="Small switch checkbox input" checked />
  </CFormField>
  <CFormField>
    <CSwitch id="flexSwitchCheckSizeDefault" label="Default switch checkbox input" checked />
  </CFormField>
  <CFormField>
    <CSwitch id="flexSwitchCheckSizeLg" size="lg" label="Large switch checkbox input" checked />
  </CFormField>
  <CFormField>
    <CSwitch
      id="flexSwitchCheckSizeXl"
      size="xl"
      label="Extra large switch checkbox input"
      checked
    />
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CSwitch } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

Any other size is that one property:

```vue
<CSwitch :style="{ '--cui-switch-height': '2rem' }" aria-label="..." />
```

The proportion is a Sass variable, `$switch-aspect-ratio`, so a squarer or longer track is set once for every size.

## Without a label

A switch with no label text is the input on its own. Give it an accessible name some other way — `aria-label`, for instance. The name says what the switch turns on or off, like `aria-label="Email notifications"`, and replaces the `...` placeholder in the example below. See the [forms overview](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/overview/#accessibility) for details.

```html
<template>
  <CSwitch id="switchNoLabel" aria-label="..." />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CSwitch } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CSwitch id="fieldSwitch" label="Email notifications" />
    <CFormText>Turn this off and we will only contact you about your account.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CFormText, CSwitch } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Theme variants

Modify the appearance of checked switches with the `theme` property — it sets the checked background and border color to the theme color.

```html
<template>
  <div class="d-flex flex-column gap-3">
    <CFormField>
      <CSwitch id="switchThemePrimary" theme="primary" label="Primary switch" checked />
    </CFormField>
    <CFormField>
      <CSwitch id="switchThemeSecondary" theme="secondary" label="Secondary switch" checked />
    </CFormField>
    <CFormField>
      <CSwitch id="switchThemeSuccess" theme="success" label="Success switch" checked />
    </CFormField>
    <CFormField>
      <CSwitch id="switchThemeDanger" theme="danger" label="Danger switch" checked />
    </CFormField>
    <CFormField>
      <CSwitch id="switchThemeWarning" theme="warning" label="Warning switch" checked />
    </CFormField>
    <CFormField>
      <CSwitch id="switchThemeInfo" theme="info" label="Info switch" checked />
    </CFormField>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CSwitch } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

- [&lt;CSwitch /&gt;](./api/#cswitch)

# Vue Switch Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Switch component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CSwitch

```jsx
import { CSwitch } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | - | The id attribute of the input. Generated automatically when a label is set. |
| `label` | `string` | - | The label rendered after the input, already wired to it with `for`. |
| `modelValue` | `boolean` | `undefined` | The checked state, used with v-model. |
| `size` | `string` | - | Size the switch small, large or extra large. |
| `theme` | `Color` | - | Sets the color context of the checked state to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the checked state emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `change` | Event occurs when the checked value has been changed. |
| `update:modelValue` | Emit the new checked state whenever there’s a change event. |
| `update:validationState` | Event occurs with `undefined` when the user changes the checked state, or the form is reset, while `validationState` is set. A given state is a verdict on the choice it was given for; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it and let the browser's own validation show again. |

## CFormSwitch

```jsx
import { CFormSwitch } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | - | The id global attribute defines an identifier (ID) that must be unique in the whole document |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control invalid. |
| `label` | `string` | - | The element represents a caption for a component. |
| `modelValue` | `boolean\|string` | - | The default name for a value passed using v-model. |
| `reverse` | `boolean` | - | Put checkboxes or radios on the opposite side. |
| `size` | `string` | - | Size the component large or extra large. Works only with `switch`. |
| `theme` | `Color` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |
| `type` | `string` | `'checkbox'` | Specifies the type of component. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control valid. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the checked state emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `change` | Event occurs when the checked value has been changed. |
| `update:modelValue` | Emit the new value whenever there’s a change event. |
| `update:validationState` | Event occurs with `undefined` when the user changes the checked state, or the form is reset, while `validationState` (or the deprecated `invalid`) is set. A given state is a verdict on the choice it was given for; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it and let the browser's own validation show again. |

# Vue Switch Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Switch component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

Vue Switch reads its own custom properties, so restyling it does not touch checkboxes or radios. Set them on the control itself — an ancestor cannot override a token the element declares for itself.

```scss
$switch-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-switch-width: calc(var(--cui-switch-height) * 1.75),
    --cui-switch-height: 1.25rem,
    --cui-switch-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-pill),
    --cui-switch-transition-duration: var(--cui-control-transition-duration),
    --cui-switch-transition-timing: var(--cui-control-transition-timing),
    --cui-switch-bg: var(--cui-bg-3),
    --cui-switch-box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-black) 5%, transparent),
    --cui-switch-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-switch-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-switch-padding: .0625rem,
    --cui-switch-thumb-bg: var(--cui-white),
    --cui-switch-thumb-size: calc(var(--cui-switch-height) - var(--cui-switch-padding) * 2 - var(--cui-switch-border-width) * 2),
    --cui-switch-thumb-shadow: 0 1px 2px color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-black) 10%, transparent),
    --cui-switch-checked-bg: var(--cui-control-checked-bg),
    --cui-switch-checked-border-color: var(--cui-control-checked-border-color),
    --cui-switch-checked-thumb-bg: var(--cui-primary-contrast),
    --cui-switch-disabled-bg: var(--cui-control-disabled-bg),
    --cui-switch-disabled-thumb-bg: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-switch-disabled-opacity: var(--cui-control-disabled-opacity),
    --cui-switch-margin-top: calc((var(--cui-body-line-height) * 1em - var(--cui-switch-height)) * .5),
    --cui-switch-active-filter: var(--cui-control-active-filter),
    --cui-switch-label-disabled-opacity: var(--cui-control-label-disabled-opacity),
  ),
  $switch-tokens
);
```

#### How to use CSS variables

```vue
<CSwitch :style="{ '--cui-switch-width': '2.5em', '--cui-switch-checked-bg': '#198754' }" />
```

### Shared variables

The checkbox, the radio and the switch share their size and their focus, active and disabled states. Those live on `:root` as `--cui-control-*`, so one declaration retunes all three at runtime:

```scss
--cui-control-size: 1em,
--cui-control-checked-bg: var(--cui-primary-base),
--cui-control-checked-border-color: var(--cui-primary-base),
--cui-control-indeterminate-bg: var(--cui-primary-base),
--cui-control-indeterminate-border-color: var(--cui-primary-base),
--cui-control-active-filter: brightness(90%),
--cui-control-focus-border-color: var(--cui-btn-input-focus-border-color),
--cui-control-disabled-bg: var(--cui-bg-3),
--cui-control-disabled-opacity: .5,
--cui-control-label-disabled-opacity: .5,
--cui-control-transition-duration: .15s,
--cui-control-transition-timing: cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1),
```

### Sass maps

Each entry is one `.switch-{size}` class with its own height and font size, and the map merges with your overrides — add a key to define a size, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$switch-sizes: defaults(
  (
    sm: (height: 1rem,    font-size: var(--cui-font-size-sm)),
    lg: (height: 1.5rem,  font-size: var(--cui-font-size-lg)),
    xl: (height: 1.75rem, font-size: var(--cui-font-size-lg))
  ),
  $switch-sizes
);
```

The second map lists which of those sizes also answer to the deprecated `.form-switch-{size}` spelling. It holds names only — the heights come from the map above — so a size you add is reachable under the current spelling without appearing here:

```scss
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$form-switch-sizes: defaults(
  ("lg", "xl"),
  $form-switch-sizes
);
```

# Vue Bootstrap Switch Component

> Learn how to create responsive toggle switches using CoreUI’s Vue component styled to match Bootstrap form elements.

## How to use Vue Bootstrap Switch component

Use CoreUI’s `<CSwitch>` to create cross-browser, Bootstrap-styled toggle switches that represent binary states such as on/off, enabled/disabled, or true/false.

### Basic usage

A standard switch is a `<CSwitch>` — it renders `role="switch"` itself.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CSwitch id="flexSwitchCheckDefault" label="Default switch checkbox input" />
  </CFormField>
  <CFormField>
    <CSwitch id="flexSwitchCheckChecked" label="Checked switch checkbox input" checked />
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CSwitch } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

### Sizing

Use the `size` prop to adjust the visual scale of the switch. Available sizes include `"lg"` and `"xl"`.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <CSwitch id="flexSwitchCheckSizeSm" size="sm" label="Small switch checkbox input" checked />
  </CFormField>
  <CFormField>
    <CSwitch id="flexSwitchCheckSizeDefault" label="Default switch checkbox input" checked />
  </CFormField>
  <CFormField>
    <CSwitch id="flexSwitchCheckSizeLg" size="lg" label="Large switch checkbox input" checked />
  </CFormField>
  <CFormField>
    <CSwitch
      id="flexSwitchCheckSizeXl"
      size="xl"
      label="Extra large switch checkbox input"
      checked
    />
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CSwitch } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

### Reverse layout

The reverse layout exists only on the deprecated `<CFormSwitch>` — its `reverse` property places the control after the label.

```html
<template>
  <CFormSwitch id="reverseFormSwitch1" reverse label="Reverse switch" />
  <CFormSwitch id="reverseFormSwitch2" reverse label="Disabled reverse switch" disabled />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormSwitch } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## API reference

Refer to the API documentation below for a complete list of available props for the Vue Bootstrap Switch component.

- [&lt;CSwitch /&gt;](../api/#cswitch)
- [&lt;CFormSwitch /&gt;](../api/#cformswitch)

# Vue Form Text Component

> Vue textarea components. Give textual form `<textarea>`s an upgrade with custom styles, sizing, focus states, validation, and more.

## Example

```html
<template>
  <CFormTextarea
    id="exampleFormControlTextarea1"
    label="Example textarea"
    rows="3"
    text="Must be 8-20 words long."
  ></CFormTextarea>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

If you need to add custom classs to form's components, or need to add some custom elements you can add each form component separately. Please check the example below.

```vue
<CFormLabel for="exampleFormControlTextarea1">Example textarea</CFormLabel>
<CFormTextarea id="exampleFormControlTextarea1" rows="3"></CFormTextarea>
<CFormText as="span" id="passwordHelpInline">Must be 8-20 words long.</CFormText>
```

You can also use slots.

```vue
<CFormTextarea id="exampleFormControlTextarea1" rows="3">
  <template #label>Example textarea</template>
  <template #text>Must be 8-20 word long.</template>
</CFormTextarea>
```

## Disabled

Add the `disabled` boolean attribute on an input to give it a grayed out appearance and remove pointer events.

```html
<template>
  <CFormTextarea
    class="mb-4"
    placeholder="Disabled textarea"
    aria-label="Disabled textarea example"
    disabled
  ></CFormTextarea>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Readonly

Add the `readonly` boolean attribute on an textarea to prevent modification of the textarea's value. Read-only textareas appear lighter (just like disabled textareas), but retain the standard cursor.

```html
<template>
  <CFormTextarea
    placeholder="Readonly textarea"
    aria-label="Readonly textarea example"
    disabled
    readonly
  ></CFormTextarea>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

- [&lt;CFormTextarea /&gt;](./api/#cformtextarea)
- [&lt;CFormFeedback /&gt;](./api/#cformfeedback)
- [&lt;CFormLabel /&gt;](./api/#cformlabel)
- [&lt;CFormText /&gt;](./api/#cformtext)

# Vue Form control Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Form control component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CFormTextarea

```jsx
import { CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `feedback` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable feedback. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable feedback. |
| `feedbackValid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable invalid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied two CSS pseudo-classes, `:invalid` and `:valid`. |
| `floatingLabel` | `string` | - | Provide a floating label for the component — the text rests inside the field and floats once it has focus or a value. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `id` | `string` | - | The id global attribute defines an identifier (ID) that must be unique in the whole document. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control invalid. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `modelValue` | `string` | - | The default name for a value passed using v-model. |
| `plainText` | `boolean` | - | Render the component styled as plain text. Removes the default form field styling and preserve the correct margin and padding. Recommend to use only along side `readonly`. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the readonly state for the component. |
| `text` | `string` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control valid. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the value emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `change` | Event occurs when the element loses focus, after the content has been changed. |
| `input` | Event occurs immediately after the value of a component has changed. |
| `update:modelValue` | Emit the new value whenever there’s an input or change event. |
| `update:validationState` | Event occurs with `undefined` when the user changes the value, or the form is reset, while `validationState` (or the deprecated `invalid`) is set. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it and let the browser's own validation show again. |

## CFormFeedback

```jsx
import { CFormFeedback } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `string` | `'div'` | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Style the feedback as the invalid message. |
| `tooltip` | `boolean` | - | If your form layout allows it, you can display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Style the feedback as the valid message. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state this feedback belongs to, rendered as the `{state}-feedback` (or `{state}-tooltip`) class. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. |

# Vue Time Input Component

> Create Vue time fields with a section-based input mask. Users type the hour, minutes, and seconds in separate sections with automatic navigation and validation — like the native time input, but with full control over the format.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Example

_Added in 5.22.0._

The Vue Time Input component renders a masked time field. The mask is split into hour, minute, and — depending on the locale — AM/PM sections. Click or focus a section and type, use arrow keys to adjust values, and the caret moves to the next section automatically.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CTimeInput label="Meeting time" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CTimeInput time="14:30" label="Meeting time" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <span class="form-label">Meeting time</span>
    <CTimeInput locale="en-US" name="meetingTime" />
    <CFormText>Local time, in your own time zone.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CFormText } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Formats

Set an explicit format with the `format` property: `HH`/`H` for the 23-hour cycle, `hh`/`h` for the 12-hour cycle, `mm` for minutes, `ss` for seconds, and `A`/`a` for the day period. Type `a` or `p` in the AM/PM section to switch it, or use the arrow keys.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-4 mb-4 mb-lg-0">
      <CTimeInput format="HH:mm" label="HH:mm" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-4 mb-4 mb-lg-0">
      <CTimeInput format="HH:mm:ss" label="HH:mm:ss" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CTimeInput format="hh:mm A" label="hh:mm A" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Locale

Without an explicit format, the hour cycle and layout follow the locale set via the `locale` property — `en-US` gets a 12-hour clock with an AM/PM section, `pl-PL` or `de-DE` a 24-hour one.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-4 mb-4 mb-lg-0">
      <CTimeInput label="en-US" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-4 mb-4 mb-lg-0">
      <CTimeInput label="pl-PL" locale="pl-PL" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CTimeInput label="de-DE" locale="de-DE" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Seconds

Without an explicit format, enable the seconds section with the `seconds` property.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CTimeInput label="Time with seconds" seconds />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Min and max times

Constrain the selectable range with `minDate` and `maxDate` — time strings work here too. A completed time outside the range gets the `.is-invalid` class and the component reports `null`, and submits no time, until the value is corrected.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CTimeInput
        time="09:30"
        format="HH:mm"
        label="Business hours (09:00–17:00)"
        max-date="17:00"
        min-date="09:00"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Validation

The field takes its validation state [the same way as the date input](../date-input/#validation): a completed time outside `minDate`/`maxDate` makes it invalid whatever else is set, then `validationState`, then a validation that reported the field, and in a form with the `validate` property of `<CForm>` the `:user-invalid` state of its value field, with `validate="valid"` also its `:user-valid` state. A given state is a verdict on the time it was given for: when the user changes the time, or the form is reset, the component emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`, so bind it with `v-model:validation-state`, while a change your code makes through `time` emits nothing. A given `'invalid'` blocks the submit with the text of the linked message, or `Invalid value.` when there is none. The `feedbackValid`/`feedbackInvalid` texts render like for any other form control, and while the field is invalid the error, its own or one you render after the field, describes every section.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row g-4" novalidate validate>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CTimeInput
        feedback-invalid="Please provide a meeting time."
        format="HH:mm"
        label="Meeting time (required)"
        name="meeting"
        required
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CTimeInput
        v-model:validation-state="roomState"
        feedback="The room is taken at this time."
        format="HH:mm"
        label="Room booking"
        name="room"
        time="12:30"
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-12">
      <CButton color="primary" type="submit">Submit</CButton>
    </div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CForm, CTimeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const roomState = ref('invalid')
</script>
```

## Floating labels

Use the `floatingLabel` property. When the field is empty and not focused, the mask placeholders are hidden so the label can rest inside the field; focusing the field floats the label and reveals the mask.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-5">
      <CTimeInput id="floatingTimeInput" floating-label="Meeting time" format="HH:mm" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

Set `floatingLabelAlways` to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the mask showing.

## Sizing

The field renders as a `.form-control`, so the standard sizing works — set the `size` property to `lg` or `sm`.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-4 mb-4 mb-lg-0">
      <CTimeInput format="HH:mm" label="Large" size="lg" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-4 mb-4 mb-lg-0">
      <CTimeInput format="HH:mm" label="Default" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CTimeInput format="HH:mm" label="Small" size="sm" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Disabled and readonly

Set the `disabled` property to disable the field, or `readOnly` to make it focusable but non-editable.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CTimeInput time="14:30" disabled format="HH:mm" label="Disabled" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CTimeInput time="14:30" format="HH:mm" label="Readonly" read-only />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Value semantics

The component reports a `Date` object anchored to `1970-01-01` — the same convention as the CoreUI time picker — so only the time part is meaningful. `minDate`/`maxDate` therefore constrain the time of day. A native reset of the form puts back the time the field started with and emits `time-change` when that changes it; a bound field only asks for its first `time` through `update:time` and `time-change`.

## Accessibility

The time input shares the [accessibility model of the date input](../date-input/#accessibility): `role="group"` on the container, named by `label`, a `role="spinbutton"` with full ARIA value attributes per section, a single tab stop with roving focus, and `inputmode` hints for mobile keyboards. Clicking the label that names the field moves focus to the first empty section. The AM/PM section announces its localized name via `aria-valuetext` and can be toggled with the <kbd>A</kbd>/<kbd>P</kbd> letters or arrow keys.

The [keyboard support table](../date-input/#keyboard-support) applies unchanged, including <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> (select all), <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> (copy), and paste.

```jsx
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaDayLabel` | `string` | `'Day'` | The `aria-label` of the day section. |
| `ariaHourLabel` | `string` | `'Hour'` | The `aria-label` of the hour section. |
| `ariaMeridiemLabel` | `string` | `'AM/PM'` | The `aria-label` of the meridiem section. |
| `ariaMinuteLabel` | `string` | `'Minute'` | The `aria-label` of the minute section. |
| `ariaMonthLabel` | `string` | `'Month'` | The `aria-label` of the month section. |
| `ariaQuarterLabel` | `string` | `'Quarter'` | The `aria-label` of the quarter section. |
| `ariaSecondLabel` | `string` | `'Second'` | The `aria-label` of the second section. |
| `ariaWeekLabel` | `string` | `'Week'` | The `aria-label` of the week section. |
| `ariaYearLabel` | `string` | `'Year'` | The `aria-label` of the year section. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | - | Focus the first section right after mounting, like the native `autofocus` attribute. |
| `dayPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `DD` the day section shows while it is empty. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `disabledDates` | `DisabledDate \| DisabledDate[]` | `undefined` | Specify the list of dates that cannot be selected. It can be a single `Date`, an `[start, end]` range, a matcher function, or an array of these. |
| `feedback` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable feedback to your users with HTML5 form validation feedback. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable invalid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied `validationState="invalid"`. |
| `feedbackValid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable valid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied `validationState="valid"`. |
| `floatingClassName` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the floating label wrapper. |
| `floatingLabel` | `string` | - | Wrap the field in a floating label. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `format` | `string \| ((locale: string) => DateSection[])` | `undefined` | The mask layout. A string is parsed as dayjs/moment or date-fns/luxon format tokens, a function receives the locale and returns the section layout, and `undefined` derives the layout from the locale. |
| `hourPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `HH` (`hh` on a 12-hour clock) the hour section shows while it is empty. |
| `id` | `string` | - | The id attribute of the field. |
| `inputDateParse` | `(value: string) => Date \| null` | `undefined` | Custom function to parse text pasted into the field into a `Date` object, e.g. with an external date library. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `locale` | `string` | `'default'` | Sets the default locale for the component. If not set, it is inherited from the browser. |
| `maxDate` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | Max selectable date. |
| `meridiemPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `AM` the meridiem section shows while it is empty. |
| `minDate` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | Min selectable date. |
| `minutePlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `mm` the minute section shows while it is empty. |
| `monthNames` | `string[]` | `undefined` | Twelve custom month names for text month sections (`MMM`/`MMMM`), overriding the locale-derived, date-context grammatical form. |
| `monthPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `MM` the month section shows while it is empty. |
| `name` | `string` | - | Name of the value input the value is submitted under. Without it the field is not submitted with the form. |
| `quarterPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `Q` the quarter section shows while it is empty. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the readonly state for the component. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | When present, it specifies that the field must be filled out before submitting the form. |
| `secondPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `ss` the second section shows while it is empty. |
| `seconds` | `boolean` | - | Include a seconds section in the locale-derived layout. |
| `size` | `string` | `undefined` | Size the component small or large. |
| `text` | `string` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `time` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | The time — a `Date` or a time string like `'14:30'` or `'2:30 PM'`. Passed one-way it seeds the field, which keeps managing itself; bound with `v-model:time` it follows your state. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` on every section and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. A field of a date range whose end is before its start draws no other state. The user's next change of the value emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`. |
| `weekPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `WW` the week section shows while it is empty. |
| `yearPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `YYYY` the year section shows while it is empty. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `error` | Callback fired when the validation state changes; receives `'incomplete'`, `'minDate'`, `'maxDate'`, `'disabledDate'`, or `null` when the value is valid or the field is empty. When one change moves both the value and the validation state, it fires after `time-change`, so a value set from it replaces the one just reported. |
| `time-change` | Callback fired when the time changes; receives a `Date` anchored to 1970-01-01 (or `null` while incomplete or invalid) and the formatted value. |
| `update:time` | Emit the new time to support the `v-model:time` binding. |
| `update:validationState` | Event occurs with `undefined` when the user changes the time, or the form is reset, while `validationState` is set. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it and let the browser's own validation show again. |

# Vue Time Input Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Time Input component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

### CSS variables

The date, time, and date-time inputs share one set of styles under the `form-date-time` name. The field is a [`.form-control`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/input/styling/#css-variables), so its frame comes from the `--cui-control-*` tokens; the ones below style the sections inside it. Both sets sit on the field, where `class` and `style` on `<CTimeInput>` land, and can be set on a single element.

```scss
// Redeclaring a --cui-control-* token here would shadow `.form-control`
// on the same element, and with it the validation states.
$form-date-time-tokens: () !default;
$form-date-time-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-date-time-placeholder-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-form-date-time-section-border-radius: .25rem,
    --cui-form-date-time-section-focus-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg-subtle),
  ),
  $form-date-time-tokens
);
```

# Vue Time Picker Component

> The Vue Time Picker Component offers a seamless way for users to select time values in any Vue-based application.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Example

To create a basic Vue Time Picker, use:

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
      <CTimePicker label="Time" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CTimePicker label="Time" locale="en-US" time="02:17:35 PM" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTimePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### With v-model

The `v-model:time` binding keeps the selected time in sync with your component's state.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row mb-4">
    <div class="col-lg-6">
      <CTimePicker v-model:time="vTime" label="Time" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
  </div>
  <div>{{ vTime }}</div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTimePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
import { ref } from 'vue'
const vTime = ref('02:17:35 PM')
</script>
```

### With footer

The `footer` slot projects your own content below the time selection. Its slot props carry the picker's context — `setTime`, `now`, `clear`, `reset`, `close`, `isTimeSelectable`, `time` and `disabled` — so a projected button acts on the picker and reads its state. That is also how a "Now" button disables itself when the current time falls outside `minDate` or `maxDate`; the example checks when the panel renders and again on click, so a time that crosses a limit while the panel is open is not written.

Any descendant can reach the same context with the `useTimePicker()` composable.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CTimePicker locale="en-US" max-date="17:00" min-date="09:00">
        <template #footer="{ clear, close, isTimeSelectable, now }">
          <CButton
            class="me-auto"
            theme="danger"
            :disabled="!isTimeSelectable(new Date())"
            size="sm"
            variant="ghost"
            @click="isTimeSelectable(new Date()) && now()"
          >
            Now
          </CButton>
          <CButton theme="primary" size="sm" variant="ghost" @click="clear">Clear</CButton>
          <CButton theme="primary" size="sm" @click="close">OK</CButton>
        </template>
      </CTimePicker>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CButton, CTimePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

A native reset of the form returns the picker to the time it started with and drops the state a submit set; a picker bound with `v-model:time` asks for the time it started with through `update:time` and `time-change` and shows the time your page gives until the page takes it.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField>
    <span class="form-label">Meeting time</span>
    <CTimePicker locale="en-US" name="meetingTime" />
    <CFormText>Local time, in your own time zone.</CFormText>
  </CFormField>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CFormField, CFormText } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CTimePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Floating labels

Set `floatingLabel` and the component wraps its input in `.form-floating` and renders the label itself — the text also becomes the field's accessible name. No wrapper markup is needed, and the mask placeholders stay hidden while the label rests inside the field.

```html
<template>
  <CTimePicker floating-label="Meeting time" locale="en-US" />
</template>
```

Set `floatingLabelAlways` to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the mask showing.

## Sizing

```html
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="row">

    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
```

```html
</script>
```

## Min and max times

Constrain the times the user can pick with `min-date` and `max-date`, given as time strings like `'09:30'` or as dates, of which only the time of day counts. The panel disables the hours that hold no allowed time and, once an hour is chosen, the minutes and seconds outside the range, and a time picked in the panel that crosses a limit moves to it. A time typed in the field outside the range gets the `.is-invalid` class, the picker emits `update:time` with `null` and submits no time until the value is corrected. A `maxDate` at midnight covers the whole day; any other `maxDate` before the `minDate` leaves no time to pick.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CTimePicker
        label="Opening hours (09:30–17:00)"
        locale="en-GB"
        max-date="17:00"
        min-date="09:30"
        :seconds="false"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTimePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Validation

The picker takes its validation state [the way the date picker does](../date-picker/#validation): `validationState` gives `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`, with `invalid` and `valid` as deprecated aliases that ask to be dropped the same way, though only a `validation-state` bound with `v-model:validation-state` is cleared by it. When the user changes the time, with a time picked in the panel, the cleaner, a footer button that changes the time through the context, or typing in the field, or the form is reset, the picker emits `update:validationState` with `undefined` before `time-change`, so bind it with `v-model:validation-state`, while a change your code makes through `time` emits nothing. While the given state is `'invalid'`, the sections of the field carry `aria-invalid="true"`, are described by the message after the picker, and the picker blocks the submit with its text, or `Invalid value.` when there is none.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row g-4" novalidate validate>
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CTimePicker
        feedback-invalid="Please provide a meeting time."
        label="Meeting time (required)"
        locale="en-US"
        name="meeting"
        required
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CTimePicker
        v-model:validation-state="roomState"
        feedback="The room is taken at this time."
        label="Room booking"
        locale="en-US"
        name="room"
        time="12:30:00"
      />
    </div>
    <div class="col-12">
      <CButton color="primary" type="submit">Submit</CButton>
    </div>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CForm, CTimePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const roomState = ref('invalid')
</script>
```

### Custom hours, minutes and seconds

Tailor the Vue Time Picker to your needs by specifying custom values for hours, minutes, and seconds. Use arrays to define selectable options or functions for dynamic filtering. Hours are 0 to 23 in every locale. On a 12-hour clock the column still lists 1 to 12 next to AM/PM: picking an hour that only one period allows sets that period, and the period the picked hour does not allow is disabled, so the example below offers 8 AM to 4 PM, minutes in quarters and seconds under 20.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
      <CTimePicker
        locale="en-US"
        :hours="[8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16]"
        :minutes="[0, 15, 30, 45]"
        :seconds="(s) => s < 20"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTimePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Locale

Tailor the Vue Time Picker to match different locales, offering an inclusive user experience across diverse languages. Automatically adapt or set specific locales to meet your application's needs.

The locale decides whether the field and the time columns use a 12-hour or a 24-hour clock, and names the day periods in its own words, 오전 and 오후 in Korean. A `format` pins the clock in every locale, `'HH:mm'` for 24 hours and `'hh:mm a'` for 12.

### Auto

Our Time Picker component automatically detects and adapts to the user's locale, ensuring a localized experience without explicit configuration.

With server-side rendering, pass `locale` explicitly: by default the server writes the text in its own locale and the browser in the reader's, and Vue reports a hydration mismatch when the two differ.

```html
<template>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-lg-4">
      <CTimePicker />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTimePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Open state

_Added in 6.0.0._

Bind `v-model:show` and the panel renders what you pass — dismiss gestures only emit `update:show`, so the binding feeds the change back. Here a checkbox pins the panel open, and a dismiss gesture unchecks it.

```html
<template>
  <CFormField class="mb-4">
    <CCheckbox id="timePickerControlledShow" v-model="show" label="Keep the time selection open" />
  </CFormField>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-4">
      <CTimePicker v-model:show="show" label="Time" locale="en-US" />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField, CTimePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

### Initial open state

Without a binding the picker manages its own panel. Pass `show` to seed it open on mount.

```vue
<CTimePicker show />
```

The `update:show` event fires either way whenever the panel requests an open-state change — a dismiss gesture (Escape, a click outside) or any internal toggle — so you can watch the state without taking it over. The deprecated `visible` prop keeps its old behavior and is ignored when `show` is set.

## Accessibility

The field is a group of spinbutton sections, so its own arrow keys belong to the value and the panel opens on the native control's dropdown keys instead. The field takes its name from an `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label` you pass to the picker, otherwise from `floatingLabel` or, without one, from `label`, and it is described by an `aria-describedby` you pass to the picker, then by `text` and the feedback that matches its state. Clicking the label that names the field moves focus to its first empty section. Each column of the roll is an ARIA listbox, and a roving tabindex keeps the whole body to a single tab stop, with the arrows moving between the columns. While the field is empty no option is selected, and the tab stop and each column start on their first option the limits allow.

The toggle button carries the panel's state — `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-controls` pointing at the popup while it is open, and `aria-expanded` — so a screen reader announces what the button does and whether the panel is showing. The panel itself is a `dialog` with `aria-modal`, so focus moves into it on open, stays there while it is open, and returns to the field when it closes.

### Keyboard support

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd> (<kbd>Option</kbd> on macOS) + <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> / <kbd>F4</kbd> | Open the panel and move focus into it |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close the panel and return focus to the field |
| <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> | Move between the cells of a column |
| <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> | Move between the columns |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | Jump to the ends of a column |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Select the focused value and move to the next column |
