# Vue Time Picker Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Time Picker component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## CTimePicker

```jsx
import { CTimePicker } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaCleanerLabel` | `string` | `'Clear time'` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that clears the value. |
| `ariaDayLabel` | `string` | `'Day'` | The `aria-label` of the day section. |
| `ariaHourLabel` | `string` | `'Hour'` | The `aria-label` of the hour section. |
| `ariaMeridiemLabel` | `string` | `'AM/PM'` | The `aria-label` of the meridiem section. |
| `ariaMinuteLabel` | `string` | `'Minute'` | The `aria-label` of the minute section. |
| `ariaMonthLabel` | `string` | `'Month'` | The `aria-label` of the month section. |
| `ariaPickerLabel` | `string` | `'Toggle time selection'` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that opens the time selection. |
| `ariaPopupLabel` | `string` | `'Time selection'` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the time selection panel, which opens as a `role="dialog"`. |
| `ariaQuarterLabel` | `string` | `'Quarter'` | The `aria-label` of the quarter section. |
| `ariaSecondLabel` | `string` | `'Second'` | The `aria-label` of the second section. |
| `ariaSelectHoursLabel` | `string` | `'Select hours'` | Sets the accessible label of the hours column. |
| `ariaSelectMeridiemLabel` | `string` | `'Select AM/PM'` | Sets the accessible label of the AM/PM column. |
| `ariaSelectMinutesLabel` | `string` | `'Select minutes'` | Sets the accessible label of the minutes column. |
| `ariaSelectSecondsLabel` | `string` | `'Select seconds'` | Sets the accessible label of the seconds column. |
| `ariaWeekLabel` | `string` | `'Week'` | The `aria-label` of the week section. |
| `ariaYearLabel` | `string` | `'Year'` | The `aria-label` of the year section. |
| `cleaner` | `boolean` | `true` | Renders the button that clears the value. |
| `container` | `HTMLElement \| (() => HTMLElement) \| string` | `'body'` | The element the time selection is rendered into instead of `document.body`. Implies `portal`. Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert. |
| `dayPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `DD` the day section shows while it is empty. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggles the disabled state. |
| `feedback` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable feedback to your users with HTML5 form validation feedback. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable invalid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied `invalid` prop. |
| `feedbackValid` | `string` | - | Provide valuable, actionable valid feedback when using standard HTML form validation which applied `valid` prop. |
| `floatingLabel` | `string` | - | Renders a floating label inside the field — the component wraps its input in `.form-floating` and the text also becomes the field's accessible name. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `format` | `string \| ((locale: string) => DateSection[])` | `undefined` | The mask layout of the field. A string is parsed as dayjs/moment or date-fns/luxon format tokens, a function receives the locale and returns the section layout, and `undefined` derives the layout from the locale. The mask's hour cycle also drives the columns. |
| `hourPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `HH` (`hh` on a 12-hour clock) the hour section shows while it is empty. |
| `hours` | `number[] \| ((hour: number) => boolean)` | `undefined` | Narrows the hours to a list, or to the ones a predicate accepts. Hours are 0 to 23 in every locale; on a 12-hour clock an hour that only one day period allows sets that period when picked. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control invalid. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `locale` | `string` | `'default'` | Sets the default locale for the component. If not set, it is inherited from the browser. |
| `maxDate` | - | - | The latest time the user can pick: a time string such as `'17:00'`, or a `Date` of which only the time of day counts. The panel disables the times after it, a time picked in the panel moves back to it, and the field rejects a later time. |
| `meridiemPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `AM` the meridiem section shows while it is empty. |
| `minDate` | - | - | The earliest time the user can pick: a time string such as `'09:30'`, or a `Date` of which only the time of day counts. The panel disables the times before it, a time picked in the panel moves up to it, and the field rejects an earlier time. |
| `minutePlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `mm` the minute section shows while it is empty. |
| `minutes` | `boolean \| number[] \| ((minute: number) => boolean)` | `true` | Renders the minutes column, optionally narrowed the way `hours` is. |
| `monthPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `MM` the month section shows while it is empty. |
| `name` | `string` | - | Name of the value input the value is submitted under. Without it the field is not submitted with the form. |
| `pickerIcon` | `boolean` | `true` | The button that opens the panel. Set to `false` to render no button; replace the artwork through the `pickerIcon` slot. |
| `portal` | `boolean` | `true` | Renders the time selection through a portal: into the open `<dialog>` the field sits in, otherwise into `document.body`. |
| `quarterPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `Q` the quarter section shows while it is empty. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the readonly state for the component. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | When present, it specifies that the field must be filled out before submitting the form. |
| `secondPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `ss` the second section shows while it is empty. |
| `seconds` | `boolean \| number[] \| ((second: number) => boolean)` | `true` | Renders the seconds column, optionally narrowed the way `hours` is. |
| `show` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Control the open state via `v-model:show`. When set, the time selection renders what `show` says and dismiss gestures only emit `update:show`. |
| `size` | `string` | `undefined` | Sizes the control, the way `.form-control-sm` and `.form-control-lg` size a form control. |
| `text` | `string` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `time` | `Date \| string \| null` | `undefined` | The time — a `Date` or a time string like `'14:30'`. Passed one-way it seeds the field, which keeps managing itself; bound with `v-model:time` it follows your state. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control valid. |
| `validationState` | `string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` on every section of the field and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the time emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Controls the visibility of the time selection. |
| `weekPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `WW` the week section shows while it is empty. |
| `yearPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `YYYY` the year section shows while it is empty. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `error` | Callback fired when the validation state changes; receives `'incomplete'`, `'minDate'`, `'maxDate'`, `'disabledDate'`, or `null` when the value is valid or the field is empty. When one change moves both the value and the validation state, it fires after `time-change`, so a value set from it replaces the one just reported. |
| `hide` | Callback fired when the time selection is hidden. |
| `show` | Callback fired when the time selection is shown. |
| `time-change` | Callback fired once when the value changes, whether from the field, the panel or the context methods; receives the `Date` the field holds, anchored to 1970-01-01 and cut to the units the field shows, or `null` while the field is empty or incomplete, and the formatted value. |
| `update:show` | Emit the requested open state to support the `v-model:show` binding. |
| `update:time` | Emit the new time to support the `v-model:time` binding. |
| `update:validationState` | Event occurs with `undefined` when the user changes the time, or the form is reset, while `validationState` (or the deprecated `invalid`/`valid`) is set. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it and let the browser's own validation show again. |

# Vue Time Picker Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Time Picker component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

### CSS variables

The field is a [`.form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/form-control-group/styling/#css-variables) on the picker element itself, so its frame, the cleaner and the toggle read the `--cui-control-*` and `--cui-control-group-*` tokens. `class` and `style` on `<CTimePicker>` land on that element; set the tokens there to restyle one field.

The picker declares its local CSS variables on its panel, `.time-picker-popup`. Values are set via Sass, so Sass customization is supported too.

```scss
$time-picker-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-time-picker-footer-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-time-picker-footer-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-time-picker-footer-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-time-picker-footer-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-time-picker-footer-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-time-picker-col-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-time-picker-col-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-time-picker-cell-width: 3rem,
    --cui-time-picker-cell-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-time-picker-cell-height: 2rem,
    --cui-time-picker-cell-hover-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-time-picker-cell-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-2),
    --cui-time-picker-cell-disabled-color: var(--cui-fg-4),
    --cui-time-picker-cell-selected-color: var(--cui-primary-contrast),
    --cui-time-picker-cell-selected-bg: var(--cui-primary-base),
    --cui-time-picker-cell-selected-hover-color: var(--cui-primary-contrast),
    --cui-time-picker-cell-selected-hover-bg: oklch(from var(--cui-primary-base) calc(l * var(--cui-theme-hover-lightness)) calc(c * var(--cui-theme-hover-chroma)) h),
  ),
  $time-picker-tokens
);
```

The panel is a `.popup`: its surface, border, shadow, stacking and fade come from the tokens every popup panel shares with the other pickers, the combobox, autocomplete and multi select.

```scss
$popup-tokens: () !default;
$popup-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-popup-zindex: var(--cui-z-dropdown),
    --cui-popup-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-popup-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-popup-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-popup-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-popup-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow),
    --cui-popup-transition-duration: .15s,
    --cui-popup-transition-timing: var(--cui-transition-timing-overlay),
  ),
  $popup-tokens
);
```

#### How to use CSS variables

Each part of the panel declares its tokens itself, and the panel is rendered into `document.body` unless `portal` is `false`, so a variable set on `CTimePicker` through `style` styles the field but reaches none of them. Set them with a rule on the part that declares them:

```css
.time-picker-popup {
  --cui-popup-bg: #f8f9fa;
  --cui-time-picker-col-border-color: #dee2e6;
}
```

# Vue Form Layout

> Give your forms some structure—from inline to horizontal to custom grid implementations—with our form layout options.

## Forms

Every group of form fields should reside in a `<CForm>` element. CoreUI provides no default styling for the `<CForm>` element, but there are some powerful browser features that are provided by default.

- New to browser forms? Consider reviewing [the MDN form docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/form) for an overview and complete list of available attributes.
- `<CButton>`s within a `<CForm>` default to `type="submit"`, so strive to be specific and always include a `type`.
- You can disable every form element within a form with the `disabled` attribute on the `<CForm>`.

Since CoreUI applies `display: block` and `width: 100%` to almost all our form controls, forms will by default stack vertically. Additional classes can be used to vary this layout on a per-form basis.

## Utilities

[Margin utilities](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/margin/) are the easiest way to add some structure to forms. They provide basic grouping of labels, controls, optional form text, and form validation messaging. We recommend sticking to `margin-bottom` utilities, and using a single direction throughout the form for consistency.

## Form grid

More complex forms can be built using our grid classes. Use these for form layouts that require multiple columns, varied widths, and additional alignment options.

```html
<template>
  <CRow>
    <CCol xs>
      <CFormInput placeholder="First name" aria-label="First name" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs>
      <CFormInput placeholder="Last name" aria-label="Last name" />
    </CCol>
  </CRow>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CRow, CCol, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Gutters

By adding [gutter modifier classes](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/layout/gutters/), you can have control over the gutter width in as well the inline as block direction.

```html
<template>
  <CRow class="g-4">
    <CCol xs>
      <CFormInput placeholder="First name" aria-label="First name" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs>
      <CFormInput placeholder="Last name" aria-label="Last name" />
    </CCol>
  </CRow>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CRow, CCol, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

More complex layouts can also be created with the grid system.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row g-4">
    <CCol md="6">
      <CFormLabel for="inputEmail4">Email</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput id="inputEmail4" type="email" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="6">
      <CFormLabel for="inputPassword4">Password</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput id="inputPassword4" type="password" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CFormLabel for="inputAddress">Address</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput id="inputAddress" placeholder="1234 Main St" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CFormLabel for="inputAddress2">Address 2</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput id="inputAddress2" placeholder="Apartment, studio, or floor" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="6">
      <CFormLabel for="inputCity">City</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput id="inputCity" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="4">
      <CFormLabel for="inputState">State</CFormLabel>
      <CFormSelect id="inputState">
        <option>Choose...</option>
        <option>...</option>
      </CFormSelect>
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="2">
      <CFormLabel for="inputZip">Zip</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput id="inputZip" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="gridCheck" label="Check me out" />
      </CFormField>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">Sign in</CButton>
    </CCol>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CForm,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CFormSelect,
} from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Horizontal form

Create horizontal forms with the grid by adding the `.row` class to form groups and using the `.col-*-*` classes to specify the width of your labels and controls. Be sure to add `.col-form-label` to your `<CFormLabel>`s as well so they're vertically centered with their associated form controls.

At times, you maybe need to use margin or padding utilities to create that perfect alignment you need. For example, we've removed the `padding-top` on our stacked radio inputs label to better align the text baseline.

```html
<template>
  <CForm>
    <CRow class="mb-4">
      <CFormLabel for="inputEmail3" class="col-sm-2 col-form-label">Email</CFormLabel>
      <CCol sm="10">
        <CFormInput id="inputEmail3" type="email" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
    <CRow class="mb-4">
      <CFormLabel for="inputPassword3" class="col-sm-2 col-form-label">Password</CFormLabel>
      <CCol sm="10">
        <CFormInput id="inputPassword3" type="password" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
    <fieldset class="row mb-4">
      <legend class="col-form-label col-sm-2 pt-0">Radios</legend>
      <CCol sm="10">
        <CFormField>
          <CRadio id="gridRadios1" name="gridRadios" value="option1" label="First radio" checked />
        </CFormField>
        <CFormField>
          <CRadio id="gridRadios2" name="gridRadios" value="option2" label="Second radio" />
        </CFormField>
        <CFormField>
          <CRadio
            id="gridRadios3"
            name="gridRadios"
            value="option3"
            label="Third disabled radio"
            disabled
          />
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>
    </fieldset>
    <CRow class="mb-4">
      <div class="col-sm-10 offset-sm-2">
        <CFormField>
          <CCheckbox id="gridCheck1" label="Example checkbox" />
        </CFormField>
      </div>
    </CRow>
    <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">Sign in</CButton>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CForm,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CRadio,
  CRow,
} from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

### Horizontal form label sizing

Be sure to use `.col-form-label-sm` or `.col-form-label-lg` to your `<CFormLabel>`s or `<legend>`s to correctly follow the size of `.form-control-lg` and `.form-control-sm`.

```html
<template>
  <CRow class="mb-4">
    <CFormLabel for="colFormLabelSm" class="col-sm-2 col-form-label col-form-label-sm"
      >Email</CFormLabel
    >
    <CCol sm="10">
      <CFormInput
        id="colFormLabelSm"
        type="email"
        class="form-control form-control-sm"
        placeholder="col-form-label-sm"
      />
    </CCol>
  </CRow>
  <CRow class="mb-4">
    <CFormLabel for="colFormLabel" class="col-sm-2 col-form-label">Email</CFormLabel>
    <CCol sm="10">
      <CFormInput id="colFormLabel" type="email" placeholder="col-form-label" />
    </CCol>
  </CRow>
  <CRow>
    <CFormLabel for="colFormLabelLg" class="col-sm-2 col-form-label col-form-label-lg"
      >Email</CFormLabel
    >
    <CCol sm="10">
      <CFormInput
        id="colFormLabelLg"
        type="email"
        class="form-control form-control-lg"
        placeholder="col-form-label-lg"
      />
    </CCol>
  </CRow>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CRow, CFormLabel, CCol, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Column sizing

As shown in the previous examples, our grid system allows you to place any number of `<CCol>`s within a `<CRow>`. They'll split the available width equally between them. You may also pick a subset of your columns to take up more or less space, while the remaining `<CCol>`s equally split the rest, with specific column classes like `<CCol sm="7">`.

```html
<template>
  <CRow class="g-4">
    <CCol sm="7">
      <CFormInput placeholder="City" aria-label="City" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol sm>
      <CFormInput placeholder="State" aria-label="State" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol sm>
      <CFormInput placeholder="Zip" aria-label="Zip" />
    </CCol>
  </CRow>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CRow, CCol, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Auto-sizing

The example below uses a flexbox utility to vertically center the contents and changes `<CCol>` to `<CCol xs="auto">` so that your columns only take up as much space as needed. Put another way, the column sizes itself based on the contents.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row gy-3 gx-4 align-items-center">
    <CCol xs="auto">
      <CFormLabel class="visually-hidden" for="autoSizingInput">Name</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput id="autoSizingInput" placeholder="Jane Doe" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="auto">
      <CFormLabel class="visually-hidden" for="autoSizingInputGroup">Username</CFormLabel>
      <CInputGroup>
        <CInputGroupText>@</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput id="autoSizingInputGroup" placeholder="Username" />
      </CInputGroup>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="auto">
      <CFormLabel class="visually-hidden" for="autoSizingSelect">Preference</CFormLabel>
      <CFormSelect id="autoSizingSelect">
        <option>Choose...</option>
        <option value="1">One</option>
        <option value="2">Two</option>
        <option value="3">Three</option>
      </CFormSelect>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="auto">
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="autoSizingCheck" label="Remember me" />
      </CFormField>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="auto">
      <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">Submit</CButton>
    </CCol>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CForm,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CFormSelect,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
} from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

You can then remix that once again with size-specific column classes.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row gx-4 gy-3 align-items-center">
    <CCol sm="3">
      <CFormLabel class="visually-hidden" for="specificSizeInputName">Name</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput id="specificSizeInputName" placeholder="Jane Doe" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol sm="3">
      <CFormLabel class="visually-hidden" for="specificSizeInputGroupUsername">Username</CFormLabel>
      <CInputGroup>
        <CInputGroupText>@</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput id="specificSizeInputGroupUsername" placeholder="Username" />
      </CInputGroup>
    </CCol>
    <CCol sm="3">
      <CFormLabel class="visually-hidden" for="specificSizeSelect">Preference</CFormLabel>
      <CFormSelect id="specificSizeSelect">
        <option>Choose...</option>
        <option value="1">One</option>
        <option value="2">Two</option>
        <option value="3">Three</option>
      </CFormSelect>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="auto">
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="autoSizingCheck2" label="Remember me" />
      </CFormField>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="auto">
      <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">Submit</CButton>
    </CCol>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CForm,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CFormSelect,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
} from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Inline forms

Use the `<CCol xs="auto">` class to create horizontal layouts. By adding [gutter modifier classes](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/layout/gutters/), we will have gutters in horizontal and vertical directions. The `.align-items-center` aligns the form elements to the middle, making the `<CCheckbox>` align properly.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row row-cols-lg-auto g-4 align-items-center">
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CFormLabel class="visually-hidden" for="inlineFormInputGroupUsername">Username</CFormLabel>
      <CInputGroup>
        <CInputGroupText>@</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput id="inlineFormInputGroupUsername" placeholder="Username" />
      </CInputGroup>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CFormLabel class="visually-hidden" for="inlineFormSelectPref">Preference</CFormLabel>
      <CFormSelect id="inlineFormSelectPref">
        <option>Choose...</option>
        <option value="1">One</option>
        <option value="2">Two</option>
        <option value="3">Three</option>
      </CFormSelect>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="inlineFormCheck" label="Remember me" />
      </CFormField>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">Submit</CButton>
    </CCol>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CForm,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CFormSelect,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
} from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

# Vue Bootstrap Layout Component

> Learn how to use CoreUI’s Vue Layout component with Bootstrap styles for flexible, framework-consistent UI.

## Forms

Every group of form fields should reside in a `<CForm>` element. CoreUI provides no default styling for the `<CForm>` element, but there are some powerful browser features that are provided by default.

- New to browser forms? Consider reviewing [the MDN form docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/form) for an overview and complete list of available attributes.
- `<CButton>`s within a `<CForm>` default to `type="submit"`, so strive to be specific and always include a `type`.
- You can disable every form element within a form with the `disabled` attribute on the `<CForm>`.

Since CoreUI applies `display: block` and `width: 100%` to almost all our form controls, forms will by default stack vertically. Additional classes can be used to vary this layout on a per-form basis.

## Utilities

[Margin utilities](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/margin/) are the easiest way to add some structure to forms. They provide basic grouping of labels, controls, optional form text, and form validation messaging. We recommend sticking to `margin-bottom` utilities, and using a single direction throughout the form for consistency.

## Form grid

More complex forms can be built using our grid classes. Use these for form layouts that require multiple columns, varied widths, and additional alignment options.

```html
<template>
  <CRow>
    <CCol xs>
      <CFormInput placeholder="First name" aria-label="First name" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs>
      <CFormInput placeholder="Last name" aria-label="Last name" />
    </CCol>
  </CRow>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CRow, CCol, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Gutters

By adding [gutter modifier classes](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/layout/gutters/), you can have control over the gutter width in as well the inline as block direction.

```html
<template>
  <CRow class="g-4">
    <CCol xs>
      <CFormInput placeholder="First name" aria-label="First name" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs>
      <CFormInput placeholder="Last name" aria-label="Last name" />
    </CCol>
  </CRow>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CRow, CCol, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

More complex layouts can also be created with the grid system.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row g-4">
    <CCol md="6">
      <CFormLabel for="inputEmail4">Email</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput id="inputEmail4" type="email" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="6">
      <CFormLabel for="inputPassword4">Password</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput id="inputPassword4" type="password" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CFormLabel for="inputAddress">Address</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput id="inputAddress" placeholder="1234 Main St" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CFormLabel for="inputAddress2">Address 2</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput id="inputAddress2" placeholder="Apartment, studio, or floor" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="6">
      <CFormLabel for="inputCity">City</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput id="inputCity" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="4">
      <CFormLabel for="inputState">State</CFormLabel>
      <CFormSelect id="inputState">
        <option>Choose...</option>
        <option>...</option>
      </CFormSelect>
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="2">
      <CFormLabel for="inputZip">Zip</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput id="inputZip" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="gridCheck" label="Check me out" />
      </CFormField>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">Sign in</CButton>
    </CCol>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>

  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CForm,

  CFormSelect,

```

## Horizontal form

Create horizontal forms with the grid by adding the `.row` class to form groups and using the `.col-*-*` classes to specify the width of your labels and controls. Be sure to add `.col-form-label` to your `<CFormLabel>`s as well so they're vertically centered with their associated form controls.

At times, you maybe need to use margin or padding utilities to create that perfect alignment you need. For example, we've removed the `padding-top` on our stacked radio inputs label to better align the text baseline.

```html
<template>
  <CForm>
    <CRow class="mb-4">
      <CFormLabel for="inputEmail3" class="col-sm-2 col-form-label">Email</CFormLabel>
      <CCol sm="10">
        <CFormInput id="inputEmail3" type="email" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
    <CRow class="mb-4">
      <CFormLabel for="inputPassword3" class="col-sm-2 col-form-label">Password</CFormLabel>
      <CCol sm="10">
        <CFormInput id="inputPassword3" type="password" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
    <fieldset class="row mb-4">
      <legend class="col-form-label col-sm-2 pt-0">Radios</legend>
      <CCol sm="10">
        <CFormField>
          <CRadio id="gridRadios1" name="gridRadios" value="option1" label="First radio" checked />
        </CFormField>
        <CFormField>
          <CRadio id="gridRadios2" name="gridRadios" value="option2" label="Second radio" />
        </CFormField>
        <CFormField>
          <CRadio
            id="gridRadios3"
            name="gridRadios"
            value="option3"
            label="Third disabled radio"
            disabled
          />
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>
    </fieldset>
    <CRow class="mb-4">
      <div class="col-sm-10 offset-sm-2">
        <CFormField>
          <CCheckbox id="gridCheck1" label="Example checkbox" />
        </CFormField>
      </div>
    </CRow>
    <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">Sign in</CButton>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CForm,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CRadio,
  CRow,
} from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

### Horizontal form label sizing

Be sure to use `.col-form-label-sm` or `.col-form-label-lg` to your `<CFormLabel>`s or `<legend>`s to correctly follow the size of `.form-control-lg` and `.form-control-sm`.

```html
<template>
  <CRow class="mb-4">
    <CFormLabel for="colFormLabelSm" class="col-sm-2 col-form-label col-form-label-sm"
      >Email</CFormLabel
    >
    <CCol sm="10">
      <CFormInput
        id="colFormLabelSm"
        type="email"
        class="form-control form-control-sm"
        placeholder="col-form-label-sm"
      />
    </CCol>
  </CRow>
  <CRow class="mb-4">
    <CFormLabel for="colFormLabel" class="col-sm-2 col-form-label">Email</CFormLabel>
    <CCol sm="10">
      <CFormInput id="colFormLabel" type="email" placeholder="col-form-label" />
    </CCol>
  </CRow>
  <CRow>
    <CFormLabel for="colFormLabelLg" class="col-sm-2 col-form-label col-form-label-lg"
      >Email</CFormLabel
    >
    <CCol sm="10">
      <CFormInput
        id="colFormLabelLg"
        type="email"
        class="form-control form-control-lg"
        placeholder="col-form-label-lg"
      />
    </CCol>
  </CRow>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CRow, CFormLabel, CCol, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Column sizing

As shown in the previous examples, our grid system allows you to place any number of `<CCol>`s within a `<CRow>`. They'll split the available width equally between them. You may also pick a subset of your columns to take up more or less space, while the remaining `<CCol>`s equally split the rest, with specific column classes like `<CCol sm="7">`.

```html
<template>
  <CRow class="g-4">
    <CCol sm="7">
      <CFormInput placeholder="City" aria-label="City" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol sm>
      <CFormInput placeholder="State" aria-label="State" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol sm>
      <CFormInput placeholder="Zip" aria-label="Zip" />
    </CCol>
  </CRow>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CRow, CCol, CFormInput } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Auto-sizing

The example below uses a flexbox utility to vertically center the contents and changes `<CCol>` to `<CCol xs="auto">` so that your columns only take up as much space as needed. Put another way, the column sizes itself based on the contents.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row gy-3 gx-4 align-items-center">
    <CCol xs="auto">
      <CFormLabel class="visually-hidden" for="autoSizingInput">Name</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput id="autoSizingInput" placeholder="Jane Doe" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="auto">
      <CFormLabel class="visually-hidden" for="autoSizingInputGroup">Username</CFormLabel>
      <CInputGroup>
        <CInputGroupText>@</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput id="autoSizingInputGroup" placeholder="Username" />
      </CInputGroup>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="auto">
      <CFormLabel class="visually-hidden" for="autoSizingSelect">Preference</CFormLabel>
      <CFormSelect id="autoSizingSelect">
        <option>Choose...</option>
        <option value="1">One</option>
        <option value="2">Two</option>
        <option value="3">Three</option>
      </CFormSelect>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="auto">
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="autoSizingCheck" label="Remember me" />
      </CFormField>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="auto">
      <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">Submit</CButton>
    </CCol>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CForm,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CFormSelect,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
} from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

You can then remix that once again with size-specific column classes.

# Vue Form Validation

> Provide valuable, actionable feedback to your users with HTML5 form validation, via browser default behaviors or custom styles and JavaScript.

## Example

For custom CoreUI form validation messages, add the `validate` and `novalidate` properties to your `<CForm>`. The `validate` property renders the `data-coreui-validate` attribute, which opts in to the `:user-invalid` styling — validation styles appear only after the user interacts with a control or attempts to submit, so required fields don't show up as invalid on page load. Pass `validate="valid"` to also show success styling for valid fields. `novalidate` disables the browser default feedback tooltips and hands their job to `<CForm>`. Try to submit the form below.

When the form is submitted with an invalid control, `<CForm>` stops the submit, so the `submit` event is emitted only for a submit that goes through, as with the browser's own validation, and `@submit.prevent` stays safe to use. It marks every invalid control with `.is-invalid` and `aria-invalid="true"`, and adds the message the stylesheet shows for it to its `aria-describedby` while it stays invalid, so a screen reader reads the error with the field. Then it moves focus to the first invalid control, as the browser does. Under `validate="valid"` the valid controls get `.is-valid`. The state follows the corrections the user makes until the form is reset. A message placed where the stylesheet does not show it for the control can be named in `data-coreui-invalid-feedback` on the control. A [`CAutocomplete`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/autocomplete/#validation), a [`CMultiSelect`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/multi-select/#validation), a [`CChipInput`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/chip-input/#validation), a [`CCombobox`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/combobox/#validation), a [`COneTimePassword`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/one-time-password-input/#validation), the [date and time fields](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/date-input/#validation) and the [date](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/date-picker/#validation), [time](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/time-picker/#validation) and [range](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/date-range-picker/#validation) pickers show the state on their frame and on the control that takes the focus, and `<CForm>` leaves the field that carries their value to them. So does a [`CRangeSlider`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/range-slider/#validation), with its handles, and a [`CRating`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/rating/#validation), with its radios.

Custom feedback styles apply custom colors, borders and focus styles to communicate feedback.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row g-4" novalidate validate="valid">
    <CCol md="4">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationCustom01"
        feedback-valid="Looks good!"
        label="First name"
        required
        value="Mark"
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="4">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationCustom02"
        feedback-valid="Looks good!"
        label="Last name"
        value="Otto"
        required
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="4">
      <CFormLabel for="validationCustomUsername">Username</CFormLabel>
      <CFormField>
        <CInputGroup>
          <CInputGroupText id="inputGroupPrepend">@</CInputGroupText>
          <CFormInput id="validationCustomUsername" aria-describedby="inputGroupPrepend" required />
        </CInputGroup>
        <CFormFeedback validation-state="invalid">Please choose a username.</CFormFeedback>
      </CFormField>
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="6">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationCustom03"
        feedback-invalid="Please provide a valid city."
        label="City"
        required
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="3">
      <CFormSelect
        id="validationCustom04"
        feedback-invalid="Please select a valid state."
        label="State"
        required
      >
        <option selected="" disabled="" value="">Choose...</option>
        <option>...</option>
      </CFormSelect>
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="3">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationCustom05"
        feedback-invalid="Please provide a valid zip."
        label="Zip"
        required
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="invalidCheck" label="Agree to terms and conditions" required />
        <CFormFeedback validation-state="invalid">You must agree before submitting.</CFormFeedback>
      </CFormField>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">Submit form</CButton>
    </CCol>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CForm,
  CFormFeedback,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CFormSelect,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
} from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

### Handling the result yourself

The `validate` event is emitted first, with `isValid` telling whether every control passed. A validity a listener sets with `setCustomValidity()`, for example when two passwords differ, counts for the rest of the validation. A listener that moves focus to an element already on the page keeps it there; `<CForm>` still marks the controls and stops an invalid submit. A listener that calls `preventDefault()` takes the whole result over: `<CForm>` then neither stops the submit, nor marks the controls, nor moves focus, and `submit` is emitted, so stop an invalid submit there yourself. Keep `event.isValid` for that rather than calling `checkValidity()`: the call reports every invalid control again, and the components that follow those reports, such as `CMultiSelect` or the date fields, then show their error. Do that for an error summary that renders only after the `validate` event, and move focus to it once it is rendered. A submit from a button with `formnovalidate` is not validated.

```vue
<CForm
  validate
  novalidate
  @validate="(event) => { event.preventDefault(); isValid = event.isValid; showErrorSummary(event.form, event.isValid) }"
  @submit="(event) => { if (!isValid) event.preventDefault() }"
>
  <!-- controls -->
</CForm>
```

## Custom validation

In case you require custom or server-side validation, set the state yourself with the `validation-state` property: `"valid"` or `"invalid"` renders the matching `is-*` class, and `"invalid"` also sets `aria-invalid` on the control. Any custom state you add to the `$form-validation-states` Sass map — `"warning"`, say — is accepted the same way. `"invalid"` also blocks the submit until it is cleared, with the text of the control's invalid feedback as the message the browser shows. A disabled control is not blocked, nor is a read-only text field, since the browser leaves them out of the validation. A control the user cannot reach, such as one in a hidden tab or a collapsed section, still blocks while the browser has nowhere to show its message, so clear the state of a field you hide. A state you give is a verdict on the value it was given for, so when the user changes the value, or the form is reset, the control emits `update:validationState` with `undefined`; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop the state and let the browser's own validation show again, as the example below does. Only the radio the user checks hears the change, so give a radio group's state to every radio in it. The fields that build their own markup, such as [`CAutocomplete`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/autocomplete/#validation), [`CMultiSelect`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/multi-select/#validation), [`CChipInput`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/chip-input/#validation), [`CCombobox`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/combobox/#validation), [`COneTimePassword`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/one-time-password-input/#validation), the date and time fields and the pickers, work the same way and describe the details on their pages.

Pair it with the `feedback` property: the message is rendered only while a state is set, styled after that state, and added to the control's `aria-describedby` after any `id` you pass there. `feedback-valid` and `feedback-invalid` belong to the client-side mode above, where the browser decides the state and the stylesheet reveals the matching message. The control watches the same `:user-invalid` and `:user-valid` states the stylesheet reveals the messages by, so it is described by `feedback-invalid` while the invalid message shows and by `feedback-valid` while the valid one does. A field the form reports invalid through `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()` counts as reported until the form is reset, even before the user touches it: whenever its value is invalid it gets `aria-invalid` and is described by `feedback-invalid`, just as after the user has edited it. The [Stepper](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/stepper/#form-validation) relies on this when a step fails, so call `checkValidity()` only when the page shows the errors. The date and time fields and the pickers follow their own verdict the same way; the browser judges them by whether a `required` one holds a date they accept, and blocks them while a state you give is `"invalid"`. A `validation-state` you set takes precedence over the state the browser or the field reports.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row g-4">
    <CCol md="4">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationServer01"
        v-model="email"
        feedback="Looks good!"
        label="Email"
        required
        v-model:validation-state="states.email"
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="4">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationServer02"
        v-model="repeatEmail"
        feedback="Looks good!"
        label="Repeat email"
        required
        v-model:validation-state="states.repeatEmail"
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="4">
      <CFormLabel for="validationServerUsername">Username</CFormLabel>
      <CFormField>
        <CInputGroup>
          <CInputGroupText id="inputGroupPrepend03">@</CInputGroupText>
          <CFormInput
            id="validationServerUsername"
            aria-describedby="inputGroupPrepend03 validationServerUsernameFeedback"
            v-model:validation-state="states.username"
            required
          />
        </CInputGroup>
        <CFormFeedback id="validationServerUsernameFeedback" validation-state="invalid">
          Please choose a username.
        </CFormFeedback>
      </CFormField>
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="6">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationServer03"
        feedback="Please provide a valid city."
        v-model:validation-state="states.city"
        label="City"
        required
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="3">
      <CFormSelect
        id="validationServer04"
        feedback="Please select a valid state."
        v-model:validation-state="states.state"
        label="State"
      >
        <option selected disabled value="">Choose...</option>
        <option>...</option>
      </CFormSelect>
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="3">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationServer05"
        feedback="Please provide a valid zip."
        v-model:validation-state="states.zip"
        label="zip"
        required
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox
          id="invalidCheck"
          v-model:validation-state="states.terms"
          label="Agree to terms and conditions"
          required
        />
        <CFormFeedback validation-state="invalid">You must agree before submitting.</CFormFeedback>
      </CFormField>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">Submit form</CButton>
    </CCol>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>

  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
```

## Form components

[`CMultiSelect`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/multi-select/#validation), [`CChipInput`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/chip-input/#validation), [`CCombobox`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/combobox/#validation), [`COneTimePassword`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/one-time-password-input/#validation), [`CDateInput`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/date-input/#validation), [`CTimeInput`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/time-input/#validation) and the pickers built on them keep their value in a native field laid invisibly over the component. That field carries the `name`, takes part in the browser's validation and hands the focus to the component when the browser points at it. [`CAutocomplete`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/autocomplete/#validation) validates its own input, [`CRangeSlider`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/range-slider/#validation) its handles, and [`CRating`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/rating/#validation) its radios. Each of these components shows one validation state, on its frame and on what takes the focus, and decides it in this order:

1. its own error, such as a date outside `minDate` and `maxDate` or an incomplete code;
2. the `validation-state` you give it;
3. the state a validation reports for its field: a submit, `<CForm>`, the [Stepper](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/stepper/#form-validation), or your own `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()` call;
4. `:user-invalid` or `:user-valid` of its field, in a `<CForm validate>`.

`CAutocomplete`, `CMultiSelect`, `COneTimePassword` and the pickers also take the deprecated `invalid` and `valid` props. Pass the message with the state, through `feedback` or `feedback-invalid`, so it is linked to the field when the state shows.

A given `'invalid'` blocks the submit, with the text of the component's invalid feedback as the message the browser shows, or `Invalid value.` when it has none. `'valid'` and a custom state such as `'warning'` do not block, and neither does a disabled component. A given `'valid'` shows over a reported error, but the browser's own constraints still apply, so an empty `required` field keeps blocking. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for: when the user changes the value, such as with a pick, a removed chip, the cleaner, <kbd>Backspace</kbd> or a native form reset, the component emits `update:validationState` with `undefined` before it reports the change. Bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop the state; without it, the state stays until you clear it. A change of the value from props keeps it.

You can bring your own validation in three ways:

- **Your own rules next to the browser's.** Give `validation-state` as above, or call `setCustomValidity()` on the field that carries the value, which you reach through `form.elements` by its name. The component leaves a validity you set as it is.
- **Taking the whole result over.** Call `preventDefault()` in a `validate` listener and keep `event.isValid`, as [handling the result yourself](#handling-the-result-yourself) shows. No field is reported then, so the components show only `:user-invalid` or `:user-valid` of their field, as a plain field in the same form does after a submit attempt.
- **Showing the errors.** A `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()` call reports every invalid field and each component marks itself, so make that call only when the page shows the errors.

## Supported elements

Validation styles are available for the following form controls and components:

- `<CCheckbox>`s
- `<CFormInput>`s
- `<CFormSelect>`s
- `<CFormTextarea>`s
- `<CRadio>`s

## Tooltips

If your form layout allows it, you can swap the text for the tooltip to display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. Be sure to have a parent with `position: relative` on it for tooltip positioning. In the example below, our column classes have this already, but your project may require an alternative setup.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row g-4" novalidate validate="valid">
    <CCol md="4" class="position-relative">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationTooltip01"
        feedback-valid="Looks good!"
        label="First name"
        required
        tooltip-feedback
        value="Mark"
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="4" class="position-relative">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationTooltip02"
        feedback-valid="Looks good!"
        label="Last name"
        required
        tooltip-feedback
        value="Otto"
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="4" class="position-relative">
      <CFormLabel for="validationTooltipUsername">Username</CFormLabel>
      <CFormField>
        <CInputGroup>
          <CInputGroupText id="validationTooltipUsernamePrepend">@</CInputGroupText>
          <CFormInput
            id="validationTooltipUsername"
            aria-describedby="validationTooltipUsernamePrepend"
            required
          />
        </CInputGroup>
        <CFormFeedback tooltip validation-state="invalid">Please choose a username.</CFormFeedback>
      </CFormField>
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="6" class="position-relative">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationTooltip03"
        feedback-invalid="Please provide a valid city."
        label="City"
        required
        tooltip-feedback
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="3" class="position-relative">
      <CFormSelect
        id="validationTooltip04"
        feedback-invalid="Please select a valid state."
        label="State"
        required
        tooltip-feedback
      >
        <option selected="" disabled="" value="">Choose...</option>
        <option>...</option>
      </CFormSelect>
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="3" class="position-relative">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationTooltip05"
        feedback-invalid="Please provide a valid zip."
        label="Zip"
        required
        tooltip-feedback
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12" class="position-relative">
      <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">Submit form</CButton>
    </CCol>
  </CForm>
</template>
```

# Vue Form Validation Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue form validation with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

CoreUI for Vue components use local CSS variables for validation for enhanced real-time customization. Values for the CSS variables are set via Sass, so Sass customization is still supported, too.

A validation state names a theme colour and every value is a slot of it, so the
state follows that colour in both colour modes without a second set of variables.

### Sass maps

This is the validation Sass map from `scss/mixins/_form-validation.scss`. Override or extend this to generate different or additional states.

```scss
$form-validation-states: (
  "valid": (
    "theme": "success",
  ),
  "invalid": (
    "theme": "danger",
  )
) !default;
```

Maps of `$form-validation-states` can contain three optional parameters to override tooltips and focus styles.

### Sass mixins

Two mixins are combined together, through our [loop](#sass-loops), to generate our form validation feedback styles.

```scss
@mixin form-validation-state-selector($state) {
  @if $state == "invalid" {
    [data-coreui-validate] #{if(sass(&): "&"; else: "")}:user-invalid,
    #{if(sass(&): "&"; else: "")}.is-#{$state} {
      @content;
    }
  } @else if $state == "valid" {
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] #{if(sass(&): "&"; else: "")}:user-valid,
    #{if(sass(&): "&"; else: "")}.is-#{$state} {
      @content;
    }
  } @else {
    #{if(sass(&): "&"; else: "")}.is-#{$state} {
      @content;
    }
  }
}
```

```scss
@mixin form-validation-state(
  $state,
  $theme,
  $color: var(--cui-#{$theme}-fg),
  $tooltip-color: var(--cui-#{$theme}-contrast),
  $focus-ring-color: var(--cui-#{$theme}-focus-ring),
  $border-color: var(--cui-#{$theme}-fg)
) {
  $without-error: ":not(.is-invalid, :has(.is-invalid, > :user-invalid, > .form-floating > :user-invalid))";
  $form-otp-state: ".form-otp:is(.is-#{$state}, :has(.is-#{$state}))";
  $range-without-error: "";

  @if $state != "invalid" {
    $form-otp-state: "#{$form-otp-state}#{$without-error}";
    $range-without-error: ":not(.is-invalid)";
  }

  .#{$state}-feedback {
    @include tokens($form-feedback-tokens);

    display: none;
    width: 100%;
    margin-top: var(--cui-form-feedback-margin-top);
    font-size: var(--cui-form-feedback-font-size);
    font-style: var(--cui-form-feedback-font-style, inherit);
    color: $color;
  }

  // More specific to override base tooltip styles
  .tooltip.#{$state}-tooltip,
  .#{$state}-tooltip {
    @include tokens($form-feedback-tokens);

    position: absolute;
    top: 100%;
    z-index: 5;
    display: none;
    max-width: 100%; // Contain to parent when possible
    padding: var(--cui-tooltip-padding-y, var(--cui-form-feedback-tooltip-padding-y)) var(--cui-tooltip-padding-x, var(--cui-form-feedback-tooltip-padding-x));
    margin-top: .1rem;
    font-size: var(--cui-tooltip-font-size, var(--cui-form-feedback-tooltip-font-size));
    line-height: var(--cui-form-feedback-tooltip-line-height, inherit);
    color: $tooltip-color;
    background-color: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg);
    opacity: 1;
    @include border-radius(var(--cui-tooltip-border-radius, var(--cui-form-feedback-tooltip-border-radius)));
  }

  // Generic sibling feedback display — works for .form-control, .form-range,
  // and any element where feedback is a direct sibling.
  @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
    ~ .#{$state}-feedback,
    ~ .#{$state}-tooltip {
      display: block;
    }
  }

  // Form control
  .form-control {
    @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
      --cui-control-border-color: #{$border-color};
      --cui-control-focus-border-color: #{$border-color};

      &:focus,
      &.form-date-time:focus-within {
        &:not(.form-control-group .form-control) {
          @include focus-ring(true, $color: $focus-ring-color);
        }
      }
    }
  }

  // stylelint-disable selector-no-qualifying-type
  select.form-control,
  .form-control-caret,
  .form-select {
    @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
      --cui-control-border-color: #{$border-color};
      --cui-control-focus-border-color: #{$border-color};

      &:focus:not(.form-control-group .form-control) {
        @include focus-ring(true, $color: $focus-ring-color);
      }
    }
  }
  // stylelint-enable selector-no-qualifying-type

  // Checkbox — control-level styling (border, checked bg, focus ring).
  .check {
    @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
      --cui-check-border: var(--cui-border-width) solid #{$border-color};
      --cui-check-checked-bg: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg);
      --cui-check-checked-border-color: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg);

      &:checked:not(:indeterminate) {
        background-color: var(--cui-check-checked-bg);
        border-color: var(--cui-check-checked-border-color);
      }

      &:focus-visible {
        @include focus-ring(true, $color: $focus-ring-color);
      }
    }
  }

  // Checkbox — label color and feedback display via .form-field:has().
  .form-field:has(.check.is-#{$state}) {
    label { color: $color; }

    .#{$state}-feedback,
    .#{$state}-tooltip { display: block; }
  }

  @if $state == "invalid" {
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-field:has(.check:user-invalid) {
      label { color: $color; }

      .invalid-feedback,
      .invalid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  } @else if $state == "valid" {
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] .form-field:has(.check:user-valid) {
      label { color: $color; }

      .valid-feedback,
      .valid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  }

  // Radio — control-level styling.
  .radio {
    @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
      --cui-radio-border: var(--cui-border-width) solid #{$border-color};
      --cui-radio-checked-bg: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg);
      --cui-radio-checked-border-color: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg);

      &:checked {
        background-color: var(--cui-radio-checked-bg);
        border-color: var(--cui-radio-checked-border-color);
      }

      &:focus-visible {
        @include focus-ring(true, $color: $focus-ring-color);
      }
    }
  }

  // Radio — label color and feedback display via .form-field:has().
  .form-field:has(.radio.is-#{$state}) {
    label { color: $color; }

    .#{$state}-feedback,
    .#{$state}-tooltip { display: block; }
  }

  @if $state == "invalid" {
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-field:has(.radio:user-invalid) {
      label { color: $color; }

      .invalid-feedback,
      .invalid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  } @else if $state == "valid" {
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] .form-field:has(.radio:user-valid) {
      label { color: $color; }

      .valid-feedback,
      .valid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  }

  // Switch — control-level styling.
  .switch {
    @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
      --cui-switch-border-color: #{$border-color};
      --cui-switch-checked-bg: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg);
      --cui-switch-checked-border-color: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg);

      &:checked {
        background-color: var(--cui-switch-checked-bg);
        border-color: var(--cui-switch-checked-border-color);
      }

      &:focus-visible {
        @include focus-ring(true, $color: $focus-ring-color);
      }
    }
  }

  // Switch — label color and feedback display via .form-field:has().
  .form-field:has(.switch.is-#{$state}) {
    label { color: $color; }

    .#{$state}-feedback,
    .#{$state}-tooltip { display: block; }
  }

  @if $state == "invalid" {
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-field:has(.switch:user-invalid) {
      label { color: $color; }

      .invalid-feedback,
      .invalid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  } @else if $state == "valid" {
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] .form-field:has(.switch:user-valid) {
      label { color: $color; }

      .valid-feedback,
      .valid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  }

  // The state has to reach the group: a custom property set on the control
  // inside it only inherits downwards, never back up to the frame.
  .form-control-group.is-#{$state},
  .is-#{$state} > .form-control-group,
  .form-control-group:has(> .form-control.is-#{$state}),
  .form-control-group:has(> .form-floating > .form-control.is-#{$state}) {
    @include form-control-group-validation-state($color, $border-color, $focus-ring-color);
  }

  @if $state == "invalid" {
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-control-group:has(> .form-control:user-invalid),
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-control-group:has(> .form-floating > .form-control:user-invalid),
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-control-group:has(> select:user-invalid) {
      @include form-control-group-validation-state($color, $border-color, $focus-ring-color);
    }
  } @else if $state == "valid" {
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] .form-control-group#{$without-error}:has(> .form-control:user-valid),
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] .form-control-group#{$without-error}:has(> .form-floating > .form-control:user-valid),
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] .form-control-group#{$without-error}:has(> select:user-valid) {
      @include form-control-group-validation-state($color, $border-color, $focus-ring-color);
    }
  }

  .form-control-group:where(.is-#{$state}, :has(> .is-#{$state}), :has(> .form-floating > .is-#{$state})) {
    ~ .#{$state}-feedback,
    ~ .#{$state}-tooltip { display: block; }
  }

  .form-field:where(:has(.form-control-group.is-#{$state}, .form-control-group > .is-#{$state}, .form-control-group > .form-floating > .is-#{$state})) {
    .#{$state}-feedback,
    .#{$state}-tooltip { display: block; }
  }

  @if $state == "invalid" {
    [data-coreui-validate] {
      .form-control-group:has(> :user-invalid),
      .form-control-group:has(> .form-floating > :user-invalid) {
        ~ .invalid-feedback,
        ~ .invalid-tooltip { display: block; }
      }

      .form-field:has(.form-control-group > :user-invalid),
      .form-field:has(.form-control-group > .form-floating > :user-invalid) {
        .invalid-feedback,
        .invalid-tooltip { display: block; }
      }
    }
  } @else if $state == "valid" {
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] {
      .form-control-group#{$without-error}:has(> .form-control:user-valid),
      .form-control-group#{$without-error}:has(> .form-floating > .form-control:user-valid),
      .form-control-group#{$without-error}:has(> select:user-valid) {
        ~ .valid-feedback,
        ~ .valid-tooltip { display: block; }
      }

      .form-field:not(:has(.is-invalid, :user-invalid)):has(.form-control-group > .form-control:user-valid),
      .form-field:not(:has(.is-invalid, :user-invalid)):has(.form-control-group > .form-floating > .form-control:user-valid),
      .form-field:not(:has(.is-invalid, :user-invalid)):has(.form-control-group > select:user-valid) {
        .valid-feedback,
        .valid-tooltip { display: block; }
      }
    }

    .form-control-group.is-invalid,
    .form-control-group:has(.is-invalid),
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-control-group:has(:user-invalid) {
      ~ .valid-feedback,
      ~ .valid-tooltip { display: none; }
    }

    .form-field:has(.form-control-group.is-invalid),
    .form-field:has(.form-control-group .is-invalid),
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-field:has(.form-control-group :user-invalid) {
      .valid-feedback,
      .valid-tooltip { display: none; }
    }
  }

  // Range — the validation class lives on .form-range-input, while feedback sits outside
  // the .form-range wrapper, so we use :has() to toggle it.
  .form-range-input#{$range-without-error},
  input.form-range#{$range-without-error} {
    @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
      &::-webkit-slider-thumb { background: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg); }
      &::-moz-range-thumb { background: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg); }

      &:focus-visible {
        &::-webkit-slider-thumb {
          @include focus-ring(true, $color: $focus-ring-color);
        }
        &::-moz-range-thumb {
          @include focus-ring(true, $color: $focus-ring-color);
        }
      }
    }
  }

  .form-range:has(.form-range-input.is-#{$state}) {
    ~ .#{$state}-feedback,
    ~ .#{$state}-tooltip { display: block; }
  }

  .rating.is-#{$state} .rating-item {
    --cui-theme-focus-ring: #{$focus-ring-color};
  }

  // Input group — feedback lives outside the input-group in the parent
  // .form-field, so we use :has() to toggle display.
  .form-field:where(:has(.input-group .form-control.is-#{$state}, .input-group .form-select.is-#{$state})) {
    .#{$state}-feedback,
    .#{$state}-tooltip { display: block; }
  }

  @if $state == "invalid" {
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-field:has(.input-group .form-control:user-invalid, .input-group .form-select:user-invalid) {
      .invalid-feedback,
      .invalid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  } @else if $state == "valid" {
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] .form-field:not(:has(.is-invalid, :user-invalid)):has(.input-group .form-control:user-valid, .input-group .form-select:user-valid) {
      .valid-feedback,
      .valid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  }

  .input-group {
    > .autocomplete:focus-within,
    > .date-picker:focus-within,
    > .time-picker:focus-within,
    > .form-control-group:focus-within,
    > .multi-select:focus-within,
    > .form-control:focus,
    > .form-select:focus,
    > .form-floating:focus-within {
      @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
        @if $state == "valid" {
          z-index: 3;
        } @else if $state == "invalid" {
          z-index: 4;
        }
      }
    }
  }

  .form-otp-control {
    @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
      @include form-otp-control-validation-state($border-color, $focus-ring-color);
    }
  }

  #{$form-otp-state} {
    .form-otp-control {
      @include form-otp-control-validation-state($border-color, $focus-ring-color);
    }

    ~ .#{$state}-feedback,
    ~ .#{$state}-tooltip { display: block; }
  }

  @if $state == "invalid" {
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-otp:has(:user-invalid) {
      .form-otp-control {
        @include form-otp-control-validation-state($border-color, $focus-ring-color);
      }

      ~ .invalid-feedback,
      ~ .invalid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  } @else if $state == "valid" {
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] .form-otp#{$without-error}:not(:has(:user-invalid)):has(> input:not(.form-otp-control):user-valid) {
      .form-otp-control {
        @include form-otp-control-validation-state($border-color, $focus-ring-color);
      }

      ~ .valid-feedback,
      ~ .valid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  }
}
```

### Sass loops

Used to iterate over `$form-validation-states` map values to generate our validation styles. Any modifications to the above Sass map will be reflected in your compiled CSS via this loop.

```scss
@each $state, $data in $form-validation-states {
  @include form-validation-state($state, $data...);
}
```

# Vue Bootstrap Validation Component

> Learn how to use CoreUI’s Vue Validation component with Bootstrap styles for flexible, framework-consistent UI.

## Example

For custom CoreUI form validation messages, add the `validate` and `novalidate` properties to your `<CForm>`. The `validate` property renders the `data-coreui-validate` attribute, which opts in to the `:user-invalid` styling — validation styles appear only after the user interacts with a control or attempts to submit, so required fields don't show up as invalid on page load. Pass `validate="valid"` to also show success styling for valid fields. `novalidate` disables the browser default feedback tooltips and hands their job to `<CForm>`, which stops an invalid submit, marks the invalid controls, links their messages and moves focus to the first, as described on the [validation page](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/validation/). Try to submit the form below.

Custom feedback styles apply custom colors, borders and focus styles to communicate feedback.

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row g-4" novalidate validate="valid">
    <CCol md="4">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationCustom01"
        feedback-valid="Looks good!"
        label="First name"
        required
        value="Mark"
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="4">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationCustom02"
        feedback-valid="Looks good!"
        label="Last name"
        value="Otto"
        required
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="4">
      <CFormLabel for="validationCustomUsername">Username</CFormLabel>
      <CFormField>
        <CInputGroup>
          <CInputGroupText id="inputGroupPrepend">@</CInputGroupText>
          <CFormInput id="validationCustomUsername" aria-describedby="inputGroupPrepend" required />
        </CInputGroup>
        <CFormFeedback validation-state="invalid">Please choose a username.</CFormFeedback>
      </CFormField>
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="6">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationCustom03"
        feedback-invalid="Please provide a valid city."
        label="City"
        required
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="3">
      <CFormSelect
        id="validationCustom04"
        feedback-invalid="Please select a valid state."
        label="State"
        required
      >
        <option selected="" disabled="" value="">Choose...</option>
        <option>...</option>
      </CFormSelect>
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="3">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationCustom05"
        feedback-invalid="Please provide a valid zip."
        label="Zip"
        required
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="invalidCheck" label="Agree to terms and conditions" required />
        <CFormFeedback validation-state="invalid">You must agree before submitting.</CFormFeedback>
      </CFormField>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">Submit form</CButton>
    </CCol>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>

  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
```

## Custom validation

In case you require custom or server-side validation, indicate invalid and valid form fields with the `validation-state` property. `"invalid"` also blocks the submit until it is cleared; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` to drop it when the user changes the value, as the example below does.

The `feedback`, `feedback-invalid` and `feedback-valid` messages of a form control are linked to it for you. A feedback element you add yourself, like the one below, has to be associated with the field using `aria-describedby` (noting that this attribute allows more than one `id` to be referenced, in case the field already points to additional form text).

```html
<template>
  <CForm class="row g-4">
    <CCol md="4">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationServer01"
        v-model="email"
        feedback="Looks good!"
        label="Email"
        required
        v-model:validation-state="states.email"
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="4">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationServer02"
        v-model="repeatEmail"
        feedback="Looks good!"
        label="Repeat email"
        required
        v-model:validation-state="states.repeatEmail"
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="4">
      <CFormLabel for="validationServerUsername">Username</CFormLabel>
      <CFormField>
        <CInputGroup>
          <CInputGroupText id="inputGroupPrepend03">@</CInputGroupText>
          <CFormInput
            id="validationServerUsername"
            aria-describedby="inputGroupPrepend03 validationServerUsernameFeedback"
            v-model:validation-state="states.username"
            required
          />
        </CInputGroup>
        <CFormFeedback id="validationServerUsernameFeedback" validation-state="invalid">
          Please choose a username.
        </CFormFeedback>
      </CFormField>
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="6">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationServer03"
        feedback="Please provide a valid city."
        v-model:validation-state="states.city"
        label="City"
        required
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="3">
      <CFormSelect
        id="validationServer04"
        feedback="Please select a valid state."
        v-model:validation-state="states.state"
        label="State"
      >
        <option selected disabled value="">Choose...</option>
        <option>...</option>
      </CFormSelect>
    </CCol>
    <CCol md="3">
      <CFormInput
        id="validationServer05"
        feedback="Please provide a valid zip."
        v-model:validation-state="states.zip"
        label="zip"
        required
      />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox
          id="invalidCheck"
          v-model:validation-state="states.terms"
          label="Agree to terms and conditions"
          required
        />
        <CFormFeedback validation-state="invalid">You must agree before submitting.</CFormFeedback>
      </CFormField>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="12">
      <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">Submit form</CButton>
    </CCol>
  </CForm>
</template>

<script setup>
import { reactive, ref } from 'vue'
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CForm,
  CFormFeedback,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CFormSelect,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
} from '@coreui/vue'

const email = ref('name@surname.com')
const repeatEmail = ref('name@surname.com')
const states = reactive({
  city: 'invalid',
  email: 'valid',
  repeatEmail: 'valid',
  state: 'invalid',
  terms: 'invalid',
  username: 'invalid',
  zip: 'invalid',
})
</script>
```
