# Vue Collapse Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Collapse component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CCollapse

```jsx
import { CCollapse } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hiddenUntilFound` | `boolean` | - | Hide the collapsed content with `hidden="until-found"` instead of taking it out of the layout, so the browser's find-in-page searches it and reveals it on a match. The `show` event fires when it does — set `show` from it, or the stylesheet hides the content the reader was just sent to. |
| `horizontal` | `boolean` | - | Set horizontal collapsing to transition the width instead of height. |
| `show` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Toggle the visibility of component. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the visibility of component. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `hide` | Callback fired when the component requests to be hidden. |
| `show` | Callback fired when the component requests to be shown. |

# Vue Collapse Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Collapse component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

## CSS variables

Vue Collapse supports CSS variables for easy customization. These variables are set via Sass but allow direct overrides in your stylesheets or inline styles.

The three variables are declared on both `.collapse` and `.collapsing`, so overriding them on an ancestor retimes every collapse below it.

`--cui-transition-collapse-property` names what animates. Adding to the animation is one declaration instead of a whole new `transition` — that is how `.collapse-horizontal` switches from `height` to `width`, and how the findable option adds `content-visibility`. Keep `display` in the list: it is what holds the element in the layout until the closing transition ends.

```scss
$collapse-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-transition-collapse-property: #{"block-size, display"},
    --cui-transition-collapse-duration: .35s,
    --cui-transition-collapse-timing: ease,
  ),
  $collapse-tokens
);
```

### How to use CSS variables

```vue
<template>
  <CCollapse :style="vars">...</CCollapse>
</template>

<script setup>
const vars = {
  '--cui-transition-collapse-duration': '.5s',
}
</script>
```

## Classes

Collapse transition classes can be found in `scss/_transitions.scss` as these are shared across multiple components (collapse and accordion).

```scss
// Both classes carry the tokens: `.collapsing` marks a running transition on
// either path, and find-in-page reveals the content with neither toggle
// happening.
.collapse,
.collapsing {
  @include tokens($collapse-tokens);
}

// As wide as its content, not as wide as its container: the open size is the
// animation's target, and a target of `auto` would spend most of the run
// growing an empty box past the content.
.collapse-horizontal {
  width: fit-content;
}

// The browser animates the size itself: `interpolate-size` lets the `0` of
// the closed state interpolate to the `auto` of the open one, and `display`
// transitions discretely, so the element stays laid out until the size
// reaches `0`.
@supports (interpolate-size: allow-keywords) {
  .collapse {
    interpolate-size: allow-keywords;
    @include transition-props(
      var(--cui-transition-collapse-property),
      var(--cui-transition-collapse-duration),
      var(--cui-transition-collapse-timing),
      allow-discrete
    );

    // `until-found` content is hidden by the browser instead, which keeps it
    // laid out so find-in-page can reach it. `display: none` would take it
    // back out of the layout and undo that.
    &:not(.show, [hidden="until-found"]) {
      display: none;
      height: 0;
    }

    // The box is clipped only while the move runs, so a dropdown inside an
    // open collapse can still spill out of it.
    &.collapsing {
      overflow: hidden;
    }

    // A hidden collapse is not rendered, so the opening side needs a start
    // value of its own — but only when JavaScript marks the run: a collapse
    // that loads already open must not play an entrance.
    &.show.collapsing {
      @starting-style {
        height: 0;
      }
    }

    &.collapse-horizontal {
      --cui-transition-collapse-property: width, display;

      &:not(.show, [hidden="until-found"]) {
        width: 0;
        height: auto;
      }

      &.show.collapsing {
        @starting-style {
          width: 0;
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

// Everywhere else JavaScript measures the two sizes and the stylesheet still
// times the move between them.
@supports not (interpolate-size: allow-keywords) {
  .collapse:not(.show, .collapsing, [hidden="until-found"]) {
    display: none;
  }

  .collapsing {
    height: 0;
    overflow: hidden;
    @include transition-props(
      var(--cui-transition-collapse-property),
      var(--cui-transition-collapse-duration),
      var(--cui-transition-collapse-timing)
    );

    &.collapse-horizontal {
      --cui-transition-collapse-property: width;

      width: 0;
      height: auto;
    }
  }
}
```

# Vue Bootstrap Collapse Component

> Learn how to use CoreUI’s Vue Collapse component with Bootstrap styles for flexible, framework-consistent UI.

## How it works

The collapse component is used to show and hide content. Buttons or anchors are used as triggers that are mapped to specific elements you toggle. Collapsing an element will animate the `height` from its current value to `0`. Given how CSS handles animations, you cannot use `padding` on a `.collapse` element. Instead, use the class as an independent wrapping element.

## Example

You can use a link or a button component.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" href="#" @click.prevent="visible = !visible">Link</CButton>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="visible = !visible">Button</CButton>
  <CCollapse :show="visible">
    <CCard class="mt-4">
      <CCardBody>
        Anim pariatur cliche reprehenderit, enim eiusmod high life accusamus terry richardson ad
        squid. Nihil anim keffiyeh helvetica, craft beer labore wes anderson cred nesciunt sapiente
        ea proident.
      </CCardBody>
    </CCard>
  </CCollapse>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CButton, CCollapse, CCard, CCardBody } from '@coreui/vue'
import { ref } from 'vue'
const visible = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Horizontal

The collapse plugin also supports horizontal collapsing. Add the `horizontal` property to transition the `width` instead of `height` and set a `width` on the immediate child element.

```html
<template>
  <CButton
    class="mb-4"
    theme="primary"
    aria-expanded="{visible}"
    aria-controls="collapseWidthExample"
    @click="visibleHorizontal = !visibleHorizontal"
    >Button</CButton
  >
  <div style="min-height: 120px">
    <CCollapse horizontal :show="visibleHorizontal">
      <CCard style="width: 300px">
        <CCardBody>
          This is some placeholder content for a horizontal collapse. It's hidden by default and
          shown when triggered.
        </CCardBody>
      </CCard>
    </CCollapse>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CButton, CCollapse, CCard, CCardBody } from '@coreui/vue'
import { ref } from 'vue'
const visibleHorizontal = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Multiple targets

A `<CButton>` can show and hide multiple elements.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="visibleA = !visibleA">Toggle first element</CButton>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="visibleB = !visibleB">Toggle second element</CButton>
  <CButton
    theme="primary"
    @click="
      () => {
        visibleA = !visibleA
        visibleB = !visibleB
      }
    "
  >
    Toggle both elements
  </CButton>
  <CRow>
    <CCol xs="6">
      <CCollapse :show="visibleA">
        <CCard class="mt-4">
          <CCardBody>
            Anim pariatur cliche reprehenderit, enim eiusmod high life accusamus terry richardson ad
            squid. Nihil anim keffiyeh helvetica, craft beer labore wes anderson cred nesciunt
            sapiente ea proident.
          </CCardBody>
        </CCard>
      </CCollapse>
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="6">
      <CCollapse :show="visibleB">
        <CCard class="mt-4">
          <CCardBody>
            Anim pariatur cliche reprehenderit, enim eiusmod high life accusamus terry richardson ad
            squid. Nihil anim keffiyeh helvetica, craft beer labore wes anderson cred nesciunt
            sapiente ea proident.
          </CCardBody>
        </CCard>
      </CCollapse>
    </CCol>
  </CRow>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CButton, CRow, CCol, CCollapse, CCard, CCardBody } from '@coreui/vue'
import { ref } from 'vue'
const visibleA = ref(false)
const visibleB = ref(false)
</script>
```

# Vue Dialog Component

> Vue Dialog component built on the native <dialog> element — top layer rendering, blurred native backdrop, focus trapping, and accessible semantics out of the box.

## Overview

_Added in 6.0.0._

`<CDialog>` renders a popup on the native `<dialog>` element, so accessibility, focus management and the backdrop come from the browser rather than from a custom implementation. It carries the look Bootstrap 6 introduces under the same name — a centered floating panel over a blurred backdrop.

Dialog shares its behavior with [Modal](../modal/). Modal keeps the classic look and the v5 vocabulary; Dialog carries the new look and the `dialog-*` classes. Pick one — they are independent components, and **Modal is deprecated for removal in v7**.

What the native element provides:

- **Modal or non-modal** — `modal` (default `true`) promotes the dialog to the top layer with a backdrop and focus trapping; `:modal="false"` leaves the page interactive.
- **A built-in backdrop** through the `::backdrop` pseudo-element. `backdrop="static"` locks clicks outside; `:backdrop="false"` suppresses it visually.
- **Escape handling** closes the dialog; `:keyboard="false"` disables it.
- **Accessibility** — focus is trapped inside a modal dialog and returned to the trigger on close, with no `role`, `aria-modal`, `aria-hidden` or `tabindex` in the markup.
- **Animated open and close** — the exit transition, the `::backdrop` fade included, plays in every browser, because the dialog stays in the top layer until the transition ends.

## Example

Toggle a dialog by clicking the button below.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Launch dialog</CButton>
  <CDialog v-model:show="show">
    <CDialogHeader>
      <CDialogTitle>Dialog title</CDialogTitle>
    </CDialogHeader>
    <CDialogBody>Woohoo, you are reading this text in a dialog!</CDialogBody>
    <CDialogFooter>
      <CButton theme="secondary" @click="show = false">Close</CButton>
      <CButton theme="primary">Save changes</CButton>
    </CDialogFooter>
  </CDialog>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import {
  CButton,
  CDialog,
  CDialogBody,
  CDialogFooter,
  CDialogHeader,
  CDialogTitle,
} from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Slide animations

Dialogs fade in and out by default. `animation` picks a different entry: `"slide-down"` comes in from above, `"slide-up"` from below — and the exit reverses it. The value names the variant rather than the direction, so further ones are added to the stylesheet without touching the prop.

```html
<template>
  <div class="hstack gap-3">
    <CButton theme="primary" @click="open('slide-down')">Slide down</CButton>
    <CButton theme="primary" @click="open('slide-up')">Slide up</CButton>
  </div>
  <!-- The variant is held past the close, or the exit would reverse a different entry. -->
  <CDialog v-model:show="show" :animation="animation">
    <CDialogHeader>
      <CDialogTitle>{{ animation }}</CDialogTitle>
    </CDialogHeader>
    <CDialogBody>The exit reverses the entry.</CDialogBody>
  </CDialog>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDialog, CDialogBody, CDialogHeader, CDialogTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

const animation = ref('slide-down')
const show = ref(false)

const open = (value) => {
  animation.value = value
  show.value = true
}
</script>
```

## Static backdrop

With `backdrop="static"` the dialog does not close on a click outside — it plays a scale bounce instead.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Launch static backdrop dialog</CButton>
  <CDialog v-model:show="show" backdrop="static">
    <CDialogHeader>
      <CDialogTitle>Dialog title</CDialogTitle>
    </CDialogHeader>
    <CDialogBody>
      Clicking outside plays a bounce instead of closing. Escape still closes it.
    </CDialogBody>
  </CDialog>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDialog, CDialogBody, CDialogHeader, CDialogTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Backdrop

The backdrop reads three tokens from `:root` — `--cui-backdrop-color`, `--cui-backdrop-opacity` and `--cui-backdrop-blur` — and every overlay component paints it the same way. A dialog defaults to a dark scrim; the drawer defaults to a translucent tint of the page. Pick the other look with the `backdrop-variant` prop — a [backdrop preset](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/helpers/backdrop/) on the component: `translucent` here, `scrim` on a drawer; `:backdrop="false"` on either drops the layer altogether.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Launch dialog with a translucent backdrop</CButton>
  <CDialog v-model:show="show" backdrop-variant="translucent">
    <CDialogHeader>
      <CDialogTitle>Translucent backdrop</CDialogTitle>
    </CDialogHeader>
    <CDialogBody
      >The page behind stays readable through a light tint instead of a dark scrim.</CDialogBody
    >
  </CDialog>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDialog, CDialogBody, CDialogHeader, CDialogTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Scrolling long content

Add `scrollable` to scroll the dialog body while the header and footer stay put.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Launch scrollable dialog</CButton>
  <CDialog v-model:show="show" scrollable>
    <CDialogHeader>
      <CDialogTitle>Scrollable body</CDialogTitle>
    </CDialogHeader>
    <CDialogBody>
      <p v-for="index in 20" :key="index">
        Placeholder paragraph {{ index }} — the body scrolls while the header stays put.
      </p>
    </CDialogBody>
  </CDialog>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDialog, CDialogBody, CDialogHeader, CDialogTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Toggle between dialogs

A trigger inside an open dialog can swap to another one — the backdrop stays up, so there is no flash between them. Drive both from one piece of state rather than closing the first and opening the second.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="open = 'first'">Open first dialog</CButton>

  <CDialog :show="open === 'first'" @update:show="(show) => !show && (open = undefined)">
    <CDialogHeader>
      <CDialogTitle>First dialog</CDialogTitle>
    </CDialogHeader>
    <CDialogBody>
      <CButton theme="primary" @click="open = 'second'">Open second dialog</CButton>
    </CDialogBody>
  </CDialog>

  <CDialog :show="open === 'second'" @update:show="(show) => !show && (open = undefined)">
    <CDialogHeader>
      <CDialogTitle>Second dialog</CDialogTitle>
    </CDialogHeader>
    <CDialogBody>
      <CButton theme="secondary" @click="open = 'first'">Back to the first</CButton>
    </CDialogBody>
  </CDialog>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDialog, CDialogBody, CDialogHeader, CDialogTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

const open = ref()
</script>
```

## Non-modal dialogs

Set `:modal="false"` to show the dialog without the top layer — no backdrop, no focus trap, and the rest of the page stays interactive.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Launch non-modal dialog</CButton>
  <CDialog v-model:show="show" :modal="false">
    <CDialogHeader>
      <CDialogTitle>Non-modal</CDialogTitle>
    </CDialogHeader>
    <CDialogBody>
      No backdrop, no focus trap — the rest of the page stays interactive and scrollable.
    </CDialogBody>
  </CDialog>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDialog, CDialogBody, CDialogHeader, CDialogTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Optional sizes

Dialogs have three optional sizes.

| Size | Prop | Dialog max-width |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Small | `size="sm"` | `280px` |
| Default | — | `500px` |
| Large | `size="lg"` | `800px` |
| Extra large | `size="xl"` | `1140px` |

```html
<template>
  <div class="hstack gap-3">
    <CButton v-for="value in sizes" :key="value" theme="primary" @click="open(value)">
      {{ value }} dialog
    </CButton>
  </div>
  <CDialog v-model:show="show" :size="size">
    <CDialogHeader>
      <CDialogTitle>Size {{ size }}</CDialogTitle>
    </CDialogHeader>
    <CDialogBody>Placeholder content for the dialog body.</CDialogBody>
  </CDialog>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDialog, CDialogBody, CDialogHeader, CDialogTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

const sizes = ['sm', 'lg', 'xl']
const size = ref('lg')
const show = ref(false)

const open = (value) => {
  size.value = value
  show.value = true
}
</script>
```

## Fullscreen dialog

Add `fullscreen` for a dialog that covers the viewport. Pass a breakpoint instead — `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl` or `2xl` — to cover it only below that width and keep the floating panel above it.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Fullscreen dialog</CButton>
  <CDialog v-model:show="show" fullscreen>
    <CDialogHeader>
      <CDialogTitle>Fullscreen</CDialogTitle>
    </CDialogHeader>
    <CDialogBody>The dialog covers the entire viewport.</CDialogBody>
  </CDialog>
</template>

<script setup>

import { CButton, CDialog, CDialogBody, CDialogHeader, CDialogTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Dark variant

Add `dark` and the dialog flips the tokens its own surface reads, so the dialog and everything in it — including the close button — turns dark on a light page.

```html

  <CDialog v-model:show="show" dark>
    <CDialogHeader>
      <CDialogTitle>Dark dialog</CDialogTitle>
    </CDialogHeader>
    <CDialogBody>The surface, the text and the dividers all read the flipped tokens.</CDialogBody>
  </CDialog>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDialog, CDialogBody, CDialogHeader, CDialogTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

</script>
```

## Usage with v-model

Bind `v-model:show` and the dialog renders exactly what your state says — dismiss gestures only emit `update:show`, and nothing closes until you flip the prop. That makes confirm-before-close possible: instead of feeding a close request straight back (which is what `v-model:show` does), ask first.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Launch dialog</CButton>
  <CDialog :show="show" @update:show="handleShowChange">
    <CDialogHeader>
      <CDialogTitle>Unsaved changes</CDialogTitle>
    </CDialogHeader>
    <CDialogBody>
      {{
        confirming
          ? 'Close without saving? Your changes will be lost.'
          : 'Try to close this dialog with Escape or a click on the backdrop — it will ask first.'
      }}
    </CDialogBody>
    <CDialogFooter>
      <template v-if="confirming">
        <CButton theme="secondary" @click="confirming = false">Keep editing</CButton>
        <CButton theme="danger" @click="close">Discard and close</CButton>
      </template>
      <CButton v-else theme="primary" @click="close">Save and close</CButton>
    </CDialogFooter>
  </CDialog>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import {
  CButton,
  CDialog,
  CDialogBody,
  CDialogFooter,
  CDialogHeader,
  CDialogTitle,
} from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
const confirming = ref(false)

const handleShowChange = (nextShow) => {
  if (!nextShow) {
    confirming.value = true
    return
  }

  show.value = nextShow
}

const close = () => {
  confirming.value = false
  show.value = false
}
</script>
```

Use it when closing has consequences — unsaved form input, an interrupted upload — or when the open state belongs to something else, like a route.

### Initial open state

Give the dialog a starting point and let it close itself — dismiss gestures are handled internally.

```vue
<CDialog show>
```

`update:show` fires either way whenever the dialog requests an open-state change — a dismiss gesture (Escape, a click on the backdrop) or any internal toggle — so you can watch the state without taking it over. The deprecated `visible` prop keeps its old behavior and is ignored when `show` is set.

## Accessibility

The native `<dialog>` carries the semantics: a modal dialog traps focus, marks the rest of the page inert and returns focus to the trigger on close, and it is exposed as a dialog to assistive technology without any ARIA attribute of ours. Give the dialog an accessible name by pointing `aria-labelledby` at your `<CDialogTitle>`.

## API

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

- [&lt;CDialog /&gt;](./api/#cdialog)

- [&lt;CDialogFooter /&gt;](./api/#cdialogfooter)
- [&lt;CDialogHeader /&gt;](./api/#cdialogheader)
- [&lt;CDialogTitle /&gt;](./api/#cdialogtitle)

# Vue Dialog Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Dialog component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CDialog

```jsx
import { CDialog } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animation` | `boolean\|string` | `true` | How the dialog comes in. Left out it fades in place, `false` turns the animation off, and a variant name picks one — the value names the variant, so further ones are added to the stylesheet rather than to this prop. |
| `backdrop` | `boolean\|string` | `true` | Apply a backdrop while the dialog is open. `'static'` keeps the dialog open on a backdrop click and bounces it instead. |
| `backdropVariant` | `string` | - | Pick the backdrop's look: the dark scrim or the translucent tint of the page. Left out, the component keeps its own default. |
| `dark` | `boolean` | - | Flip the dialog to the dark color mode, whatever the page around it uses. |
| `fullscreen` | `boolean\|string` | - | Cover the whole viewport — always with `true`, or only below the given breakpoint. |
| `keyboard` | `boolean` | `true` | Closes the dialog when escape key is pressed. |
| `modal` | `boolean` | `true` | Open the dialog modally, taking over the page. Set it to `false` for a dialog that leaves the rest of the page interactive. |
| `scrollable` | `boolean` | - | Create a scrollable dialog that allows scrolling the dialog body. |
| `show` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Control the open state. When set, the dialog renders what `show` says and dismiss gestures only emit `update:show` — nothing closes until the parent flips the prop. |
| `size` | `string` | - | Size the component small, large, or extra large. |
| `unmountOnClose` | `boolean` | `true` | By default the component is unmounted after close animation, if you want to keep the component mounted set this property to false. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Toggle the visibility of the dialog component. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `close` | Callback fired once the component has closed. |
| `close-prevented` | Callback fired when the dialog is shown, its backdrop is static and a click outside the dialog or an escape key press is performed with the keyboard option set to false. |
| `show` | Callback fired when the component requests to be shown. |
| `update:show` | Callback fired when the dialog requests an open-state change — a dismiss gesture (Escape, backdrop click) or any internal toggle. In controlled mode update `show` yourself, or the dialog stays as it is. |

# Vue Dialog Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Dialog component with CSS variables and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

## CSS variables

Vue Dialog supports CSS variables for easy customization. These variables are set via Sass but allow direct overrides in your stylesheets or inline styles.

```scss
$dialog-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-dialog-zindex: var(--cui-z-dialog),
    --cui-dialog-padding-y: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-dialog-padding-x: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-dialog-width: 500px,
    --cui-dialog-margin: 1.75rem,
    --cui-dialog-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-dialog-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-dialog-border-color: var(--cui-border-color-translucent),
    --cui-dialog-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-dialog-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-dialog-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow-lg),
    --cui-dialog-transition-property: #{"opacity, transform, visibility"},
    --cui-dialog-transition-duration: .3s,
    --cui-dialog-transition-timing: var(--cui-transition-timing-overlay),
    --cui-dialog-backdrop-bg: color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-backdrop-color) var(--cui-backdrop-opacity), transparent),
    --cui-dialog-backdrop-blur: var(--cui-backdrop-blur),
    --cui-dialog-header-padding-y: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-dialog-header-padding-x: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-dialog-header-border-color: var(--cui-border-color-translucent),
    --cui-dialog-header-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-dialog-title-line-height: var(--cui-body-line-height),
    --cui-dialog-footer-padding-y: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-dialog-footer-padding-x: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-dialog-footer-border-color: var(--cui-border-color-translucent),
    --cui-dialog-footer-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-dialog-footer-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-dialog-slide-distance: 3rem,
    --cui-dialog-scale-transform: scale(1.02),
  ),
  $dialog-tokens
);
```

### How to use CSS variables

```vue
<template>
  <CDialog :style="customVars" />
</template>

<script setup>
const customVars = {
  '--cui-dialog-bg': '#f8f9fa',
  '--cui-dialog-border-radius': '1rem',
}
</script>
```

The three optional sizes come from a map, so a size the map does not name is one entry rather than a new rule.

```scss
$dialog-sizes: () !default;
$dialog-sizes: defaults(
  (
    sm: 280px,
    lg: 800px,
    xl: 1140px,
  ),
  $dialog-sizes
);
```

# Vue Drawer Component

> Vue Drawer component built on the native <dialog> element — a floating side panel with top layer rendering, a native backdrop and accessible semantics out of the box.

## Overview

_Added in 6.0.0._

`<CDrawer>` is a panel that slides in from an edge of the viewport, built on the native `<dialog>` element. It carries the look Bootstrap 6 introduces under the same name — a floating, inset, rounded panel.

Drawer shares its behavior with [Offcanvas](../offcanvas/). Offcanvas keeps the classic look and the v5 vocabulary; Drawer carries the new look and the `drawer-*` classes. Pick one — they are independent components, and **Offcanvas is deprecated for removal in v7**.

## Example

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Toggle drawer</CButton>
  <CDrawer v-model:show="show" placement="start">
    <CDrawerHeader>
      <CDrawerTitle>Drawer</CDrawerTitle>
    </CDrawerHeader>
    <CDrawerBody>Content for the drawer goes here.</CDrawerBody>
  </CDrawer>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDrawer, CDrawerBody, CDrawerHeader, CDrawerTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Placement

Drawers can slide in from any edge of the viewport — `placement` picks which one:

- `placement="start"` — left side of the viewport (shown above)
- `placement="end"` — right side of the viewport
- `placement="top"` — top of the viewport
- `placement="bottom"` — bottom of the viewport
- `fullscreen` — covers the viewport (minus the inset), and needs no placement

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Right drawer</CButton>
  <CDrawer v-model:show="show" placement="end">
    <CDrawerHeader>
      <CDrawerTitle>Drawer right</CDrawerTitle>
      <CCloseButton @click="show = false" />
    </CDrawerHeader>
    <CDrawerBody>Content for the drawer goes here.</CDrawerBody>
  </CDrawer>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import {
  CButton,
  CCloseButton,
  CDrawer,
  CDrawerBody,
  CDrawerHeader,
  CDrawerTitle,
} from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Top drawer</CButton>
  <CDrawer v-model:show="show" placement="top">
    <CDrawerHeader>
      <CDrawerTitle>Drawer top</CDrawerTitle>
      <CCloseButton @click="show = false" />
    </CDrawerHeader>
    <CDrawerBody>Content for the drawer goes here.</CDrawerBody>
  </CDrawer>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import {
  CButton,
  CCloseButton,
  CDrawer,
  CDrawerBody,
  CDrawerHeader,
  CDrawerTitle,
} from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

```html

  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Bottom drawer</CButton>
  <CDrawer v-model:show="show" placement="bottom">
    <CDrawerHeader>
      <CDrawerTitle>Drawer bottom</CDrawerTitle>
      <CCloseButton @click="show = false" />
    </CDrawerHeader>
    <CDrawerBody>Content for the drawer goes here.</CDrawerBody>
```

```html
const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Variants

`sheet` drops the inset and the rounded corners so the panel sits flush against the edge, `translucent` blurs what is behind it, `fitContent` sizes it to its content, and `fullscreen` covers the viewport.

```html
<template>
  <div class="hstack gap-3 flex-wrap">
    <CButton v-for="value in variants" :key="value" theme="primary" @click="open(value)">
      {{ value }}
    </CButton>
  </div>
  <CDrawer v-model:show="show" placement="end" v-bind="{ [variant]: true }">
    <CDrawerHeader>
      <CDrawerTitle>{{ variant }}</CDrawerTitle>
    </CDrawerHeader>
    <CDrawerBody>Placeholder content for the drawer body.</CDrawerBody>
  </CDrawer>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDrawer, CDrawerBody, CDrawerHeader, CDrawerTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

const variants = ['sheet', 'translucent', 'fitContent', 'fullscreen']
const variant = ref('sheet')
const show = ref(false)

const open = (value) => {
  variant.value = value
  show.value = true
}
</script>
```

### Footer

Add a `<CDrawerFooter>` below the `<CDrawerBody>` for the panel's actions. It is a flex row that wraps and keeps its children spaced and vertically centered, so a row of buttons needs no utilities.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Toggle drawer with footer</CButton>
  <CDrawer v-model:show="show" placement="end">
    <CDrawerHeader>
      <CDrawerTitle>Drawer with footer</CDrawerTitle>
    </CDrawerHeader>
    <CDrawerBody>Placeholder content for the drawer body.</CDrawerBody>
    <CDrawerFooter>
      <CButton theme="secondary" variant="outline" @click="show = false">Close</CButton>
      <CButton theme="primary">Save changes</CButton>
    </CDrawerFooter>
  </CDrawer>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import {
  CButton,
  CDrawer,
  CDrawerBody,
  CDrawerFooter,
  CDrawerHeader,
  CDrawerTitle,
} from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

### Backdrop presets

The backdrop reads `--cui-backdrop-color`, `--cui-backdrop-opacity` and `--cui-backdrop-blur`; a drawer defaults to a translucent tint of the page. For the dialog's dark scrim set `backdrop-variant="scrim"`; the [presets](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/helpers/backdrop/) work on every overlay component.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Toggle drawer with a dark backdrop</CButton>
  <CDrawer v-model:show="show" backdrop-variant="scrim" placement="start">
    <CDrawerHeader>
      <CDrawerTitle>Dark backdrop</CDrawerTitle>
    </CDrawerHeader>
    <CDrawerBody>The scrim the dialog uses, on a drawer.</CDrawerBody>
  </CDrawer>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDrawer, CDrawerBody, CDrawerHeader, CDrawerTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

### No backdrop

Set `:backdrop="false"` to hide the backdrop while keeping the drawer modal — the panel still takes the top layer and traps focus, but nothing dims the page behind it. Pair it with `scroll` to make the drawer non-modal instead.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Drawer without a backdrop</CButton>
  <CDrawer v-model:show="show" :backdrop="false" placement="end">
    <CDrawerHeader>
      <CDrawerTitle>No backdrop</CDrawerTitle>
    </CDrawerHeader>
    <CDrawerBody>Nothing dims the page, but focus is still trapped here.</CDrawerBody>
  </CDrawer>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDrawer, CDrawerBody, CDrawerHeader, CDrawerTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

### Instant

Set `:animation="false"` on a drawer that should appear and disappear at once, with no slide and no backdrop fade — it renders with `.drawer-instant`, and it applies to both directions.

### Dark

Add `dark` and the drawer flips the tokens its own surface reads, so the panel and everything in it — including the close button — turns dark on a light page.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Dark drawer</CButton>
  <CDrawer v-model:show="show" dark placement="end">
    <CDrawerHeader>
      <CDrawerTitle>Dark drawer</CDrawerTitle>
    </CDrawerHeader>
    <CDrawerBody>The surface, the text and the dividers all read the flipped tokens.</CDrawerBody>
  </CDrawer>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDrawer, CDrawerBody, CDrawerHeader, CDrawerTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Body scrolling

A visible backdrop needs the top layer, so `scroll` alone only unlocks the page scroll. Pair it with `:backdrop="false"` and the drawer opens **non-modally** — the page behind it stays interactive as well as scrollable.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Enable body scrolling</CButton>
  <CDrawer v-model:show="show" placement="start" scroll :backdrop="false">
    <CDrawerHeader>
      <CDrawerTitle>Body scrolling</CDrawerTitle>
    </CDrawerHeader>
    <CDrawerBody>
      Without a backdrop the drawer opens non-modally, so the page behind it stays interactive and
      scrollable.
    </CDrawerBody>
  </CDrawer>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDrawer, CDrawerBody, CDrawerHeader, CDrawerTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Static backdrop

With `backdrop="static"` the drawer does not close on a click outside — it plays a bounce instead.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Toggle static drawer</CButton>
  <CDrawer v-model:show="show" placement="start" backdrop="static">
    <CDrawerHeader>
      <CDrawerTitle>Static backdrop</CDrawerTitle>
    </CDrawerHeader>
    <CDrawerBody>Clicking outside plays a bounce instead of closing.</CDrawerBody>
  </CDrawer>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDrawer, CDrawerBody, CDrawerHeader, CDrawerTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Responsive

`responsive` keeps the content in the page from the given breakpoint up, and turns it into a drawer below it. Once the window grows past the breakpoint, an open drawer asks to close through `update:show`: uncontrolled it closes, with `v-model:show` it waits for your state.

```html
<template>
  <CButton class="d-lg-none" theme="primary" @click="show = true">
    Toggle responsive drawer
  </CButton>
  <CDrawer v-model:show="show" placement="start" responsive="lg">
    <CDrawerHeader>
      <CDrawerTitle>Responsive drawer</CDrawerTitle>
    </CDrawerHeader>
    <CDrawerBody>
      Below <code>lg</code> this is a drawer; from <code>lg</code> up the content sits in the page.
    </CDrawerBody>
  </CDrawer>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDrawer, CDrawerBody, CDrawerHeader, CDrawerTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Usage with v-model

Bind `v-model:show` and the drawer renders exactly what your state says — dismiss gestures only emit `update:show`, so feed the change back, or nothing closes — `v-model:show` is that loop in one attribute.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" @click="show = true">Open drawer</CButton>
  <CDrawer placement="end" :show="show" @update:show="(value) => (show = value)">
    <CDrawerHeader>
      <CDrawerTitle>Controlled drawer</CDrawerTitle>
    </CDrawerHeader>
    <CDrawerBody>
      The drawer renders what the state says. Escape and the backdrop click land in
      <code>update:show</code>, and feeding them back is what closes the panel.
    </CDrawerBody>
  </CDrawer>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDrawer, CDrawerBody, CDrawerHeader, CDrawerTitle } from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

Use it when the open state belongs to something else — a route, a filter panel toggled from a toolbar, a cart the whole page reads — or when closing should be intercepted first.

### Initial open state

Give the drawer a starting point and let it close itself.

```vue
<CDrawer show placement="end">
```

`update:show` fires either way whenever the drawer requests an open-state change — a dismiss gesture (Escape, a click on the backdrop) or any internal toggle. The deprecated `visible` prop keeps its old behavior and is ignored when `show` is set.

## Accessibility

The native `<dialog>` carries the semantics: a modal drawer traps focus, marks the rest of the page inert and returns focus to the trigger on close, without any ARIA attribute of ours. Give the drawer an accessible name by pointing `aria-labelledby` at your `<CDrawerTitle>`.

## API

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

- [&lt;CDrawer /&gt;](./api/#cdrawer)
- [&lt;CDrawerBody /&gt;](./api/#cdrawerbody)
- [&lt;CDrawerFooter /&gt;](./api/#cdrawerfooter)
- [&lt;CDrawerHeader /&gt;](./api/#cdrawerheader)
- [&lt;CDrawerTitle /&gt;](./api/#cdrawertitle)

# Vue Drawer Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Drawer component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CDrawer

```jsx
import { CDrawer } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animation` | `boolean` | `true` | How the drawer comes in. Left out it slides in from its placement; `false` turns the animation off. |
| `backdrop` | `boolean\|string` | `true` | Apply a backdrop while the drawer is open. `'static'` keeps it open on a backdrop click and bounces it instead. |
| `backdropVariant` | `string` | - | Pick the backdrop's look: the dark scrim or the translucent tint of the page. Left out, the component keeps its own default. |
| `dark` | `boolean` | - | Flip the drawer to the dark color mode, whatever the page around it uses. |
| `fitContent` | `boolean` | - | Size the drawer to its content instead of the full edge. |
| `fullscreen` | `boolean` | - | Set the drawer to cover the entire user viewport. |
| `keyboard` | `boolean` | `true` | Closes the drawer when escape key is pressed. |
| `placement` | `string` | - | The edge the drawer slides in from. A `fullscreen` drawer covers the viewport and needs none. |
| `responsive` | `boolean\|string` | `true` | Hide the drawer outside the viewport from a specified breakpoint and down. |
| `scroll` | `boolean` | `false` | Allow the page behind the drawer to scroll. |
| `sheet` | `boolean` | - | Drop the inset and the rounded corners, so the drawer sits flush against the edge. |
| `show` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Control the open state. When set, the drawer renders what `show` says and dismiss gestures only emit `update:show` — nothing closes until the parent flips the prop. |
| `translucent` | `boolean` | - | Blur and saturate whatever is behind the drawer. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Toggle the visibility of the drawer component. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `close` | Callback fired once the component has closed. |
| `close-prevented` | Callback fired when a static backdrop or a disabled `keyboard` refuses a close request. |
| `show` | Callback fired when the component requests to be shown. |
| `update:show` | Callback fired when the drawer requests an open-state change — a dismiss gesture (Escape, backdrop click) or any internal toggle. In controlled mode update `show` yourself, or the drawer stays as it is. |

## CDrawerBody

```jsx

```

## CDrawerFooter

```jsx
import { CDrawerFooter } from '@coreui/vue'
```

## CDrawerHeader

```jsx

```


# Vue Drawer Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Drawer component with CSS variables and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

## CSS variables

Vue Drawer supports CSS variables for easy customization. These variables are set via Sass but allow direct overrides in your stylesheets or inline styles.

```scss
$drawer-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-drawer-inset: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-drawer-zindex: var(--cui-z-drawer),
    --cui-drawer-width: 400px,
    --cui-drawer-height: 30vh,
    --cui-drawer-sheet-width: 760px,
    --cui-drawer-padding-x: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-drawer-padding-y: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-drawer-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-drawer-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-drawer-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-drawer-border-color: var(--cui-border-color-translucent),
    --cui-drawer-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-drawer-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow-lg),
    --cui-drawer-transition-property: #{"transform, visibility"},
    --cui-drawer-transition-duration: .3s,
    --cui-drawer-transition-timing: var(--cui-transition-timing-overlay),
    --cui-drawer-title-line-height: var(--cui-body-line-height),
    --cui-drawer-body-gap: var(--cui-drawer-padding-y),
    --cui-drawer-footer-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-backdrop-color: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-backdrop-opacity: 25%,
    --cui-drawer-backdrop-bg: color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-backdrop-color) var(--cui-backdrop-opacity), transparent),
    --cui-drawer-backdrop-blur: var(--cui-backdrop-blur),
    --cui-drawer-scale-transform: scale(1.02),
  ),
  $drawer-tokens
);
```

```vue
  '--cui-drawer-inset': '1rem',
}

```

# Vue Context Menu Component

> Vue Context Menu opens a menu at the pointer on right-click or the keyboard's Menu key - built on the Menu component with the same items, submenus, keyboard navigation and dismissal.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Overview

_Added in 6.0.0._

Context menus replace the browser's native menu on an element with a [Menu](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/menu/). `<CContextMenu>` renders the trigger area; put the content in it and a `<CMenuContent>` next to it. A right-click (or <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd> / the <kbd>Menu</kbd> key when the area has focus) opens the menu at the pointer, and every menu feature - items, icons, dividers, headers, submenus and the keyboard navigation - works unchanged.

```html
<template>
  <CContextMenu class="border rounded-3 p-6 text-center fg-2" tabindex="0">
    Right-click anywhere in this area
    <CMenuContent>
      <CMenuItem>Copy</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuItem>Cut</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuItem>Paste</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuDivider />
      <CMenuItem theme="danger">Delete</CMenuItem>
    </CMenuContent>
  </CContextMenu>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CContextMenu, CMenuContent, CMenuDivider, CMenuItem } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

Context menus are built on a third party library, [Floating UI](https://floating-ui.com/), which keeps the menu inside the viewport: it flips above the pointer near the bottom edge and shifts sideways near the right one.

## Examples

### Submenus

Submenus work as in [Menu](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/menu/#submenus): wrap a `<CMenuItem>` trigger and a nested `<CMenuContent>` in a `<CSubmenu>`.

```html
<template>
  <CContextMenu class="border rounded-3 p-6 text-center fg-2" tabindex="0">
    Right-click to see the submenus
    <CMenuContent>
      <CSubmenu>
        <CMenuItem>New</CMenuItem>
        <CMenuContent>
          <CMenuItem>Folder</CMenuItem>
          <CMenuItem>Text document</CMenuItem>
          <CMenuItem>Spreadsheet</CMenuItem>
        </CMenuContent>
      </CSubmenu>
      <CSubmenu>
        <CMenuItem>Sort by</CMenuItem>
        <CMenuContent>
          <CMenuItem>Name</CMenuItem>
          <CMenuItem>Date modified</CMenuItem>
          <CMenuItem>Size</CMenuItem>
        </CMenuContent>
      </CSubmenu>
      <CMenuDivider />
      <CMenuItem>Refresh</CMenuItem>
    </CMenuContent>
  </CContextMenu>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CContextMenu, CMenuContent, CMenuDivider, CMenuItem, CSubmenu } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### One menu for many rows

A context menu belongs to the `<CContextMenu>` area and opens for right-clicks anywhere inside it. Wrap the container - a table, a list, a file grid - rather than every row, and read the row from its own `@contextmenu` handler: the event bubbles to the area afterwards, which opens the menu. One menu, one component, no matter how many rows.

```html
<template>
  <CContextMenu>
    <CTable hover>
      <CTableHead @contextmenu.prevent>
        <CTableRow>
          <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Name</CTableHeaderCell>
          <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Modified</CTableHeaderCell>
          <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Size</CTableHeaderCell>
        </CTableRow>
      </CTableHead>
      <CTableBody>
        <CTableRow v-for="file in files" :key="file.name" @contextmenu="selected = file.name">
          <CTableDataCell>{{ file.name }}</CTableDataCell>
          <CTableDataCell>{{ file.modified }}</CTableDataCell>
          <CTableDataCell>{{ file.size }}</CTableDataCell>
        </CTableRow>
      </CTableBody>
    </CTable>
    <CMenuContent>
      <CMenuHeader>{{ selected }}</CMenuHeader>
      <CMenuItem>Open</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuItem>Rename</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuItem>Download</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuDivider />
      <CMenuItem theme="danger">Delete</CMenuItem>
    </CMenuContent>
  </CContextMenu>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import {
  CContextMenu,
  CMenuContent,
  CMenuDivider,
  CMenuHeader,
  CMenuItem,
  CTable,
  CTableBody,
  CTableDataCell,
  CTableHead,
  CTableHeaderCell,
  CTableRow,
} from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const files = [
  { name: 'Quarterly report.pdf', modified: '2 hours ago', size: '1.2 MB' },
  { name: 'Logo.svg', modified: 'Yesterday', size: '24 KB' },
  { name: 'Notes.txt', modified: '3 days ago', size: '2 KB' },
]

const selected = ref()
</script>
```

A handler that prevents the event (`@contextmenu.prevent`) keeps the menu closed and the browser's own menu away too - the right-click on the header row above opens nothing.

### Container

The menu is positioned with `position: fixed` at the pointer, so it escapes ancestors with `overflow: hidden` on its own. A `transform`, `filter` or `contain` on an ancestor turns that ancestor into the containing block for fixed elements and the menu drifts; render it through a Teleport with `portal` (or `container`) in that case.

```html
<template>
  <CContextMenu
    class="border rounded-3 p-6 text-center fg-2 overflow-hidden"
    portal
    style="transform: translateZ(0)"
    tabindex="0"
  >
    Right-click inside a transformed, clipping container
    <CMenuContent>
      <CMenuItem>Still in the viewport</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuItem>Another action</CMenuItem>
    </CMenuContent>
  </CContextMenu>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CContextMenu, CMenuContent, CMenuItem } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Accessibility

Pointing devices are not the only way in: with focus on the area, <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd> and the <kbd>Menu</kbd> key open the menu anchored to the element instead of the pointer. <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd> is the Windows convention the [WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/) adopt for opening a context menu from the keyboard; the component handles the keys itself, so they work on macOS too, where no system shortcut exists and browsers never turn them into a `contextmenu` event. On Apple keyboards the function keys default to their media actions, so the shortcut is <kbd>Fn</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd> unless the system is set to use them as standard function keys. Give a non-interactive area `tabindex="0"` so keyboard users can reach it, and describe the gesture somewhere nearby - nothing in the markup announces that an element has a context menu.

Focus moves into the menu when it opens and returns to the area when it closes. Like [Menu](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/menu/#accessibility), the component adds no `menuitem` roles on its own; add them yourself when the menu is a true application menu.

### Keyboard navigation

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd>, <kbd>Menu</kbd> | Open the context menu anchored to the focused area (<kbd>Fn</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd> on Apple keyboards) |
| `↓` / `↑` | Navigate to next/previous menu item |
| `→` | Enter submenu (or `←` in RTL) |
| `←` | Exit submenu and return to parent (or `→` in RTL) |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Activate focused item or open submenu |
| `Esc` | Close the menu and return focus to the area |
| `Home` / `End` | Jump to first/last menu item |
| `Tab` | Move focus and close the menu |

- [&lt;CContextMenu /&gt;](./api/#ccontextmenu)

- [&lt;CSubmenu /&gt;](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/menu/api/#csubmenu)

# Vue Context Menu Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Context Menu component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## CContextMenu

```jsx
import { CContextMenu } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `autoClose` | `boolean \| 'inside' \| 'outside'` | `true` | Configures the auto close behavior: - `true` — closes on a click inside or outside the menu, - `'inside'` — closes on a click inside the menu only, - `'outside'` — closes on a click outside the menu only, - `false` — closes only on the Escape key. |
| `container` | `HTMLElement \| (() => HTMLElement) \| string` | `'body'` | The element the panel is rendered into instead of `document.body`. You can pass an HTML element or function that returns a single element. Implies `portal`. Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert. |
| `dark` | `boolean` | - | Renders the panel in the dark theme. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the menu closed and lets the browser's own menu through. |
| `offset` | `[number, number]` | `() => [0, 2]` | The distance of the panel from the pointer, as `[skidding, distance]`. |
| `placement` | `string` | `'bottom-start'` | Where the panel opens relative to the pointer. It flips when that side of the viewport is short, and a logical `start` or `end` side resolves to the side the writing direction puts it on. |
| `portal` | `boolean` | - | Renders the panel through a Teleport. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `hide` | Callback fired when the menu is hidden. |
| `show` | Callback fired when the menu is shown. |

The menu itself is a [`<CMenuContent>`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/menu/api/#cmenucontent) with the same items, headers, dividers and submenus as a [Menu](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/menu/api/).

# Vue Context Menu Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Context Menu component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

The menu a context menu opens is a regular menu, so it is styled by the [Menu](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/menu/styling/) tokens.

## CSS variables

```scss
$menu-tokens: defaults(

    --cui-menu-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-menu-border-color: var(--cui-border-color-translucent),
    --cui-menu-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-menu-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-menu-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow-lg),
    --cui-menu-divider-bg: var(--cui-border-color-translucent),
    --cui-menu-divider-margin-y: .125rem,
    --cui-menu-divider-margin-x: .25rem,
    --cui-menu-item-color: var(--cui-menu-color, var(--cui-fg-body)),
    --cui-menu-item-hover-color: var(--cui-menu-color, var(--cui-fg-body)),
    --cui-menu-item-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-menu-item-active-color: var(--cui-primary-contrast),
    --cui-menu-item-active-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg),
    --cui-menu-item-disabled-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-menu-item-font-weight: var(--cui-font-weight-normal),
    --cui-menu-item-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-menu-item-padding-x: .75rem,
    --cui-menu-item-padding-y: .25rem,
    --cui-menu-item-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-5),
    --cui-menu-icon-size: 1rem,
    --cui-menu-description-font-size: calc(var(--cui-body-font-size) * .75),
    --cui-menu-check-color: currentcolor,
    --cui-menu-header-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-menu-header-padding-x: .75rem,
    --cui-menu-header-padding-y: .25rem,

  ),

```

### How to use CSS variables

```vue
<template>
  <CContextMenu>
    ...
    <CMenuContent :style="vars">...</CMenuContent>
  </CContextMenu>
</template>

  '--cui-menu-min-width': '14rem',
}
</script>
```

# Vue Dropdown Component

> Vue dropdown component allows you to toggle contextual overlays for displaying lists, links, and more html elements.

## Overview

Dropdowns are toggleable, contextual overlays for displaying lists of links and more.

> Since v6 the Vue Dropdown is a compatibility surface over the [Menu](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/menu/) component — the props, class names and markup below keep working, and both share one engine underneath. **Dropdown may be removed in v7**, so prefer Menu for new work.

Dropdowns are built on a third party library, [Floating UI](https://floating-ui.com/), which provides dynamic positioning and viewport detection. Floating UI isn't used to position dropdowns in navbars though as dynamic positioning isn't required.

## Examples

Bind the dropdown's toggle and the dropdown menu inside `<CDropdown>`, or different element that declares `position: relative;`. Dropdowns can be triggered from `<a>` or `<button>` elements to better fit your possible requirements.

### Single button

Here's how you can put them to work with either `<button>` elements:
```html
<template>
  <CDropdown>
    <CDropdownToggle theme="primary">Dropdown Button</CDropdownToggle>
    <CDropdownMenu>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
    </CDropdownMenu>
  </CDropdown>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDropdown, CDropdownToggle, CDropdownMenu, CDropdownItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

And with `<a>` elements:

```html
<template>
  <CDropdown color="secondary" toggler-text="Dropdown button">
    <CDropdownToggle as="a" theme="primary">Dropdown Button</CDropdownToggle>
    <CDropdownMenu>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
    </CDropdownMenu>
  </CDropdown>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDropdown, CDropdownToggle, CDropdownMenu, CDropdownItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

The best part is you can do this with any button variant, too:

```html
<template>
  <template
    v-for="item in ['primary', 'secondary', 'success', 'info', 'warning', 'danger']"
    :key="item"
  >
    <CDropdown :color="item" :toggler-text="item" variant="btn-group">
      <CDropdownToggle :theme="item">{{ item }}</CDropdownToggle>
      <CDropdownMenu>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
      </CDropdownMenu>
    </CDropdown>
  </template>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDropdown, CDropdownToggle, CDropdownMenu, CDropdownItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

### Split button

Similarly, create split button dropdowns with virtually the same markup as single button dropdowns, but with the addition of boolean prop `split` for proper spacing around the dropdown caret.

We use this extra class to reduce the horizontal `padding` on either side of the caret by 25% and remove the `margin-left` that's attached for normal button dropdowns. Those additional changes hold the caret centered in the split button and implement a more properly sized hit area next to the main button.

```html
<template>
  <template
    v-for="item in ['primary', 'secondary', 'success', 'info', 'warning', 'danger']"
    :key="item"
  >
    <CDropdown :color="item" :toggler-text="item" variant="btn-group">
      <CButton :theme="item">{{ item }}</CButton>
      <CDropdownToggle :theme="item" split>{{ item }}</CDropdownToggle>
      <CDropdownMenu>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
      </CDropdownMenu>
    </CDropdown>
  </template>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDropdown, CButton, CDropdownToggle, CDropdownMenu, CDropdownItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Sizing

Button dropdowns work with buttons of all sizes, including default and split dropdown buttons.

```html
<template>
  <CDropdown variant="btn-group">
    <CDropdownToggle theme="secondary" size="lg">Large button</CDropdownToggle>
    <CDropdownMenu>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownDivider />
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Separated link</CDropdownItem>
    </CDropdownMenu>
  </CDropdown>
  <CDropdown variant="btn-group">
    <CButton theme="secondary" size="lg">Large split button</CButton>
    <CDropdownToggle theme="secondary" size="lg" split>Large button</CDropdownToggle>
    <CDropdownMenu>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownDivider />
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Separated link</CDropdownItem>
    </CDropdownMenu>
  </CDropdown>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CDropdown,
  CDropdownToggle,
  CDropdownMenu,
  CDropdownItem,
  CDropdownDivider,
  CButton,
} from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

```html
<template>
  <CDropdown variant="btn-group">
    <CDropdownToggle theme="secondary" size="sm">Small button</CDropdownToggle>
    <CDropdownMenu>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownDivider />
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Separated link</CDropdownItem>
    </CDropdownMenu>
  </CDropdown>
  <CDropdown variant="btn-group">
    <CButton theme="secondary" size="sm">Small split button</CButton>
    <CDropdownToggle theme="secondary" size="sm" split>Small button</CDropdownToggle>
    <CDropdownMenu>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownDivider />
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Separated link</CDropdownItem>
    </CDropdownMenu>
  </CDropdown>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CDropdown,
  CDropdownToggle,
  CDropdownMenu,
  CDropdownItem,
  CDropdownDivider,
  CButton,
} from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

```html
  CDropdownDivider,
```

## Directions

```html
    </CDropdownMenu>
  </CDropdown>
```

### Placement option

_Added in 6.0.0._

The directions above pick one of six fixed positions. The `placement` prop takes the same values [Menu](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/menu/#placement) takes — physical (`top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`), logical (`start`, `end`, which mirror in RTL) and every `-start`/`-end` alignment — and it wins over `direction` and `alignment` when both are present. Breakpoint prefixes make it responsive: `bottom-start md:top-end` reads as bottom-start below `md` and top-end from `md` up.

```html
<template>
  <CDropdown placement="top-end">
    <CDropdownToggle theme="secondary">Top end</CDropdownToggle>
    <CDropdownMenu>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
    </CDropdownMenu>
  </CDropdown>
  <CDropdown placement="bottom-start md:end-start">
    <CDropdownToggle theme="secondary">Bottom start, end from md</CDropdownToggle>
    <CDropdownMenu>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
    </CDropdownMenu>
  </CDropdown>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDropdown, CDropdownToggle, CDropdownMenu, CDropdownItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

With `popper` disabled, or with a responsive `alignment` object, the menu is positioned by the direction classes alone and the prop is ignored.

### Responsive alignment

A responsive `alignment` object becomes a responsive placement — `:alignment="{ lg: 'end' }"` reads as bottom-start below `lg` and bottom-end from `lg` up — and dynamic positioning stays on.

To align **right** the dropdown menu with the given breakpoint or larger, add `aligment="xs|sm|md|lg|xl|2xl: end"`.

```html
<template>
  <CDropdown color="secondary" :alignment="{ lg: 'end' }">
    <CDropdownToggle theme="secondary"
      >Left-aligned but right aligned when large screen</CDropdownToggle
    >
    <CDropdownMenu>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownDivider />
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Separated link</CDropdownItem>
    </CDropdownMenu>
  </CDropdown>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CDropdown,
  CDropdownToggle,
  CDropdownMenu,
  CDropdownItem,
  CDropdownDivider,
} from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

To align **left** the dropdown menu with the given breakpoint or larger, add `aligment="xs|sm|md|lg|xl|2xl: start"`.

```html
<template>
  <CDropdown color="secondary" :alignment="{ xs: 'end', lg: 'start' }">
    <CDropdownToggle theme="secondary"
      >Right-aligned but left aligned when large screen</CDropdownToggle
    >
    <CDropdownMenu>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
      <CDropdownDivider />
      <CDropdownItem href="#">Separated link</CDropdownItem>
    </CDropdownMenu>
  </CDropdown>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CDropdown,
  CDropdownToggle,
  CDropdownMenu,
  CDropdownItem,
  CDropdownDivider,
} from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Menu content

### Headers

Add a header to label sections of actions in any dropdown menu.

In the following example we use `div` instead of `<CDropdownMenu>` to show `<CDropdownMenu>` content.

```html
<template>
  <div class="dropdown-menu">
    <CDropdownHeader>Dropdown header</CDropdownHeader>
    <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
    <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDropdownHeader, CDropdownItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

### Dividers

Separate groups of related menu items with a divider.

In the following example we use `div` instead of `<CDropdownMenu>` to show `<CDropdownMenu>` content.

```html
<template>
  <div class="dropdown-menu">
    <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
    <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
    <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
    <CDropdownDivider />
    <CDropdownItem href="#">Separated link</CDropdownItem>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDropdownItem, CDropdownDivider } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```
### Text

Place any freeform text within a dropdown menu with text. Note that you'll likely need additional sizing styles to constrain the menu width.

```html
<template>
  <div class="border rounded p-5 fg-2" style="max-width: 200px">
    <p>Some example text that's free-flowing within the dropdown menu.</p>
    <p class="mb-0">And this is more example text.</p>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup></script>
```

### Forms

Put a form within a dropdown menu, or make it into a dropdown menu.

```html
<template>
  <div class="dropdown-menu">

        <CFormInput id="exampleDropdownFormPassword1" type="password" placeholder="Password" />

      </CFormField>

```

## Dropdown options

Use `offset` to displace the dropdown from its default position. The value is a string with two numbers separated by a comma, e.g. `:offset="[10, 20]"`. Use `teleport` property to render dropdowns in `body` instead of the parent element. This helps to avoid any overflow or z-index issues.

```html
<template>
  <div class="d-flex gap-1">
    <CDropdown :offset="[10, 20]">
      <CDropdownToggle theme="secondary">Offset</CDropdownToggle>
      <CDropdownMenu>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
      </CDropdownMenu>
    </CDropdown>
    <CDropdown teleport>
      <CDropdownToggle theme="secondary" aria-controls="dropdownMenuInTeleport">
        Teleport
      </CDropdownToggle>
      <CDropdownMenu id="dropdownMenuInTeleport">
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
      </CDropdownMenu>
    </CDropdown>
    <CDropdown reference="parent">
      <CButton theme="secondary">Reference</CButton>
      <CDropdownToggle theme="secondary" split />
      <CDropdownMenu>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
      </CDropdownMenu>
    </CDropdown>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDropdown, CDropdownToggle, CDropdownMenu, CDropdownItem, CButton } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

### Auto close behavior

By default, dropdowns are closed when clicking outside of the dropdown menu or the toggle button. You can change this behavior with the `autoClose` property. Set `autoClose` to: 

- `true` - Close on clicks inside or outside of the Vue.js dropdown menu.
- `false` - Disable auto-close; close manually by setting the `:visible="false"` (also not closed by `Escape`).
- `'inside'` - Close only when clicking inside the Vue.js dropdown menu.
- `'outside'` - Close only when clicking outside the Vue.js dropdown menu.

```html
<template>
  <div class="d-flex gap-1">
    <CDropdown>
      <CDropdownToggle theme="secondary">Default dropdown</CDropdownToggle>
      <CDropdownMenu>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
      </CDropdownMenu>
    </CDropdown>
    <CDropdown auto-close="inside">
      <CDropdownToggle theme="secondary">Clickable inside</CDropdownToggle>
      <CDropdownMenu>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
      </CDropdownMenu>
    </CDropdown>
    <CDropdown auto-close="outside">
      <CDropdownToggle theme="secondary">Clickable outside</CDropdownToggle>
      <CDropdownMenu>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
      </CDropdownMenu>
    </CDropdown>
    <CDropdown :auto-close="false">
      <CDropdownToggle theme="secondary">Manual close</CDropdownToggle>
      <CDropdownMenu>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
      </CDropdownMenu>
    </CDropdown>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CDropdown, CDropdownToggle, CDropdownMenu, CDropdownItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Usage with v-model

_Added in 6.0.0._

Pass `show` and the dropdown renders what you pass — the toggle and the dismiss gestures only emit `@update:show`, so feed the change back, or nothing moves. The `v-model:show` binding is that loop in one attribute. Here an external button drives the same state the dropdown's own gestures request changes to.

```html
<template>
  <div class="d-flex gap-3">
    <CButton theme="secondary" variant="outline" @click="show = !show">
      {{ show ? 'Close the dropdown' : 'Open the dropdown' }}
    </CButton>
    <CDropdown v-model:show="show">
      <CDropdownToggle theme="secondary">Dropdown button</CDropdownToggle>
      <CDropdownMenu>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Another action</CDropdownItem>
        <CDropdownItem href="#">Something else here</CDropdownItem>
      </CDropdownMenu>
    </CDropdown>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CDropdown, CDropdownItem, CDropdownMenu, CDropdownToggle } from '@coreui/vue'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

Use it when the open state belongs to something else — a keyboard shortcut, a tour step, or a control outside the dropdown like the button above.

### Initial open state

Without a binding the toggle manages the menu. Pass `show` to seed it open on mount.

```vue
<CDropdown show>
```

`@update:show` fires either way whenever the dropdown requests an open-state change — a dismiss gesture (Escape, an outside click, an item click) or any internal toggle. The deprecated `visible` prop keeps its old behavior and is ignored when `show` is set.

# Vue Dropdown Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Dropdown component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CDropdown

```jsx
import { CDropdown } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `alignment` | `string \| Alignments` | - | Set alignment of the dropdown menu. A responsive object aligns the menu per breakpoint and keeps dynamic positioning; `placement` wins over it. |
| `autoClose` | `boolean \| 'inside' \| 'outside'` | `true` | Configure the auto close behavior of the dropdown: - `true` - the dropdown will be closed by clicking outside or inside the dropdown menu. - `false` - the dropdown will be closed by clicking the toggle button and manually calling hide or toggle method. (Also will not be closed by pressing esc key) - `'inside'` - the dropdown will be closed (only) by clicking inside the dropdown menu. - `'outside'` - the dropdown will be closed (only) by clicking outside the dropdown menu. |
| `container` | `HTMLElement \| (() => HTMLElement) \| string` | `'body'` | Appends the vue dropdown menu to a specific element. You can pass an HTML element or function that returns a single element. By default `document.body`. Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert. |
| `dark` | `boolean` | - | Sets a darker color scheme to match a dark navbar. |
| `direction` | `string` | - | Sets a specified  direction and location of the dropdown menu. |
| `floatingConfig` | `\| Partial<ComputePositionConfig> \| (( defaultFloatingConfig: Partial<ComputePositionConfig> ) => Partial<ComputePositionConfig>)` | `undefined` | A Floating UI configuration object, or a function that receives the default configuration and returns a modified one, used to customize the positioning of the dropdown menu. [Read more](https://floating-ui.com/docs/computePosition#options) |
| `offset` | `array` | `[0, 2]` | Offset of the dropdown menu relative to its target. |
| `placement` | `string` | `undefined` | Where the menu opens. Logical placements (`'start'`, `'end'`) resolve to the side the writing direction puts them on, and `-start`/`-end` are already logical. Breakpoint prefixes make it responsive — `'bottom-start md:top-end'` reads as bottom-start below `md` and top-end from `md` up. An explicit placement wins over `direction` and `alignment`; left unset, the placement follows those two props. |
| `popper` | `boolean` | `true` | Enables or disables dynamic positioning. When disabled, the menu is rendered statically and carries `data-coreui-popper="static"`. |
| `reference` | `'parent' \| 'toggle' \| HTMLElement \| Ref<HTMLElement \| null>` | `'toggle'` | Sets the reference element for positioning the Vue Dropdown Menu. - `toggle` - The Vue Dropdown Toggle button (default). - `parent` - The Vue Dropdown wrapper element. - `HTMLElement` - A custom HTML element. - `Ref` - A custom reference element. |
| `show` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Control the open state. When set, the dropdown renders what `show` says and dismiss gestures only emit `update:show` — nothing closes until the parent flips the prop. Supports the `v-model:show` binding. |
| `teleport` | `boolean` | `false` | Generates dropdown menu using Teleport. |
| `variant` | `string` | `'dropdown'` | Set the dropdown variant to an btn-group, dropdown, input-group, and nav-item. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Toggle the visibility of dropdown menu component. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `hide` | Callback fired when the component requests to be hidden. |
| `show` | Callback fired when the component requests to be shown. |
| `update:show` | Emit the requested open state to support the `v-model:show` binding — a dismiss gesture (Escape, outside click, item click) or any internal toggle. |

## CDropdownToggle

```jsx
import { CDropdownToggle } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `string` | `'button'` | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |
| `caret` | `boolean` | `true` | Enables pseudo element caret on toggler. |
| `color` | `Color` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |
| `custom` | `boolean` | - | Create a custom toggler which accepts any content. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `navLink` | `boolean` | `true` | If a dropdown `variant` is set to `nav-item` then render the toggler as a link instead of a button. |
| `shape` | `Shape` | - |  |
| `size` | `string` | - | Size the component small or large. |
| `split` | `boolean` | - | Similarly, create split button dropdowns with virtually the same markup as single button dropdowns, but with the addition of `.dropdown-toggle-split` className for proper spacing around the dropdown caret. |
| `splitLabel` | `string` | `'Toggle Dropdown'` | Screen reader label for split button dropdown toggle. |
| `theme` | `Color` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. Pair it with `variant` for the shape — a button is a shape plus a colour. |
| `trigger` | `Triggers` | `'click'` | Sets which event handlers you’d like provided to your toggle prop. You can specify one trigger or an array of them. |
| `variant` | `string` | - | Set the shape of the button — how much ink it uses. Defaults to `solid` when `theme` is set. |
