# Vue List Box Component

> A keyboard-driven list of values built on the ARIA listbox pattern: single, multiple or no selection, sections, descriptions, links, an empty state and an aria-activedescendant mode that keeps the focus in your own input.

## Overview

_Added in 6.0.0._

A list box presents a set of values and lets the user pick from them. `<CListBox>` renders a `.list-box` container with the `.list-box-options` list inside it, and owns the roles, the selection state and the keyboard: it writes `role="listbox"` on the options and `role="option"` on each of them, keeps `aria-selected` in step with the selection, moves a roving `tabindex` as the highlight moves, and scrolls the highlighted option into view. Before the highlight has moved that `tabindex` sits on the first navigable entry, which is a selectable section label when one comes first, so <kbd>Tab</kbd> enters the list where the arrows would. The `header` slot sits above the options, inside the container — that is where `<CListBoxHeader>` goes.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox aria-label="Sandwich" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption value="lettuce">Lettuce</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="tomato">Tomato</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="onion">Onion</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="cheese">Cheese</CListBoxOption>
  </CListBox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListBox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

Every option carries its value in `value`; an option without one is worth its text. Values are what the events report, so an option can be hidden or re-rendered without disturbing the selection.

### When to use

<div class="table-responsive">

| Component | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| List box | Choosing a value — the choice stays on screen and is reported back to you. |
| [Menu](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/menu/) | Running an action — the surface opens, something happens, it closes. |
| [List group](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/list-group/) | Displaying content — a list of things to read, not to pick from. |

</div>

A list box is also the primitive the picker components are built from, so its markup and classes carry over to them.

### Options from data

Pass `items` and the default slot becomes the option template, called once per entry with `item` and `index`. Without a slot each entry renders as a `<CListBoxOption>` showing its `label`.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox :items="items" aria-label="Sandwich" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <template #default="{ item }">
      <CListBoxOption :key="item.value" :description="item.description" :value="item.value">
        {{ item.label }}
      </CListBoxOption>
    </template>
  </CListBox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListBox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const items = [
  { description: 'Crisp and green', label: 'Lettuce', value: 'lettuce' },
  { description: 'Ripe', label: 'Tomato', value: 'tomato' },
  { description: 'Sliced thin', label: 'Onion', value: 'onion' },
]
</script>
```

## Selection

`selectionMode` decides what a click and <kbd>Space</kbd> do. In `single` (the default) one option is selected at a time and picking another replaces it. Pass `selected` to seed the selection and let the list box manage it from there, or bind `v-model:selected` to drive it from your own state; `@selected-change` fires either way with the new values.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox v-model:selected="selected" aria-label="Single" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption value="lettuce">Lettuce</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="tomato">Tomato</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="onion">Onion</CListBoxOption>
  </CListBox>
  <p class="fg-2">Selected: {{ selected.length > 0 ? selected.join(', ') : 'nothing' }}</p>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CListBox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const selected = ref(['tomato'])
</script>
```

In `multiple` a click toggles one option, <kbd>Shift</kbd> extends the selection from the last one, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> (<kbd>Cmd</kbd> on macOS) adds one without clearing the rest, and <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> takes everything. `aria-multiselectable` is written for you.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox
    v-model:selected="selected"
    aria-label="Multiple"
    selection-mode="multiple"
    style="max-width: 20rem"
  >
    <CListBoxOption value="lettuce">Lettuce</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="tomato">Tomato</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="onion">Onion</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="cheese">Cheese</CListBoxOption>
  </CListBox>
  <p class="fg-2">Selected: {{ selected.length > 0 ? selected.join(', ') : 'nothing' }}</p>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CListBox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const selected = ref([])
</script>
```

`<CListBoxHeader>` is the strip above the list, inside the container. `<CListBoxSelectAll>` is a toggle button that switches the whole selection: it selects every visible enabled option, or drops that same set once they are all selected, so a value a filter hid stays selected; `useListBoxContext().clear()`, or an empty `v-model:selected`, empties everything. It looks like an option and reports its state through `aria-pressed` — `true`, `false`, or `mixed` while part of the list is selected — with `aria-controls` pointing at the options; its default slot is the label (`Select all` when you leave it out). It is reached with <kbd>Tab</kbd> rather than the arrows, which is the point: an option pretending to be a value had to lie through `aria-selected`. The header takes arbitrary content, so a title, a counter or controls of your own go in it too: `<CListBoxTitle>` and `<CListBoxSubtitle>` are the text pair, both `as`-polymorphic, and `useListBoxContext()` — or `v-model:selected` — is where a "2 of 4 selected" line gets its numbers.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox aria-label="Toppings" selection-mode="multiple" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <template #header>
      <CListBoxHeader>
        <CListBoxSelectAll />
      </CListBoxHeader>
    </template>
    <CListBoxOption value="lettuce">Lettuce</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="tomato">Tomato</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="onion">Onion</CListBoxOption>
  </CListBox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListBox, CListBoxHeader, CListBoxOption, CListBoxSelectAll } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

With `none` nothing is ever selected and no `aria-selected` is written; activating an option emits `action` instead, which turns the list into a keyboard-navigable list of commands.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox
    aria-label="Actions"
    selection-mode="none"
    style="max-width: 20rem"
    @action="last = $event"
  >
    <CListBoxOption value="copy">Copy</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="rename">Rename</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="delete">Delete</CListBoxOption>
  </CListBox>
  <p class="fg-2">Last action: {{ last ?? 'none' }}</p>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CListBox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const last = ref()
</script>
```

### Selection limit

`selectionLimit` stops the selection at a number of options. Once it is reached the next pick — a click, <kbd>Space</kbd>, a <kbd>Shift</kbd> range, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>A</kbd> or the select-all button — is refused and `@selection-limit` fires once per interaction with the first value that did not fit. Deselecting always works and no option is disabled, so the list keeps saying what it holds instead of going grey. A range or a select all fills in document order until the limit; the select-all button reads as pressed once the limit is reached, and clicking it then clears.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox
    v-model:selected="selected"
    :selection-limit="2"
    aria-label="Toppings"
    selection-mode="multiple"
    style="max-width: 20rem"
    @selection-limit="refused = $event"
  >
    <template #header>
      <CListBoxHeader>
        <CListBoxSelectAll />
      </CListBoxHeader>
    </template>
    <CListBoxOption value="lettuce">Lettuce</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="tomato">Tomato</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="onion">Onion</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="cheese">Cheese</CListBoxOption>
  </CListBox>
  <p class="fg-2">
    Selected: {{ selected.length > 0 ? selected.join(', ') : 'nothing' }} — two at a time<span
      v-if="refused"
      >, {{ refused }} did not fit</span
    >
  </p>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CListBox, CListBoxHeader, CListBoxOption, CListBoxSelectAll } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const refused = ref('')
const selected = ref([])
</script>
```

## Checkboxes

`indicator="checkbox"` writes `data-coreui-indicator` on the container and puts a checkbox in front of every option, so a multiple selection reads the way a list of checkboxes does — without leaving the listbox pattern: the boxes are decorative (`aria-hidden`), and what assistive technology announces is still `aria-selected` on the option. `<CListBoxSelectAll>` takes the same indicator and the same `selected` / `indeterminate` look, so the header lines up with the list.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox
    v-model:selected="selected"
    aria-label="Toppings"
    indicator="checkbox"
    selection-mode="multiple"
    style="max-width: 20rem"
  >
    <template #header>
      <CListBoxHeader>
        <CListBoxSelectAll />
      </CListBoxHeader>
    </template>
    <CListBoxOption value="lettuce">Lettuce</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="tomato">Tomato</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="onion">Onion</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="cheese">Cheese</CListBoxOption>
  </CListBox>
  <p class="fg-2">Selected: {{ selected.length > 0 ? selected.join(', ') : 'nothing' }}</p>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CListBox, CListBoxHeader, CListBoxOption, CListBoxSelectAll } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const selected = ref(['tomato'])
</script>
```

## Counter

`counter` puts a counter built by `selectedLabel` at the end of the header and keeps it there: both numbers read the options on screen — the same set the select-all button works on — so a value hidden by a search or disabled counts in neither. Fill the header with anything you like — the counter is appended to it — or leave the slot empty and the list box renders the header for it.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox
    :items="items"
    aria-label="Sandwich"
    counter
    indicator="checkbox"
    selection-mode="multiple"
    style="max-width: 20rem"
  >
    <template #header>
      <CListBoxHeader>
        <CListBoxSelectAll>Toppings</CListBoxSelectAll>
      </CListBoxHeader>
    </template>
  </CListBox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListBox, CListBoxHeader, CListBoxSelectAll } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const items = [
  { label: 'Lettuce', value: 'lettuce' },
  { label: 'Tomato', value: 'tomato' },
  { label: 'Onion', value: 'onion' },
  { label: 'Cheese', value: 'cheese' },
]
</script>
```

## Sections

Group options in a `<CListBoxSection>` and name it with `label` or the `label` slot. The section renders `role="group"` and points `aria-labelledby` at its label, so the group is announced with its name.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox aria-label="Sandwich" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxSection label="Veggies">
      <CListBoxOption value="lettuce">Lettuce</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="tomato">Tomato</CListBoxOption>
    </CListBoxSection>
    <CListBoxSection label="Protein">
      <CListBoxOption value="ham">Ham</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="tuna">Tuna</CListBoxOption>
    </CListBoxSection>
  </CListBox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListBox, CListBoxOption, CListBoxSection } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### Selectable sections

`sectionsSelectable` turns every section label into a tri-state button that takes or drops the section's visible options at once — `aria-pressed` carries `true`, `false` or `mixed`, and the label joins the arrow order in front of the options it stands for. It works in the `multiple` mode and respects `selectionLimit`: values selected outside the section count against it, so a label reads `true` once the section holds what the limit leaves, and pressing it then clears the section. A label whose section has no enabled option on screen carries `aria-disabled`, leaves the arrow order and shows the state of the section's disabled options. With `indicator="checkbox"` the label shows the same checkbox the options do, and `disabled` on `<CListBoxSection>` disables every option in it.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox
    aria-label="Sandwich"
    indicator="checkbox"
    sections-selectable
    selection-mode="multiple"
    style="max-width: 20rem"
  >
    <CListBoxSection label="Veggies">
      <CListBoxOption value="lettuce">Lettuce</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="tomato">Tomato</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="onion">Onion</CListBoxOption>
    </CListBoxSection>
    <CListBoxSection label="Protein">
      <CListBoxOption value="ham">Ham</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="tuna">Tuna</CListBoxOption>
    </CListBoxSection>
  </CListBox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListBox, CListBoxOption, CListBoxSection } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Descriptions

An option can carry a second line through `description` or the `description` slot — typeahead then matches the label alone, so typing skips the description text.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox aria-label="Plan" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption description="One project, community support" value="free">Free</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption description="Unlimited projects, shared billing" value="team"
      >Team</CListBoxOption
    >
  </CListBox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListBox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

Descriptions and the checkbox indicator work together: the indicator stays centred against the whole option and both lines of the text start past it, so a two-line option keeps the same left column as the select-all button above.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox
    aria-label="Plan"
    indicator="checkbox"
    selection-mode="multiple"
    style="max-width: 22rem"
  >
    <template #header>
      <CListBoxHeader>
        <CListBoxSelectAll />
      </CListBoxHeader>
    </template>
    <CListBoxOption description="One project, community support" value="free">Free</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption description="Unlimited projects, shared billing" value="team">
      Team
    </CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption description="SSO, audit log and a named contact" value="enterprise">
      Enterprise
    </CListBoxOption>
  </CListBox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListBox, CListBoxHeader, CListBoxOption, CListBoxSelectAll } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Links

An option with an `href` renders as a link, navigates on click and on <kbd>Enter</kbd>, and emits `action` on the way out — so a list of destinations keeps working with the keyboard without losing the browser's own link behavior.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox aria-label="Documentation" selection-mode="none" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption href="/components/menu/" value="menu">Menu</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption href="/components/list-group/" value="list-group">List group</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption href="/components/dropdown/" value="dropdown">Dropdown</CListBoxOption>
  </CListBox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListBox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Disabled items

`disabled` keeps the user out: it takes an option out of the keyboard order and out of every selection the user makes, the arrows, a click, a section label, a range and select all, and writes `aria-disabled` on it. Your code is not kept out of the values it sets, as with a native `<select>`: a disabled value in `defaultSelected` or in a selection you drive through `selected` is selected and read as selected. `select`, `toggle` and `selectAll` from `useListBox` act as the user would and leave a disabled option alone. The same prop on `<CListBox>` does that for all of it and writes `aria-disabled` on the list.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox aria-label="Sandwich" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption value="lettuce">Lettuce</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption disabled value="tomato">Tomato — out of stock</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="onion">Onion</CListBoxOption>
  </CListBox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListBox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Search

`search` puts a field above the options and filters on what is typed. A non-matching option is hidden rather than removed, so everything downstream follows — the arrows skip it, the empty state takes over once nothing is left, and the select-all button takes only what is on screen — while the selection itself survives the filtering.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox aria-label="Sandwich" search selection-mode="multiple" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption value="lettuce">Lettuce</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="tomato">Tomato</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="onion">Onion</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="cheese">Cheese</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="bacon">Bacon</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxEmpty>No results</CListBoxEmpty>
  </CListBox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListBox, CListBoxEmpty, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

`searchPlaceholder` is the field's placeholder and `ariaSearchLabel` its accessible name; the field carries `aria-controls` pointing at the options it filters.

`searchNormalize` compares both sides without their diacritics, so `zoe` matches `Zoë` and `oe` matches both. It normalizes to `NFD` and drops the combining diacritics, which leaves the labels themselves untouched — only the comparison changes.

`search="external"` hides nothing and reports instead: every keystroke arrives as the `search` event, and the answer comes back as `items`. Fetching, debouncing and filtering are the caller's, which is what lets a list of any size live on a server — pair it with `loading` so the wait is announced.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox
    :items="items"
    :loading="loading"
    aria-label="Users"
    search="external"
    search-placeholder="Search users"
    style="max-width: 20rem"
    @search="onSearch"
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CListBox } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const items = ref([])
const loading = ref(false)

let timer

const loadUsers = async (query) => {
  loading.value = true

  try {
    const response = await fetch(
      `https://apitest.coreui.io/demos/users?first_name=${query}&limit=10`
    )
    const users = await response.json()

    items.value = users.records.map((user) => ({
      label: `${user.first_name} ${user.last_name}`,
      value: String(user.id),
    }))
  } finally {
    loading.value = false
  }
}

const onSearch = (query) => {
  clearTimeout(timer)
  timer = setTimeout(() => loadUsers(query), 300)
}

loadUsers('')
</script>
```

### Filtering from your own field

`query` runs the same filter from a field you own, so the list can sit under a search input that is not part of it. A non-matching option is hidden rather than removed — the arrows skip it, a section with nothing left hides with its label, and the selection survives; `null` clears the filter. `searchNormalize` applies here too.

```html
<template>
  <CFormInput
    v-model="query"
    aria-label="Filter the sandwich"
    class="mb-3"
    placeholder="Filter…"
    style="max-width: 20rem"
    type="search"
  />
  <CListBox :query="query" aria-label="Sandwich" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption value="lettuce">Lettuce</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="tomato">Tomato</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="onion">Onion</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="cheese">Cheese</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxEmpty>No results</CListBoxEmpty>
  </CListBox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CFormInput, CListBox, CListBoxEmpty, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const query = ref('')
</script>
```

## Empty state

`<CListBoxEmpty>` is shown whenever nothing is left to navigate and hidden as soon as something is, so filtering a list has somewhere to land. `hidden` on an option takes it out of the navigation and leaves the selection alone — which is what makes a filter cheap.

```html
<template>
  <CFormInput
    v-model="query"
    aria-label="Filter"
    class="mb-3"
    placeholder="Filter"
    style="max-width: 20rem"
  />
  <CListBox aria-label="Results" style="max-width: 20rem">
    <CListBoxOption
      v-for="item in items"
      :key="item"
      :hidden="!item.toLowerCase().startsWith(query.toLowerCase())"
      :value="item"
    >
      {{ item }}
    </CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxEmpty>No results</CListBoxEmpty>
  </CListBox>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CFormInput, CListBox, CListBoxEmpty, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const items = ['Lettuce', 'Tomato', 'Onion', 'Cheese']
const query = ref('')
</script>
```

## Loading

`loading` covers the wait: it writes `aria-busy="true"` on the options element, shows a row with a spinner and the `loadingLabel` text below the options, announces that text to screen readers when the wait starts or the list shows up waiting, and holds the empty state back, so "No results" never flashes before the answer arrives. The options stay as they are and can still be picked, so a choice from the shown results counts.

## Long lists

`optionsMaxHeight` caps the options list and scrolls it past that, in pixels or as a CSS length. `virtualScroller` goes further and mounts only the options in view, so a thousand of them cost a window of `visibleItems`; the selection and the keyboard are untouched — the scroller is only the viewport.

```html
<template>
  <CListBox
    :items="items"
    :visible-items="8"
    aria-label="Numbers"
    selection-mode="multiple"
    style="max-width: 20rem"
    virtual-scroller
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListBox } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const items = Array.from({ length: 1000 }, (_, index) => ({
  label: `Option ${index + 1}`,
  value: String(index + 1),
}))
</script>
```

## With an input

Pass `activeDescendant` an input — an element or a CSS selector — and the focus never leaves it: the list box drops the roving `tabindex`, gives every option an `id`, and keeps `aria-activedescendant` and `aria-controls` on the field pointing at the highlighted option. The arrows, <kbd>Home</kbd>, <kbd>End</kbd>, <kbd>Space</kbd> and <kbd>Enter</kbd> are handled on the field, so typing and choosing happen in one place — a combobox in two elements.

```html
<template>
  <CFormLabel for="listBoxField">Filter</CFormLabel>
  <CFormInput
    id="listBoxField"
    v-model="query"
    aria-expanded="true"
    autocomplete="off"
    class="mb-3"
    role="combobox"
    style="max-width: 20rem"
    type="text"
  />
  <CListBox
    v-model:selected="selected"
    active-descendant="#listBoxField"
    aria-label="Sandwich"
    style="max-width: 20rem"
  >
    <CListBoxOption
      v-for="item in items"
      :key="item"
      :hidden="!item.toLowerCase().startsWith(query.toLowerCase())"
      :value="item"
    >
      {{ item }}
    </CListBoxOption>
  </CListBox>
  <p class="fg-2">Selected: {{ selected.length > 0 ? selected.join(', ') : 'nothing' }}</p>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CFormInput, CFormLabel, CListBox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const items = ['Lettuce', 'Tomato', 'Onion', 'Cheese']
const query = ref('')
const selected = ref([])
</script>
```

## Accessibility

`<CListBox>` writes `role="listbox"` on the options element, `role="option"` on every option, `role="group"` on every section, `aria-multiselectable` in `multiple` mode and `aria-selected` on every option outside `none` mode. Name the list yourself with `ariaLabel`, which lands on the options element together with the roles. `<CListBoxSelectAll>` is a `<button>` in its own tab stop: `aria-pressed` carries `true` / `false` / `mixed`, and `aria-controls` points at the options.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `↓` / `↑` | Move the highlight to the next/previous option; it stops at the ends |
| `Home` / `End` | Move the highlight to the first/last option |
| `Space` | Toggle the option in `multiple` mode, select it in `single` |
| `Enter` | Select the option; on a link, follow it; in `none` mode, emit `action` |
| `Shift` + `↓` / `↑` | Extend the selection to the next/previous option |
| `Shift` + `Home` / `End` | Extend the selection to the first/last option |
| `Ctrl` / `Cmd` + `A` | Select every option (`multiple` mode) |
| `A` – `Z` | Move the highlight to the next option whose label starts with what you typed |

### CSS variables

```css
--cui-list-box-border-radius
--cui-list-box-border-width

--cui-list-box-header-border-color
--cui-list-box-header-border-width
--cui-list-box-header-gap
--cui-list-box-header-padding-x
--cui-list-box-header-padding-y
--cui-list-box-option-active-bg
--cui-list-box-option-active-color
--cui-list-box-option-border-radius
--cui-list-box-option-description-color
--cui-list-box-option-description-font-size
--cui-list-box-option-disabled-color
--cui-list-box-option-gap
--cui-list-box-option-hover-bg
--cui-list-box-option-hover-color
--cui-list-box-option-indicator-width
--cui-list-box-option-padding-x
--cui-list-box-option-padding-y
--cui-list-box-option-selected-bg
--cui-list-box-option-selected-color
--cui-list-box-padding-x
--cui-list-box-padding-y
--cui-list-box-search-margin
--cui-list-box-section-label-color
--cui-list-box-section-label-font-size
--cui-list-box-section-label-padding
```

`translucent` renders the list on a translucent, blurred background — the same treatment the menu surfaces use.

# Vue List Box Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue List Box component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CListBox

```jsx
import { CListBox } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | `string \| null` | `undefined` | The highlighted value. When set, the component highlights that option and only reports the moves through the `activeChange` event. Supports the `v-model:active` binding. |
| `activeDescendant` | `HTMLElement \| string` | - | The field that keeps the focus, as an element or a CSS selector. The list box then drops the roving `tabindex`, keeps `aria-activedescendant` and `aria-controls` on the field, and handles the keyboard there — an input and a list box become a combobox. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | - | A string that provides an accessible name for the list box. Screen readers announce it before the options. |
| `ariaLabelledby` | `string` | - | The id of the element that names the list box. Screen readers announce it before the options. |
| `ariaSearchLabel` | `string` | `'Search options'` | A string that provides an accessible name for the search field. |
| `counter` | `boolean` | - | Puts a `selectedLabel` counter at the end of the header, counting the selection among the options on screen — the same set the select-all button works on. The header is rendered for it when nothing else fills one. |
| `defaultActive` | `string` | - | The initially highlighted value, when the highlight is not controlled through `active`. |
| `defaultSelected` | `string \| string[]` | - | The initially selected values, when the selection is not controlled through `selected`. In the `single` mode only the first one is taken. A disabled value is taken too: disabled keeps the user out, not your code. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Turns the whole list box off: nothing is selectable, the keyboard does nothing and `aria-disabled` is written on the list. |
| `indicator` | `ListBoxIndicator` | `'none'` | Renders a checkbox in every option, so a multiple selection reads as a list of checkboxes. The select-all option shows the indeterminate state while only part of the list is selected. |
| `items` | `ListBoxOption[]` | - | The options to render. Each entry is passed to the default slot as `item`, so the slot works as the option template; without a slot every entry renders as a `<CListBoxOption>` showing its `label`. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | - | Covers the wait: it writes `aria-busy` on the options, shows a row with a spinner and `loadingLabel` below them, announces that text when the wait starts or the list shows up waiting, and holds the empty state back. The options stay usable. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | `'Loading…'` | Text of the loading row, announced to screen readers when the list starts loading on the page or shows up loading. |
| `optionsId` | `string` | `undefined` | The id of the element carrying `role="listbox"`, so a field outside the list box can point its `aria-controls` at it. Generated when left out. |
| `optionsMaxHeight` | `number\|string` | `'auto'` | Caps the height of the options list and scrolls it past that, in pixels or as a CSS length. |
| `query` | `string \| null` | `undefined` | The filter the list runs on, when the field that drives it is yours. A non-matching option is hidden rather than removed, so the arrows skip it and the selection survives; `null` clears the filter. |
| `search` | `boolean \| 'external'` | `false` | Puts a search field above the options. It hides the options that do not match, so the arrows skip them, the empty state takes over and the select-all button takes only what is left on screen — the selection itself survives filtering. With `'external'` nothing is hidden here: every keystroke is reported through the `search` event and the answer arrives as new `items`. |
| `searchNormalize` | `boolean` | - | Compares both sides of the filter without their diacritics, so `zoe` matches `Zoë`. It normalizes to `NFD` and drops the combining diacritics, which leaves the labels themselves untouched — only the comparison changes. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | `'Search'` | Placeholder of the search field. |
| `sectionsSelectable` | `boolean` | - | Turns every section label into a tri-state button that takes or drops the section's visible options at once. Only in the `multiple` mode; the label joins the arrow order in front of the options it stands for. |
| `selected` | `string \| string[] \| null` | `undefined` | The selected values. When set, the component renders that selection and only reports the user's changes through the `selectedChange` event. Supports the `v-model:selected` binding. |
| `selectedLabel` | `CountLabel` | `() => defaultSelectedLabel` | The header's count text. A function `(count, total) => string`, or a string in which `{count}` and `{total}` are replaced. |
| `selectionLimit` | `number \| null` | `undefined` | The number of options the selection stops at, in the `multiple` mode. Once it is reached every further selection is refused and reported through the `selectionLimit` event; deselecting always works and no option is disabled. |
| `selectionMode` | `ListBoxSelectionMode` | `'single'` | How many options can be selected at once. With `none` nothing is ever selected and activating an option fires `action` instead. |
| `translucent` | `boolean` | - | Renders the list box on a translucent background. |
| `typeahead` | `boolean` | `true` | Move the highlight to the option matching what the user types. The buffer resets after 500 ms. |
| `virtualScroller` | `boolean` | - | Renders only the options in view, so a long list costs a window instead of every option. The selection and the keyboard are untouched — the scroller is only the viewport. |
| `visibleItems` | `number` | `10` | The number of options the virtualized viewport is tall. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `action` | Callback fired when an option is activated in the `none` selection mode or when the option is a link. |
| `activeChange` | Callback fired when the highlight moves. |
| `search` | Callback fired when the search field changes. In the `'external'` search mode it is the only report the component makes — nothing is hidden here. |
| `selectedChange` | Callback fired when the selection changes. |
| `selectionLimit` | Callback fired when a selection is refused because the selection limit is reached. It fires once per interaction with the first refused value. |
| `update:active` | Emit the highlighted value to support the `v-model:active` binding. |
| `update:selected` | Emit the selected values to support the `v-model:selected` binding. |

## CListBoxOption

```jsx
import { CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | `string` | - | The second line of the option. Typeahead then matches the label alone, so typing skips the description. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Takes the option out of the keyboard order and out of every selection method. |
| `hidden` | `boolean` | - | Takes the option out of the navigation without touching the selection — this is how a filtered list keeps what the user already picked. |
| `href` | `string` | - | The href attribute specifies the URL of the page the option goes to. The option is rendered as a link, navigates on click and on Enter, and fires `action` on the way out. |
| `textValue` | `string` | - | The text typeahead matches. Defaults to the option's label. |
| `value` | `string` | - | The value the option carries. It is what the selection reports and what the methods take, so an option can be hidden or re-rendered without disturbing the selection. Defaults to the option's text. |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `label` | `string` | - | The name of the group, rendered above its options and announced with them. |

## CListBoxSelectAll


### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `indeterminate` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Shows the button in the partial state. Read only together with `selected`, and ignored while `selected` is `true`. |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Whether everything the button stands for is selected. When set, the button renders that state and leaves the acting to the `toggle` event — the scope it works on is then yours to define. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `toggle` | Callback fired when the button is pressed. The value is the state the button asks for. |

# Vue List Group Component

> Vue List Group component allows displaying a series of content. Learn how to use Vue list group to build complex list structure on your website.

## Basic example

The default list group is an unordered list with items and the proper CSS classes. Build upon it with the options that follow, or with your CSS as required.

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup>
    <CListGroupItem>Cras justo odio</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Morbi leo risus</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Porta ac consectetur ac</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Vestibulum at eros</CListGroupItem>
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Active items

Add `active` boolean property to a `<CListGroupItem>` to show the current active selection.

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup>
    <CListGroupItem active>Cras justo odio</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Morbi leo risus</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Porta ac consectetur ac</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Vestibulum at eros</CListGroupItem>
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Disabled items

Add `disabled` boolean property to a `<CListGroupItem>` to make it appear disabled.

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup>
    <CListGroupItem disabled>Cras justo odio</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Morbi leo risus</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Porta ac consectetur ac</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Vestibulum at eros</CListGroupItem>
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Links and buttons

Use `<a>`s or `<button>`s to create _actionable_ list group items with hover, disabled, and active states by adding `as="a|button"`. We separate these pseudo-classes to ensure list groups made of non-interactive elements (like `<li>`s or `<div>`s) don't provide a click or tap affordance.

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup>
    <CListGroupItem as="a" href="#" active>Cras justo odio</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="a" href="#">Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="a" href="#">Morbi leo risus</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="a" href="#">Porta ac consectetur ac</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="a" href="#" disabled>Vestibulum at eros</CListGroupItem>
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup>
    <CListGroupItem as="button" active>Cras justo odio</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="button">Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="button">Morbi leo risus</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="button">Porta ac consectetur ac</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="button" disabled>Vestibulum at eros</CListGroupItem>
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Numbered

_Added in 6.0.0._

Add `numbered` (and `as="ol"`, so the markup matches the visual order) to opt into numbered list group items. The numbers come from CSS counters, so they follow the rendered order.

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup as="ol" numbered>
    <CListGroupItem as="li">A first item</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="li">A second item</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="li">A third item</CListGroupItem>
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Flush

Add `flush` boolean property to remove some borders and rounded corners to render list group items edge-to-edge in a parent container (e.g., cards).

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup flush>
    <CListGroupItem>Cras justo odio</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Morbi leo risus</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Porta ac consectetur ac</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Vestibulum at eros</CListGroupItem>
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Horizontal

Add `layout="horizontal"` to change the layout of list group items from vertical to horizontal across all breakpoints. Alternatively, choose a responsive variant `.layout="horizontal-{sm|md|lg|xl|2xl}"` to make a list group horizontal starting at that breakpoint's `min-width`. Currently **horizontal list groups cannot be combined with flush list groups.**

```html
<template>
  <template v-for="item in ['', '-sm', '-md', '-lg', '-xl', '-2xl']" :key="item">
    <CListGroup class="mb-3" :layout="'horizontal' + item">
      <CListGroupItem>Cras justo odio</CListGroupItem>
      <CListGroupItem>Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
      <CListGroupItem>Morbi leo risus</CListGroupItem>
    </CListGroup>
  </template>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Variants

Set `theme` on an item to color it. The same theme class works on the `<CListGroup>` above it — pass it as `className` — so one setting colors the whole list, and an item's own `theme` wins over the one it inherits.

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup>
    <CListGroupItem>Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem
      v-for="item in ['primary', 'secondary', 'success', 'danger', 'warning', 'info', 'inverse']"
      :key="item"
      :theme="item"
      >A simple {{ item }} list group item</CListGroupItem
    >
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

Themes also work on `<a>`s and `<button>`s. Note the addition of the hover styles here not present in the previous example. Also supported is the `active` state; apply it to indicate an active selection on a themed list group item.

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup>
    <CListGroupItem as="a" href="#">Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem
      v-for="item in ['primary', 'secondary', 'success', 'danger', 'warning', 'info', 'inverse']"
      :key="item"
      as="a"
      href="#"
      :theme="item"
      >A simple {{ item }} list group item</CListGroupItem
    >
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

> Using color to add meaning only provides a visual indication, which will not be conveyed to users of assistive technologies – such as screen readers. Ensure that information denoted by the color is either obvious from the content itself (e.g. the visible text), or is included through alternative means, such as additional text hidden with the .visually-hidden class.

## With badges

Add badges to any list group item to show unread counts, activity, and more.

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup>
    <CListGroupItem class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center"
      >Cras justo odio<CBadge theme="primary" shape="rounded-pill">14</CBadge></CListGroupItem
    >
    <CListGroupItem class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center"
      >Dapibus ac facilisis in<CBadge theme="primary" shape="rounded-pill"
        >2</CBadge
      ></CListGroupItem
    >
    <CListGroupItem class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center"
      >Morbi leo risus<CBadge theme="primary" shape="rounded-pill">1</CBadge></CListGroupItem
    >
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem, CBadge } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

```html
    <CListGroupItem as="label"><CCheckbox class="me-1" /> Porta ac consectetur ac</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="label"><CCheckbox class="me-1" /> Vestibulum at eros</CListGroupItem>
  </CListGroup>
</template>

</script>
```

```html
<template>
```

# Vue List group Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue List group component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CListGroup

```jsx
import { CListGroup } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `string` | `'ul'` | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |
| `flush` | `boolean` | - | Remove some borders and rounded corners to render list group items edge-to-edge in a parent component (e.g., `<CCard>`) |
| `layout` | `string` | - | Specify a layout type. |
| `numbered` | `boolean` | - | Number the items - pair it with `as="ol"`, so the markup matches the visual order. |

## CListGroupItem

```jsx
import { CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the active state for the component. |
| `as` | `string` | `'li'` | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |
| `color` | `Color` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `theme` | `Color` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |

# Vue List group Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue List group component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

## CSS variables

Vue list groups use local CSS variables on `.list-group` for enhanced real-time customization. Values for the CSS variables are set via Sass, so Sass customization is still supported, too.

```scss
$list-group-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-list-group-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-list-group-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-list-group-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-list-group-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-list-group-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-5),
    --cui-list-group-item-padding-x: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-list-group-item-padding-y: var(--cui-spacer-3),
    --cui-list-group-action-color: var(--cui-fg-2),
    --cui-list-group-action-hover-color: var(--cui-fg-1),
    --cui-list-group-action-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-list-group-action-active-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-list-group-action-active-bg: var(--cui-bg-2),
    --cui-list-group-disabled-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-list-group-disabled-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-list-group-active-color: var(--cui-primary-contrast),
    --cui-list-group-active-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg),
    --cui-list-group-active-border-color: var(--cui-primary-bg),
  ),
  $list-group-tokens
);
```

### How to use CSS variables

```vue
<template>
  <CListGroup :style="vars">...</CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
const vars = {
  '--cui-list-group-color': '#333',
  '--cui-list-group-bg': '#f8f9fa',
}
</script>
```

## Sass loops

_Deprecated in 6.0.0._

Loop that generates the deprecated colour classes for `.list-group-item`s. Each class sets the same generic `--cui-theme-*` tokens that `.theme-{color}` sets, which is why the two spellings render identically — the item, its `.active` state and `.list-group-item-action` all read those tokens directly. They ship in the opt-in `coreui-legacy.css`, so a build that leaves that stylesheet out drops them.

```scss
// List group contextual variants
//
// Add modifier classes to change text and background color on individual items.
@each $state in map.keys($theme-colors) {
  .list-group-item-#{$state} {
    @include theme-tokens($state);
  }
}
```

# Vue Bootstrap List group Component

> Learn how to use CoreUI’s Vue List group component with Bootstrap styles for flexible, framework-consistent UI.

## Basic example

The default list group is an unordered list with items and the proper CSS classes. Build upon it with the options that follow, or with your CSS as required.

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup>
    <CListGroupItem>Cras justo odio</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Morbi leo risus</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Porta ac consectetur ac</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Vestibulum at eros</CListGroupItem>
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Active items

Add `active` boolean property to a `<CListGroupItem>` to show the current active selection.

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup>
    <CListGroupItem active>Cras justo odio</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Morbi leo risus</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Porta ac consectetur ac</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Vestibulum at eros</CListGroupItem>
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Disabled items

Add `disabled` boolean property to a `<CListGroupItem>` to make it appear disabled.

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup>
    <CListGroupItem disabled>Cras justo odio</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Morbi leo risus</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Porta ac consectetur ac</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Vestibulum at eros</CListGroupItem>
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Links and buttons

Use `<a>`s or `<button>`s to create _actionable_ list group items with hover, disabled, and active states by adding `as="a|button"`. We separate these pseudo-classes to ensure list groups made of non-interactive elements (like `<li>`s or `<div>`s) don't provide a click or tap affordance.

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup>
    <CListGroupItem as="a" href="#" active>Cras justo odio</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="a" href="#">Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="a" href="#">Morbi leo risus</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="a" href="#">Porta ac consectetur ac</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="a" href="#" disabled>Vestibulum at eros</CListGroupItem>
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup>
    <CListGroupItem as="button" active>Cras justo odio</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="button">Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="button">Morbi leo risus</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="button">Porta ac consectetur ac</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="button" disabled>Vestibulum at eros</CListGroupItem>
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Flush

Add `flush` boolean property to remove some borders and rounded corners to render list group items edge-to-edge in a parent container (e.g., cards).

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup flush>
    <CListGroupItem>Cras justo odio</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Morbi leo risus</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Porta ac consectetur ac</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem>Vestibulum at eros</CListGroupItem>
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Horizontal

Add `layout="horizontal"` to change the layout of list group items from vertical to horizontal across all breakpoints. Alternatively, choose a responsive variant `.layout="horizontal-{sm|md|lg|xl|2xl}"` to make a list group horizontal starting at that breakpoint's `min-width`. Currently **horizontal list groups cannot be combined with flush list groups.**

```html
<template>
  <template v-for="item in ['', '-sm', '-md', '-lg', '-xl', '-2xl']" :key="item">
    <CListGroup class="mb-3" :layout="'horizontal' + item">
      <CListGroupItem>Cras justo odio</CListGroupItem>
      <CListGroupItem>Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
      <CListGroupItem>Morbi leo risus</CListGroupItem>
    </CListGroup>
  </template>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Contextual classes

Use contextual classes to style list items with a stateful background and color.

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup>
    <CListGroupItem>Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem
      v-for="item in ['primary', 'secondary', 'success', 'danger', 'warning', 'info', 'inverse']"
      :key="item"
      :theme="item"
      >A simple {{ item }} list group item</CListGroupItem
    >
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

Contextual classes also work with `<a>`s or `<button>`s. Note the addition of the hover styles here not present in the previous example. Also supported is the `active` state; apply it to indicate an active selection on a contextual list group item.

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup>
    <CListGroupItem as="a" href="#">Dapibus ac facilisis in</CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem
      v-for="item in ['primary', 'secondary', 'success', 'danger', 'warning', 'info', 'inverse']"
      :key="item"
      as="a"
      href="#"
      :theme="item"
      >A simple {{ item }} list group item</CListGroupItem
    >
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

> Using color to add meaning only provides a visual indication, which will not be conveyed to users of assistive technologies – such as screen readers. Ensure that information denoted by the color is either obvious from the content itself (e.g. the visible text), or is included through alternative means, such as additional text hidden with the .visually-hidden class.

## With badges

Add badges to any list group item to show unread counts, activity, and more.

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup>
    <CListGroupItem class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center"
      >Cras justo odio<CBadge theme="primary" shape="rounded-pill">14</CBadge></CListGroupItem
    >
    <CListGroupItem class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center"
      >Dapibus ac facilisis in<CBadge theme="primary" shape="rounded-pill"
        >2</CBadge
      ></CListGroupItem
    >
    <CListGroupItem class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center"
      >Morbi leo risus<CBadge theme="primary" shape="rounded-pill">1</CBadge></CListGroupItem
    >
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem, CBadge } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Custom content

Add nearly any HTML within, even for linked list groups like the one below, with the help of [flexbox utilities](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/flex/).

```html
<template>
  <CListGroup>
    <CListGroupItem as="a" href="#" active>

      </div>
      <p class="mb-1">
        Donec id elit non mi porta gravida at eget metus. Maecenas sed diam eget risus varius
        blandit.
      </p>
      <small class="fg-2">Donec id elit non mi porta.</small>
    </CListGroupItem>
    <CListGroupItem as="a" href="#">
      <div class="d-flex w-100 justify-content-between">
        <h5 class="mb-1">List group item heading</h5>
        <small class="fg-2">3 days ago</small>
      </div>
      <p class="mb-1">
        Donec id elit non mi porta gravida at eget metus. Maecenas sed diam eget risus varius
        blandit.
      </p>
      <small class="fg-2">Donec id elit non mi porta.</small>
    </CListGroupItem>
  </CListGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CListGroup, CListGroupItem } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Checkboxes and radios

Place CoreUI's checkboxes and radios within list group items. Render the item as a `<label>` with `as="label"` and the whole row toggles the control, so the hit area is the item itself.

# Vue Loading Button Component

> Vue loading buttons are interactive elements that provide visual feedback to users, indicating that an action is being processed. These buttons typically display a loading spinner or animation.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Example

Create basic Vue Loading Buttons with different styles: primary, outline, and ghost. These buttons show a loading state when clicked.

```html
<template>
  <CLoadingButton theme="primary" :timeout="2000">Submit</CLoadingButton>
  <CLoadingButton theme="primary" :timeout="2000" variant="outline">Submit</CLoadingButton>
  <CLoadingButton theme="primary" :timeout="2000" variant="ghost">Submit</CLoadingButton>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CLoadingButton } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Spinners

### Border (Default)

The default option. Use loading buttons with a border spinner to indicate loading status.

```html
<template>
  <CLoadingButton theme="info" :timeout="2000">Submit</CLoadingButton>
  <CLoadingButton theme="success" variant="outline" :timeout="2000">Submit</CLoadingButton>
  <CLoadingButton theme="warning" variant="ghost" :timeout="2000">Submit</CLoadingButton>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CLoadingButton } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### Grow

Switch to a grow spinner for Vue loading buttons by adding `spinnerVariant="grow"`.

```html
<template>
  <CLoadingButton theme="info" spinner-variant="grow" :timeout="2000">Submit</CLoadingButton>
  <CLoadingButton theme="success" spinner-variant="grow" variant="outline" :timeout="2000"
    >Submit</CLoadingButton
  >
  <CLoadingButton theme="warning" spinner-variant="grow" variant="ghost" :timeout="2000"
    >Submit</CLoadingButton
  >
</template>

<script setup>
import { CLoadingButton } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Accessibility

- While the button loads with `disabledOnLoading`, it keeps focus. It gets `aria-disabled="true"` and the `.disabled` class rather than the `disabled` attribute, and activating it does nothing until it stops.
- While it loads, the spinner is named by `ariaLoadingLabel`, so the button reads as "Loading Save" to anyone who reaches it.
- When the button has focus, the start of loading is announced through [`announce()`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/accessibility/screen-readers/#announcing-messages) as its name followed by `ariaLoadingLabel` ("Save, Loading"), and the end, politely, as its name again. Nothing is announced while focus is elsewhere.

## API

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

- [&lt;CLoadingButton /&gt;](./api/#cloadingbutton)

# Vue Loading Button Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Loading Button component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## CLoadingButton

```jsx
import { CLoadingButton } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLoadingLabel` | `string` | `'Loading'` | Names the spinner while the button loads and follows the button's name when the start is announced. An empty string hides the spinner from assistive technologies. |
| `disabledOnLoading` | `boolean` | - | Blocks the button while it is loading: it gets `aria-disabled="true"` and `.disabled`, keeps focus, and ignores clicks and form submission. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Loading state (set to true to start animation). |
| `spinnerType` | `string` | `undefined` | Sets type of spinner. |
| `spinnerVariant` | `string` | `undefined` | The spinner variant. |
| `timeout` | `number` | `undefined` | Automatically starts loading animation and stops after a determined amount of milliseconds. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `click` | Event called when the user clicks on a component. |

# Vue Menu Component

> Contextual overlays for lists, links and actions: one panel component with submenus, responsive placement and viewport-aware flipping.

## Example

_Added in 6.0.0._

The Vue Menu component is the contextual overlay the library builds its menus on. [Dropdown](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/dropdown/) is a compatibility surface over it, so new work belongs here.

```html
<template>
  <CMenu>
    <CMenuToggle theme="secondary">Toggle menu</CMenuToggle>
    <CMenuContent>
      <CMenuItem href="#">Action</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuItem href="#">Another action</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuItem href="#">Something else here</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuDivider />
      <CMenuItem href="#">Separated link</CMenuItem>
    </CMenuContent>
  </CMenu>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMenu, CMenuContent, CMenuDivider, CMenuItem, CMenuToggle } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### Split button

Put the toggle beside a plain button in a [button group](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/button-group/) to build a split menu; only the toggle opens the panel. Give the toggle `split`, which narrows its padding so the pair reads as one control.

```html
<template>
  <CButtonGroup>
    <CButton theme="secondary">Split</CButton>
    <CMenu>
      <CMenuToggle theme="secondary" split>
        <CIcon :icon="cilOptions" />
        <span class="visually-hidden">Toggle menu</span>
      </CMenuToggle>
      <CMenuContent>
        <CMenuItem href="#">Action</CMenuItem>
        <CMenuItem href="#">Another action</CMenuItem>
      </CMenuContent>
    </CMenu>
  </CButtonGroup>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CButton, CButtonGroup } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CMenu, CMenuContent, CMenuItem, CMenuToggle } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
import { CIcon } from '@coreui/icons-vue'
import { cilOptions } from '@coreui/icons'
</script>
```

### Dark menus

Pass `dark` to render the panel in the dark theme, matching a dark navbar or a custom style.

```html
<template>
  <CMenu dark>
    <CMenuToggle theme="secondary">Dark menu</CMenuToggle>
    <CMenuContent>
      <CMenuItem href="#">Action</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuItem href="#">Another action</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuItem href="#">Something else here</CMenuItem>
    </CMenuContent>
  </CMenu>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMenu, CMenuContent, CMenuItem, CMenuToggle } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### Translucent menus

Blur and saturate the background of menus to create a translucent effect with the `translucent` class on `<CMenuContent>`.

```html
<template>
  <CMenu>
    <CMenuToggle theme="secondary">Menu button</CMenuToggle>
    <CMenuContent translucent>
      <CMenuItem class="active" href="#">Active menu item</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuItem href="#">Menu item</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuItem href="#">Menu item</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuItem href="#">Menu item</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuItem href="#">Menu item</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuDivider />
      <CMenuItem class="theme-danger" href="#">Danger menu item</CMenuItem>
    </CMenuContent>
  </CMenu>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMenu, CMenuContent, CMenuDivider, CMenuItem, CMenuToggle } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Placement

The `placement` property takes any Floating UI placement — `bottom-start` by default. The panel flips when the viewport runs out, and the `-start`/`-end` half of a placement is logical, so `bottom-start` opens from the right edge in a right-to-left context.

```html
<template>
  <div class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap">
    <CMenu
      v-for="placement in ['bottom-start', 'bottom-end', 'top-start', 'right-start']"
      :key="placement"
      :placement="placement"
    >
      <CMenuToggle theme="secondary">{{ placement }}</CMenuToggle>
      <CMenuContent>
        <CMenuItem href="#">Action</CMenuItem>
        <CMenuItem href="#">Another action</CMenuItem>
      </CMenuContent>
    </CMenu>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMenu, CMenuContent, CMenuItem, CMenuToggle } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### Responsive

Breakpoint prefixes make a placement responsive: `bottom-start md:top-end` reads as bottom-start below `md` and top-end from `md` up. The breakpoints are the Sass ones — `sm` 576px, `md` 768px, `lg` 1024px, `xl` 1280px, `2xl` 1536px.

```html
<template>
  <CMenu placement="bottom-start md:top-end">
    <CMenuToggle theme="secondary">Responsive placement</CMenuToggle>
    <CMenuContent>
      <CMenuItem href="#">Action</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuItem href="#">Another action</CMenuItem>
    </CMenuContent>
  </CMenu>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMenu, CMenuContent, CMenuItem, CMenuToggle } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Offset

The `offset` property moves the panel away from its toggle, as `[skidding, distance]` in pixels — skidding along the toggle, distance away from it. It defaults to `[0, 2]`.

```html
<template>
  <CMenu :offset="[10, 20]">
    <CMenuToggle>Offset</CMenuToggle>
    <CMenuContent>
      <CMenuItem href="#">Action</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuItem href="#">Another action</CMenuItem>
    </CMenuContent>
  </CMenu>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMenu, CMenuContent, CMenuItem, CMenuToggle } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Teleport

The panel renders where it sits in the markup, so an ancestor with `overflow: hidden`, a `transform` or its own stacking context clips it — the left menu below is inside a box 80px tall. Pass `portal` to render the panel through a [Teleport](https://vuejs.org/guide/built-ins/teleport.html) into `body` instead, and it escapes.

```html
<template>
  <div class="d-flex gap-4">
    <div class="border rounded p-4 overflow-hidden" style="height: 80px">
      <CMenu>
        <CMenuToggle theme="secondary">Clipped</CMenuToggle>
        <CMenuContent>
          <CMenuItem href="#">Action</CMenuItem>
          <CMenuItem href="#">Another action</CMenuItem>
          <CMenuItem href="#">Something else here</CMenuItem>
        </CMenuContent>
      </CMenu>
    </div>
    <div class="border rounded p-4 overflow-hidden" style="height: 80px">
      <CMenu portal>
        <CMenuToggle theme="secondary">Teleport</CMenuToggle>
        <CMenuContent>
          <CMenuItem href="#">Action</CMenuItem>
          <CMenuItem href="#">Another action</CMenuItem>
          <CMenuItem href="#">Something else here</CMenuItem>
        </CMenuContent>
      </CMenu>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMenu, CMenuContent, CMenuItem, CMenuToggle } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

`container` sends the panel somewhere other than the body — a CSS selector, an element, or a function returning one. Anything but `body` implies `portal`.

```vue
<CMenu container="#app-shell">
```

## Menu items

`<CMenuItem>` renders an `<a>` when it has an `href` and a `<button>` otherwise, so an action is focusable and the arrow keys reach it; pass `as` to render something else.

```html

    <CMenuToggle theme="secondary">Menu items</CMenuToggle>
    <CMenuContent>
      <CMenuItem as="button">Action</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuItem as="button">Another action</CMenuItem>
      <CMenuItem as="button">Something else here</CMenuItem>
    </CMenuContent>
  </CMenu>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMenu, CMenuContent, CMenuItem, CMenuToggle } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### Active

`active` styles the item as the current page and sets `aria-current="page"` for assistive technologies.

```html

      <CMenuItem href="#">Regular link</CMenuItem>

</script>
```

### Disabled

`disabled` styles the item as unavailable and stops it from being activated.


### Variants

Colour an individual item with a [`.theme-*` class](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/customize/components/#theme-variants). The item reads the theme's foreground while at rest and swaps to the theme's fill with a contrasting label once it is `active`, so one class covers both states.

```html
<template>
  <div class="d-flex gap-4">
    <CMenu>
      <CMenuToggle theme="secondary">At rest</CMenuToggle>
      <CMenuContent>
        <CMenuItem v-for="theme in themes" :key="theme" :class="`theme-${theme}`" href="#">
          {{ theme }} link
        </CMenuItem>
      </CMenuContent>
    </CMenu>
    <CMenu>
      <CMenuToggle theme="secondary">Active</CMenuToggle>
      <CMenuContent>
        <CMenuItem v-for="theme in themes" :key="theme" active :class="`theme-${theme}`" href="#">
          {{ theme }} link
        </CMenuItem>
      </CMenuContent>
    </CMenu>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMenu, CMenuContent, CMenuItem, CMenuToggle } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const themes = ['primary', 'secondary', 'success', 'danger']
</script>
```

### Selected

`selected` marks the current choice and sets `aria-current`. Give every item a `.menu-item-check` `<svg>` and only the selected one shows it, so the panel keeps its width as the choice moves.

```html
<template>
  <CMenu>
    <CMenuToggle theme="secondary">Select status</CMenuToggle>
    <CMenuContent>
      <CMenuItem
        v-for="option in statuses"
        :key="option.value"
        as="button"
        :selected="status === option.value"
        @click="status = option.value"
      >
        <span class="menu-item-content">
          {{ option.label }}
          <small class="menu-item-description">{{ option.description }}</small>
        </span>
        <svg
          class="menu-item-check"
          width="16"
          height="16"
          fill="none"
          stroke="currentColor"
          stroke-linecap="round"
          stroke-linejoin="round"
          stroke-width="2"
          viewBox="0 0 16 16"
        >
          <path d="m2 7 4 5 8-8" />
        </svg>
      </CMenuItem>
    </CMenuContent>
  </CMenu>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CMenu, CMenuContent, CMenuItem, CMenuToggle } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const statuses = [
  { value: 'published', label: 'Published', description: 'Currently visible to users' },
  { value: 'draft', label: 'Draft', description: 'Not yet published' },
  { value: 'archived', label: 'Archived', description: 'Kept, but out of the way' },
]

const status = ref('published')
</script>
```

## Submenus

`<CSubmenu>` nests a menu inside a menu. Its `toggler` becomes the parent item, and the nested panel opens on hover and on click. Below `576px` a submenu stacks over the parent panel with a back button instead of flying out to the side.

```html
<template>
  <CMenu>
    <CMenuToggle theme="secondary">Submenus</CMenuToggle>
    <CMenuContent>
      <CSubmenu toggler="File">
        <CMenuItem href="#">New</CMenuItem>
        <CMenuItem href="#">Open</CMenuItem>
        <CMenuItem href="#">Save</CMenuItem>
      </CSubmenu>
      <CSubmenu toggler="Edit">
        <CMenuItem href="#">Cut</CMenuItem>
        <CMenuItem href="#">Copy</CMenuItem>
        <CMenuItem href="#">Paste</CMenuItem>
      </CSubmenu>
      <CSubmenu toggler="View">
        <CMenuItem href="#">Zoom In</CMenuItem>
        <CMenuItem href="#">Zoom Out</CMenuItem>
      </CSubmenu>
      <CMenuDivider />
      <CMenuItem href="#">Preferences</CMenuItem>
    </CMenuContent>
  </CMenu>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CMenu,
  CMenuContent,
  CMenuDivider,
  CMenuItem,
  CMenuToggle,
  CSubmenu,
} from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

### Nested

Submenus nest to any depth. Each level opens to the side and flips direction when the viewport runs out.

```html
<template>
  <CMenu>
    <CMenuToggle theme="secondary">Multi-level menu</CMenuToggle>
    <CMenuContent>
      <CMenuItem href="#">Level 1 action</CMenuItem>
      <CSubmenu toggler="Level 1 submenu">
        <CMenuItem href="#">Level 2 action</CMenuItem>
        <CSubmenu toggler="Level 2 submenu">
          <CMenuItem href="#">Level 3 action A</CMenuItem>
          <CMenuItem href="#">Level 3 action B</CMenuItem>
        </CSubmenu>
        <CMenuItem href="#">Another level 2</CMenuItem>
      </CSubmenu>
      <CMenuItem href="#">Another level 1</CMenuItem>
    </CMenuContent>
  </CMenu>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMenu, CMenuContent, CMenuItem, CMenuToggle, CSubmenu } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Auto close behavior

By default a menu closes on a click inside or outside it. `autoClose` narrows that to `'inside'` or `'outside'`, and `false` leaves only the toggle. Escape always closes the menu and returns focus to the toggle, whatever the setting.

```html
<template>
  <div class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap">
    <CMenu
      v-for="autoClose in [true, 'inside', 'outside', false]"
      :key="String(autoClose)"
      :auto-close="autoClose"
    >
      <CMenuToggle theme="secondary">autoClose: {{ autoClose }}</CMenuToggle>
      <CMenuContent>
        <CMenuItem href="#">Action</CMenuItem>
        <CMenuItem href="#">Another action</CMenuItem>
      </CMenuContent>
    </CMenu>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CMenu, CMenuContent, CMenuItem, CMenuToggle } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Usage with v-model

Pass `show` and the menu renders what you pass — the toggle and the dismiss gestures only emit `@update:show`, so feed the change back, or nothing moves. The `v-model:show` binding is that loop in one attribute. Here an external button drives the same state the menu's own gestures request changes to.

```html
<template>
  <div class="d-flex gap-3">
    <CButton theme="secondary" variant="outline" @click="show = !show">
      {{ show ? 'Close the menu' : 'Open the menu' }}
    </CButton>
    <CMenu v-model:show="show">
      <CMenuToggle theme="secondary">Toggle menu</CMenuToggle>
      <CMenuContent>
        <CMenuItem href="#">Action</CMenuItem>
        <CMenuItem href="#">Another action</CMenuItem>
        <CMenuItem href="#">Something else here</CMenuItem>
      </CMenuContent>
    </CMenu>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CMenu, CMenuContent, CMenuItem, CMenuToggle } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const show = ref(false)
</script>
```

Use it when the open state belongs to something else — a command palette shortcut, a tour step, or a control outside the menu like the button above.

### Initial open state

Without a binding the toggle manages the panel. Pass `show` to seed it open on mount.

```vue
<CMenu show>
```

`@update:show` fires either way whenever the menu requests an open-state change — a dismiss gesture (Escape, an outside click, an item click) or any internal toggle. The deprecated `visible` prop keeps its old behavior and is ignored when `show` is set.

## Accessibility

The toggle carries `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded`, the panel `role="menu"`, and each item `role="menuitem"`; a selected item is `aria-current`.

### Keyboard navigation

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `↓` / `↑` | Move focus to the next/previous item — from the toggle, open the panel and step into it |
| `→` | Open the focused submenu |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Activate the focused item, or open its submenu |
| `Esc` | Close the menu and return focus to the toggle |

# Vue Menu Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Menu component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CMenu

```jsx
import { CMenu } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `autoClose` | `boolean \| 'inside' \| 'outside'` | `true` | Configures the auto close behavior: - `true` — closes on a click inside or outside the menu, - `'inside'` — closes on a click inside the menu only, - `'outside'` — closes on a click outside the menu only, - `false` — closes only on the toggle or the Escape key. |
| `container` | `HTMLElement \| (() => HTMLElement) \| string` | `'body'` | The element the panel is rendered into instead of `document.body`. You can pass an HTML element or function that returns a single element. Implies `portal`. Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert. |
| `dark` | `boolean` | - | Renders the panel in the dark theme. |
| `offset` | `[number, number]` | `() => [0, 2]` | The distance of the panel from its toggle, as `[skidding, distance]`. |
| `placement` | `string` | `'bottom-start'` | Where the panel opens. Logical placements (`'start'`, `'end'`) resolve to the writing direction, and `-start`/`-end` are already logical. Breakpoint prefixes make it responsive — `'bottom-start md:top-end'` reads as bottom-start below `md` and top-end from `md` up. |
| `portal` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders the panel through a Teleport. |
| `show` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Control the open state. When set, the menu renders what `show` says and dismiss gestures only emit `update:show` — nothing closes until the parent flips the prop. Supports the `v-model:show` binding. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Controls the visibility of the menu. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `hide` | Callback fired when the menu is hidden. |
| `show` | Callback fired when the menu is shown. |
| `update:show` | Emit the requested open state to support the `v-model:show` binding — a dismiss gesture (Escape, outside click, item click) or any internal toggle. |

## CMenuContent

```jsx
import { CMenuContent } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maxHeight` | `number\|string` | `undefined` | The height at which a scrollable panel starts scrolling. |
| `scrollable` | `boolean` | - | Renders the panel with its own scrollbar once it grows past `maxHeight`. |
| `translucent` | `boolean` | - | Give the menu a translucent, blurred surface. |

## CMenuDivider

```jsx
import { CMenuDivider } from '@coreui/vue'
```

## CMenuHeader


| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `string` | `'h6'` | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |

## CMenuItem

```jsx
import { CMenuItem } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the active state for the component. |
| `as` | `string` | - | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `href` | `string` | - | The href attribute specifies the URL of the page the link goes to. |
| `selected` | `boolean` | - | Marks the item as the current selection. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |

## CMenuToggle

```jsx
import { CMenuToggle } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `string` | `'button'` | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |
| `color` | `Color` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |
| `custom` | `boolean` | - | Wire the menu to a toggle of your own instead of rendering a button. The single slot element receives the toggle behavior and keeps its own markup and classes. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `shape` | `Shape` | - |  |
| `size` | `string` | - | Size the component small or large. |
| `split` | `boolean` | - | Renders the toggle as the second half of a split button, so only it opens the menu. |
| `theme` | `Color` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. Pair it with `variant` for the shape — a button is a shape plus a colour. |
| `variant` | `string` | - | Set the shape of the button — how much ink it uses. Defaults to `solid` when `theme` is set. |

## CSubmenu

```jsx
import { CSubmenu } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `show` | `boolean` | `undefined` | The open state of the nested menu. Bind it with `v-model:show` to hand control to the parent — hover, click and the keyboard then only emit `update:show` and nothing moves until the parent flips the value. Passed one-way it seeds the starting state and the submenu keeps managing itself. |
| `toggler` | `string` | `undefined` | The trigger the nested menu opens from, rendered as the submenu's own `.menu-item`. The `toggler` slot takes precedence over the prop. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `update:show` | Emit the requested open state to support the `v-model:show` binding. |
