# Vue Progress Component

> Documentation and examples for using Vue progress bars featuring support for stacked bars, animated backgrounds, and text labels.

## Example

Progress components are built with two HTML elements, some CSS to set the width, and a few attributes. We don't use [the HTML5 `<progress>` element](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/progress), ensuring you can stack progress bars, animate them, and place text labels over them.

## Basic usage

```html
<template>
  <CProgress :value="0" />
  <CProgress :value="25" />
  <CProgress :value="50" />
  <CProgress :value="75" />
  <CProgress :value="100" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CProgress } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Labels

Add labels to your progress bars by placing text within the `<CProgressBar>`.

```html
<template>
  <CProgress :value="25">25%</CProgress>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CProgress } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

Please note that the default setting for the content within the `` is to be limited by the `overflow: hidden property`, preventing it from extending beyond the bar's boundaries. If the progress bar is shorter than its label, the content will be truncated and could be difficult to read. To modify this behavior, you can utilize the `.overflow-visible` class from the overflow utilities. However, it is important to specify a specific text color to ensure readability. It's worth noting that this approach currently does not consider color modes.

```html
<template>
  <CProgress :value="10" color="success">
    <CProgressBar class="overflow-visible fg-black px-3"
      >Long label text for the progress bar, set to a dark color</CProgressBar
    >
  </CProgress>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CProgress, CProgressBar } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

Since **v5.0.0** you can also use the `progressBarClassName` property directly on the `` component to achieve the same.

```vue
<CProgress progressBarClassName="overflow-visible fg-black px-3" color="success" :value="10">Long label text for the progress bar, set to a dark color</CProgress>
```

### Long labels

A `<CProgressBar>` clips what does not fit — it is `overflow: hidden` with `white-space: nowrap` — so a label wider than the bar is cut off rather than wrapped. Add [`overflow-visible`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/overflow/) to let it spill over the track instead.

```html
<template>
  <CProgress class="mb-4">
    <CProgressBar :value="10">Filling in your details</CProgressBar>
  </CProgress>
  <CProgress>
    <CProgressBar class="overflow-visible" :value="10">Filling in your details</CProgressBar>
  </CProgress>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CProgress, CProgressBar } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

Spilling over comes at a cost: the label then sits on two backgrounds at once, so its color has to contrast with both the bar and the track. Where it cannot, put the label outside the progress bar instead.

## Height

We only set a `height` value on the `<CProgress>`, so if you change that value the inner `<CProgressBar>` will automatically resize accordingly.

```html
<template>
  <CProgress :height="1" :value="25" />
  <CProgress :height="20" :value="25" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CProgress } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Backgrounds

Use `color` prop to change the appearance of individual progress bars.

```html
<template>
  <CProgress color="success" :value="25" />
  <CProgress color="info" :value="50" />
  <CProgress color="warning" :value="75" />
  <CProgress color="danger" :value="100" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CProgress } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

Ensure that when you incorporate labels into progress bars featuring a custom background color, you also select an appropriate text color to ensure readability and maintain adequate contrast for the labels.

```html
<template>
  <CProgress color="success" :value="25">
    <CProgressBar>25%</CProgressBar>
  </CProgress>
  <CProgress color="info" :value="50">
    <CProgressBar class="fg-black">50%</CProgressBar>
  </CProgress>
  <CProgress color="warning" :value="75">
    <CProgressBar class="fg-black">75%</CProgressBar>
  </CProgress>
  <CProgress color="danger" :value="100">
    <CProgressBar>100%</CProgressBar>
  </CProgress>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CProgress, CProgressBar } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

Since **v5.0.0** you can also use the `progressBarClassName` property directly on the `` component to achieve the same.

```vue
<CProgress color="success" :value="25">25%</CProgress>
<CProgress color="info" progressBarClassName="fg-black" :value="50">50%</CProgress>
<CProgress color="warning" progressBarClassName="fg-black" :value="75">75%</CProgress>
<CProgress color="danger" :value="100">100%</CProgress>
```

## Gradients

_Added in 6.0.0._

Set `--cui-progress-bar-bg-image` to paint the bar with a gradient instead of a flat colour. The image is sized to the bar, so the whole gradient is visible at any width and the label keeps the colour set by the theme. Set it in `style` on `<CProgress>`; the bar reads it from there.

```html
<template>
  <CProgress
    :value="45"
    style="--cui-progress-bar-bg-image: linear-gradient(to right, #e6412c, #ffb400, #ffe25a)"
  />
  <CProgress
    :value="70"
    style="
      --cui-progress-bar-bg-image: linear-gradient(
        to right,
        var(--cui-info-base),
        var(--cui-success-base)
      );
    "
  >
    70%
  </CProgress>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CProgress } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

Stripes are a second layer over the gradient, so `variant="striped"` and `animated` combine with it. Change the stripe pattern itself with `--cui-progress-bar-stripes`, or just its colour with `--cui-progress-bar-stripe-color`.

```html
<template>
  <CProgress
    animated
    :value="65"
    variant="striped"
    style="--cui-progress-bar-bg-image: linear-gradient(to right, #e6412c, #ffb400, #ffe25a)"
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CProgress } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Multiple bars

Include multiple progress bars in a progress component if you need.

> In version 5.0.0, we introduced a new &lt;CProgressStacked&gt; component to more logically wrap multiple progress bars into a single stacked progress bar. The previous structure will continue to work until the next major version.

**New markup**

```html
<template>
  <CProgressStacked>
    <CProgress :value="15" />
    <CProgress color="success" :value="30" />
    <CProgress color="info" :value="20" />
  </CProgressStacked>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CProgressStacked, CProgress } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

**Previous markup**
```vue
<CProgress>
  <CProgressBar :value="15" />
  <CProgressBar theme="success" :value="30" />
  <CProgressBar theme="info" :value="20" />
</CProgress>
```

## Segmented

_Added in 6.0.0._

Add `segmented` to cut the track into a row of rounded segments. It is a CSS mask over the whole component, so the bar keeps its transition, theme, gradient and stripes; only the rendering changes. Segments are `--cui-progress-segment-min-width` wide (.25rem) and `--cui-progress-segment-gap` apart, as many as fit; set `segments` and the track holds at most that many, scaled to its width, with the gap staying put.

The component watches the track's width and fills whole segments only: `value` is turned into the number of segments it covers, rounded down, so the fill always ends on a segment's edge and a narrow screen shows fewer segments rather than thinner ones.

```html
<template>
  <CProgress
    :height="48"
    segmented
    :value="45"
    style="--cui-progress-bar-bg-image: linear-gradient(to right, #e6412c, #ffb400, #ffe25a)"
  />
  <CProgress segmented theme="success" :value="70" />
  <CProgress
    :height="24"
    segmented
    :segments="20"
    theme="info"
    :value="30"
    style="--cui-progress-segment-gap: 0.5rem"
  />
  <CProgress
    :height="24"
    segmented
    theme="danger"
    :value="30"
    style="--cui-progress-segment-min-width: 1rem"
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CProgress } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

The corners follow `--cui-progress-segment-border-radius`, `--cui-radius-2` by default, capped at half the segment and half the track height as `border-radius` would. Set it to `0px` for square segments, or anything in between; the value feeds the mask's `calc()`, so it has to be a length.

```html
<template>
  <CProgress
    :height="24"
    segmented
    :segments="10"
    :value="60"
    style="--cui-progress-segment-border-radius: 0px"
  />
  <CProgress
    :height="24"
    segmented
    :segments="10"
    theme="warning"
    :value="60"
    style="--cui-progress-segment-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-5)"
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CProgress } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## On a colored surface

Add the `white` property to draw the bar in the current text color and the track as a faint tint of it. That way a progress bar sitting on a solid or brand-colored surface takes its colors from the text around it rather than needing a color of its own.

```html
<template>
  <CProgress white :value="50" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CProgress } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Striped

Add `variant="striped"` to any `<CProgressBar>` to apply a stripe via CSS gradient over the progress bar's background color.

```html
<template>
  <CProgress color="success" variant="striped" :value="25" />
  <CProgress color="info" variant="striped" :value="50" />
  <CProgress color="warning" variant="striped" :value="75" />
  <CProgress color="danger" variant="striped" :value="100" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CProgress } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Animated stripes

The striped gradient can also be animated. Add `animated` property to `<CProgressBar>` to animate the stripes right to left via CSS3 animations.

```html
<template>
  <CProgress color="success" variant="striped" animated :value="25" />
  <CProgress color="info" variant="striped" animated :value="50" />
  <CProgress color="warning" variant="striped" animated :value="75" />
  <CProgress color="danger" variant="striped" animated :value="100" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CProgress } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Grouping bars

Related bars need no component of their own — [stacks](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/helpers/stacks/) and [spacing utilities](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/margin/) lay them out. Put a label column beside a `vstack` of bars to compare several series against the same baseline.

```html
<template>
  <div class="hstack gap-4">
    <span class="fg-2 small flex-shrink-0" style="width: 100px">Title</span>
    <div class="vstack gap-1">
      <CProgress :height="4">
        <CProgressBar theme="info" :value="34" aria-label="First series" />
      </CProgress>
      <CProgress :height="4">
        <CProgressBar theme="danger" :value="78" aria-label="Second series" />
      </CProgress>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CProgress, CProgressBar } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

# Vue Progress Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Progress component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CProgress

```jsx
import { CProgress } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animated` | `boolean` | - | Use to animate the stripes right to left via CSS3 animations. |
| `color` | `Color` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |
| `height` | `number` | - | Sets the height of the component. If you set that value the inner `<CProgressBar>` will automatically resize accordingly. |
| `progressBarClassName` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the <CProgressBar/> component. |
| `segmented` | `boolean` | - | Cuts the track into a row of rounded segments and fills whole segments only. Set `segments` to cap how many, otherwise as many as fit above `--cui-progress-segment-min-width`. |
| `segments` | `number` | - | The most segments a segmented track holds; fewer are drawn when they would get narrower than `--cui-progress-segment-min-width`. |
| `value` | `number` | `0` | The percent to progress the ProgressBar. |
| `variant` | `string` | - | Set the progress bar variant to optional striped. |
| `white` | `boolean` | - | Change the default color to white. |

## CProgressBar

```jsx
import { CProgressBar } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `animated` | `boolean` | - | Use to animate the stripes right to left via CSS3 animations. |
| `color` | `Color` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |
| `theme` | `Color` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |
| `value` | `number` | `0` | The percent to progress the ProgressBar. |
| `variant` | `string` | - | Set the progress bar variant to optional striped. |

# Vue Progress Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Progress component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

## CSS variables

Vue cards use local CSS variables on `.card` for enhanced real-time customization. Values for the CSS variables are set via Sass, so Sass customization is still supported, too.

```scss
$progress-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-progress-height: 1rem,
    --cui-progress-font-size: var(--cui-font-size-sm),
    --cui-progress-bg: var(--cui-bg-2),
    --cui-progress-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-5),
    --cui-progress-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow-inset),
    --cui-progress-bar-color: var(--cui-primary-contrast),
    --cui-progress-bar-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg),
    --cui-progress-bar-bg-image: none,
    --cui-progress-bar-stripes: linear-gradient(45deg, var(--cui-progress-bar-stripe-color) 25%, transparent 25%, transparent 50%, var(--cui-progress-bar-stripe-color) 50%, var(--cui-progress-bar-stripe-color) 75%, transparent 75%, transparent),
    --cui-progress-bar-stripe-color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-white) 15%, transparent),
    --cui-progress-bar-transition: width .6s ease,
    --cui-progress-bar-animation: progress-bar-stripes 1s linear infinite,
  ),
  $progress-tokens
);
```

`segmented` adds the segment geometry:

```scss
$progress-segmented-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-progress-segment-gap: .25rem,
    --cui-progress-segment-min-width: .25rem,
    --cui-progress-segment-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-2),
  ),
  $progress-segmented-tokens
);

// Unset by default: the plugin then packs as many segments as fit above the minimum width
@if $progress-segments != null {
  $progress-segmented-tokens: map.set($progress-segmented-tokens, --cui-progress-segments, $progress-segments);
}
```

### How to use CSS variables

```vue
<template>
  <CProgress :style="vars">...</CProgress>
</template>

<script setup>
const vars = {
  '--cui-progress-bar-color': '#333',
  '--cui-progress-bg': '#f8f9fa',
}
</script>
```

## Sass variables

_Deprecated in 6.0.0._

Sass variables set these defaults at build time and are removed in v7. The CSS variables above reach the same values without recompiling, and can be set on a single element.

```scss
$progress-segments:                    null !default;

$progress-contrast-track-opacity:      20% !default;
```

# Vue Scrollspy Component

> Automatically update the navigation based on scroll position to indicate which section is currently active in the viewport.

## How it works

_Added in 6.0.0._

`<CScrollspy>` watches the sections you list by id and hands the id of the current one to its default slot — the navigation stays yours, controlled through the `active` property like everywhere else in Vue. It is best used with a [nav component](../navs-tabs/) or [list group](../list-group/), but any anchor elements in the page work the same way. Here's how it works.

- To start, scrollspy requires two things: a navigation, list group, or a simple set of links, plus a scrollable container. The scrollable container can be the viewport or a custom element with a set `height` and `overflow-y: scroll`.
- List the section ids in `ids`, in document order, and pass the scrollable element through `container` (a template ref) when it is not the viewport. If there is no focusable element inside the container, be sure to also include `tabindex="0"` to ensure keyboard access.
- As you scroll the container, the scoped default slot (`#default="{ activeId }"`) receives the id of the active section, and `activate` is emitted whenever it changes. Ids must resolve to an element in the DOM, otherwise they're ignored — a link `<a href="#home">` needs something like `<div id="home">` among the sections.
- Sections are looked up when the component mounts and whenever `ids` or `container` change; a section added later is picked up once `ids` changes.

### Detection

The component watches every section with an [`IntersectionObserver`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/IntersectionObserver) and decides which one is current from a single rule: an invisible **activation line** drawn across the scroll container, `topMargin` below its top edge (`12%` of the container's height by default). The result depends only on where the container is scrolled to, never on which direction it got there.

- **The active section is the lowest one whose top edge has moved up to or above the activation line.** When several sections are visible at once, the one you have scrolled furthest into wins.
- **Between two sections nothing changes.** While the gap between one section's end and the next heading crosses the line, the previous id stays active instead of the navigation going blank.
- **Above the first section the first id is active**, so the navigation is never empty once the container has content.
- **At the bottom of the container the last id is active**, even when the last section is too short for its top edge to ever reach the line.

Move the line with `topMargin` — a percentage of the container's height or a pixel value, for example `96px` to put it just below a sticky navbar; a pixel line is recomputed when the window resizes. To take over the observer's root box entirely, set `rootMargin` instead; when both are given, `rootMargin` wins. See the [API](#api).

### Scrollable containers and keyboard access

If you're making a scrollable container (other than the viewport), be sure to have a `height` set and `overflow-y: scroll;` applied to it—alongside `tabindex="0"` to ensure keyboard access.

## Examples

### Navbar

Scroll the area below the navbar and watch the active state change. Open the dropdown and watch the dropdown items be highlighted as well — the toggle lights up whenever any of its items is the active one.

```html
<template>
  <CScrollspy :ids="['spyNavHeading1', 'spyNavHeading2', ...dropdownIds]" :container="container">
    <template #default="{ activeId }">
      <CNavbar class="bg-3 px-4">
        <CNavbarBrand href="#">Navbar</CNavbarBrand>

          <CNavItem>

                Fourth
              </CDropdownItem>

                Fifth
              </CDropdownItem>
            </CDropdownMenu>
          </CDropdown>
        </CNav>
      </CNavbar>
      <div ref="pane" class="overflow-auto p-4" style="max-height: 14rem" tabindex="0">
        <h4 id="spyNavHeading1">First heading</h4>
        <p>{{ copy }}</p>
        <h4 id="spyNavHeading2">Second heading</h4>
        <p>{{ copy }}</p>
```

### Nested nav

Scrollspy also works with nested `<CNav>`s. The component reports one active id, so parent activation is yours to derive — a small map from parent to its section ids keeps the group's link lit while any of its children is active. Scroll the area next to the navbar and watch the active state change.

```html
<template>
  <CScrollspy :ids="Object.values(groups).flat()" :container="container">
    <template #default="{ activeId }">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-4">
          <CNav class="flex-column" variant="pills">
            <CNavLink href="#spyItem1" :active="parentOf(activeId) === 'spyItem1'">Item 1</CNavLink>
            <CNav class="flex-column ms-4" variant="pills">
              <CNavLink href="#spyItem1-1" :active="activeId === 'spyItem1-1'">Item 1-1</CNavLink>
              <CNavLink href="#spyItem1-2" :active="activeId === 'spyItem1-2'">Item 1-2</CNavLink>
            </CNav>
            <CNavLink href="#spyItem2" :active="parentOf(activeId) === 'spyItem2'">Item 2</CNavLink>
            <CNavLink href="#spyItem3" :active="parentOf(activeId) === 'spyItem3'">Item 3</CNavLink>
            <CNav class="flex-column ms-4" variant="pills">
              <CNavLink href="#spyItem3-1" :active="activeId === 'spyItem3-1'">Item 3-1</CNavLink>
              <CNavLink href="#spyItem3-2" :active="activeId === 'spyItem3-2'">Item 3-2</CNavLink>
            </CNav>
          </CNav>
        </div>
        <div ref="pane" class="col-8 overflow-auto" style="max-height: 16rem" tabindex="0">
          <h4 id="spyItem1">Item 1</h4>
          <p>{{ copy }}</p>
          <h5 id="spyItem1-1">Item 1-1</h5>
          <p>{{ copy }}</p>
          <h5 id="spyItem1-2">Item 1-2</h5>
          <p>{{ copy }}</p>
          <h4 id="spyItem2">Item 2</h4>
          <p>{{ copy }}</p>
          <h4 id="spyItem3">Item 3</h4>
          <p>{{ copy }}</p>
          <h5 id="spyItem3-1">Item 3-1</h5>
          <p>{{ copy }}</p>
          <h5 id="spyItem3-2">Item 3-2</h5>
          <p>{{ copy }}</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </template>
  </CScrollspy>
</template>

<script setup>
import { useTemplateRef } from 'vue'
import { CNav, CNavLink } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CScrollspy } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const copy =
  'This is some placeholder content for the scrollspy page. Note that as you scroll down the page, the appropriate navigation link is highlighted.'

const groups = {
  spyItem1: ['spyItem1', 'spyItem1-1', 'spyItem1-2'],
  spyItem2: ['spyItem2'],
  spyItem3: ['spyItem3', 'spyItem3-1', 'spyItem3-2'],
}

const container = useTemplateRef('pane')

const parentOf = (id) =>
  id ? Object.keys(groups).find((parent) => groups[parent].includes(id)) : undefined
</script>
```


```html
          </template>

      </div>
    </template>
  </CScrollspy>
```

# Vue Scrollspy Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Scrollspy component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CScrollspy

```jsx
import { CScrollspy } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `container` | `HTMLElement \| null` | `null` | The scrollable element holding the sections. Bind a template ref; without it the viewport is the root. |
| `ids` | `string[]` | - | Ids of the sections to observe, in document order. |
| `rootMargin` | `string \| null` | `null` | Raw IntersectionObserver `rootMargin`. When set it takes precedence over `topMargin` and is passed straight to the observer. |
| `threshold` | `number[]` | `() => [0]` | Intersection observer thresholds. |
| `topMargin` | `string` | `'12%'` | Position of the activation line, measured from the top of the scroll root. The active section is the deepest one whose top has scrolled to or above it. Accepts a percentage (`12%`) or pixels (`96px`, e.g. below a sticky navbar). |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `activate` | Callback fired when the active section changes. |

# Vue Search Button Component

> Vue search button component for keyboard-aware search entry points, command palettes, modals, and offcanvas panels.

## Overview

_Added in 5.9.0._

The CoreUI **Vue Search Button component** is a trigger element designed for search entry points and command-style actions. It behaves like a regular button on click, but it can also react to a configurable keyboard shortcut such as `meta+/` or `ctrl+/`.

- Use it as a standalone trigger for a custom search UI.
- Pair it with reactive state to open a modal, offcanvas, or command palette.
- Shortcut keys are rendered automatically.
- Displayed shortcut keys react to keyboard interaction and receive an `.active` state while pressed.

## Basic example

Use `<CSearchButton>` as the entry point for a search interface. Listen to `@trigger` as the main activation callback for both direct interaction and keyboard shortcuts.

```html
<template>
  <CSearchButton
    aria-label="Open search dialog"
    aria-controls="search-button-modal"
    shortcut="meta+/,ctrl+/"
    @trigger="visible = true"
  />
  <CModal
    id="search-button-modal"
    :visible="visible"
    aria-labelledby="search-button-modal-title"
    @close="visible = false"
  >
    <CModalHeader>
      <CModalTitle id="search-button-modal-title" class="w-100">
        <CFormInput type="search" placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search" />
      </CModalTitle>
    </CModalHeader>
    <CModalBody>
      <p class="fg-2 small mb-3">Recent searches</p>
      <CListGroup flush>
        <CListGroupItem
          as="button"
          type="button"
          class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center"
        >
          CoreUI components overview
          <CBadge theme="secondary" shape="rounded-pill">Open</CBadge>
        </CListGroupItem>
        <CListGroupItem
          as="button"
          type="button"
          class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center"
        >
          Modal dialog examples
          <CBadge theme="secondary" shape="rounded-pill">Open</CBadge>
        </CListGroupItem>
        <CListGroupItem
          as="button"
          type="button"
          class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center"
        >
          Sidebar navigation customization
          <CBadge theme="secondary" shape="rounded-pill">Open</CBadge>
        </CListGroupItem>
      </CListGroup>
    </CModalBody>
  </CModal>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import {
  CBadge,
  CFormInput,
  CListGroup,
  CListGroupItem,
  CModal,
  CModalBody,
  CModalHeader,
  CModalTitle,
  CSearchButton,
} from '@coreui/vue'

const visible = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Custom shortcut

Configure the shortcut with the `shortcut` prop. On macOS, the component prefers the `meta` variant for the visible label. On Windows and Linux, it prefers the `ctrl` variant.

> Shortcuts such as `meta+f`, `ctrl+f`, `meta+s`, or `ctrl+s` can override native browser or system shortcuts. Prefer safer combinations such as `meta+/` and `ctrl+/` unless replacing the default behavior is intentional.

```html
<template>
  <div>
    <CSearchButton
      aria-label="Open command palette"
      placeholder="Command palette"
      shortcut="meta+i,ctrl+i"
      @trigger="count++"
    />
    <CAlert theme="info" class="mt-4 mb-0">
      Triggered {{ count }} {{ count === 1 ? 'time' : 'times' }} with click or shortcut.
    </CAlert>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CAlert, CSearchButton } from '@coreui/vue'

const count = ref(0)
</script>
```

## Launch an offcanvas

The component works naturally with reactive state and a dedicated `@trigger` event. This demo uses `meta+shift+o` / `ctrl+shift+o` to avoid colliding with other live examples on the page.

```html
<template>
  <CSearchButton
    aria-label="Open search panel"
    aria-controls="search-button-offcanvas"
    shortcut="meta+shift+o,ctrl+shift+o"
    @trigger="visible = true"
  />
  <COffcanvas
    id="search-button-offcanvas"
    placement="end"
    :visible="visible"
    @hide="visible = false"
  >
    <COffcanvasHeader>
      <COffcanvasTitle>Search panel</COffcanvasTitle>
      <CCloseButton class="fg-reset" @click="visible = false" />
    </COffcanvasHeader>
    <COffcanvasBody>
      <CFormInput type="search" class="mb-4" placeholder="Search..." aria-label="Search in panel" />
      <p class="mb-0">Use this space for filters, recent searches, or command shortcuts.</p>
    </COffcanvasBody>
  </COffcanvas>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import {
  CCloseButton,
  CFormInput,
  COffcanvas,
  COffcanvasBody,
  COffcanvasHeader,
  COffcanvasTitle,
  CSearchButton,
} from '@coreui/vue'

const visible = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Keyboard behavior

### When the configured shortcut is pressed

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` / `Space` on a focused search button | Trigger the component activation callback |
| Configured shortcut, e.g. `⌘/` / `Ctrl+/` | Trigger the component activation callback |
| Modifier key inside the visible shortcut | Add `.active` to the corresponding `.search-button-key` while pressed |
| Final key inside the visible shortcut | Add `.active` to the corresponding `.search-button-key` while pressed |

### Keyboard state behavior

| Interaction | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Matching shortcut on `keydown` | Optionally prevents the browser's default behavior and emits `trigger` |
| Plain typing inside `input`, `textarea`, `select`, or `contenteditable` | Does not trigger the component without `meta` or `ctrl` |
| `keyup` after a shortcut key press | Removes `.active` from the rendered shortcut keys |
| Browser window `blur` | Clears all active shortcut key states |
| Multiple configured shortcuts | The component listens to all configured shortcuts and renders the platform-preferred one in the UI |

## Accessibility

Accessibility is an important part of the Search Button design. The component includes built-in behaviors that help preserve expected keyboard interaction and reduce conflicts with assistive technologies, but accessible results still depend on choosing the right markup and shortcut combinations.

### Built-in accessibility behavior

- Native button semantics are preserved because `<CSearchButton>` renders a `<button type="button">` by default.
- Rendered `.search-button-keys` are treated as visual hints only and are hidden from assistive technologies.
- Plain typing inside editable fields does not trigger the component unless the shortcut also includes `meta` or `ctrl`.
- The component keeps standard button keyboard behavior such as `Enter` and `Space`.

### Author responsibilities

- Choose shortcuts carefully and avoid overriding common browser or system shortcuts unless that behavior is intentional and clearly communicated.
- Make sure the visible button label clearly describes the action, for example `Search`, `Open search`, or `Command palette`.
- Mark decorative icons as `aria-hidden="true"` when you provide a custom `icon`.

## API

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the component.

- [&lt;CSearchButton /&gt;](./api/#csearchbutton)

```jsx
import { CSearchButton } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| `trigger` | Event called when the component is activated by click or keyboard shortcut. |

# Vue Search Button Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Search Button component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

## CSS variables

Vue Search Button uses local CSS variables on `.search-button` for enhanced real-time customization. Values for the CSS variables are set via Sass, so Sass customization is still supported, too.

```sass
--cui-search-button-height: #{$search-button-height};
--cui-search-button-padding-x: #{$search-button-padding-x};
--cui-search-button-font-family: #{$search-button-font-family};
--cui-search-button-font-size: #{$search-button-font-size};
--cui-search-button-font-weight: #{$search-button-font-weight};
--cui-search-button-color: #{$search-button-color};
--cui-search-button-bg: #{$search-button-bg};
--cui-search-button-border-width: #{$search-button-border-width};
--cui-search-button-border-color: #{$search-button-border-color};
--cui-search-button-border-radius: #{$search-button-border-radius};
```

### How to use CSS variables

```vue
<template>
  <CSearchButton placeholder="Search docs" :style="customVars" @trigger="() => {}" />
</template>

```

# Vue Bootstrap Search Button Component

> Learn how to use CoreUI’s Vue Search Button component with Bootstrap styles for flexible, framework-consistent UI.

## Overview

_Added in 5.9.0._

The CoreUI **Vue Search Button component** is a trigger element designed for search entry points and command-style actions. It behaves like a regular button on click, but it can also react to a configurable keyboard shortcut such as `meta+/` or `ctrl+/`.

- Use it as a standalone trigger for a custom search UI.
- Pair it with reactive state to open a modal, offcanvas, or command palette.
- Shortcut keys are rendered automatically.
- Displayed shortcut keys react to keyboard interaction and receive an `.active` state while pressed.

## Basic example

Use `<CSearchButton>` as the entry point for a search interface. Listen to `@trigger` as the main activation callback for both direct interaction and keyboard shortcuts.

```html
<template>
  <CSearchButton
    aria-label="Open search dialog"
    aria-controls="search-button-modal"
    shortcut="meta+/,ctrl+/"
    @trigger="visible = true"
  />
  <CModal
    id="search-button-modal"
    :visible="visible"
    aria-labelledby="search-button-modal-title"
    @close="visible = false"
  >
    <CModalHeader>
      <CModalTitle id="search-button-modal-title" class="w-100">
        <CFormInput type="search" placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search" />
      </CModalTitle>
    </CModalHeader>
    <CModalBody>
      <p class="fg-2 small mb-3">Recent searches</p>
      <CListGroup flush>
        <CListGroupItem
          as="button"
          type="button"
          class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center"
        >
          CoreUI components overview
          <CBadge theme="secondary" shape="rounded-pill">Open</CBadge>
        </CListGroupItem>
        <CListGroupItem
          as="button"
          type="button"
          class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center"
        >
          Modal dialog examples
          <CBadge theme="secondary" shape="rounded-pill">Open</CBadge>
        </CListGroupItem>
        <CListGroupItem
          as="button"
          type="button"
          class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center"
        >
          Sidebar navigation customization
          <CBadge theme="secondary" shape="rounded-pill">Open</CBadge>
        </CListGroupItem>
      </CListGroup>
    </CModalBody>
  </CModal>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import {
  CBadge,
  CFormInput,
  CListGroup,
  CListGroupItem,
  CModal,
  CModalBody,
  CModalHeader,
  CModalTitle,
  CSearchButton,
} from '@coreui/vue'

const visible = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Custom shortcut

Configure the shortcut with the `shortcut` prop. On macOS, the component prefers the `meta` variant for the visible label. On Windows and Linux, it prefers the `ctrl` variant.

> Shortcuts such as `meta+f`, `ctrl+f`, `meta+s`, or `ctrl+s` can override native browser or system shortcuts. Prefer safer combinations such as `meta+/` and `ctrl+/` unless replacing the default behavior is intentional.

```html
<template>
  <div>
    <CSearchButton
      aria-label="Open command palette"
      placeholder="Command palette"
      shortcut="meta+i,ctrl+i"
      @trigger="count++"
    />
    <CAlert theme="info" class="mt-4 mb-0">
      Triggered {{ count }} {{ count === 1 ? 'time' : 'times' }} with click or shortcut.
    </CAlert>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CAlert, CSearchButton } from '@coreui/vue'

const count = ref(0)
</script>
```

## Launch an offcanvas

The component works naturally with reactive state and a dedicated `@trigger` event. This demo uses `meta+shift+o` / `ctrl+shift+o` to avoid colliding with other live examples on the page.

```html
<template>
  <CSearchButton
    aria-label="Open search panel"
    aria-controls="search-button-offcanvas"
    shortcut="meta+shift+o,ctrl+shift+o"
    @trigger="visible = true"
  />
  <COffcanvas
    id="search-button-offcanvas"
    placement="end"
    :visible="visible"
    @hide="visible = false"
  >
    <COffcanvasHeader>
      <COffcanvasTitle>Search panel</COffcanvasTitle>
      <CCloseButton class="fg-reset" @click="visible = false" />
    </COffcanvasHeader>
    <COffcanvasBody>
      <CFormInput type="search" class="mb-4" placeholder="Search..." aria-label="Search in panel" />
      <p class="mb-0">Use this space for filters, recent searches, or command shortcuts.</p>
    </COffcanvasBody>
  </COffcanvas>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import {
  CCloseButton,
  CFormInput,
  COffcanvas,
  COffcanvasBody,
  COffcanvasHeader,
  COffcanvasTitle,
  CSearchButton,
} from '@coreui/vue'

const visible = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Keyboard behavior

### When the configured shortcut is pressed

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` / `Space` on a focused search button | Trigger the component activation callback |
| Configured shortcut, e.g. `⌘/` / `Ctrl+/` | Trigger the component activation callback |
| Modifier key inside the visible shortcut | Add `.active` to the corresponding `.search-button-key` while pressed |
| Final key inside the visible shortcut | Add `.active` to the corresponding `.search-button-key` while pressed |

### Keyboard state behavior

| Interaction | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Matching shortcut on `keydown` | Optionally prevents the browser's default behavior and emits `trigger` |
| Plain typing inside `input`, `textarea`, `select`, or `contenteditable` | Does not trigger the component without `meta` or `ctrl` |
| `keyup` after a shortcut key press | Removes `.active` from the rendered shortcut keys |
| Browser window `blur` | Clears all active shortcut key states |
| Multiple configured shortcuts | The component listens to all configured shortcuts and renders the platform-preferred one in the UI |

# Vue Sidebar Component

> Vue Sidebar is a powerful and customizable responsive navigation component for any type of vertical navigation. Bootstrap Sidebar come with built-in support for branding, navigation, and more.

## How it works

Here's what you need to know before getting started with the Vue Sidebar component:

- `CSidebar` renders the `.sidebar` container.
- On mobile devices, the sidebar is hidden by default. Control it with the `show` prop.
- On desktop devices, the sidebar is shown by default. Hide it with `:show="false"`.
- Use `narrow` to switch the sidebar to the narrow variant.
- Use `unfoldable` to switch the sidebar to the narrow-unfoldable variant.
- `CSidebarNav` renders `.sidebar-nav` and supports nested groups through `CNavGroup`.
- For accessibility, prefer semantic elements such as `nav`, or add `role="navigation"` when using `as="div"` on `CSidebarNav`.

## Supported content

Sidebar comes with built-in support for a handful of sub-components. Choose from the following as needed:

- `<CSidebarHeader>` for an optional header.
- `<CSidebarBrand>` for your company, product, or project name.
- `<CSidebarNav>` for a full-height and lightweight navigation, including nested groups.
- `<CSidebarFooter>` for an optional footer.
- `<CSidebarToggler>` for toggling the sidebar state.

### Narrow sidebar

### Narrow visibility helpers

Use the sidebar visibility helpers to swap content between regular, narrow, and narrow-unfoldable variants:

- `.d-sidebar-narrow` shows content only in the narrow state.
- `.d-sidebar-narrow-none` hides content in the narrow state.
- `.d-sidebar-narrow-unfoldable` shows content only when the sidebar uses the unfoldable variant.
- `.d-sidebar-narrow-unfoldable-none` hides content when the sidebar uses the unfoldable variant.

### Sizes

The default width is `--cui-sidebar-width`. Pass `size="sm"`, `size="lg"` or `size="xl"` for the other widths from the `$sidebar-widths` map; each size also sets the space the sidebar reserves for the content next to it, so the layout follows the width.

```html
<template>
  <CSidebar class="border-end" size="lg">
    <CSidebarNav>
      <CNavItem active href="#">
        <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilSpeedometer" /> Dashboard
      </CNavItem>
      <CNavItem href="#">
        <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilPuzzle" /> Components
      </CNavItem>
    </CSidebarNav>
  </CSidebar>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CNavItem, CSidebar, CSidebarNav } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
import { CIcon } from '@coreui/icons-vue'
import { cilPuzzle, cilSpeedometer } from '@coreui/icons'
</script>
```

## Navigation

Use `CSidebarNav` as the main navigation container inside a sidebar. It supports plain links, section titles, nested groups, tree navigation, compact navigation, and custom group indicators.

### Basic navigation

Use the following building blocks inside `CSidebarNav`:

- `<CNavTitle>` for section headings.
- `<CNavItem>` for each navigation entry.
- `<CNavLink>` for standalone navigation links.
- `CIcon` with `customClassName="nav-icon"` for optional leading icons.
- `<CBadge>` or utility classes such as `ms-auto` for trailing metadata.

### Navigation groups

Use `<CNavGroup>` for expandable navigation sections. The `togglerContent` slot defines the clickable label, and nested `CNavItem` or `CNavGroup` components become the group content.

Set `show` on `CNavGroup` when the group should be expanded by default; `v-model:show` is the controlled form — see [Controlled navigation group](#controlled-navigation-group).

Use the `compact` prop on `CNavGroup` to reduce spacing only for that nested group.

### Compact navigation

_Added in 5.9.0._

Add the `compact` prop to `CSidebarNav` to reduce the vertical padding across the entire navigation.

Use the `compact` prop on `CNavGroup` to compact only a nested section.

```html
<template>
  <CSidebar class="border-end">
    <CSidebarNav compact>
      <CNavTitle>Compact nav</CNavTitle>
      <CNavItem href="#">
        <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilSpeedometer" /> Dashboard
      </CNavItem>
      <CNavItem href="#">
        <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilLayers" /> Components
      </CNavItem>
      <CNavGroup show>
        <template #togglerContent>
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilPuzzle" /> Nested group
        </template>
        <CNavItem href="#">Compact item</CNavItem>
        <CNavItem href="#">Compact item</CNavItem>
      </CNavGroup>
    </CSidebarNav>
  </CSidebar>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CNavGroup, CNavItem, CNavTitle, CSidebar, CSidebarNav } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CIcon } from '@coreui/icons-vue'
import { cilLayers, cilPuzzle, cilSpeedometer } from '@coreui/icons'
</script>
```

### Tree navigation

_Added in 5.9.0._

Add `variant="tree"` to `CSidebarNav` to render nested groups as a tree. Nested groups automatically keep their hierarchy, making deeper navigation levels easier to scan.

```html
<template>
  <CSidebar class="border-end">
    <CSidebarNav variant="tree">
      <CNavGroup show>
        <template #togglerContent>
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilFolder" /> Parent item
        </template>
        <CNavItem href="#">
          <span class="nav-icon"><span class="nav-icon-bullet"></span></span> Child item
        </CNavItem>
        <CNavGroup show>
          <template #togglerContent>
            <span class="nav-icon"><span class="nav-icon-bullet"></span></span> Nested group
          </template>
          <CNavItem href="#">
            <span class="nav-icon"><span class="nav-icon-bullet"></span></span> Nested child
          </CNavItem>
          <CNavItem href="#">
            <span class="nav-icon"><span class="nav-icon-bullet"></span></span> Nested child
          </CNavItem>
        </CNavGroup>
      </CNavGroup>
    </CSidebarNav>
  </CSidebar>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CNavGroup, CNavItem, CSidebar, CSidebarNav } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CIcon } from '@coreui/icons-vue'
import { cilFolder } from '@coreui/icons'
</script>
```

### Group indicator

By default, `CNavGroup` renders the standard group indicator through the `.nav-group-toggle` styles, so no additional markup is required.

```html
<template>
  <CSidebar class="border-end">
    <CSidebarNav>
      <CNavGroup show>
        <template #togglerContent>
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilPuzzle" /> Items group
        </template>
        <CNavItem href="#">Items group item</CNavItem>
        <CNavItem href="#">Items group item</CNavItem>
      </CNavGroup>
    </CSidebarNav>
  </CSidebar>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CNavGroup, CNavItem, CSidebar, CSidebarNav } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CIcon } from '@coreui/icons-vue'
import { cilPuzzle } from '@coreui/icons'
</script>
```

### Custom group indicator

To replace the default indicator, pass custom indicator markup inside the `togglerContent` slot using a `.nav-group-toggle-indicator` element. The `togglerContent` slot is a scoped slot that receives `{ show }`, so you can swap icons yourself based on the group state.

```html
<template>
  <CSidebar class="border-end">
    <CSidebarNav>
      <CNavGroup show>
        <template #togglerContent="{ show }">
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilPuzzle" /> Items group
          <span class="nav-group-toggle-indicator">
            <CIcon class="icon icon-sm" :icon="show ? cilMinus : cilPlus" />
          </span>
        </template>
        <CNavItem href="#">Items group item</CNavItem>
        <CNavItem href="#">Items group item</CNavItem>
      </CNavGroup>
      <CNavGroup>
        <template #togglerContent="{ show }">
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilPuzzle" /> Alternate indicator
          <span class="nav-group-toggle-indicator">
            <CIcon
              class="icon icon-sm"
              :icon="show ? cilChevronCircleUpAlt : cilChevronCircleDownAlt"
            />
          </span>
        </template>
        <CNavItem href="#">Items group item</CNavItem>
        <CNavItem href="#">Items group item</CNavItem>
      </CNavGroup>
    </CSidebarNav>
  </CSidebar>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CNavGroup, CNavItem, CSidebar, CSidebarNav } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CIcon } from '@coreui/icons-vue'
import {
  cilChevronCircleDownAlt,
  cilChevronCircleUpAlt,
  cilMinus,
  cilPlus,
  cilPuzzle,
} from '@coreui/icons'
</script>
```

### Controlled navigation group

_Added in 5.9.0._

`CNavGroup` works uncontrolled by default—clicking the toggler expands and collapses it. To control it from the parent, bind `show` and listen to `update:show` (or use `v-model:show`). In controlled mode the toggler only requests a change through `update:show`; the group follows the `show` prop, so the parent has the final say.

This makes it possible to keep a section open even when the user clicks to collapse it—useful for a route-aware sidebar that must keep the active section expanded. Toggle the lock and try to collapse the group: while locked, the parent rejects the change and the group stays open.

```html
<template>
  <CSidebar class="border-end">
    <CSidebarNav>
      <CNavItem href="#">
        <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilSpeedometer" /> Dashboard
      </CNavItem>
      <CNavGroup :show="show" @update:show="handleShowChange">
        <template #togglerContent>
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilPuzzle" /> Active section
        </template>
        <CNavItem href="#">Overview</CNavItem>
        <CNavItem href="#">Settings</CNavItem>
      </CNavGroup>
      <CNavGroup>
        <template #togglerContent>
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilLayers" /> Components
        </template>
        <CNavItem href="#">Base</CNavItem>
        <CNavItem href="#">Buttons</CNavItem>
        <CNavGroup>
          <template #togglerContent>
            <span class="nav-icon"><span class="nav-icon-bullet"></span></span> Forms
          </template>
          <CNavItem href="#">Inputs</CNavItem>
          <CNavItem href="#">Selects</CNavItem>
        </CNavGroup>
      </CNavGroup>
      <CNavGroup>
        <template #togglerContent>
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilSettings" /> Settings
        </template>
        <CNavItem href="#">Profile</CNavItem>
        <CNavItem href="#">Security</CNavItem>
      </CNavGroup>
      <CNavItem href="https://coreui.io">
        <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilCloudDownload" /> Download CoreUI
      </CNavItem>
    </CSidebarNav>
    <CSidebarFooter class="border-top">
      <CButton theme="primary" size="sm" @click="locked = !locked">
        {{ locked ? 'Unlock collapsing' : 'Lock the active section open' }}
      </CButton>
    </CSidebarFooter>
  </CSidebar>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CNavGroup, CNavItem, CSidebar, CSidebarFooter, CSidebarNav } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CIcon } from '@coreui/icons-vue'
import { cilCloudDownload, cilLayers, cilPuzzle, cilSettings, cilSpeedometer } from '@coreui/icons'

const show = ref(true)
const locked = ref(true)

const handleShowChange = (value) => {
  if (!value && locked.value) {
    return
  }

  show.value = value
}
</script>
```

## Theme variants

Add a [`.theme-{color}` class](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/customize/components/#theme-variants) to the sidebar and it paints its surface, text, icons and the hover and active links from that colour's slots — the background from `--cui-theme-bg`, the text from `--cui-theme-contrast`, the hovered and active links from `--cui-theme-hover` and `--cui-theme-active`. Combine it with `color-scheme` when the colour needs a fixed scheme.

```html
<template>
  <div class="d-flex flex-wrap">
```

## Placement

By default, placement for sidebar components is on the left side of the viewport, but you can change it with the `placement` prop:

- `placement="start"` places the sidebar on the left side of the viewport.
- `placement="end"` places the sidebar on the right side of the viewport.

## Usage with v-model

_Added in 6.0.0._

Pass `show` and the sidebar renders what you pass — close gestures only emit `update:show`, so feed the change back, or nothing closes — `v-model:show` is that loop in one attribute. This is the classic app-shell case: a header toggler owns the state, and the sidebar follows.

```html
<template>
  <div class="d-flex align-items-start">
    <CSidebar class="border-end" :show="show" @update:show="(value) => (show = value)">
      <CSidebarNav>
        <CNavTitle>Navigation</CNavTitle>
        <CNavItem href="#">
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilSpeedometer" /> Dashboard
        </CNavItem>
        <CNavItem href="#">
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilPuzzle" /> Components
        </CNavItem>
        <CNavItem href="https://coreui.io">
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilCloudDownload" /> Download CoreUI
        </CNavItem>
      </CSidebarNav>
    </CSidebar>
    <CButton class="m-4" theme="primary" @click="show = !show">
      {{ show ? 'Hide sidebar' : 'Show sidebar' }}
    </CButton>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CNavItem, CNavTitle, CSidebar, CSidebarNav } from '@coreui/vue'

import { CIcon } from '@coreui/icons-vue'
import { cilCloudDownload, cilPuzzle, cilSpeedometer } from '@coreui/icons'

const show = ref(true)
</script>
```

### Initial open state

Seed the starting state and let the sidebar manage itself — on mobile it still closes on the backdrop click.

```vue
<CSidebar :show="false">
```

`update:show` fires either way whenever the sidebar requests an open-state change — a close gesture (the mobile backdrop click, an outside click or a nav link selection on mobile) or any internal toggle. The deprecated `visible` prop keeps its old behavior and is ignored when `show` is set.

# Vue Sidebar Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Sidebar component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CSidebar

```jsx
import { CSidebar } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `colorScheme` | `string` | `undefined` | Sets if the color of text should be colored for a light or dark background. |
| `narrow` | `boolean` | - | Make sidebar narrow. |
| `overlaid` | `boolean` | - | Set sidebar to overlaid variant. |
| `placement` | `string` | `undefined` | Components placement, there’s no default placement. |
| `position` | `string` | - | Place sidebar in non-static positions. |
| `show` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Control the open state. When set, the sidebar renders what `show` says and close gestures only emit `update:show` — nothing changes until the parent flips the prop. |
| `size` | `string` | - | Size the component small, large, or extra large. |
| `unfoldable` | `boolean` | - | Expand narrowed sidebar on hover. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Toggle the visibility of sidebar component. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `hide` | Callback fired when the component requests to be hidden. |
| `in-viewport-change` | Event emitted when the sidebar enters or leaves the viewport — the sidebar is off-canvas on narrow screens, so this reports whether it is on screen, not the `show` state. |
| `show` | Callback fired when the component requests to be shown. |
| `update:show` | Callback fired when the sidebar requests an open-state change — a close gesture (the mobile backdrop click, an outside click or a nav link selection on mobile) or any internal toggle. When `show` is bound with `v-model`, update it yourself, or the sidebar stays as it is. |
| `visible-change` | Event emitted after visibility of component changed. |

## CSidebarBrand

```jsx
import { CSidebarBrand } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `string` | `'div'` | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |
| `href` | `string` | - | The href attribute specifies the URL of the page the link goes to. |

## CSidebarFooter

```jsx
import { CSidebarFooter } from '@coreui/vue'
```

## CSidebarHeader

```jsx
import { CSidebarHeader } from '@coreui/vue'
```

## CSidebarNav

```jsx
import { CSidebarNav } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `string \| Component` | `'ul'` | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |
| `compact` | `boolean` | - | Make navigation more compact by cutting link padding in half. |
| `variant` | `'tree'` | `undefined` | Sets the navigation variant. |

## CSidebarToggler

```jsx
import { CSidebarToggler } from '@coreui/vue'
```

# Vue Sidebar Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Sidebar component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

## CSS variables

Vue sidebars use local CSS variables on `.sidebar` and `.sidebar-backdrop` for enhanced real-time customization. Values for the CSS variables are set via Sass, so Sass customization is still supported, too.

```scss
$sidebar-tokens: () !default;
$sidebar-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-sidebar-zindex: var(--cui-z-sidebar),
    --cui-sidebar-width: #{$sidebar-width},
    --cui-sidebar-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-sidebar-padding-x: #{$sidebar-padding-x},
    --cui-sidebar-padding-y: #{$sidebar-padding-y},
    --cui-sidebar-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-sidebar-brand-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-sidebar-transition: #{margin-left .15s, margin-right .15s, box-shadow .075s, transform .15s, width .15s, z-index 0s ease .15s},
    --cui-sidebar-toggler-height: .5rem,
  ),
  $sidebar-tokens
);
```

### How to use CSS variables

```vue
<template>
  <CSidebar :style="vars">...</CSidebar>
</template>

<script setup>
const vars = {
  '--cui-sidebar-color': '#333',
  '--cui-sidebar-bg': '#f8f9fa',
}
</script>
```

## Sass variables

_Deprecated in 6.0.0._

Sass variables set these defaults at build time and are removed in v7. The CSS variables above reach the same values without recompiling, and can be set on a single element.

```scss
$sidebar-width:                            16rem !default;
$sidebar-padding-y:                        var(--cui-spacer) !default;
$sidebar-padding-x:                        var(--cui-spacer) !default;
```

# Vue Bootstrap Sidebar Component

> Learn how to use CoreUI’s Vue Sidebar component with Bootstrap styles for flexible, framework-consistent UI.

## How it works

Here's what you need to know before getting started with the Vue Sidebar component:

- `CSidebar` renders the `.sidebar` container.
- On mobile devices, the sidebar is hidden by default. Control it with the `show` prop.
- On desktop devices, the sidebar is shown by default. Hide it with `:show="false"`.
- Use `narrow` to switch the sidebar to the narrow variant.
- Use `unfoldable` to switch the sidebar to the narrow-unfoldable variant.
- `CSidebarNav` renders `.sidebar-nav` and supports nested groups through `CNavGroup`.
- For accessibility, prefer semantic elements such as `nav`, or add `role="navigation"` when using `as="div"` on `CSidebarNav`.

## Supported content

Sidebar comes with built-in support for a handful of sub-components. Choose from the following as needed:

- `<CSidebarHeader>` for an optional header.
- `<CSidebarBrand>` for your company, product, or project name.
- `<CSidebarNav>` for a full-height and lightweight navigation, including nested groups.
- `<CSidebarFooter>` for an optional footer.
- `<CSidebarToggler>` for toggling the sidebar state.

## Examples

Below is a more complete sidebar example shown by default on desktop devices. It combines several optional features in a single demo, including narrow visibility helpers, tree navigation, nested groups, a custom group indicator, badges, and a footer dropdown.

```html
<template>
  <div style="height: 900px">
    <CSidebar class="border-end h-100" :unfoldable="unfoldable">
      <CSidebarHeader class="position-relative">
        <CSidebarBrand>
          <svg
            role="img"
            aria-label="CoreUI Logo Full"
            class="d-sidebar-narrow-none"
            width="88"
            height="32"
            xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
            viewBox="0 0 312 115"
          >
            <g style="fill: currentColor">
              <path
                d="M96 24.124 57 1.608a12 12 0 0 0-12 0L6 24.124a12.034 12.034 0 0 0-6 10.393V79.55a12.033 12.033 0 0 0 6 10.392l39 22.517a12 12 0 0 0 12 0l39-22.517a12.033 12.033 0 0 0 6-10.392V34.517a12.034 12.034 0 0 0-6-10.393ZM94 79.55a4 4 0 0 1-2 3.464l-39 22.517a4 4 0 0 1-4 0L10 83.014a4 4 0 0 1-2-3.464V34.517a4 4 0 0 1 2-3.464L49 8.536a4 4 0 0 1 4 0l39 22.517a4 4 0 0 1 2 3.464V79.55Z"
              ></path>
              <path
                d="M74.022 70.071h-2.866a4 4 0 0 0-1.925.494L51.95 80.05 32 68.531V45.554l19.95-11.519 17.29 9.455a4 4 0 0 0 1.919.49h2.863a2 2 0 0 0 2-2v-2.71a2 2 0 0 0-1.04-1.756L55.793 27.02a8.04 8.04 0 0 0-7.843.09L28 38.626a8.025 8.025 0 0 0-4 6.929V68.53a8 8 0 0 0 4 6.928l19.95 11.519a8.043 8.043 0 0 0 7.843.088l19.19-10.532a2 2 0 0 0 1.038-1.753v-2.71a2 2 0 0 0-2-2Z"
              ></path>
```

### Narrow sidebar

Add the `narrow` prop to make the sidebar narrow.

Use `.d-sidebar-narrow` to show content only in the narrow state and `.d-sidebar-narrow-none` to hide content in the narrow state. These utility classes replace older brand-specific visibility helpers.

### Narrow visibility helpers

Use the sidebar visibility helpers to swap content between regular, narrow, and narrow-unfoldable variants:

- `.d-sidebar-narrow` shows content only in the narrow state.
- `.d-sidebar-narrow-none` hides content in the narrow state.
- `.d-sidebar-narrow-unfoldable` shows content only when the sidebar uses the unfoldable variant.
- `.d-sidebar-narrow-unfoldable-none` hides content when the sidebar uses the unfoldable variant.

## Navigation

Use `CSidebarNav` as the main navigation container inside a sidebar. It supports plain links, section titles, nested groups, tree navigation, compact navigation, and custom group indicators.

### Basic navigation

Use the following building blocks inside `CSidebarNav`:

- `<CNavTitle>` for section headings.
- `<CNavItem>` for each navigation entry.
- `<CNavLink>` for standalone navigation links.
- `CIcon` with `customClassName="nav-icon"` for optional leading icons.
- `<CBadge>` or utility classes such as `ms-auto` for trailing metadata.

### Navigation groups

Use `<CNavGroup>` for expandable navigation sections. The `togglerContent` slot defines the clickable label, and nested `CNavItem` or `CNavGroup` components become the group content.

Set `show` on `CNavGroup` when the group should be expanded by default; `v-model:show` is the controlled form — see [Controlled navigation group](#controlled-navigation-group).

Use the `compact` prop on `CNavGroup` to reduce spacing only for that nested group.

### Compact navigation

_Added in 5.9.0._

Add the `compact` prop to `CSidebarNav` to reduce the vertical padding across the entire navigation.

Use the `compact` prop on `CNavGroup` to compact only a nested section.

```html
<template>
  <CSidebar class="border-end">
    <CSidebarNav compact>
      <CNavTitle>Compact nav</CNavTitle>
      <CNavItem href="#">
        <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilSpeedometer" /> Dashboard
      </CNavItem>
      <CNavItem href="#">
        <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilLayers" /> Components
      </CNavItem>
      <CNavGroup show>
        <template #togglerContent>
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilPuzzle" /> Nested group
        </template>
        <CNavItem href="#">Compact item</CNavItem>
        <CNavItem href="#">Compact item</CNavItem>
      </CNavGroup>
    </CSidebarNav>
  </CSidebar>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CNavGroup, CNavItem, CNavTitle, CSidebar, CSidebarNav } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CIcon } from '@coreui/icons-vue'
import { cilLayers, cilPuzzle, cilSpeedometer } from '@coreui/icons'
</script>
```

### Tree navigation

_Added in 5.9.0._

Add `variant="tree"` to `CSidebarNav` to render nested groups as a tree. Nested groups automatically keep their hierarchy, making deeper navigation levels easier to scan.

```html
<template>
  <CSidebar class="border-end">
    <CSidebarNav variant="tree">
      <CNavGroup show>
        <template #togglerContent>
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilFolder" /> Parent item
        </template>
        <CNavItem href="#">
          <span class="nav-icon"><span class="nav-icon-bullet"></span></span> Child item
        </CNavItem>
        <CNavGroup show>
          <template #togglerContent>
```

### Group indicator

### Custom group indicator

To replace the default indicator, pass custom indicator markup inside the `togglerContent` slot using a `.nav-group-toggle-indicator` element. The `togglerContent` slot is a scoped slot that receives `{ show }`, so you can swap icons yourself based on the group state.

```html
<template>
  <CSidebar class="border-end">
    <CSidebarNav>
      <CNavGroup show>
        <template #togglerContent="{ show }">
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilPuzzle" /> Items group
          <span class="nav-group-toggle-indicator">
            <CIcon class="icon icon-sm" :icon="show ? cilMinus : cilPlus" />
          </span>
        </template>
        <CNavItem href="#">Items group item</CNavItem>
        <CNavItem href="#">Items group item</CNavItem>
      </CNavGroup>
      <CNavGroup>
        <template #togglerContent="{ show }">
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilPuzzle" /> Alternate indicator
          <span class="nav-group-toggle-indicator">
            <CIcon
              class="icon icon-sm"
              :icon="show ? cilChevronCircleUpAlt : cilChevronCircleDownAlt"
            />
          </span>
        </template>
        <CNavItem href="#">Items group item</CNavItem>
        <CNavItem href="#">Items group item</CNavItem>
      </CNavGroup>
    </CSidebarNav>
  </CSidebar>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CNavGroup, CNavItem, CSidebar, CSidebarNav } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CIcon } from '@coreui/icons-vue'
import {
  cilChevronCircleDownAlt,
  cilChevronCircleUpAlt,
  cilMinus,
  cilPlus,
  cilPuzzle,
} from '@coreui/icons'
</script>
```

### Controlled navigation group

_Added in 5.9.0._

`CNavGroup` works uncontrolled by default—clicking the toggler expands and collapses it. To control it from the parent, bind `show` and listen to `update:show` (or use `v-model:show`). In controlled mode the toggler only requests a change through `update:show`; the group follows the `show` prop, so the parent has the final say.

This makes it possible to keep a section open even when the user clicks to collapse it—useful for a route-aware sidebar that must keep the active section expanded. Toggle the lock and try to collapse the group: while locked, the parent rejects the change and the group stays open.

```html
<template>
  <CSidebar class="border-end">
    <CSidebarNav>
      <CNavItem href="#">
        <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilSpeedometer" /> Dashboard
      </CNavItem>
      <CNavGroup :show="show" @update:show="handleShowChange">
        <template #togglerContent>
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilPuzzle" /> Active section
        </template>
        <CNavItem href="#">Overview</CNavItem>
        <CNavItem href="#">Settings</CNavItem>
      </CNavGroup>
      <CNavGroup>
        <template #togglerContent>
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilLayers" /> Components
        </template>
        <CNavItem href="#">Base</CNavItem>
        <CNavItem href="#">Buttons</CNavItem>
        <CNavGroup>
          <template #togglerContent>
            <span class="nav-icon"><span class="nav-icon-bullet"></span></span> Forms
          </template>
          <CNavItem href="#">Inputs</CNavItem>
          <CNavItem href="#">Selects</CNavItem>
        </CNavGroup>
      </CNavGroup>
      <CNavGroup>
        <template #togglerContent>
          <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilSettings" /> Settings
        </template>
        <CNavItem href="#">Profile</CNavItem>
        <CNavItem href="#">Security</CNavItem>
      </CNavGroup>
      <CNavItem href="https://coreui.io">
        <CIcon custom-class-name="nav-icon" :icon="cilCloudDownload" /> Download CoreUI
      </CNavItem>
    </CSidebarNav>
    <CSidebarFooter class="border-top">
      <CButton theme="primary" size="sm" @click="locked = !locked">
        {{ locked ? 'Unlock collapsing' : 'Lock the active section open' }}
      </CButton>
    </CSidebarFooter>
  </CSidebar>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CNavGroup, CNavItem, CSidebar, CSidebarFooter, CSidebarNav } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CIcon } from '@coreui/icons-vue'
import { cilCloudDownload, cilLayers, cilPuzzle, cilSettings, cilSpeedometer } from '@coreui/icons'

const show = ref(true)
const locked = ref(true)

const handleShowChange = (value) => {
  if (!value && locked.value) {
    return
  }

  show.value = value
}
</script>
```

## Placement

By default, placement for sidebar components is on the left side of the viewport, but you can change it with the `placement` prop:

- `placement="start"` places the sidebar on the left side of the viewport.
- `placement="end"` places the sidebar on the right side of the viewport.

# Vue Smart Pagination Component

> Documentation and examples for showing smart pagination to indicate a series of related content exists across multiple pages.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Overview

Vue smart pagination component consists of button-like styled links, that are arranged side by side in a horizontal list.

We use a large block of connected links for our pagination, making links hard to miss and easily scalable—all while providing large hit areas. SmartPagination is built with list HTML elements so screen readers can announce the number of available links. SmartPagination also use a wrapping `<nav>` element to identify it as a navigation section to screen readers and other assistive technologies.

In addition, as pages likely have more than one such navigation section, SmartPagination provide a descriptive `aria-label` for the `<nav>` to reflect its purpose. For example, if the pagination component is used to navigate between a set of search results, an appropriate label could be `aria-label="Search results pages"`.

```html
<template>
  <CSmartPagination :active-page="6" :pages="10" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CSmartPagination } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
</script>
```

## Working with icons

The four navigation buttons take their content from `firstButton`, `previousButton`, `nextButton` and `lastButton`. A string is rendered as HTML — that is where the default `&laquo;` and friends come from — so pass a node instead to put an icon there.

Mark the icon `aria-hidden`: the buttons already carry their own accessible names, and an icon announced on top of them would read twice.

```html
<template>
  <CSmartPagination
    :active-page="activePage"
    :pages="10"
    :first-button="h(CIcon, { icon: cilChevronDoubleLeft, 'aria-hidden': 'true' })"
    :previous-button="h(CIcon, { icon: cilChevronLeft, 'aria-hidden': 'true' })"
    :next-button="h(CIcon, { icon: cilChevronRight, 'aria-hidden': 'true' })"
    :last-button="h(CIcon, { icon: cilChevronDoubleRight, 'aria-hidden': 'true' })"
    @active-page-change="activePage = $event"
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { h, ref } from 'vue'
import { CSmartPagination } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
import { CIcon } from '@coreui/icons-vue'
import {
  cilChevronDoubleLeft,
  cilChevronDoubleRight,
  cilChevronLeft,
  cilChevronRight,
} from '@coreui/icons'

const activePage = ref(3)
</script>
```

## Sizing

Fancy larger or smaller pagination? Add `size="lg"` or `size="sm"` for additional sizes.

```html
<template>
  <CSmartPagination :active-page="6" :pages="10" size="lg" />
</template>

<script setup>

</script>
```



# Vue Smart Pagination Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Smart Pagination component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## CSmartPagination

```jsx
import { CSmartPagination } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `activePage` | `number` | `1` | Current page number |
| `align` | `string` | `'start'` | Horizontall align |
| `arrows` | `boolean` | `true` | Show/hide arrows |
| `dots` | `boolean` | `true` | Show/hide dots |
| `doubleArrows` | `boolean` | `true` | Show double arrows buttons |
| `firstButton` | `string \| VNode` | `'&laquo;'` | The content of the `firstButton` button. A string is rendered as HTML; pass a VNode to put an icon there instead. |
| `lastButton` | `string \| VNode` | `'&raquo;'` | The content of the `lastButton` button. A string is rendered as HTML; pass a VNode to put an icon there instead. |
| `limit` | `number` | `5` | Maximum items number |
| `nextButton` | `string \| VNode` | `'&rsaquo;'` | The content of the `nextButton` button. A string is rendered as HTML; pass a VNode to put an icon there instead. |
| `pages` | `number` | `1000` | Number of pages |
| `previousButton` | `string \| VNode` | `'&lsaquo;'` | The content of the `previousButton` button. A string is rendered as HTML; pass a VNode to put an icon there instead. |
| `size` | `string` | `undefined` | Size of pagination, valid values: 'sm', 'lg' |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `activePageChange` | On active page change callback. |

# Vue Smart Table Component (DataTable)

> A Vue Smart Table provides a full set of features for displaying and manipulating tabular data. It allows you to easily create dynamic and interactive tables with features such as sorting, filtering, pagination, and searching. Vue Smart Table Component (DataTables) makes it easy to work with large datasets, and it is widely used in a variety of applications, including web-based applications, e-commerce sites, and more.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Features

- Filter items by one or all columns
- Sort items by column
- Integrated with CPagination component by default
- Customize style of specific rows, columns and cells
- Customize display of columns
- Load with initial filters and sorter state
- Loading state visualization
- Default header labels generation based on column names

## Usage

```html

          theme="primary"
          variant="outline"
          square
          size="sm"
          @click="toggleDetails(item, index)"
        >
          {{ details.includes(item.id) ? 'Hide' : 'Show' }}
        </CButton>
      </td>
    </template>
    <template #details="{ item }">
      <CCollapse :show="details.includes(item.id)">
        <div class="p-4">
          <h4>
            {{ item.name }}
          </h4>
          <p class="fg-2">User since: {{ item.registered }}</p>
          <CButton size="sm" theme="info">User Settings</CButton>
          <CButton size="sm" theme="danger" class="ms-1">Delete</CButton>
        </div>
      </CCollapse>
    </template>
  </CSmartTable>
</template>
```

## Custom layout

_Added in 6.0.0._

Without a default slot `<CSmartTable>` renders the toolbar, the table and the pagination row itself. Put anything in the default slot and that layout is gone — the table becomes a state provider and you place the parts wherever you want them:

| part | renders |
| --- | --- |
| `` | the label and the input of the global filter |
| `` | the button that resets the filters and the sorter |
| `` | the table itself, with the header, the rows, the footer and the loading cover |
| `` | the pagination wired to the active page |
| `` | the label and the select of the items per page |

`` takes every [CSmartPagination](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/smart-pagination/) prop; the others take the props listed in the API below. A part renders where you put it whatever the flags say, so `globalFilter`, `cleaner` and `itemsPerPageSelect` now only mean "keep this piece of state". The exception is `pagination`, which still decides whether the items are sliced into pages. Every part prop overrides the matching default from the table, and the slots of `<CSmartTable>` — the cell and header slots, `details`, `cleanerIcon`, `loadingContent` and the sorter icons — keep working either way.

`useSmartTableContext()` reads the same state from any component inside the table, which is how you write a part of your own — a row counter, an export button, a summary row:

```js
const { activePage, currentItems, items, totalItems, totalPages, setActivePage } = useSmartTableContext()
```

It returns `activePage`, `columnFilterValue`, `currentItems` (the rows on the page), `globalFilterValue`, `items` (everything after filtering and sorting), `itemsPerPage`, `itemsPerPageOptions`, `loading`, `selected`, `selectedAll`, `sorterValue`, `totalItems` and `totalPages` as refs, plus `isSelected(item)`, `toggle(item)`, `toggleAll()`, `setActivePage`, `setColumnFilterValue`, `setGlobalFilterValue`, `setItemsPerPage`, `setSelected`, `setSorterValue` and `clean()` to write to them.

```html
<script setup>
import { defineComponent, h } from 'vue'
import {
  CCol,
  CRow,
  CSmartTable,
  CSmartTableCleaner,
  CSmartTableContent,
  CSmartTableFilter,
  CSmartTableItemsPerPage,
  CSmartTablePagination,
  useSmartTableContext,
} from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const CSmartTableCounter = defineComponent({
  setup() {
    const { activePage, currentItems, itemsPerPage, totalItems } = useSmartTableContext()

    return () => {
      const first =
        currentItems.value.length > 0 ? (activePage.value - 1) * itemsPerPage.value + 1 : 0

      return h(
        'p',
        { class: 'fg-2 mb-0' },
        `${first}–${first + currentItems.value.length - 1} of ${totalItems.value}`
      )
    }
  },
})

const items = [
  { id: 1, name: 'Samppa Nori', registered: '2021/03/01', role: 'Member' },
  { id: 2, name: 'Estavan Lykos', registered: '2018/02/07', role: 'Staff' },
  { id: 3, name: 'Chetan Mohamed', registered: '2020/01/15', role: 'Admin' },
  { id: 4, name: 'Derick Maximinus', registered: '2019/04/05', role: 'Member' },
  { id: 5, name: 'Friderik Dávid', registered: '2022/03/25', role: 'Staff' },
  { id: 6, name: 'Yiorgos Avraamu', registered: '2021/11/12', role: 'Member' },
  { id: 7, name: 'Avram Tarasios', registered: '2020/06/30', role: 'Staff' },
]
</script>

<template>
  <CSmartTable
    cleaner
    column-sorter
    :columns="['name', 'registered', 'role']"
    :default-items-per-page="3"
    global-filter
    item-key="id"
    :items="items"
    items-per-page-select
    pagination
  >
    <CRow class="align-items-end mb-3">
      <CCol xs="auto">
        <CSmartTableFilter label="Search:" placeholder="name, role..." />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs="auto">
        <CSmartTableCleaner />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs="auto" class="ms-auto">
        <CSmartTableItemsPerPage label="Rows:" :options="[3, 5, 7]" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
    <CSmartTableContent :table-props="{ hover: true, small: true }" />
    <CRow class="align-items-center">
      <CCol xs="auto">
        <CSmartTableCounter />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs="auto" class="ms-auto">
        <CSmartTablePagination :limit="5" size="sm" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  </CSmartTable>
</template>
```

## Column groups

The Vue Smart Table component allows users to group related columns under a common header. This can be useful when displaying data that has multiple categories or when comparing different sets of data. When the Smart Table is rendered, the header group will be displayed as a single header cell that spans the width of the columns included in the group. The group header cells feature can help to make the Smart Table component more organized and easier to read by grouping related data together and making it more visually distinct from other columns.

## Column sorter

The column sorter feature enables sorting Vue.js table data by column values. You can enable sorting by adding `columnSorter` to `<CSmartTable>`. If you want to disable sorting for a specific column, add `sortable: false` to the desired column.

```html
<script setup>
import { CAvatar } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CSmartTable } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
const columns = [
  {
    key: 'avatar',
    label: '',
    sortable: false,
  },
  {
    key: 'name',
    headerStyle: { width: '30%' },
  },
  {
    key: 'registered',
    sorter: (date1, date2) => {
      const a = new Date(date1.registered)
      const b = new Date(date2.registered)
      return a > b ? 1 : b > a ? -1 : 0
    },
  },
  'role',
]
```
