### Sort multiple columns

Enables sorting by multiple columns simultaneously by adding `:columnSorter="{ multiple: true }"` The sorting order will be maintained across multiple columns based on the order of user interaction. This means you can sort by multiple columns, and each column will keep its order.

```vue
<CSmartTable :columns="[...]" :columnSorter="{ multiple: true }" :items="[...]" />
```

### Resettable sorter state

When `:columnSorter="{ resettable: true }"` is set, clicking the sorter toggles through three states: ascending, descending, and unsorted. After the third click, it resets the sorting, returning the table to its initial state.

```vue
<CSmartTable :columns="[...]" :columnSorter="{ resettable: true }" :items="[...]" />
```

### Custom sorter

By default, sorting is done automatically by the component and works as expected when the values in the column are of a single data type: either string (case-insensitive) or number.

In case you want to sort non-string and non-number data, define a custom sorting function for the column. You can use this option to control how the values are compared and sorted. The function receives two arguments (`a`, `b`) corresponding to two row values and must return:

* a negative value if `a` should appear before `b`,
* zero if `a` and `b` are equal,
* a positive value if `a` should appear after `b`.

```vue
<CSmartTable
  :columns="[
    ...
    {
      key: 'registered',
      sorter: (date1, date2) => {
        const a = new Date(date1.registered)
        const b = new Date(date2.registered)
        return a > b ? 1 : b > a ? -1 : 0
      }
    },
    ...
  ]"
  :items="[...]"
/>
```

### Custom filters

CoreUI Vue Smart Table (Vue DataTables) provides the ability to use custom filtering functions. Custom filters offer advanced filtering capabilities. You can define and integrate custom filtering logic by adding a `filter` function to the desired column, enabling more complex data filtering strategies.

#### Date Range Picker

Here is an example of how you might use the `` component to apply custom filters to a Vue DataTable component:

```html
<script setup>
import { computed, h, ref } from 'vue'
import { CDateRangePicker, CSmartTable } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const startDate = ref(new Date('2022-01-21'))
const endDate = ref(new Date('2022-02-07'))

const columns = [
  {
    key: 'name',
    headerStyle: { width: '50%' },
  },
  {
    key: 'registered',
    headerStyle: { width: '50%' },
    filter: (_, onChange) => {
      return h(CDateRangePicker, {
        size: 'sm',
        startDate: startDate.value,
        endDate: endDate.value,
        minDate: minDate.value,
        maxDate: maxDate.value,
        onStartDateChange: (date) => {
          startDate.value = date
          onChange((item) => {
            if (date) {
              const itemDate = new Date(Date.parse(item))
              return endDate.value
                ? itemDate >= date && itemDate <= endDate.value
                : itemDate >= date
            }
            return true
          })
        },
        onEndDateChange: (date) => {
          endDate.value = date
          onChange((item) => {
            if (date) {
              const itemDate = new Date(Date.parse(item))
              return startDate.value
                ? itemDate <= date && itemDate >= startDate.value
                : itemDate <= date
            }
            return true
          })
        },
      })
    },
  },
]
```

#### Multi Select

Here is an example of how you might use the `` component to apply custom filters to a Vue DataTable:

```html
<script setup>
import { h } from 'vue'
import { CMultiSelect, CSmartTable } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const columns = [
  {
    key: 'name',
    headerStyle: { width: '50%' },
  },

    key: 'role',
    headerStyle: { width: '50%' },
    filter: (values, onChange) => {
      const unique = [...new Set(values)].sort()
      return h(CMultiSelect, {
        size: 'sm',
        onChange: (selected) => {
          const _selected = selected.map((element) => element.value)
          onChange(function (item) {
            return Array.isArray(_selected) && _selected.length
              ? _selected.includes(item.toLowerCase())
              : true
          })
        },

          return {
            value: element.toLowerCase(),
            label: element,
          }
        }),
```

## Selection

Add `selectable` to render a checkbox in every row and a select-all checkbox in the header; `:select-all="false"` leaves out the header one. The selection is a list of items — seed it with `defaultSelected` or own it with `selected` and the `selected-change` event — and `row-checked` reports the single row the user just toggled. A row with `_selectable: false` in the data cannot be checked, and select-all skips it. Set `itemKey` so the selection matches rows by that property instead of by the whole object, which keeps a selected row selected across a re-fetch. `ariaSelectAllLabel` and `ariaSelectRowLabel` name the two checkboxes for screen readers.

```html
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CSmartTable } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const selected = ref([{ id: 2 }])

const items = [
  { id: 1, name: 'Samppa Nori', registered: '2021/03/01', role: 'Member' },
  { id: 2, name: 'Estavan Lykos', registered: '2018/02/07', role: 'Staff' },
  { id: 3, name: 'Chetan Mohamed', registered: '2020/01/15', role: 'Admin', _selectable: false },
  { id: 4, name: 'Derick Maximinus', registered: '2019/04/05', role: 'Member' },
  { id: 5, name: 'Friderik Dávid', registered: '2022/03/25', role: 'Staff' },
]
</script>

<template>
  <p class="fg-2">
    Selected: {{ selected.length > 0 ? selected.map((item) => item.id).join(', ') : 'none' }}
  </p>
  <CSmartTable
    :columns="['name', 'registered', 'role']"
    item-key="id"
    :items="items"
    select-all
    selectable
    :selected="selected"
    @row-checked="(item, checked) => console.log(item, checked)"
    @selected-change="(items) => (selected = items)"
  />
</template>
```

## Loading

`loading` dims the table, marks it as `aria-busy` and covers the body; `loadingContent` replaces what the cover shows, as a prop or as the slot of the same name.

```html
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CButton, CSpinner } from '@coreui/vue'
import { CSmartTable } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const loading = ref(false)

const items = [
  { id: 1, name: 'Samppa Nori', registered: '2021/03/01', role: 'Member' },
  { id: 2, name: 'Estavan Lykos', registered: '2018/02/07', role: 'Staff' },
  { id: 3, name: 'Chetan Mohamed', registered: '2020/01/15', role: 'Admin' },
]

const reload = () => {
  loading.value = true
  setTimeout(() => (loading.value = false), 2000)
}
</script>

<template>
  <CButton class="mb-4" @click="reload">Reload</CButton>
  <CSmartTable
    :columns="['name', 'registered', 'role']"
    item-key="id"
    :items="items"
    :loading="loading"
  >
    <template #loadingContent>
      <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-3">
        <CSpinner size="sm" />
        Fetching users...
      </div>
    </template>
  </CSmartTable>
</template>
```

## Data sources

You can use Fetch API to load data from different sources and then  pass them to `<CSmartTable>`

### External Data (10.000+ records)

One of the key features of Vue Smart Table (Vue DataTables) is the ability to load data from an external source, such as an API or a server-side script. This can be useful if you have a large amount of data that you don't want to load all at once, or if you want to allow users to interact with the data without having to reload the page.

To load external data into a Vue Smart Table (Vue DataTables), you can use the Fetch API to the data source.

Here is an example of how you might use Vue Smart Table with external data:

```html
<script setup>
import { onMounted, ref, watch } from 'vue'
import { CSmartTable } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const activePage = ref(3)
const columnFilter = ref({})
const columnSorter = ref([{ column: 'country', direction: 'asc' }])
const itemsPerPage = ref(10)
const loading = ref(false)
const records = ref(0)
const users = ref([])

const columns = [
  {
    key: 'first_name',
    headerStyle: { minWidth: '130px' },
  },
  {
    key: 'last_name',
    headerStyle: { minWidth: '130px' },
  },
  'email',
  {
    key: 'country',
    headerStyle: { minWidth: '120px' },
  },
  {
    key: 'ip_address',
    label: 'IP',
  },
]

const getUsers = async () => {
  try {
    loading.value = true

    const offset = (activePage.value - 1) * itemsPerPage.value
    const params = new URLSearchParams()

    for (const key of Object.keys(columnFilter.value)) {
      params.append(key, columnFilter.value[key])
    }

    if (columnSorter.value[0]) {
      params.append('sort', `${columnSorter.value[0].column}%${columnSorter.value[0].direction}`)
    }

    const response = await fetch(
      `https://apitest.coreui.io/demos/users?offset=${offset}&limit=${itemsPerPage.value}&${params}`
    )
    const result = await response.json()

    records.value = result.number_of_matching_records
    users.value = result.number_of_matching_records ? result.records : []
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error fetching users:', error)
    users.value = []
  } finally {
    loading.value = false
  }
}

onMounted(getUsers)

watch([activePage, columnFilter, columnSorter, itemsPerPage], getUsers, { deep: true })
</script>

<template>
  <CSmartTable
    :active-page="activePage"
    :columns="columns"
    column-filter
    column-sorter
    external
    footer
    :items="users"
    :items-per-page="itemsPerPage"
    items-per-page-select
    :loading="loading"
    pagination
    :sorter-value="columnSorter"
    :table-props="{
      hover: true,
      responsive: true,
    }"
    :total-items="records"
    @active-page-change="(page) => (activePage = page)"
    @column-filter-change="
      (filter) => {
        activePage = 1
        columnFilter = filter
      }
    "
    @items-per-page-change="
      (pageSize) => {
        activePage = 1
        itemsPerPage = pageSize
      }
    "
    @sorter-change="(value) => (columnSorter = value)"
  />
</template>
```

### JSON (10.000+ records)

The Fetch API can be used to load JSON data by making a GET request to the endpoint where the data is located. 
In this example, the `fetch()` method is used to make a GET request to the endpoint `https://apitest.coreui.io/fake_data/users.json`, which returns a response. 
The `response.json()` method is then used to parse the response as a JSON object. 
The resulting JSON object is stored in the `users` and loaded by ``.

```html
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CSmartTable } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const loading = ref(false)
const users = ref([])

const columns = [
  {
    key: 'first_name',
    headerStyle: { minWidth: '130px' },
  },
  {
    key: 'last_name',
    headerStyle: { minWidth: '130px' },
  },
  'email',
  {
    key: 'country',
    headerStyle: { minWidth: '120px' },
  },
  {
    key: 'ip_address',
    label: 'IP',
  },
]

onMounted(() => {
  getUsers()
})
</script>

<template>
  <CSmartTable
    :columns="columns"
    column-filter
    column-sorter
    :items="users"
    items-per-page-select
    :loading="loading"
    pagination
    :table-props="{
      hover: true,
      responsive: true,
    }"
  />
</template>
```

## Controlled and uncontrolled

_Added in 6.0.0._

Every piece of the table's state works either way, and the prop you reach for is what picks the mode — independently for each piece.

| controlled prop | uncontrolled seed | change event |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `activePage` | `defaultActivePage` | `active-page-change` |
| `columnFilterValue` | `defaultColumnFilterValue` | `column-filter-change` |
| `globalFilterValue` | `defaultGlobalFilterValue` | `global-filter-change` |
| `itemsPerPage` | `defaultItemsPerPage` | `items-per-page-change` |
| `selected` | `defaultSelected` | `selected-change` |
| `sorterValue` | `defaultSorterValue` | `sorter-change` |

The events fire with the requested state in **both** modes when the user acts — so you can watch a state without taking it over. Passing a new value into a controlled prop does **not** echo its own event back at you.

A `default*` prop seeds the state once, on mount, and the table manages it from there:

```vue
<CSmartTable
  column-sorter
  :default-sorter-value="[{ column: 'name', direction: 'asc' }]"
  :items="items"
/>
```

Pass the controlled prop and the table renders exactly what you pass — an interaction only emits the event, and nothing moves until you feed the change back. That includes the page clamp: when the items shrink below the current page, an uncontrolled table jumps to page one itself, while a controlled one only requests it through `active-page-change` with `1`. Here the parent owns the active page and the sorter:

```html
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CSmartTable } from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const activePage = ref(1)
const sorterValue = ref([{ column: 'name', direction: 'asc' }])

const items = [
  { id: 1, name: 'Samppa Nori', registered: '2021/03/01', role: 'Member' },
  { id: 2, name: 'Estavan Lykos', registered: '2018/02/07', role: 'Staff' },
  { id: 3, name: 'Chetan Mohamed', registered: '2020/01/15', role: 'Admin' },
  { id: 4, name: 'Derick Maximinus', registered: '2019/04/05', role: 'Member' },
  { id: 5, name: 'Friderik Dávid', registered: '2022/03/25', role: 'Staff' },
  { id: 6, name: 'Yiorgos Avraamu', registered: '2017/01/01', role: 'Member' },
  { id: 7, name: 'Avram Tarasios', registered: '2016/02/12', role: 'Staff' },
  { id: 8, name: 'Quintin Ed', registered: '2023/01/21', role: 'Admin' },
  { id: 9, name: 'Enéas Kwadwo', registered: '2024/03/10', role: 'Member' },
  { id: 10, name: 'Agapetus Tadeáš', registered: '2015/01/10', role: 'Staff' },
  { id: 11, name: 'Carwyn Fachtna', registered: '2014/04/01', role: 'Member' },
  { id: 12, name: 'Nehemiah Tatius', registered: '2013/01/05', role: 'Staff' },
]
</script>

<template>
  <p class="fg-2">
    Page {{ activePage }}, sorted by <code>{{ sorterValue[0].column }}</code> ({{
      sorterValue[0].direction
    }})
  </p>
  <CSmartTable
    :active-page="activePage"
    :columns="['name', 'registered', 'role']"
    column-sorter
    :default-items-per-page="5"
    item-key="id"
    :items="items"
    pagination
    :sorter-value="sorterValue"
    @active-page-change="(page) => (activePage = page)"
    @sorter-change="(value) => (sorterValue = value.length > 0 ? value : sorterValue)"
  />
</template>
```

## Headless

_Added in 6.0.0._

`useSmartTable(options)` is the table without the table: it runs the filtering, the sorting, the pagination and the selection over your data and hands the result back, so you can render whatever the design asks for — a list of cards, a grid of tiles, a chart. `<CSmartTable>` itself is nothing more than this composable plus a layout.

The options are the state props of the component, and each of them takes a ref, a getter or a plain value:

```js
const { currentItems, setGlobalFilterValue } = useSmartTable({
  columns: ['name', 'registered', 'role'],
  defaultItemsPerPage: 3,
  itemKey: 'id',
  items,
  pagination: true,
})
```

Every controlled prop has its option (`activePage`, `columnFilterValue`, `globalFilterValue`, `itemsPerPage`, `selected`, `sorterValue`), every `default*` seed too, and the events arrive as callbacks — `onActivePageChange`, `onColumnFilterChange`, `onFilteredItemsChange`, `onGlobalFilterChange`, `onItemsPerPageChange`, `onRowChecked`, `onSelectedChange` and `onSorterChange`. The return holds `activePage`, `columnFilterValue`, `currentItems`, `globalFilterValue`, `items`, `itemsPerPage`, `itemsPerPageOptions`, `selected`, `selectedAll`, `sorterValue`, `totalItems` and `totalPages` as refs, and `clean()`, `isSelected(item)`, `setActivePage`, `setColumnFilterValue`, `setGlobalFilterValue`, `setItemsPerPage`, `setSelected`, `setSorterValue`, `toggle(item)` and `toggleAll()` to write to them.

```html
<script setup>
import {
  CCard,
  CCardBody,
  CCardText,
  CCardTitle,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CSmartPagination,
  useSmartTable,
} from '@coreui/vue-pro'

const items = [
  { id: 1, name: 'Samppa Nori', registered: '2021/03/01', role: 'Member' },
  { id: 2, name: 'Estavan Lykos', registered: '2018/02/07', role: 'Staff' },
  { id: 3, name: 'Chetan Mohamed', registered: '2020/01/15', role: 'Admin' },
  { id: 4, name: 'Derick Maximinus', registered: '2019/04/05', role: 'Member' },
  { id: 5, name: 'Friderik Dávid', registered: '2022/03/25', role: 'Staff' },
  { id: 6, name: 'Yiorgos Avraamu', registered: '2021/11/12', role: 'Member' },
  { id: 7, name: 'Avram Tarasios', registered: '2020/06/30', role: 'Staff' },
]

const {
  activePage,
  currentItems,
  globalFilterValue,
  setActivePage,
  setGlobalFilterValue,
  totalPages,
} = useSmartTable({
  columns: ['name', 'registered', 'role'],
  defaultItemsPerPage: 3,
  itemKey: 'id',
  items,
  pagination: true,
})
</script>

<template>
  <CFormLabel for="headless-filter">Filter:</CFormLabel>
  <CFormInput
    id="headless-filter"
    class="mb-4"
    :model-value="globalFilterValue"
    placeholder="name, role..."
    @update:model-value="(value) => setGlobalFilterValue(value)"
  />
  <CCard v-for="item in currentItems" :key="item.id" class="mb-3">
    <CCardBody>
      <CCardTitle>{{ item.name }}</CCardTitle>
      <CCardText class="fg-2">{{ item.role }} · registered {{ item.registered }}</CCardText>
    </CCardBody>
  </CCard>
  <p v-if="currentItems.length === 0" class="fg-2">No items found</p>
  <CSmartPagination
    :active-page="activePage"
    :pages="totalPages"
    size="sm"
    @active-page-change="(page) => setActivePage(page)"
  />
</template>
```

# Vue Smart Table (DataTable) Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Smart Table (DataTable) component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=vue&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## CSmartTable

```jsx
import { CSmartTable } from '@coreui/vue-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `activePage` | `number` | - | The active page. When set, the component renders that page and only reports the user's page changes through the `activePageChange` event. |
| `ariaCleanerLabel` | `string` | `'Clear filters and sorting'` | A string that provides an accessible label for the cleaner button. This label is read by screen readers to describe the action associated with the button. |
| `ariaSelectAllLabel` | `string` | `'Select all rows'` | A string that provides an accessible label for the checkbox that selects every row. This label is read by screen readers to describe the action associated with the checkbox. |
| `ariaSelectRowLabel` | `string` | `'Select row'` | A string that provides an accessible label for the checkbox that selects a single row. This label is read by screen readers to describe the action associated with the checkbox. |
| `cleaner` | `boolean` | - | When set, displays a button above the table that resets the global filter, the column filters and the sorter. The button is disabled while there is nothing to reset, and its icon can be replaced through the `cleanerIcon` slot. |
| `clickableRows` | `boolean` | - | Style table items as clickable. |
| `columnFilter` | `boolean \| ColumnFilter` | - | When set, displays an additional filter row between the table header and the items, allowing filtering by a specific column. Can be customized by passing the prop as an object with additional options as keys. Available options: - lazy (Boolean) - Set to true to trigger filter updates only on the change event. |
| `columnFilterValue` | `ColumnFilterValue` | - | The state of the column filters. Keys are column names, values are filter strings, numbers or predicates, e.g.: `{ user: 'John', age: 12 }`. When set, the component renders that state and only reports the user's changes through the `columnFilterChange` event. |
| `columns` | `(Column \| ColumnGroup \| string)[]` | - | Table columns configuration. If the prop is not defined, the table displays columns based on the first item keys, omitting keys that begin with an underscore (e.g. `_props`). Each array item represents one column and can be: - String - the column name equal to the item value. - Object - a column with the following keys: - `key` (required)(String) - the column name equal to the item key. - `label` (String) - the visible label of the column. Generated from the column name when not defined. - `filterable` (Boolean) - set to `false` to remove the filter from the column. - `filter` ((values, onChange, state) => VNode) - renders a custom filter for the column. - `sortable` (Boolean) - set to `false` to disable sorting of the column. - `sorter` ((a, b) => number) - a custom compare function for the column. - `headerProps` (Object) - props for the column's [CTableHeaderCell](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/table/#ctableheadercell). - `headerStyle` (Object) - styles for the column header (useful for defining widths). - `cellProps` (Object) - props for the column's [CTableDataCell](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/table/#ctabledatacell). - `cellStyle` (Object) - styles for the column cells. - Object with `label` and `children` - a group of columns rendered as a header spanning its children. |
| `columnSorter` | `boolean \| Sorter` | - | Enables table sorting by column value. Sorting works as expected when the values in a column are of one type: string (case insensitive) or number. Can be customized by passing the prop as an object with additional options as keys. Available options: - multiple (Boolean) - Enables sorting by multiple columns simultaneously. The sorting order is maintained across columns based on the order of interaction. - resettable (Boolean) - If set to true, clicking the sorter cycles through three states: ascending, descending and unsorted. |
| `defaultActivePage` | `number` | - | The initial active page, when the page is not controlled through `activePage`. |
| `defaultColumnFilterValue` | `ColumnFilterValue` | - | The initial state of the column filters, when they are not controlled through `columnFilterValue`. |
| `defaultGlobalFilterValue` | `string` | - | The initial value of the global filter, when it is not controlled through `globalFilterValue`. |
| `defaultItemsPerPage` | `number` | - | The initial number of items per page, when it is not controlled through `itemsPerPage`. |
| `defaultSelected` | `Item[]` | - | The initially selected items, when the selection is not controlled through `selected`. |
| `defaultSorterValue` | `SorterValue[]` | - | The initial state of the sorter, when it is not controlled through `sorterValue`. |
| `external` | `boolean` | - | Set when `items` arrive already filtered, sorted and sliced - the component renders them as they are and only reports the requested state through its events. Use `totalItems` to let it compute the number of pages. |
| `footer` | `boolean \| (FooterItem \| string)[]` | - | If `true`, displays a table footer which mirrors the table header (without the column filter). Or an array of objects or strings, where each element represents one cell in the table footer. Example items: `['FooterCell', 'FooterCell', 'FooterCell']` or `[{ label: 'FooterCell', props: { color: 'success' } }, ...]` |
| `globalFilter` | `boolean \| GlobalFilter` | - | When set, displays a filter input above the table which filters the items by the values of all columns. Can be customized by passing the prop as an object with additional options as keys. Available options: - lazy (Boolean) - Set to true to trigger filter updates only on the change event. |
| `globalFilterLabel` | `string` | `'Filter:'` | The element represents a caption for the global filter input. |
| `globalFilterPlaceholder` | `string` | `'type string...'` | Specifies a short hint that is visible in the global filter input. |
| `globalFilterValue` | `string` | - | The value of the global filter. When set, the component renders that value and only reports the user's changes through the `globalFilterChange` event. |
| `header` | `boolean` | `true` | Set to false to remove the table header. |
| `itemKey` | `string` | - | The name of the item property that identifies a row. When set, the selection and the row keys compare that value instead of the whole item. |
| `items` | `Item[]` | `() => []` | Array of objects, where each object represents one item - row in the table. Additionally, you can customize each row through the [_props](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/table/#ctablerow) key, a single cell through [_cellProps](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/table/#ctabledatacell) and `_cellStyle`, and block its selection with `_selectable: false`. Examples: - `_props: { color: 'primary', align: 'middle'}` - `_cellProps: { all: { class: 'fw-semibold'}, 'name': { color: 'info' }}` |
| `itemsPerPage` | `number` | - | The number of items per page. When set, the component renders that many items per page and only reports the user's changes through the `itemsPerPageChange` event. |
| `itemsPerPageLabel` | `string` | `'Items per page:'` | Label for the items per page selector. |
| `itemsPerPageOptions` | `number[]` | `() => [5, 10, 20, 50]` | Items per page selector options. |
| `itemsPerPageSelect` | `boolean` | - | Adds a select element under the table which controls the number of items per page. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | - | When set, the table has a loading style: a loading spinner and reduced opacity. |
| `loadingContent` | `string\|object` | - | The content rendered over the table while `loading` is set. Can also be passed through the slot of the same name. |
| `noItemsLabel` | `string` | `'No items found'` | The text rendered in place of the rows when there is nothing to show. |
| `pagination` | `boolean` | - | Enables the pagination under the table. The number of pages is computed from the number of items and `itemsPerPage` (or from `totalItems` when `external` is set). |
| `paginationProps` | `object` | - | Properties passed to the [CSmartPagination](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/smart-pagination#csmartpagination) component. |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | - | Add checkboxes to make table rows selectable. |
| `selectAll` | `boolean` | `true` | Enables the select all checkbox displayed in the header of the table. |
| `selected` | `Item[]` | - | Array of selected items - rows in the table. When set, the component renders that selection and only reports the user's changes through the `selectedChange` event. Example item: `{ name: 'John' , age: 12 }` |
| `sortAscendingIcon` | `string\|object` | - | The icon rendered in the header of a column sorted ascending. Can also be passed through the slot of the same name. |
| `sortDescendingIcon` | `string\|object` | - | The icon rendered in the header of a column sorted descending. Can also be passed through the slot of the same name. |
| `sorterValue` | `SorterValue[]` | - | The state of the sorter, ordered by the columns' precedence, e.g. `[{ column: 'status', direction: 'asc' }]`. When set, the component renders that state and only reports the user's changes through the `sorterChange` event. |
| `sortNeutralIcon` | `string\|object` | - | The icon rendered in the header of an unsorted column. Can also be passed through the slot of the same name. |
| `tableBodyProps` | `object` | - | Properties passed to the [CTableBody](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/table/#ctablebody) component. |
| `tableFootProps` | `object` | - | Properties passed to the [CTableFoot](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/table/#ctablefoot) component. |
| `tableHeadProps` | `object` | - | Properties passed to the [CTableHead](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/table/#ctablehead) component. |
| `tableProps` | `object` | - | Properties passed to the [CTable](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/table/#ctable) component. |
| `totalItems` | `number` | - | The total number of items. Set it when `items` hold only a portion of the data, so the component knows how many pages there are. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `activePageChange` | Page change callback. |
| `columnFilterChange` | Column filter change callback. |
| `filteredItemsChange` | Filtered items change callback. |
| `globalFilterChange` | Global filter change callback. |
| `itemsPerPageChange` | Items per page change callback. |
| `rowChecked` | Row checked callback. |
| `rowClick` | Row click callback. |
| `selectedChange` | Selection change callback. |
| `sorterChange` | Sorter value change callback. |

# Vue Spinner Component

> Indicate the loading state of a component or page with CoreUI spinners, built entirely with HTML, CSS, and no JavaScript.

## About

CoreUI "spinners" can be used to show the loading state in your projects. They're built only with HTML and CSS, meaning you don't need any JavaScript to create them. You will, however, need some custom JavaScript to toggle their visibility. Their appearance, alignment, and sizing can be easily customized with our amazing utility classes.

For accessibility purposes, each loader here includes `role="status"` and a nested `<span class="visually-hidden">Loading</span>`, whose text `ariaLoadingLabel` sets. When a spinner sits next to text that says what is loading, as in the [buttons](#buttons) below, pass `ariaLoadingLabel=""`, which hides the spinner from screen readers, and put `role="status"` on that text instead, so a screen reader reads the message once.

## Border spinner

Use the border spinners for a lightweight loading indicator.

```html
<template>
  <CSpinner />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CSpinner } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Growing spinner

If you don't fancy a border spinner, switch to the grow spinner. While it doesn't technically spin, it does repeatedly grow!

```html
<template>
  <CSpinner variant="grow" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CSpinner } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

Once again, this spinner is built with `currentColor`, so you can easily change its appearance. Here it is in blue, along with the supported variants.

```html
<template>
  <CSpinner color="primary" variant="grow" />
  <CSpinner color="secondary" variant="grow" />
  <CSpinner color="success" variant="grow" />
  <CSpinner color="danger" variant="grow" />
  <CSpinner color="warning" variant="grow" />
  <CSpinner color="info" variant="grow" />
  <CSpinner color="secondary" variant="grow" />
  <CSpinner color="inverse" variant="grow" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CSpinner } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Variants

Both spinners take their appearance from `currentColor`, so the `color` property — which renders one of our [text color utilities](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/colors/) — recolors either of them.

```html
<template>
  <CSpinner color="primary" />
  <CSpinner color="secondary" />
  <CSpinner color="success" />
  <CSpinner color="danger" />
  <CSpinner color="warning" />
  <CSpinner color="info" />
  <CSpinner color="secondary" />
  <CSpinner color="inverse" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CSpinner } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Alignment

CoreUI Vue spinners are built with `rems`, `currentColor`, and `display: inline-flex`. This means they can easily be resized, recolored, and quickly aligned.

### Margin

Use margin utilities like `.m-6` for easy spacing.

```html
<template>
  <CSpinner size="sm" />
  <CSpinner size="sm" variant="grow" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CSpinner } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

### Placement

Use flexbox utilities, float utilities, or text alignment utilities to place spinners exactly where you need them in any situation.

#### Flex

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" disabled>
    <CSpinner as="span" size="sm" aria-loading-label="" />
  </CButton>
  <CButton theme="primary" disabled>
    <CSpinner as="span" size="sm" aria-loading-label="" />
    Loading...
  </CButton>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CButton, CSpinner } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" disabled>
    <CSpinner as="span" size="sm" variant="grow" aria-loading-label="" />
  </CButton>
  <CButton theme="primary" disabled>
    <CSpinner as="span" size="sm" variant="grow" aria-loading-label="" />
    Loading...
  </CButton>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CButton, CSpinner } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

#### Floats

```html
<template>
  <div class="clearfix">
    <CSpinner class="float-end" />
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CSpinner } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

#### Text align

```html
<template>
  <div class="text-center">
    <CSpinner />
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CSpinner } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Size

Spinners are `1em` square, so they match the font size of whatever they sit in — drop one into a heading or a button and it scales with the text. Add `size="sm"` to make it smaller still.

```html
<template>
  <CSpinner size="sm" />
  <CSpinner size="sm" variant="grow" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CSpinner } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

Or, use custom CSS or inline styles to change the dimensions as needed.

```html
<template>
  <CSpinner :style="{ width: '3rem', height: '3rem' }" />
  <CSpinner variant="grow" :style="{ width: '3rem', height: '3rem' }" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CSpinner } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Custom spinners

Add `.spinner-rotate` to any element to spin it at the same speed as the border spinner. Use it when you want your own artwork instead of a bordered circle.

```html
<template>
  <svg
    class="spinner-rotate"
    width="2rem"
    height="2rem"
    viewBox="0 0 16 16"
    fill="none"
    stroke="currentcolor"
    stroke-width="2"
    stroke-linecap="round"
    aria-hidden="true"
  >
    <path d="M8 1V4" />
    <path opacity=".8" d="M3.05 3.05L5.17 5.17" />
    <path opacity=".6" d="M4 8L1 8" />
    <path opacity=".5" d="M5.17 10.83L3.05 12.95" />
    <path opacity=".4" d="M8 12V15" />
    <path opacity=".3" d="M10.83 10.83L12.95 12.95" />
    <path opacity=".2" d="M15 8L12 8" />
    <path opacity=".1" d="M12.95 3.05L10.83 5.17" />
  </svg>
</template>
```

## Buttons

Use spinners within buttons to indicate an action is currently processing or taking place. You may also swap the text out of the spinner element and utilize button text as needed.

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" disabled>
    <CSpinner as="span" aria-loading-label="" />
    <span class="visually-hidden" role="status">Loading...</span>
  </CButton>
  <CButton theme="primary" disabled>
    <CSpinner as="span" class="me-3" aria-loading-label="" />
    <span role="status">Loading...</span>
  </CButton>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CButton, CSpinner } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

```html
<template>
  <CButton theme="primary" disabled>
    <CSpinner as="span" variant="grow" aria-loading-label="" />
    <span class="visually-hidden" role="status">Loading...</span>
  </CButton>
  <CButton theme="primary" disabled>
    <CSpinner as="span" class="me-3" variant="grow" aria-loading-label="" />
    <span role="status">Loading...</span>
  </CButton>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CButton, CSpinner } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## API

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

- [&lt;CSpinner /&gt;](./api/#cspinner)

# Vue Spinner Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Spinner component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CSpinner

```jsx
import { CSpinner } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLoadingLabel` | `string` | `undefined` | Sets the text screen readers read as the spinner's status, `'Loading'` unless set. An empty string hides the spinner from assistive technologies. |
| `as` | `string` | `'div'` | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |
| `color` | `string` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |
| `size` | `string` | - | Size the component small. |
| `variant` | `string` | `'border'` | Set the button variant to an outlined button or a ghost button. |
| `visuallyHiddenLabel` | `string` | `undefined` | Sets the visually hidden label of the spinner. |

# Vue Spinner Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Spinner component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

## CSS variables

Vue spinners use local CSS variables on `.spinner-border` and `.spinner-grow` for enhanced real-time customization. Values for the CSS variables are set via Sass, so Sass customization is still supported, too.

Border spinner variables:

```scss
$spinner-border-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-spinner-width: 1em,
    --cui-spinner-height: 1em,
    --cui-spinner-border-width: .125em,
    --cui-spinner-animation-speed: #{$spinner-animation-speed},
    --cui-spinner-animation-timing-function: #{$spinner-animation-timing-function},
    --cui-spinner-animation-name: spinner-border,
  ),
  $spinner-border-tokens
);
```

Growing spinner variables:

```scss
$spinner-grow-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-spinner-width: 1em,
    --cui-spinner-height: 1em,
    --cui-spinner-animation-speed: #{$spinner-animation-speed},
    --cui-spinner-animation-timing-function: ease-in-out,
    --cui-spinner-animation-name: spinner-grow,
  ),
  $spinner-grow-tokens
);
```

For both spinners, small spinner modifier classes are used to update the values of these CSS variables as needed. For example, the `.spinner-border-sm` class does the following:

```scss
--cui-spinner-width: #{.75em};
--cui-spinner-height: #{.75em};
```

### How to use CSS variables

```vue
<template>
  <CSpinner :style="vars">...</CSpinner>
</template>

<script setup>
const vars = {
  '--cui-spinner-width': '1rem',
  '--cui-spinner-height': '1rem',
}
</script>
```

# Vue Tab Component

> The CoreUI Vue Tabs component provides a flexible and accessible way to create tabbed navigation in your application. It supports various styles and configurations to meet different design requirements.

## Example

The basic Vue tabs example uses the `variant="tabs"` props to generate a tabbed interface.

```html
<template>
  <CTabs active-item-key="profile">
    <CTabList variant="tabs">
      <CTab item-key="home">Home</CTab>
      <CTab item-key="profile">Profile</CTab>
      <CTab item-key="contact">Contact</CTab>
      <CTab disabled item-key="disabled">Disabled</CTab>
    </CTabList>
    <CTabContent>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" item-key="home"> Home tab content </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" item-key="profile"> Profile tab content </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" item-key="contact"> Contact tab content </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" item-key="disabled"> Disabled tab content </CTabPanel>
    </CTabContent>
  </CTabs>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTabs, CTabList, CTab, CTabContent, CTabPanel } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Available styles

Change the style of `<CTabs>`'s component with modifiers and utilities. Mix and match as needed, or build your own.

### Unstyled

If you don’t provide the `variant` prop, the component will default to a basic style.

```html
<template>
  <CTabs active-item-key="profile">
    <CTabList>
      <CTab item-key="home">Home</CTab>
      <CTab item-key="profile">Profile</CTab>
      <CTab item-key="contact">Contact</CTab>
      <CTab disabled item-key="disabled">Disabled</CTab>
    </CTabList>
    <CTabContent>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" item-key="home"> Home tab content </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" item-key="profile"> Profile tab content </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" item-key="contact"> Contact tab content </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" item-key="disabled"> Disabled tab content </CTabPanel>
    </CTabContent>
  </CTabs>
</template>

<script setup>
```

```html
</script>
```

### Fill and justify

Force your `<CTabs>`'s contents to extend the full available width one of two modifier classes. To proportionately fill all available space use `layout="fill"`. Notice that all horizontal space is occupied, but not every nav item has the same width.

```html
<template>
  <CTabs :active-item-key="2">
    <CTabList variant="tabs" layout="fill">
      <CTab aria-controls="home-tab-pane" :item-key="1">Home</CTab>
      <CTab aria-controls="profile-tab-pane" :item-key="2">Profile tab with longer content</CTab>
      <CTab aria-controls="contact-tab-pane" :item-key="3">Contact</CTab>
      <CTab aria-controls="disabled-tab-pane" disabled :item-key="4">Disabled</CTab>
    </CTabList>
    <CTabContent>
      <CTabPanel class="py-4" aria-labelledby="home-tab-pane" :item-key="1">
        Home tab content
      </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="py-4" aria-labelledby="profile-tab-pane" :item-key="2">
        Profile tab content
      </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="py-4" aria-labelledby="contact-tab-pane" :item-key="3">
        Contact tab content
      </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="py-4" aria-labelledby="disabled-tab-pane" :item-key="4">
        Disabled tab content
      </CTabPanel>
    </CTabContent>
  </CTabs>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTabs, CTabList, CTab, CTabContent, CTabPanel } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

For equal-width elements, use `layout="justified"`. All horizontal space will be occupied by nav links, but unlike the `layout="fill"` above, every nav item will be the same width.

```html
<template>
  <CTabs :active-item-key="2">
    <CTabList variant="tabs" layout="justified">
      <CTab aria-controls="home-tab-pane" :item-key="1">Home</CTab>
      <CTab aria-controls="profile-tab-pane" :item-key="2">Profile</CTab>
      <CTab aria-controls="contact-tab-pane" :item-key="3">Contact</CTab>
      <CTab aria-controls="disabled-tab-pane" disabled :item-key="4">Disabled</CTab>
    </CTabList>
    <CTabContent>
      <CTabPanel class="py-4" aria-labelledby="home-tab-pane" :item-key="1">
        Home tab content
      </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="py-4" aria-labelledby="profile-tab-pane" :item-key="2">
        Profile tab content
      </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="py-4" aria-labelledby="contact-tab-pane" :item-key="3">
        Contact tab content
      </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="py-4" aria-labelledby="disabled-tab-pane" :item-key="4">
        Disabled tab content
      </CTabPanel>
    </CTabContent>
  </CTabs>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTabs, CTabList, CTab, CTabContent, CTabPanel } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Usage with v-model

Bind `v-model:active-item-key` and the tabs keep the value in step with your state — useful when the active tab has to follow something else, like a route or a wizard step.

```html
<template>
  <p>
    Active tab: <strong>{{ activeKey }}</strong>
  </p>
  <CTabs v-model:active-item-key="activeKey">
    <CTabList variant="tabs">
      <CTab :item-key="1">Home</CTab>
      <CTab :item-key="2">Profile</CTab>
      <CTab :item-key="3">Contact</CTab>
    </CTabList>
    <CTabContent>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" :item-key="1">Home panel.</CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" :item-key="2">Profile panel.</CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" :item-key="3">Contact panel.</CTabPanel>
    </CTabContent>
  </CTabs>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CTab, CTabContent, CTabList, CTabPanel, CTabs } from '@coreui/vue'

const activeKey = ref(1)
</script>
```

The `change` event fires alongside it, on user interaction only. Moving the tab from your own code does not echo back, so a handler that writes to the bound value cannot loop.

## Accessibility

Dynamic tabbed interfaces, as described in the [<abbr title="Web Accessibility Initiative">WAI</abbr> <abbr title="Accessible Rich Internet Applications">ARIA</abbr> Authoring Practices](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-practices/#tabpanel), require `role="tablist"`, `role="tab"`, `role="tabpanel"`, and additional `aria-` attributes in order to convey their structure, functionality and current state to users of assistive technologies (such as screen readers).

### WAI-ARIA Roles

- The element that serves as the container for the set of tabs has the role `tablist`.
- Each element that serves as a tab has the role `tab` and is contained within the element with the role `tablist`.
- Each element that contains the content panel for a tab has the role `tabpanel`.
- If the tab list has a visible label, the element with the role `tablist` has `aria-labelledby` set to a value that refers to the labeling element. Otherwise, the `tablist` element has a label provided by `aria-label`.
- Each element with the role `tab` has the property `aria-controls` referring to its associated `tabpanel` element.
- The active tab element has the state `aria-selected` set to `true`, and all other tab elements have it set to `false`.
- Each element with the role `tabpanel` has the property `aria-labelledby` referring to its associated `tab` element.

Our Vue Tabs component automatically manages all `role="..."` and `aria-` attributes for accessibility. It also handles the selected state by adding `aria-selected="true"` to the active tab. Additionally, you have the flexibility to manually set these attributes, as shown in the example below:

```vue
<CTabs :active-item-key="2">
  <CTabList variant="tabs">
    <CTab id="home-tab" aria-controls="home-tab-pane" :item-key="1">Home</CTab>
    <CTab id="profile-tab" aria-controls="profile-tab-pane" :item-key="2">Profile</CTab>
    <CTab id="contact-tab" aria-controls="contact-tab-pane" :item-key="3">Contact</CTab>
    <CTab id="disabled-tab" aria-controls="disabled-tab-pane" disabled :item-key="4">Disabled</CTab>
  </CTabList>
  <CTabContent>
    <CTabPanel id="home-tab-pane" class="p-4" aria-labelledby="home-tab" :item-key="1">
      Home tab content
    </CTabPanel>
    <CTabPanel id="profile-tab-pane" class="p-4" aria-labelledby="profile-tab" :item-key="2">
      Profile tab content
    </CTabPanel>
    <CTabPanel id="contact-tab-pane" class="p-4" aria-labelledby="contact-tab" :item-key="3">
      Contact tab content
    </CTabPanel>
    <CTabPanel id="disabled-tab-pane" class="p-4" aria-labelledby="disabled-tab" :item-key="4">
      Disabled tab content
    </CTabPanel>
  </CTabContent>
</CTabs>
```

This example demonstrates how to manually set `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, and `aria-labelledby` attributes on your `<CTab>`'s and `<CTabPanels>`'s.

### Keyboard Interaction

**When focus enters the tab list:**

<kbd>Tab</kbd>: It places focus on the active `tab` element.

**When focus is on a tab element:**

<kbd>Tab</kbd>: Moves focus to the next element in the tab sequence, typically the tabpanel unless the first focusable element inside the tabpanel is found earlier.

<kbd>Left Arrow</kbd>: Moves focus to the previous tab. If on the first tab, it wraps around to the last tab.

<kbd>Right Arrow</kbd>: Moves focus to the next tab. If on the last tab, it wraps around to the first tab.

<kbd>Home</kbd>: Moves focus to the first tab.

<kbd>End</kbd>: Moves focus to the last tab.

# Vue Tabs Component API

> Explore the API reference for the Vue Tabs component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CTab

```jsx
import { CTab } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `itemKey` | `number\|string` | - | Item key. |
## CTabContent

```jsx
import { CTabContent } from '@coreui/vue'
```
## CTabList

```jsx
import { CTabList } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layout` | `string` | - | Specify a layout type for component. |
| `variant` | `string` | - | Set the nav variant to tabs or pills. |
## CTabPanel

```jsx
import { CTabPanel } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `itemKey` | `number\|string` | - | Item key. |
| `show` | `boolean` | `undefined` | Toggle the visibility of component. |
| `transition` | `boolean` | `true` | Enable fade in and fade out transition. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | `false` | Toggle the visibility of component. |

### Events

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `hide` | Callback fired when the component requests to be hidden. |
| `show` | Callback fired when the component requests to be shown. |

```jsx
import { CTabs } from '@coreui/vue'
```

# Vue Tabs Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the Vue Tabs component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

## CSS variables

Vue tabs use local CSS variables on `.nav`, `.nav-tabs`, `.nav-pills`, `.nav-underline` and `.nav-underline-border` for enhanced real-time customization. Values for the CSS variables are set via Sass, so Sass customization is still supported, too.

On the `.nav` base class:

```scss
$nav-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-nav-gap: 0,
    --cui-nav-link-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-nav-link-align: center,
    --cui-nav-link-justify: center,
    --cui-nav-link-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-5),
    --cui-nav-link-padding-x: 1rem,
    --cui-nav-link-padding-y: #{$nav-link-padding-y},
    --cui-nav-link-font-size: inherit,
    --cui-nav-link-font-weight: inherit,
    --cui-nav-link-color: var(--cui-fg-2),
    --cui-nav-link-hover-color: var(--cui-fg-1),
    --cui-nav-link-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-nav-link-active-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-nav-link-active-bg: var(--cui-bg-2),
    --cui-nav-link-disabled-color: var(--cui-fg-4),
    --cui-nav-link-transition-property: #{color, background-color, border-color},
    --cui-nav-link-transition-duration: .15s,
    --cui-nav-link-transition-timing: ease-in-out,
  ),
  $nav-tokens
);
```

On the `.nav-tabs` modifier class:

```scss
$nav-tabs-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-nav-tabs-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-nav-tabs-border-color: #{$nav-tabs-border-color},
    --cui-nav-tabs-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-5),
    --cui-nav-tabs-link-hover-border-color: #{var(--cui-border-subtle) var(--cui-border-subtle) $nav-tabs-border-color},
    --cui-nav-tabs-link-active-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-nav-tabs-link-active-bg: #{$nav-tabs-link-active-bg},
    --cui-nav-tabs-link-active-border-color: #{var(--cui-border-color) var(--cui-border-color) $nav-tabs-link-active-bg},
  ),
  $nav-tabs-tokens
);
```

On the `.nav-pills` modifier class:

```scss
$nav-pills-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-nav-pills-border-radius: 3rem,
    --cui-nav-pills-link-active-color: var(--cui-primary-contrast),
    --cui-nav-pills-link-active-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg),
  ),
  $nav-pills-tokens
);
```

On the `.nav-underline` modifier class:

```scss
$nav-underline-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-nav-underline-gap: 1rem,
    --cui-nav-underline-border-width: .125rem,
    --cui-nav-underline-link-active-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
  ),
  $nav-underline-tokens
);
```

On the `.nav-underline-border` modifier class:

```scss
$nav-underline-border-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-nav-underline-border-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-nav-underline-border-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-nav-underline-border-border-width: .125rem,
    --cui-nav-underline-border-link-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-nav-underline-border-link-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-nav-underline-border-link-color: var(--cui-fg-2),
    --cui-nav-underline-border-link-active-color: var(--cui-primary-base),
    --cui-nav-underline-border-link-disabled-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
  ),
  $nav-underline-border-tokens
);
```

### How to use CSS variables

```vue
<template>
  <CTabs :style="vars">...</CTabs>
</template>

<script setup>
const vars = {
  '--cui-nav-link-color': '#333',
  '--cui-nav-link-hover-color': '#f8f9fa',
}
</script>
```

## Sass variables

_Deprecated in 6.0.0._

Sass variables set these defaults at build time and are removed in v7. The CSS variables above reach the same values without recompiling, and can be set on a single element.

```scss
$nav-link-padding-y:                .5rem !default;

$nav-tabs-border-color:             var(--cui-border-color) !default;
$nav-tabs-link-active-bg:           var(--cui-bg-body) !default;
```

# Vue Tabs Component Accessibility

> Detailed overview of the accessibility features implemented in CoreUI Vue Tabs, ensuring compliance with WAI-ARIA guidelines.

## Accessibility

Dynamic tabbed interfaces, as described in the [<abbr title="Web Accessibility Initiative">WAI</abbr> <abbr title="Accessible Rich Internet Applications">ARIA</abbr> Authoring Practices](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-practices/#tabpanel), require `role="tablist"`, `role="tab"`, `role="tabpanel"`, and additional `aria-` attributes in order to convey their structure, functionality and current state to users of assistive technologies (such as screen readers).

### WAI-ARIA Roles

- The element that serves as the container for the set of tabs has the role `tablist`.
- Each element that serves as a tab has the role `tab` and is contained within the element with the role `tablist`.
- Each element that contains the content panel for a tab has the role `tabpanel`.
- If the tab list has a visible label, the element with the role `tablist` has `aria-labelledby` set to a value that refers to the labeling element. Otherwise, the `tablist` element has a label provided by `aria-label`.
- Each element with the role `tab` has the property `aria-controls` referring to its associated `tabpanel` element.
- The active tab element has the state `aria-selected` set to `true`, and all other tab elements have it set to `false`.
- Each element with the role `tabpanel` has the property `aria-labelledby` referring to its associated `tab` element.

Our Vue Tabs component automatically manages all `role="..."` and `aria-` attributes for accessibility. It also handles the selected state by adding `aria-selected="true"` to the active tab. Additionally, you have the flexibility to manually set these attributes, as shown in the example below:

```jsx
<CTabs :activeItemKey="2">
  <CTabList variant="tabs">
    <CTab id="home-tab" aria-controls="home-tab-pane" :itemKey="1">Home</CTab>
    <CTab id="profile-tab" aria-controls="profile-tab-pane" :itemKey="2">Profile</CTab>
    <CTab id="contact-tab" aria-controls="contact-tab-pane" :itemKey="3">Contact</CTab>
    <CTab id="disabled-tab" aria-controls="disabled-tab-pane" disabled :itemKey="4">Disabled</CTab>
  </CTabList>
  <CTabContent>
    <CTabPanel id="home-tab-pane" class="p-4" aria-labelledby="home-tab-pane" aria-labelledby="home-tab" :itemKey="1">
      Home tab content
    </CTabPanel>
    <CTabPanel id="profile-tab-pane" class="p-4" aria-labelledby="profile-tab-pane" aria-labelledby="profile-tab" :itemKey="2">
      Profile tab content
    </CTabPanel>
    <CTabPanel id="contact-tab-pane" class="p-4" aria-labelledby="contact-tab-pane" aria-labelledby="contact-tab" :itemKey="3">
      Contact tab content
    </CTabPanel>
    <CTabPanel id="disabled-tab-pane" class="p-4" aria-labelledby="disabled-tab-pane" aria-labelledby="disabled-tab" :itemKey="4">
      Disabled tab content
    </CTabPanel>
  </CTabContent>

```

This example demonstrates how to manually set `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, and `aria-labelledby` attributes on your `<CTab>`'s and `<CTabPanels>`'s.

### Keyboard Interaction

<kbd>Tab</kbd>: It places focus on the active `tab` element.

**When focus is on a tab element:**

<kbd>Tab</kbd>: Moves focus to the next element in the tab sequence, typically the tabpanel unless the first focusable element inside the tabpanel is found earlier.

<kbd>Left Arrow</kbd>: Moves focus to the previous tab. If on the first tab, it wraps around to the last tab.

<kbd>Right Arrow</kbd>: Moves focus to the next tab. If on the last tab, it wraps around to the first tab.

<kbd>Home</kbd>: Moves focus to the first tab.

<kbd>End</kbd>: Moves focus to the last tab.


---

# Vue Bootstrap Tab Component

> Learn how to use CoreUI’s Vue Tabs component with Bootstrap styles for flexible, framework-consistent UI.

## Example

The basic Vue tabs example uses the `variant="tabs"` props to generate a tabbed interface.

```html
<template>
  <CTabs active-item-key="profile">
    <CTabList variant="tabs">
      <CTab item-key="home">Home</CTab>
      <CTab item-key="profile">Profile</CTab>
      <CTab item-key="contact">Contact</CTab>
      <CTab disabled item-key="disabled">Disabled</CTab>
    </CTabList>
    <CTabContent>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" item-key="home"> Home tab content </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" item-key="profile"> Profile tab content </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" item-key="contact"> Contact tab content </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" item-key="disabled"> Disabled tab content </CTabPanel>
    </CTabContent>
  </CTabs>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTabs, CTabList, CTab, CTabContent, CTabPanel } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Available styles

Change the style of `<CTabs>`'s component with modifiers and utilities. Mix and match as needed, or build your own.

### Unstyled

If you don’t provide the `variant` prop, the component will default to a basic style.

```html
<template>
  <CTabs active-item-key="profile">
    <CTabList>
      <CTab item-key="home">Home</CTab>
      <CTab item-key="profile">Profile</CTab>
      <CTab item-key="contact">Contact</CTab>
      <CTab disabled item-key="disabled">Disabled</CTab>
    </CTabList>
    <CTabContent>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" item-key="home"> Home tab content </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" item-key="profile"> Profile tab content </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" item-key="contact"> Contact tab content </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" item-key="disabled"> Disabled tab content </CTabPanel>
    </CTabContent>
  </CTabs>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTabs, CTabList, CTab, CTabContent, CTabPanel } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

### Pills

Take that same code, but use `variant="pills"` instead:

```html
<template>
  <CTabs :active-item-key="2">
    <CTabList variant="pills">
      <CTab aria-controls="home-tab-pane" :item-key="1">Home</CTab>
      <CTab aria-controls="profile-tab-pane" :item-key="2">Profile</CTab>
      <CTab aria-controls="contact-tab-pane" :item-key="3">Contact</CTab>
      <CTab aria-controls="disabled-tab-pane" disabled :item-key="4">Disabled</CTab>
    </CTabList>
    <CTabContent>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" aria-labelledby="home-tab-pane" :item-key="1">
        Home tab content
      </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" aria-labelledby="profile-tab-pane" :item-key="2">
        Profile tab content
      </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" aria-labelledby="contact-tab-pane" :item-key="3">
        Contact tab content
      </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="p-4" aria-labelledby="disabled-tab-pane" :item-key="4">
        Disabled tab content
      </CTabPanel>

</template>

import { CTabs, CTabList, CTab, CTabContent, CTabPanel } from '@coreui/vue'
```

### Fill and justify

Force your `<CTabs>`'s contents to extend the full available width one of two modifier classes. To proportionately fill all available space use `layout="fill"`. Notice that all horizontal space is occupied, but not every nav item has the same width.

```html
<template>
  <CTabs :active-item-key="2">
    <CTabList variant="tabs" layout="fill">
      <CTab aria-controls="home-tab-pane" :item-key="1">Home</CTab>
      <CTab aria-controls="profile-tab-pane" :item-key="2">Profile tab with longer content</CTab>
      <CTab aria-controls="contact-tab-pane" :item-key="3">Contact</CTab>
      <CTab aria-controls="disabled-tab-pane" disabled :item-key="4">Disabled</CTab>
    </CTabList>
    <CTabContent>
      <CTabPanel class="py-4" aria-labelledby="home-tab-pane" :item-key="1">
        Home tab content
      </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="py-4" aria-labelledby="profile-tab-pane" :item-key="2">
        Profile tab content
      </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="py-4" aria-labelledby="contact-tab-pane" :item-key="3">
        Contact tab content
      </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="py-4" aria-labelledby="disabled-tab-pane" :item-key="4">
        Disabled tab content
      </CTabPanel>
    </CTabContent>
  </CTabs>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTabs, CTabList, CTab, CTabContent, CTabPanel } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

For equal-width elements, use `layout="justified"`. All horizontal space will be occupied by nav links, but unlike the `layout="fill"` above, every nav item will be the same width.

```html
<template>
  <CTabs :active-item-key="2">
    <CTabList variant="tabs" layout="justified">
      <CTab aria-controls="home-tab-pane" :item-key="1">Home</CTab>
      <CTab aria-controls="profile-tab-pane" :item-key="2">Profile</CTab>
      <CTab aria-controls="contact-tab-pane" :item-key="3">Contact</CTab>
      <CTab aria-controls="disabled-tab-pane" disabled :item-key="4">Disabled</CTab>
    </CTabList>
    <CTabContent>
      <CTabPanel class="py-4" aria-labelledby="home-tab-pane" :item-key="1">
        Home tab content
      </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="py-4" aria-labelledby="profile-tab-pane" :item-key="2">
        Profile tab content
      </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="py-4" aria-labelledby="contact-tab-pane" :item-key="3">
        Contact tab content
      </CTabPanel>
      <CTabPanel class="py-4" aria-labelledby="disabled-tab-pane" :item-key="4">
        Disabled tab content
      </CTabPanel>
    </CTabContent>
  </CTabs>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTabs, CTabList, CTab, CTabContent, CTabPanel } from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

# Vue Table Component

> Documentation and examples for opt-in styling of tables.

## Overview

Due to the widespread use of `<CTable>` elements across third-party widgets like calendars and date pickers, CoreUI's tables are **opt-in**. All table styles are not inherited in CoreUI, meaning any nested tables can be styled independent from the parent.

Using the most basic table CoreUI, here's how `<CTable>`-based tables look in CoreUI.

```html
<template>
  <CTable :columns="columns" :items="items" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTable } from '@coreui/vue'
const columns = [
  {
    key: 'id',
    label: '#',
    _props: { scope: 'col' },
  },
  {
    key: 'class',
    _props: { scope: 'col' },
  },
  {
    key: 'heading_1',
    label: 'Heading',
    _props: { scope: 'col' },
  },
  {
    key: 'heading_2',
    label: 'Heading',
    _props: { scope: 'col' },
  },
]
const items = [
  {
    id: 1,
    class: 'Mark',
    heading_1: 'Otto',
    heading_2: '@mdo',
    _cellProps: { id: { scope: 'row' } },
  },
  {
    id: 2,
    class: 'Jacob',
    heading_1: 'Thornton',
    heading_2: '@fat',
    _cellProps: { id: { scope: 'row' } },
  },
  {
    id: 3,
    class: 'Larry the Bird',
    heading_2: '@twitter',
    _cellProps: { id: { scope: 'row' }, class: { colSpan: 2 } },
  },
]
</script>
```
In version **4.5.0** we introduced a new way to create a table, similarly to our [Smart Table component](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/smart-table/).

```vue
<template>
  <CTable :columns="columns" :items="items" />
</template>
```

You can also put all table components together manually as hitherto.

```vue
<CTable>
  <CTableHead>
    <CTableRow>
      <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">#</CTableHeaderCell>
      <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Class</CTableHeaderCell>
      <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Heading</CTableHeaderCell>
      <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Heading</CTableHeaderCell>
    </CTableRow>
  </CTableHead>
  <CTableBody>
    <CTableRow>
      <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">1</CTableHeaderCell>
      <CTableDataCell>Mark</CTableDataCell>
      <CTableDataCell>Otto</CTableDataCell>
      <CTableDataCell>@mdo</CTableDataCell>
    </CTableRow>
    <CTableRow>
      <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">2</CTableHeaderCell>
      <CTableDataCell>Jacob</CTableDataCell>
      <CTableDataCell>Thornton</CTableDataCell>
      <CTableDataCell>@fat</CTableDataCell>
    </CTableRow>
    <CTableRow>
      <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">3</CTableHeaderCell>
      <CTableDataCell colspan="2">Larry the Bird</CTableDataCell>
      <CTableDataCell>@twitter</CTableDataCell>
    </CTableRow>
  </CTableBody>
</CTable>
```

## Variants

Use contextual classes to color tables, table rows or individual cells.

```html
<template>
  <CTable :columns="columnsVariantExample" :items="itemsVariantExample" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTable } from '@coreui/vue'
const columnsVariantExample = [
  { key: 'class', _props: { scope: 'col' } },
  { key: 'heading_1', label: 'Heading', _props: { scope: 'col' } },
  { key: 'heading_2', label: 'Heading', _props: { scope: 'col' } },
]
const itemsVariantExample = [
  {
    class: 'Default',
    heading_1: 'Cell',
    heading_2: 'Cell',
    _cellProps: { class: { scope: 'row' } },
  },
  {
    class: 'Primary',
    heading_1: 'Cell',
    heading_2: 'Cell',
    _cellProps: { class: { scope: 'row' } },
    _props: { color: 'primary' },
  },
  {
    class: 'Secondary',
    heading_1: 'Cell',
    heading_2: 'Cell',
    _cellProps: { class: { scope: 'row' } },
    _props: { color: 'secondary' },
  },
  {
    class: 'Success',
    heading_1: 'Cell',
    heading_2: 'Cell',
    _cellProps: { class: { scope: 'row' } },
    _props: { color: 'success' },
  },
  {
    class: 'Danger',
    heading_1: 'Cell',
    heading_2: 'Cell',
    _cellProps: { class: { scope: 'row' } },
    _props: { color: 'danger' },
  },
  {
    class: 'Warning',
    heading_1: 'Cell',
    heading_2: 'Cell',
    _cellProps: { class: { scope: 'row' } },
    _props: { color: 'warning' },
  },
  {
    class: 'Info',
    heading_1: 'Cell',
    heading_2: 'Cell',
    _cellProps: { class: { scope: 'row' } },
    _props: { color: 'info' },
  },
  {
    class: 'Light',
    heading_1: 'Cell',
    heading_2: 'Cell',
    _cellProps: { class: { scope: 'row' } },
    _props: { color: 'light' },
  },
  {
    class: 'Dark',
    heading_1: 'Cell',
    heading_2: 'Cell',
    _cellProps: { class: { scope: 'row' } },
    _props: { color: 'dark' },
  },
]
</script>
```

Since version **4.5.0** also this way.

```vue
<template>
  <CTable :columns="columnsVariantExample" :items="itemsVariantExample" />
</template>
```

## Accented tables

### Striped rows

Use `striped` property to add zebra-striping to any table row within the `<CTableBody>`.

```html
<template>
  <CTable striped>
    <CTableHead>
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">#</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Class</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Heading</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Heading</CTableHeaderCell>
      </CTableRow>
    </CTableHead>
    <CTableBody>
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">1</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableDataCell>Mark</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>Otto</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>@mdo</CTableDataCell>
      </CTableRow>
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">2</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableDataCell>Jacob</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>Thornton</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>@fat</CTableDataCell>
      </CTableRow>
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">3</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableDataCell colspan="2">Larry the Bird</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>@twitter</CTableDataCell>
      </CTableRow>
    </CTableBody>
  </CTable>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CTable,
  CTableHead,
  CTableRow,
  CTableHeaderCell,
  CTableBody,
  CTableDataCell,

</script>
```

### Active tables

Highlight a table row or cell by adding a `active` property.

```html
<template>
  <CTable :columns="columnsActiveTableExample" :items="itemsActiveTableExample" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTable } from '@coreui/vue'
const columnsActiveTableExample = [
  {
    key: 'id',
    label: '#',
    _props: { scope: 'col' },
  },
  {
    key: 'class',
    _props: { scope: 'col' },
  },
  {
    key: 'heading_1',
    label: 'Heading',
    _props: { scope: 'col' },
  },
  {
    key: 'heading_2',
    label: 'Heading',
    _props: { scope: 'col' },
  },
]
const itemsActiveTableExample = [
  {
    id: 1,
    class: 'Mark',
    heading_1: 'Otto',
    heading_2: '@mdo',
    _props: { active: true },
    _cellProps: { id: { scope: 'row' } },
  },
  {
    id: 2,
    class: 'Jacob',
    heading_1: 'Thornton',
    heading_2: '@fat',
    _cellProps: { id: { scope: 'row' } },
  },
  {
    id: 3,
    class: 'Larry the Bird',
    heading_2: '@twitter',
    _cellProps: { id: { scope: 'row' }, class: { active: true, colSpan: 2 } },
  },
]
</script>
```
As mentioned before since version **4.5.0** we have two ways to generate tables, also with custom properties for rows, and cells.

## Card-like tables

Need a bordered, rounded table without nesting it in a [card](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/card/)? Wrap the table and clip the corners.

### With utilities

Compose [border](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/border/), [border radius](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/border-radius/), and [overflow](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/overflow/) utilities. Drop the table's bottom margin with `.mb-0`.

```html
<template>
  <div class="border rounded overflow-hidden">
    <CTable class="mb-0" striped :columns="columns" :items="items" />
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTable } from '@coreui/vue'
const columns = [
  {
    key: 'id',
    label: '#',
    _props: { scope: 'col' },
  },
  {
    key: 'class',
    _props: { scope: 'col' },
  },
  {
    key: 'heading_1',
    label: 'Heading',
    _props: { scope: 'col' },
  },
  {
    key: 'heading_2',
    label: 'Heading',
    _props: { scope: 'col' },
  },
]
const items = [
  {
    id: 1,
    class: 'Mark',
    heading_1: 'Otto',
    heading_2: '@mdo',
    _cellProps: { id: { scope: 'row' } },
  },
  {
    id: 2,
    class: 'Jacob',
    heading_1: 'Thornton',
    heading_2: '@fat',
    _cellProps: { id: { scope: 'row' } },
  },
  {
    id: 3,
    class: 'Larry the Bird',
    heading_2: '@twitter',
    _cellProps: { id: { scope: 'row' }, class: { colSpan: 2 } },
  },
]
</script>
```

### With `card`

Add the `card` property for the card look in one step. The table gets the default border and corner radius of a [card](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/card/), and a `.theme-*` class on an ancestor colours the frame the way it colours a card. The cells are clipped, and the borders that would stack on the frame go: the last row's bottom border and the outer borders of a `bordered` table. A caption at the bottom keeps the line above it.

```html
<template>
  <CTable card hover :columns="columns" :items="items" />
</template>

<script setup>
import { CTable } from '@coreui/vue'
const columns = [
  {
    key: 'id',
    label: '#',
    _props: { scope: 'col' },
  },
  {
    key: 'class',
    _props: { scope: 'col' },
  },
  {
    key: 'heading_1',
    label: 'Heading',
    _props: { scope: 'col' },
  },
  {
    key: 'heading_2',
    label: 'Heading',
    _props: { scope: 'col' },
  },
]
const items = [
  {
    id: 1,
    class: 'Mark',
    heading_1: 'Otto',
    heading_2: '@mdo',
    _cellProps: { id: { scope: 'row' } },
  },
  {
    id: 2,
    class: 'Jacob',
    heading_1: 'Thornton',
    heading_2: '@fat',
    _cellProps: { id: { scope: 'row' } },
  },
  {
    id: 3,
    class: 'Larry the Bird',
    heading_2: '@twitter',
    _cellProps: { id: { scope: 'row' }, class: { colSpan: 2 } },
  },
]
</script>
```

Combine it with `responsive` when the table can overflow; both land on the same wrapper.

```html

  <CTable card responsive striped :columns="columns" :items="items" />
</template>
```

> ##### Clipping
> 
> `card` clips everything at the rounded edge: a dropdown menu opened from a cell, the focus ring of a control in an edge cell, and columns wider than the frame. Render menus outside the table with the dropdown's [`teleport`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/dropdown/api/#cdropdown) property, and add `responsive` when the table can be wider than its container.

## Table group dividers

Add a thicker, darker border between table groups—`<CTableHead>`, `<CTableBody>`, and `<CTableFoot>`—with `.table-group-divider`. Customize the color by changing the `border-top-color` (which we don't currently provide a utility class for at this time).

```html
<template>
  <CTable>
    <CTableHead>
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">#</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">First</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Last</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Handle</CTableHeaderCell>
      </CTableRow>
    </CTableHead>
    <CTableBody class="table-group-divider">
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">1</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableDataCell>Mark</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>Otto</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>@mdo</CTableDataCell>
      </CTableRow>
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">2</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableDataCell>Jacob</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>Thornton</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>@fat</CTableDataCell>
      </CTableRow>
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">3</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableDataCell :colspan="2">Larry the Bird</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>@twitter</CTableDataCell>
      </CTableRow>
    </CTableBody>
  </CTable>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CTable,
  CTableBody,
  CTableDataCell,
  CTableHead,
  CTableHeaderCell,
  CTableRow,
} from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Vertical alignment

Table cells of `<CTableHead>` are always vertical aligned to the bottom. Table cells in `<CTableBody>` inherit their alignment from `<CTable>` and are aligned to the the top by default. Use the align property to re-align where needed.

```html
<template>
  <CTable align="middle" reponsive>
    <CTableHead>
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col" class="w-25">Heading 1</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col" class="w-25">Heading 2</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col" class="w-25">Heading 3</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col" class="w-25">Heading 4</CTableHeaderCell>
      </CTableRow>
    </CTableHead>
    <CTableBody>
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableDataCell
          >This cell inherits <code>vertical-align: middle;</code> from the table</CTableDataCell
        >
        <CTableDataCell
```

## Nesting

Border styles, active styles, and table variants are not inherited by nested tables.

```html
<template>
  <CTable striped>
    <CTableHead>
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">#</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Class</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Heading</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Heading</CTableHeaderCell>
      </CTableRow>
    </CTableHead>
    <CTableBody>
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">1</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableDataCell>Mark</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>Otto</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>@mdo</CTableDataCell>
      </CTableRow>
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell colspan="4">
          <CTable>
            <CTableHead>
              <CTableRow>
                <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Header</CTableHeaderCell>
                <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Header</CTableHeaderCell>
                <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Header</CTableHeaderCell>
              </CTableRow>
            </CTableHead>
            <CTableBody>
              <CTableRow>
                <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">A</CTableHeaderCell>
                <CTableDataCell>First</CTableDataCell>
                <CTableDataCell>Last</CTableDataCell>
              </CTableRow>
              <CTableRow>
                <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">B</CTableHeaderCell>
                <CTableDataCell>First</CTableDataCell>
                <CTableDataCell>Last</CTableDataCell>
              </CTableRow>
              <CTableRow>
                <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">C</CTableHeaderCell>
                <CTableDataCell>First</CTableDataCell>
                <CTableDataCell>Last</CTableDataCell>
              </CTableRow>
            </CTableBody>
          </CTable>
        </CTableHeaderCell>
      </CTableRow>
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">3</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableDataCell colspan="2">Larry the Bird</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>@twitter</CTableDataCell>
      </CTableRow>
    </CTableBody>
  </CTable>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CTable,
  CTableHead,
  CTableRow,
  CTableHeaderCell,
  CTableBody,
  CTableDataCell,
} from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

## Anatomy

### Table head

Similar to tables and dark tables, use the modifier prop `color="secondary"` or `color="inverse"` to make `<CTableHead>`s appear light or dark gray.

```html
<template>
  <CTable>
    <CTableHead theme="secondary">
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">#</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Class</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Heading</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Heading</CTableHeaderCell>
      </CTableRow>
    </CTableHead>
    <CTableBody>
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">1</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableDataCell>Mark</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>Otto</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>@mdo</CTableDataCell>
      </CTableRow>
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">2</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableDataCell>Jacob</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>Thornton</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>@fat</CTableDataCell>
      </CTableRow>
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">3</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableDataCell>Larry</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>the Bird</CTableDataCell>
        <CTableDataCell>@twitter</CTableDataCell>
      </CTableRow>
    </CTableBody>
  </CTable>
</template>

<script setup>
import {
  CTable,
  CTableHead,
  CTableRow,
  CTableHeaderCell,
  CTableBody,
  CTableDataCell,
} from '@coreui/vue'
</script>
```

If you generate a table using the new method incorporated in version **4.5.0**, you have to use tableHeadProps property to pass properties to the table header component.

```vue
<template>
  <CTable :columns="columns" :items="items" :tableHeadProps="{ color: 'light' }" />
</template>
```

```html
<template>
  <CTable>
    <CTableHead theme="inverse">
      <CTableRow>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">#</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Class</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Heading</CTableHeaderCell>
        <CTableHeaderCell scope="col">Heading</CTableHeaderCell>

    </CTableHead>

        <CTableHeaderCell scope="row">1</CTableHeaderCell>
```
