# Vue Utilities API

> The utility API is a Sass-based tool to generate utility classes.

CoreUI for Vue utilities are generated with our utility API and can be used to modify or extend our default set of utility classes via Sass. Our utility API is based on a series of Sass maps and functions for generating families of classes with various options. If you're unfamiliar with Sass maps, read up on the [official Sass docs](https://sass-lang.com/documentation/values/maps/) to get started.

The `$utilities` map contains all our utilities and is later merged with your custom `$utilities` map, if present. The utility map contains a keyed list of utility groups which accept the following options:

| Option | Type | Default&nbsp;value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`property`](#property) | **Required** | – | Name of the property, a space-separated list of them, or a [map](#property-map) spelling out every declaration the rule writes. |
| [`values`](#values) | **Required** | – | List of values, or a map if you don't want the class name to be the same as the value. If `null` is used as map key, `class` is not prepended to the class name. |
| [`class`](#class) | Optional | null | Name of the generated class. If not provided and `property` is an array of strings, `class` will default to the first element of the `property` array. If not provided and `property` is a string, the `values` keys are used for the `class` names. |
| [`child-selector`](#child-selector) | Optional | null | Selector for the children to style instead of the element itself, wrapped in `:where()`. |
| [`selector`](#selector-type) | Optional | `class` | `class`, `attr-starts` or `attr-includes` — whether the rule is written as a class or as an attribute selector. |
| [`state`](#states) | Optional | null | List of pseudo-class variants (e.g., `:hover` or `:focus`) to generate. |
| [`responsive`](#responsive) | Optional | `false` | Boolean indicating if responsive classes should be generated. |
| [`print`](#print) | Optional | `false` | Boolean indicating if print classes need to be generated. |
| `at-property` | Optional | `true` | Set to `false` to keep the utility's custom properties inheriting (see [property map](#property-map)). |
| [`enabled`](#remove-utilities) | Optional | `true` | Set to `false` to skip the utility without removing its definition. |

Every key is checked while the utility is generated: `property` and `values` are required, a boolean option given a non-boolean errors, and a key outside this table is reported as a warning rather than ignored — a misspelled `responsiv` used to cost you the responsive classes with nothing said about it.

## API explained

All utility variables are added to the `$utilities` variable within our `_utilities.scss` stylesheet. Each group of utilities looks something like this:

```scss
$utilities: (
  "opacity": (
    property: opacity,
    values: (
      0: 0,
      25: .25,
      50: .5,
      75: .75,
      100: 1,
    )
  )
);
```

Which outputs the following:

```css
.opacity-0 { opacity: 0; }
.opacity-25 { opacity: .25; }
.opacity-50 { opacity: .5; }
.opacity-75 { opacity: .75; }
.opacity-100 { opacity: 1; }
```

### Property

The required `property` key must be set for any utility, and it must contain a valid CSS property. This property is used in the generated utility's ruleset. When the `class` key is omitted, it also serves as the default class name. Consider the `text-decoration` utility:

```scss
$utilities: (
  "text-decoration": (
    property: text-decoration,
    values: none underline line-through
  )
);
```

Output:

```css
.text-decoration-none { text-decoration: none; }
.text-decoration-underline { text-decoration: underline; }
.text-decoration-line-through { text-decoration: line-through; }
```

### Values

Use the `values` key to specify which values for the specified `property` should be used in the generated class names and rules. Can be a list or map (set in the utilities or in a Sass variable).

As a list, like with [`text-decoration` utilities](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/text-decoration/):

```scss
values: none underline line-through
```

As a map, like with [`opacity` utilities](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/opacity/):

```scss
values: (
  0: 0,
  25: .25,
  50: .5,
  75: .75,
  100: 1,
)
```

As a Sass variable that sets the list or map, as in our [`position` utilities](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/position/):

```scss
values: $position-values
```

### Class

Use the `class` option to change the class prefix used in the compiled CSS. For example, to change from `.opacity-*` to `.o-*`:

```scss
$utilities: (
  "opacity": (
    property: opacity,
    class: o,
    values: (
      0: 0,
      25: .25,
      50: .5,
      75: .75,
      100: 1,
    )
  )
);
```

Output:

```css
.o-0 { opacity: 0; }
.o-25 { opacity: .25; }
.o-50 { opacity: .5; }
.o-75 { opacity: .75; }
.o-100 { opacity: 1; }
```

If `class: null`, generates classes for each of the `values` keys:

```scss
$utilities: (
  "visibility": (
    property: visibility,
    class: null,
    values: (
      visible: visible,
      invisible: hidden,
    )
  )
);
```

Output:

```css
.visible { visibility: visible; }
.invisible { visibility: hidden; }
```

### Child selector

Some utilities describe the relationship between an element's children rather
than the element itself — spacing *between* items, or a divider *between* them.
Give such a utility a `child-selector`, and the generated rule targets the
children:

```scss
$utilities: (
  "space-x": (
    property: margin-inline-end,
    class: space-x,
    child-selector: "> :not(:last-child)",
    values: $spacers
  )
);
```

Output:

```css
:where(.space-x-5 > :not(:last-child)) { margin-inline-end: 1rem; }
```

The rule is wrapped in `:where()`, which contributes **no specificity**. That is
deliberate: a child that carries a margin utility of its own, or a component
with its own spacing, keeps winning without needing `!important` or a longer
selector.

### Selector type

By default a utility writes a class selector. Set `selector` to `attr-starts` or
`attr-includes` and it writes an attribute selector instead, so a single rule
serves a whole family of classes — useful when the class only has to set a
custom property that one shared rule then reads:

```scss
$utilities: (
  "aspect-ratio": (
    property: --#{$prefix}ratio,
    class: ratio,
    values: (1x1: 1, 16x9: calc(16 / 9))
  ),
  "aspect-ratio-attr": (
    property: aspect-ratio,
    class: "ratio-",
    selector: "attr-includes",
    values: var(--#{$prefix}ratio)
  )
);
```

Output:

```css
.ratio-1x1 { --cui-ratio: 1; }
.ratio-16x9 { --cui-ratio: calc(16 / 9); }
[class*="ratio-"] { aspect-ratio: var(--cui-ratio); }
```

`attr-starts` matches `[class^="…"]` (the class begins with the name),
`attr-includes` matches `[class*="…"]` (it appears anywhere in the attribute, so
it also works when the utility is not the first class). Both require a `class`
key — that is the string they match on.

### Property map

`property` is usually one property name, or a space-separated list of them. It
can also be a **map**, which spells out exactly what the rule writes and in what
order. An entry whose value is `null` receives the utility's value; every other
entry is written as declared:

```scss
$utilities: (
  "bg-color": (
    property: (
      --#{$prefix}bg: null,
      background-color: var(--#{$prefix}bg),
    ),
    class: bg,
    values: $utilities-bg-colors
  )
);
```

Output:

```css
.bg-primary {
  --cui-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg);
  background-color: var(--cui-bg);
}
```

This is what lets a utility **store its value in a custom property and consume
it in the same rule**. The colour lives in `--cui-bg`, so anything that reads
the token sees the colour the class chose. A companion utility then reads it
back through an expression of its own:

```scss
$utilities: (
  "bg-opacity": (
    class: bg,
    property: background-color,
    values: theme-opacity-values(--#{$prefix}bg)
  )
);
```

```css
.bg-50 { background-color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-bg) 50%, transparent); }
```

The two rules write the same property, so the order of the map decides: the
opacity family is declared after the colour family, and `.bg-primary.bg-50`
mixes the primary colour whichever order the classes appear in the attribute.
On its own, `.bg-50` reads a token nobody set, so the declaration is invalid at
computed-value time and the background stays as it was.

> Every custom property a utility assigns to is registered with
> `@property { inherits: false }`, so the value applies to the element that
> carries the class and does not leak into its descendants. A utility that
> deliberately writes an inheriting token — `.focus-ring-*` sets the global
> `--cui-focus-ring-color` — opts out with `at-property: false`.

### States

Use the `state` option to generate pseudo-class variations. Example pseudo-classes are `:hover` and `:focus`. When a list of states are provided, classnames are created for that pseudo-class. For example, to change opacity on hover, add `state: hover` and you'll get `.opacity-hover:hover` in your compiled CSS.

Need multiple pseudo-classes? Use a space-separated list of states: `state: hover focus`.

```scss
$utilities: (
  "opacity": (
    property: opacity,
    class: opacity,
    state: hover,
    values: (
      0: 0,
      25: .25,
      50: .5,
      75: .75,
      100: 1,
    )
  )
);
```

Output:

```css
.opacity-0-hover:hover { opacity: 0; }
.opacity-25-hover:hover { opacity: .25; }
.opacity-50-hover:hover { opacity: .5; }
.opacity-75-hover:hover { opacity: .75; }
.opacity-100-hover:hover { opacity: 1; }
```

### Responsive

Add the `responsive` boolean to generate responsive utilities (e.g., `.opacity-md-25`) across [all breakpoints](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/layout/breakpoints/).

```scss
$utilities: (
  "opacity": (
    property: opacity,
    responsive: true,
    values: (
      0: 0,
      25: .25,
      50: .5,
      75: .75,
      100: 1,
    )
  )
);
```

Output:

```css
.opacity-0 { opacity: 0; }
.opacity-25 { opacity: .25; }
.opacity-50 { opacity: .5; }
.opacity-75 { opacity: .75; }
.opacity-100 { opacity: 1; }

@media (min-width: 576px) {
  .opacity-sm-0 { opacity: 0; }
  .opacity-sm-25 { opacity: .25; }
  .opacity-sm-50 { opacity: .5; }
  .opacity-sm-75 { opacity: .75; }
  .opacity-sm-100 { opacity: 1; }
}

@media (min-width: 768px) {
  .opacity-md-0 { opacity: 0; }
  .opacity-md-25 { opacity: .25; }
  .opacity-md-50 { opacity: .5; }
  .opacity-md-75 { opacity: .75; }
  .opacity-md-100 { opacity: 1; }
}

@media (min-width: 1024px) {
  .opacity-lg-0 { opacity: 0; }
  .opacity-lg-25 { opacity: .25; }
  .opacity-lg-50 { opacity: .5; }
  .opacity-lg-75 { opacity: .75; }
  .opacity-lg-100 { opacity: 1; }
}

@media (min-width: 1280px) {
  .opacity-xl-0 { opacity: 0; }
  .opacity-xl-25 { opacity: .25; }
  .opacity-xl-50 { opacity: .5; }
  .opacity-xl-75 { opacity: .75; }
  .opacity-xl-100 { opacity: 1; }
}

@media (min-width: 1536px) {
  .opacity-2xl-0 { opacity: 0; }
  .opacity-2xl-25 { opacity: .25; }
  .opacity-2xl-50 { opacity: .5; }
  .opacity-2xl-75 { opacity: .75; }
  .opacity-2xl-100 { opacity: 1; }
}
```

### Print

Enabling the `print` option will **also** generate utility classes for print, which are only applied within the `@media print { ... }` media query.

```scss
$utilities: (
  "opacity": (
    property: opacity,
    print: true,
    values: (
      0: 0,
      25: .25,
      50: .5,
      75: .75,
      100: 1,
    )
  )
);
```

Output:

```css
.opacity-0 { opacity: 0; }
.opacity-25 { opacity: .25; }
.opacity-50 { opacity: .5; }
.opacity-75 { opacity: .75; }
.opacity-100 { opacity: 1; }

@media print {
  .opacity-print-0 { opacity: 0; }
  .opacity-print-25 { opacity: .25; }
  .opacity-print-50 { opacity: .5; }
  .opacity-print-75 { opacity: .75; }
  .opacity-print-100 { opacity: 1; }
}
```

## Importance

Utilities carry no `!important`. They do not need it: the API emits them into the
`utilities` cascade layer, which is declared last, so every utility already wins
against every component and modifier class regardless of selector specificity.
See [cascade layers](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/migration/v6/#cascade-layers) for the full order.

One case the suffix did cover is CSS of your own written **outside** any layer:
unlayered styles beat every layer, so a plain `.card-title { text-align: left }`
loaded after CoreUI wins over `.text-center`. Move that CSS into `@layer custom`
— the slot reserved for it, between components and helpers — and utilities win
again. There is no switch that brings the suffix back: the layer is the mechanism.
## Using the API

Now that you're familiar with how the utilities API works, learn how to add your own custom classes and modify our default utilities.

`$utilities` is a configurable variable of the `scss/utilities` module, so you change it with `@use ... with ()` rather than by reassigning it after an import. Two patterns cover every case:

- **One file** — configure `$utilities` where you load `@coreui/coreui/scss/coreui`. Use this to add a utility, replace one, or remove one.
- **Two files** — put the change in a partial that loads `@coreui/coreui/scss/utilities`, then load that partial before CoreUI. Use this when your change has to *read* the default definition: a new value on an existing group, a renamed class, or responsive variants on a group you keep.

Sass cannot read a module and configure the same module in one file, which is the whole reason the second pattern exists. In the partial, load the module with `as *` so `$utilities` needs no namespace prefix; assigning to it writes back into the module, and CoreUI picks the new map up when it loads.

```scss
// my-coreui.scss
@use "@coreui/coreui/scss/coreui" with (
  $utilities: (
    // Your utility groups go here
  )
);
```

Your map is merged over the defaults, and the merge is shallow: a group you supply replaces the whole default group under that key. Include `property` and `values` in every group that emits CSS.

For a utilities-only build, load the utilities module and then the API module, which emits the classes and nothing else:

```scss
// my-coreui-utilities.scss
@use "@coreui/coreui/scss/utilities" with (
  $utilities: (
    // Your utility groups go here
  )
);
@use "@coreui/coreui/scss/utilities/api";
```

### Override utilities

Override an existing utility by reusing its key. For example, to make the overflow utilities responsive and change their values:

```scss
// my-coreui.scss
@use "@coreui/coreui/scss/coreui" with (
  $utilities: (
    "overflow": (
      property: overflow,
      responsive: true,
      values: visible hidden scroll auto,
    ),
  )
);
```

Your group replaces the default one, so keep the `property` key or the build stops with an error.

### Add utilities

Add a new utility the same way — supply only what is new:

```scss
// my-coreui.scss
@use "@coreui/coreui/scss/coreui" with (
  $utilities: (
    "cursor": (
      property: cursor,
      class: cursor,
      responsive: true,
      values: auto pointer grab,
    ),
  )
);
```

### Modify utilities

Modifying a utility means reading its default definition first, so this needs the two-file pattern. Below we add another value to the `width` utilities:

```scss
// _my-utilities.scss
@use "sass:map";
// `as *` so `$utilities` needs no prefix, and assigning to it writes back
@use "@coreui/coreui/scss/utilities" as *;

$utilities: map.merge(
  $utilities,
  (
    "width": map.merge(
      map.get($utilities, "width"),
      (
        values: map.merge(
          map.get(map.get($utilities, "width"), "values"),
          (10: 10%),
        ),
      ),
    ),
  )
);
```

Load your partial first, then CoreUI:

```scss
// my-coreui.scss
@use "my-utilities";
@use "@coreui/coreui/scss/coreui";
```

#### Enable responsive

You can turn on responsive classes for a group that isn't responsive by default. This keeps the rest of the definition, so it takes the two-file pattern:

```scss
// _my-utilities.scss
@use "sass:map";
@use "@coreui/coreui/scss/utilities" as *;

$utilities: map.merge(
  $utilities,
  (
    "border": map.merge(
      map.get($utilities, "border"),
      (responsive: true),
    ),
  )
);
```

This will now generate responsive variations of `.border` and `.border-0` for each breakpoint. Your generated CSS will look like this:

```css
.border { ... }
.border-0 { ... }

@media (min-width: 576px) {
  .border-sm { ... }
  .border-sm-0 { ... }
}

@media (min-width: 768px) {
  .border-md { ... }
  .border-md-0 { ... }
}

@media (min-width: 1024px) {
  .border-lg { ... }
  .border-lg-0 { ... }
}

@media (min-width: 1280px) {
  .border-xl { ... }
  .border-xl-0 { ... }
}

@media (min-width: 1536px) {
  .border-2xl { ... }
  .border-2xl-0 { ... }
}
```

#### Rename utilities

Missing v4 utilities, or used to another naming convention? The utilities API can override the resulting `class` of a given utility — for example, to rename `.ms-*` back to `.ml-*`. It reads the default definition, so it takes the two-file pattern:

```scss
// _my-utilities.scss
@use "sass:map";
@use "@coreui/coreui/scss/utilities" as *;

$utilities: map.merge(
  $utilities,
  (
    "margin-start": map.merge(
      map.get($utilities, "margin-start"),
      (class: ml),
    ),
  )
);
```

### Remove utilities

Set a group to `null` to drop it:

```scss
// my-coreui.scss
@use "@coreui/coreui/scss/coreui" with (
  $utilities: (
    "width": null,
  )
);
```

To switch one off while keeping its definition around — so you can read it, or turn it back on later — set `enabled: false` instead. That reads the default definition, so it takes the two-file pattern:

```scss
// _my-utilities.scss
@use "sass:map";
@use "@coreui/coreui/scss/utilities" as *;

$utilities: map.merge(
  $utilities,
  (
    "width": map.merge(map.get($utilities, "width"), (enabled: false)),
  )
);
```

### Add, remove, modify

Anything that only adds or removes goes in one file:

```scss
// my-coreui.scss
@use "@coreui/coreui/scss/coreui" with (
  $utilities: (
    // Remove the `width` utility
    "width": null,

    // Add a new one
    "cursor": (
      property: cursor,
      class: cursor,
      responsive: true,
      values: auto pointer grab,
    ),
  )
);
```

As soon as one change has to read a default — making `border` responsive, say — the whole set moves into the partial:

```scss
// _my-utilities.scss
@use "sass:map";
@use "@coreui/coreui/scss/utilities" as *;

$utilities: map.merge(
  $utilities,
  (
    // Remove the `width` utility
    "width": null,

    // Make an existing utility responsive
    "border": map.merge(
      map.get($utilities, "border"),
      (responsive: true),
    ),

    // Add new utilities
    "cursor": (
      property: cursor,
      class: cursor,
      responsive: true,
      values: auto pointer grab,
    ),
  )
);
```

# Vue Aspect ratio Utilities

> Make an element hold an aspect ratio of your choosing. Perfect for responsively handling video or slideshow embeds based on the width of the parent.

## Example

Add an aspect ratio class to the element you want to size — an `<iframe>`, a `<video>`, an `<img>`, or a plain `<div>`. The class sets the CSS `aspect-ratio` property, so the element sizes itself; there is no wrapper to add and no child to position.

```html
<iframe class="w-100 ratio-16x9" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/zpOULjyy-n8?rel=0" title="YouTube video" allowfullscreen></iframe>
```

> **Pro-Tip!** You don't need `frameborder="0"` on your ``s as we override that for you in [Reboot](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/content/reboot/).

## Aspect ratios

Swap the class for a different ratio. These come from the `$aspect-ratios` map:

```html
<div class="ratio-1x1">1x1</div>
<div class="ratio-4x3">4x3</div>
<div class="ratio-16x9">16x9</div>
<div class="ratio-21x9">21x9</div>
```

They pair with the [width utilities](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/width/) — the ratio decides the height once the width is known.

## Custom ratios

The class sets `--cui-ratio` and a separate rule reads it, so a ratio the map does not name is an inline override away. Use `.ratio-auto` to opt in to the reading rule without picking a named ratio:

```html
<div class="w-25 ratio-auto" style="--cui-ratio: 2 / 1">
  2x1
</div>
```

Because it is a custom property, it can also change across breakpoints:

```scss
.ratio-4x3 {
  @include media-breakpoint-up(md) {
    --cui-ratio: 2 / 1;
  }
}
```

```html
<div class="ratio-4x3">4x3, then 2x1</div>
```

## Customizing

### Sass variables

Change the ratios you want to generate in the `$aspect-ratios` map.

```scss
$aspect-ratios: () !default;
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$aspect-ratios: defaults(
  (
    "auto":  auto,
    "1x1":   #{"1 / 1"},
    "4x3":   #{"4 / 3"},
    "16x9":  #{"16 / 9"},
    "21x9":  #{"21 / 9"}
  ),
  $aspect-ratios
);
```

Aspect ratio utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
// Two halves: `.ratio-*` sets the token, and any element carrying such a class reads
// it. Splitting them is what lets `--cui-ratio` be overridden inline for a
// ratio the map does not name.
"aspect-ratio-attr": (
  selector: "attr-includes",
  class: "ratio-",
  property: aspect-ratio,
  values: var(--cui-ratio)
),
"aspect-ratio": (
  property: --cui-ratio,
  class: ratio,
  values: $aspect-ratios
),
```

# Vue Align content Utilities

> Distribute the space between and around rows of a wrapped flex container.

## Align content

Use `align-content` utilities on flexbox containers to align flex items *together* on the cross axis. Choose from `start` (browser default), `end`, `center`, `between`, `around`, or `stretch`. To demonstrate these utilities, we've enforced `flex-wrap: wrap` and increased the number of flex items.

**Heads up!** This property has no effect on single rows of flex items.

```vue
<div class="d-flex align-content-start flex-wrap">
  ...
</div>
```

```vue
<div class="d-flex align-content-end flex-wrap">...</div>
```

```vue
<div class="d-flex align-content-center flex-wrap">...</div>
```

```vue
<div class="d-flex align-content-between flex-wrap">...</div>
```

```vue
<div class="d-flex align-content-around flex-wrap">...</div>
```

```vue
<div class="d-flex align-content-stretch flex-wrap">...</div>
```

Responsive variations also exist for `align-content`.

- `.align-content-start`
- `.align-content-end`
- `.align-content-center`
- `.align-content-around`

- `.align-content-sm-around`
- `.align-content-sm-stretch`
- `.align-content-md-start`
- `.align-content-md-end`
- `.align-content-md-center`
- `.align-content-md-around`
- `.align-content-md-stretch`
- `.align-content-lg-start`
- `.align-content-lg-end`
- `.align-content-lg-center`
- `.align-content-lg-around`
- `.align-content-lg-stretch`

# Vue Align self Utilities

> Override the container’s cross-axis alignment for a single item.

## Align self

Use `align-self` utilities on flexbox items to individually change their alignment on the cross axis (the y-axis to start, x-axis if `flex-direction: column`). Choose from the same options as `align-items`: `start`, `end`, `center`, `baseline`, or `stretch` (browser default).

```vue
<div class="align-self-start">Aligned flex item</div>

<div class="align-self-center">Aligned flex item</div>
<div class="align-self-baseline">Aligned flex item</div>
<div class="align-self-stretch">Aligned flex item</div>
```

- `.align-self-sm-baseline`
- `.align-self-sm-stretch`

- `.align-self-md-end`

- `.align-self-2xl-baseline`
- `.align-self-2xl-stretch`

# Vue Background Utilities

> Convey meaning through `background-color` and add decoration with gradients.

## Background color

Similar to the contextual text color classes, set the background of an element to any contextual class. Background utilities **do not set `color`**, so in some cases you'll want to use `.fg-*` [color utilities](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/colors/).

Each theme color comes in three weights: the solid color, `.bg-muted-*` and `.bg-subtle-*`. The two lighter ones are surfaces to read text on, and `.fg-emphasis-*` is the color that reads on them — `.bg-muted-*` is the step you want when a subtle surface has to separate from a subtle surface behind it, which is what a hovered row or a selected item needs.

```html
<div class="p-4 mb-3 text-bg-${c.name}">.bg-${c.name}</div>
<div class="p-4 mb-3 bg-muted-${c.name} fg-emphasis-${c.name}">.bg-muted-${c.name}</div>
<div class="p-4 mb-3 bg-subtle-${c.name} fg-emphasis-${c.name}">.bg-subtle-${c.name}</div>
<div class="p-4 mb-3 bg-body fg-body">.bg-body</div>
<div class="p-4 mb-3 bg-black fg-white">.bg-black</div>
<div class="p-4 mb-3 bg-white fg-black">.bg-white</div>
<div class="p-4 mb-3 bg-transparent fg-body">.bg-transparent</div>
```

## Surface ladder

Five neutral surfaces run from the page background to the deepest panel. The numbers say how far a surface sits from the body — `.bg-1` is barely off the page, `.bg-4` is the deepest — and the ladder keeps its order in both color schemes.

```html
<div class="p-4 mb-3 bg-body">.bg-body</div>
<div class="p-4 mb-3 bg-1">.bg-1</div>
<div class="p-4 mb-3 bg-2">.bg-2</div>
<div class="p-4 mb-3 bg-3">.bg-3</div>
<div class="p-4 mb-3 bg-4">.bg-4</div>
```

`.bg-body-secondary` and `.bg-body-tertiary` are deprecated names for `.bg-3` and `.bg-2` — they render identically and go away in v7. The ordinal names replace them because the old adjectives ran backwards for backgrounds: "tertiary" sat *closer* to the page than "secondary".

## Background gradient

By adding a `.bg-gradient` class, a linear gradient is added as background image to the backgrounds. This gradient starts with a semi-transparent white which fades out to the bottom.

Do you need a gradient in your custom CSS? Just add `background-image: var(gradient);`.

<div class="p-4 mb-3 text-bg-primary bg-gradient">.bg-primary.bg-gradient</div>
<div class="p-4 mb-3 text-bg-secondary bg-gradient">.bg-secondary.bg-gradient</div>
<div class="p-4 mb-3 text-bg-success bg-gradient">.bg-success.bg-gradient</div>
<div class="p-4 mb-3 text-bg-danger bg-gradient">.bg-danger.bg-gradient</div>
<div class="p-4 mb-3 text-bg-warning bg-gradient">.bg-warning.bg-gradient</div>
<div class="p-4 mb-3 text-bg-info bg-gradient">.bg-info.bg-gradient</div>
<div class="p-4 mb-3 bg-black bg-gradient fg-white">.bg-black.bg-gradient</div>

## Opacity

Every `.bg-*` utility writes its colour into `--cui-bg` and reads it back, so a companion `.bg-{percentage}` class can mix that colour with `transparent` through `color-mix()`, in the browser, without recompiling Sass.

```css
.bg-success {
  --cui-bg: var(--cui-success-bg);
  background-color: var(--cui-bg);
}

.bg-50 {
  background-color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-bg) 50%, transparent);
}
```

Override `--cui-bg` to repaint the utility with another colour; the opacity class keeps working, because it reads whatever the token holds.

```html
<div class="text-bg-success p-3">This is default success background</div>
<div class="bg-success p-3 bg-90">This is 90% opacity success background</div>
<div class="bg-success p-3 bg-70">This is 70% opacity success background</div>
<div class="bg-success p-3 bg-50">This is 50% opacity success background</div>
<div class="bg-success p-3 bg-30">This is 30% opacity success background</div>
<div class="bg-success p-3 bg-10">This is 10% opacity success background</div>
```

`.bg-opacity-{10|15|25|50|75|100}` and `.bg-{color}-subtle` / `.bg-{color}-muted` are the deprecated v5 spellings of `.bg-{percentage}`, `.bg-subtle-{color}` and `.bg-muted-{color}`; they still render and are removed in v7.

## Customizing

In addition to the following Sass functionality, consider reading about our included [CSS custom properties](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/customize/css-variables/) (aka CSS variables) for colors and more.

### Sass variables

Most `background-color` utilities are generated by our theme colors, reassigned from our generic color palette variables.

```scss
$primary: oklch(52.945% 0.19103 278.34) !default;
$success: oklch(55.1% 0.173 145) !default;
$info:    oklch(57.4% 0.196 256) !default;
$warning: oklch(84% 0.172 85) !default;
$danger:  oklch(58.7% 0.237 23.81) !default;
$gray:    oklch(60% 0.03948 265.02) !default;
```

### Sass maps

The surface ladder is one map: each key is one `.bg-{key}` utility and the `--cui-bg-{key}` token behind it, in light and dark mode. Add a key to add a rung, override one to retune it:

```scss
$theme-bgs: () !default;
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$theme-bgs: defaults(
  (
    "body":        light-dark(var(--cui-white), var(--cui-gray-975)),
    "1":           light-dark(var(--cui-gray-025), var(--cui-gray-950)),
    "2":           light-dark(var(--cui-gray-050), var(--cui-gray-900)),
    "3":           light-dark(var(--cui-gray-100), var(--cui-gray-800)),
    "4":           light-dark(var(--cui-gray-200), var(--cui-gray-700)),
    "fg":          var(--cui-fg-body),
    "white":       var(--cui-white),
    "black":       var(--cui-black),
    "transparent": transparent,
    "inherit":     inherit,
  ),
  $theme-bgs
);
```

`.bg-{color}-subtle` and `.bg-{color}-muted` read the `bg-subtle` and `bg-muted` slot of every entry through `theme-color-refs()`, in light and dark mode.

Theme colors are then put into a Sass map so we can loop over them to generate our utilities, component modifiers, and more.

```scss
$theme-colors: () !default;
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$theme-colors: defaults(
  (
    "primary": (
      "base":          var(--cui-primary-500),
      "fg":            light-dark(var(--cui-primary-600), var(--cui-primary-400)),
      "fg-emphasis":   light-dark(var(--cui-primary-800), var(--cui-primary-200)),
      "bg":            var(--cui-primary-500),
      "bg-subtle":     light-dark(var(--cui-primary-100), var(--cui-primary-900)),
      "bg-muted":      light-dark(var(--cui-primary-200), var(--cui-primary-800)),
      "border":        light-dark(var(--cui-primary-300), var(--cui-primary-600)),
      "focus-ring":    color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-primary-base) calc(var(--cui-focus-ring-opacity) * 100%), transparent),
      "contrast":      var(--cui-white),
    ),
    "secondary": (
      "base":          var(--cui-gray-200),
      "fg":            light-dark(var(--cui-gray-600), var(--cui-gray-400)),
      "fg-emphasis":   light-dark(var(--cui-gray-800), var(--cui-gray-200)),
      "bg":            light-dark(var(--cui-gray-100), var(--cui-gray-600)),
      "bg-subtle":     light-dark(var(--cui-gray-025), var(--cui-gray-800)),
      "bg-muted":      light-dark(var(--cui-gray-050), var(--cui-gray-700)),
      "border":        light-dark(var(--cui-gray-300), var(--cui-gray-600)),
      "focus-ring":    color-mix(in oklch, light-dark(var(--cui-gray-500), var(--cui-gray-300)) calc(var(--cui-focus-ring-opacity) * 100%), transparent),
      "contrast":      light-dark(var(--cui-gray-900), var(--cui-white)),
    ),
    "success": (
      "base":          var(--cui-success-500),
      "fg":            light-dark(var(--cui-success-600), var(--cui-success-400)),
      "fg-emphasis":   light-dark(var(--cui-success-800), var(--cui-success-200)),
      "bg":            var(--cui-success-500),
      "bg-subtle":     light-dark(var(--cui-success-100), var(--cui-success-900)),
      "bg-muted":      light-dark(var(--cui-success-200), var(--cui-success-800)),
      "border":        light-dark(var(--cui-success-300), var(--cui-success-600)),
      "focus-ring":    color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-success-base) calc(var(--cui-focus-ring-opacity) * 100%), transparent),
      "contrast":      var(--cui-white),
    ),
    "info": (
      "base":          var(--cui-info-500),
      "fg":            light-dark(var(--cui-info-700), var(--cui-info-300)),
      "fg-emphasis":   light-dark(var(--cui-info-800), var(--cui-info-200)),
      "bg":            var(--cui-info-500),
      "bg-subtle":     light-dark(var(--cui-info-100), var(--cui-info-900)),
      "bg-muted":      light-dark(var(--cui-info-200), var(--cui-info-800)),
      "border":        light-dark(var(--cui-info-300), var(--cui-info-600)),
      "focus-ring":    color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-info-base) calc(var(--cui-focus-ring-opacity) * 100%), transparent),
      "contrast":      var(--cui-white),
    ),
    "warning": (
      "base":          var(--cui-warning-500),
      "fg":            light-dark(var(--cui-warning-700), var(--cui-warning-300)),
      "fg-emphasis":   light-dark(var(--cui-warning-800), var(--cui-warning-200)),
      "bg":            var(--cui-warning-500),
      "bg-subtle":     light-dark(var(--cui-warning-100), var(--cui-warning-900)),
      "bg-muted":      light-dark(var(--cui-warning-200), var(--cui-warning-800)),
```

Grayscale colors are also available as a Sass map. **This map is not used to generate any utilities.**

```scss
$grays: () !default;

// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$grays: defaults(
  (
    "025": gray("025"),
    "050": gray("050"),
    "100": gray("100"),
    "200": gray("200"),
    "300": gray("300"),
    "400": gray("400"),
    "500": gray("500"),
    "600": gray("600"),
    "700": gray("700"),
    "800": gray("800"),
    "900": gray("900"),
    "950": gray("950"),
    "975": gray("975")
  ),
  $grays
);
```

Background color opacities are applied through a map consumed by the utilities API, which mixes each color with `transparent` at the requested amount:

```scss
$utilities-bg-colors: map.merge(
  theme-color-refs("bg"),
  (
    "black": var(--cui-black),
    "white": var(--cui-white),
    "body": var(--cui-bg-body)
  )
) !default;

$utilities-bg-subtle: theme-color-refs("bg-subtle", "-subtle") !default;
$utilities-bg-muted: theme-color-refs("bg-muted", "-muted") !default;
```

### Sass mixins

**No mixins are used to generate our background utilities**, but we do have some additional mixins for other situations where you'd like to create your own gradients.

```scss
@mixin gradient-bg($color: null) {
  background-color: $color;

  @if $enable-gradients {
    background-image: var(--cui-gradient);
  }
}
```

```scss
// Horizontal gradient, from left to right
//
// Creates two color stops, start and end, by specifying a color and position for each color stop.
@mixin gradient-x($start-color: var(--cui-gray-700), $end-color: var(--cui-gray-800), $start-percent: 0%, $end-percent: 100%) {
  background-image: linear-gradient(to right, $start-color $start-percent, $end-color $end-percent);
}

// Vertical gradient, from top to bottom
//
// Creates two color stops, start and end, by specifying a color and position for each color stop.
@mixin gradient-y($start-color: var(--cui-gray-700), $end-color: var(--cui-gray-800), $start-percent: null, $end-percent: null) {
  background-image: linear-gradient(to bottom, $start-color $start-percent, $end-color $end-percent);
}

@mixin gradient-directional($start-color: var(--cui-gray-700), $end-color: var(--cui-gray-800), $deg: 45deg) {
  background-image: linear-gradient($deg, $start-color, $end-color);
}

@mixin gradient-x-three-colors($start-color: var(--cui-info-500), $mid-color: var(--cui-primary-500), $color-stop: 50%, $end-color: var(--cui-danger-500)) {
  background-image: linear-gradient(to right, $start-color, $mid-color $color-stop, $end-color);
}

@mixin gradient-y-three-colors($start-color: var(--cui-info-500), $mid-color: var(--cui-primary-500), $color-stop: 50%, $end-color: var(--cui-danger-500)) {
  background-image: linear-gradient($start-color, $mid-color $color-stop, $end-color);
}

@mixin gradient-radial($inner-color: var(--cui-gray-700), $outer-color: var(--cui-gray-800)) {
  background-image: radial-gradient(circle, $inner-color, $outer-color);
}

@mixin gradient-striped($color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-white) 15%, transparent), $angle: 45deg) {
  background-image: linear-gradient($angle, $color 25%, transparent 25%, transparent 50%, $color 50%, $color 75%, transparent 75%, transparent);
}
```

### Utilities API

Background utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
"bg-color": (
  property: (
    --cui-bg: null,
    background-color: var(--cui-bg),
  ),
  class: bg,
  values: map.merge(
    map.merge($utilities-bg-colors, theme-token-refs($theme-bgs, "bg")),
    (
      "body-secondary": var(--cui-bg-3), // deprecated
      "body-tertiary": var(--cui-bg-2), // deprecated
    )
  )
),
"bg-color-subtle": (
  property: (
    --cui-bg: null,
    background-color: var(--cui-bg),
  ),
  class: bg-subtle,
  values: theme-color-refs("bg-subtle")
),
"bg-color-muted": (
  property: (
    --cui-bg: null,
    background-color: var(--cui-bg),
  ),
  class: bg-muted,
  values: theme-color-refs("bg-muted")
),
"bg-opacity": (
  class: bg,
  property: background-color,
  values: theme-opacity-values(--cui-bg)
),
// deprecated
"bg-color-subtle-legacy": (
  property: (
    --cui-bg: null,
    background-color: var(--cui-bg),
  ),
  class: bg,
  values: $utilities-bg-subtle
),
// deprecated
"bg-color-muted-legacy": (
  property: (
    --cui-bg: null,
    background-color: var(--cui-bg),
  ),
  class: bg,
  values: $utilities-bg-muted
),
// deprecated
"bg-opacity-legacy": (
  class: bg-opacity,
  property: background-color,
  values: theme-opacity-values(--cui-bg, null, (10: .1, 15: .15, 25: .25, 50: .5, 75: .75, 100: 1))
),
```

# Vue Border Utilities

> Use border utilities to add or remove an element's borders, and to set how thick they are.

## Additive

Use border utilities to add or remove an element's borders. Choose from all borders, one at a time, or a facing pair — `.border-x` draws the two inline sides, `.border-y` the two block sides.

```html
<span class="border"></span>
<span class="border-top"></span>
<span class="border-end"></span>
<span class="border-bottom"></span>
<span class="border-start"></span>
<span class="border-x"></span>
<span class="border-y"></span>
```

_Added in 6.0.0._

`.border-x` and `.border-y` set the `border-inline` and `border-block` shorthands, so they follow the writing direction the way the single-side classes do.

## Subtractive

Or remove borders:

```html
<span class="border border-0"></span>
<span class="border border-top-0"></span>
<span class="border border-end-0"></span>
<span class="border border-bottom-0"></span>
<span class="border border-start-0"></span>
<span class="border border-x-0"></span>
<span class="border border-y-0"></span>
```

## Width

_Added in 6.0.0._

`.border-keyline` sits below `1px`, for a hairline that stays hairline on a high-density screen instead of thickening to a full device pixel.

```html
<span class="border border-keyline"></span>
<span class="border border-1"></span>
<span class="border border-2"></span>
<span class="border border-3"></span>
<span class="border border-4"></span>
<span class="border border-5"></span>

<span class="border border-1 border-info"></span>
<span class="border border-2 border-info"></span>
<span class="border border-3 border-info"></span>
<span class="border border-4 border-info"></span>
<span class="border border-5 border-info"></span>

<span class="border-start border-start-keyline"></span>
<span class="border-start border-start-1"></span>
<span class="border-start border-start-2"></span>
<span class="border-start border-start-3"></span>
<span class="border-start border-start-4"></span>
<span class="border-start border-start-5"></span>

<span class="border-start border-start-1 border-start-info"></span>
<span class="border-start border-start-2 border-start-info"></span>
<span class="border-start border-start-3 border-start-info"></span>
<span class="border-start border-start-4 border-start-info"></span>
<span class="border-start border-start-5 border-start-info"></span>
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

```scss
--cui-border-width: 1px,
--cui-border-style: solid,
--cui-border-color: light-dark(var(--cui-gray-200), var(--cui-gray-700)),
--cui-border-color-translucent: color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-fg-body) 15%, transparent),
```

### Sass maps

Each neutral border is one entry: the key is one `.border-{key}` utility and the `--cui-border-{key}` token behind it, in light and dark mode. `--cui-border-color`, the default every component reads, is a separate knob above:

```scss
$theme-borders: () !default;
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$theme-borders: defaults(
  (
    "bg":          var(--cui-bg-body),
    "body":        light-dark(var(--cui-gray-300), var(--cui-gray-800)),
    "muted":       light-dark(var(--cui-gray-200), var(--cui-gray-800)),
    "subtle":      light-dark(color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-gray-100), var(--cui-gray-200)), color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-gray-800), var(--cui-gray-900))),
    "emphasized":  light-dark(var(--cui-gray-400), var(--cui-gray-600)),
    "white":       var(--cui-white),
    "black":       var(--cui-black),
  ),
  $theme-borders
);
```

Each entry is one `.border-{width}` class and the width it sets. Add a key to define a width, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
$border-widths: () !default;
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$border-widths: defaults(
  (
    keyline: calc(var(--cui-border-width) * .5),
    1: var(--cui-border-width),
    2: calc(var(--cui-border-width) * 2),
    3: calc(var(--cui-border-width) * 3),
    4: calc(var(--cui-border-width) * 4),
    5: calc(var(--cui-border-width) * 5)
  ),
  $border-widths
);
```

### Utilities API

Border utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
"border": (
  property: border,
  values: (
    null: var(--cui-border-width) var(--cui-border-style) var(--cui-border-color),
    0: 0,
  ),
),
"border-top": (
  property: border-top,
  values: (
    null: var(--cui-border-width) var(--cui-border-style) var(--cui-border-color),
    0: 0,
  )
),
"border-end": (
  property: border-inline-end,
  class: border-end,
  values: (
    null: var(--cui-border-width) var(--cui-border-style) var(--cui-border-color),
    0: 0,
  ),
),
"border-bottom": (
  property: border-bottom,
  values: (
    null: var(--cui-border-width) var(--cui-border-style) var(--cui-border-color),
    0: 0,
  )
),
"border-start": (
  property: border-inline-start,
  class: border-start,
  values: (
    null: var(--cui-border-width) var(--cui-border-style) var(--cui-border-color),
    0: 0,
  ),
),
"border-x": (
  property: border-inline,
  class: border-x,
  values: (
    null: var(--cui-border-width) var(--cui-border-style) var(--cui-border-color),
    0: 0,
  ),
),
"border-y": (
  property: border-block,
  class: border-y,
  values: (
    null: var(--cui-border-width) var(--cui-border-style) var(--cui-border-color),
    0: 0,
  ),
),
```

```scss
"border-width": (
  property: border-width,
  class: border,
  values: $utilities-border-widths
),
"border-top-width": (
  property: border-top-width,
  class: border-top,
  values: $utilities-border-widths
),
"border-end-width": (
  property: border-inline-end-width,
  class: border-end,
  values: $utilities-border-widths,
),
"border-bottom-width": (
  property: border-bottom-width,
  class: border-bottom,
  values: $utilities-border-widths
),
"border-start-width": (
  property: border-inline-start-width,
  class: border-start,
  values: $utilities-border-widths,
),
```

# Vue Border color Utilities

> Change the border color of an element with utilities built on our theme colors, and fade it with the opacity utilities.

## Color

Change the border color using utilities built on our theme colors.

```html
<span class="border border-${c.name}"></span>
  <span class="border border-subtle-${c.name}"></span>

<span class="border border-black"></span>
  <span class="border border-white"></span>
```

## Neutral

Four weights sit between the page and a themed border, for lines that separate content without naming a color. `.border-emphasized` is the strongest, the default `--cui-border-color` sits in the middle, and `.border-subtle` is the faintest.

```html
<span class="border border-emphasized"></span>
<span class="border"></span>
<span class="border border-muted"></span>
<span class="border border-subtle"></span>
```

Each is a `light-dark()` pair, so the ladder keeps its order in both color schemes rather than fading out in one of them.

## Sides

Using utilities you can change the border on one side only, or you can change all borders to make them different colors.

```html
<span class="border-top border-top-primary"></span>
<span class="border-end border-end-primary"></span>
<span class="border-bottom border-bottom-primary"></span>
<span class="border-start border-start-primary"></span>
<span class="border-start border-start-primary border-end border-end-danger"></span>
<span class="border-top border-top-primary border-end border-end-danger border-bottom border-bottom-success"></span>
<span class="border border-top-primary border-end-danger border-bottom-success border-start-info"></span>
```

## Recoloring a component

The same utilities repaint the border a component ships with:

```html
<div class="mb-5">
  <CFormLabel for="exampleFormControlInput1">Email address</CFormLabel>
  <CFormInput type="email" class="border-success" id="exampleFormControlInput1" placeholder="name@example.com" />
</div>

<div class="h4 pb-3 mb-5 fg-danger border-bottom border-danger">
  Dangerous heading
</div>

<div class="p-4 bg-info bg-10 border border-info border-start-0 rounded-end">
  Changing border color and width
</div>
```

## Opacity

Every `.border-{color}` utility writes its colour into `--cui-border` and reads it back, so a companion `.border-{percentage}` class can mix that colour with `transparent` through `color-mix()`, in the browser, without recompiling Sass.

```css
.border-success {
  --cui-border: var(--cui-success-bg);
  border-color: var(--cui-border);
}

.border-50 {
  border-color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-border) 50%, transparent);
}
```

Override `--cui-border` to repaint the utility with another colour; the opacity class keeps working, because it reads whatever the token holds.

```html
<div class="border border-success p-3 mb-3">This is default success border</div>
<div class="border border-success p-3 mb-3 border-70">This is 70% opacity success border</div>
<div class="border border-success p-3 mb-3 border-50">This is 50% opacity success border</div>
<div class="border border-success p-3 mb-3 border-30">This is 30% opacity success border</div>
<div class="border border-success p-3 border-10">This is 10% opacity success border</div>
```

`.border-opacity-{10|25|50|75|100}` and `.border-{color}-subtle` are the deprecated v5 spellings of `.border-{percentage}` and `.border-subtle-{color}`; they still render and are removed in v7.

## Customizing

### Sass variables

Border color utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
"border-color": (
  property: (
    --cui-border: null,
    border-color: var(--cui-border),
  ),
  class: border,
  values: $utilities-border-colors
),
"border-top-color": (
  property: border-top-color,
  class: border-top,
  values: map.merge(theme-color-refs("bg"), ("white": var(--cui-white)))
),
"border-end-color": (
  property: border-inline-end-color,
  class: border-end,
  values: map.merge(theme-color-refs("bg"), ("white": var(--cui-white)))
),
"border-bottom-color": (
  property: border-bottom-color,
  class: border-bottom,
  values: map.merge(theme-color-refs("bg"), ("white": var(--cui-white)))
),
"border-start-color": (
  property: border-inline-start-color,
  class: border-start,
  values: map.merge(theme-color-refs("bg"), ("white": var(--cui-white)))
),
```

```scss
"border-color-subtle": (
  property: (
    --cui-border: null,
    border-color: var(--cui-border),
  ),
  class: border-subtle,
  values: theme-color-refs("border")
),
"border-opacity": (
  class: border,
  property: border-color,
  values: theme-opacity-values(--cui-border)
),
// deprecated
"border-color-subtle-legacy": (
  property: (
    --cui-border: null,
    border-color: var(--cui-border),
  ),
  class: border,
  values: $utilities-border-subtle

// deprecated
"border-opacity-legacy": (
  class: border-opacity,
  property: border-color,
```

## Sizes

Use the scaling classes for larger or smaller rounded corners. Sizes range from `0` to `9` — the stops of the `$radii` scale, `--cui-radius-0` through `--cui-radius-9` — plus `circle` and `pill`, and can be configured by modifying the utilities API. `.rounded` without a number is size `5`, the radius buttons and form controls use.

## Setting the size without applying it

_Added in 6.0.0._

`.rounded-size-*` writes the radius into `--cui-rounded-size` without setting `border-radius` itself. The unprefixed corner classes — `.rounded`, `.rounded-top`, `.rounded-end`, `.rounded-bottom`, `.rounded-start` — read that token, so one size class drives whichever corners you round.

Without a `.rounded-size-*` in scope the corner classes fall back to `--cui-radius-5`. A numbered `.rounded-{n}` also writes the token, so `.rounded-3 .rounded-top` keeps the top corners on size 3 while a side class with its own number (`.rounded-top-3`) sets that side directly and ignores the token.

## Customizing

### CSS variables

The radius scale is emitted on `:root` as `--cui-radius-0` through `--cui-radius-9`, plus `--cui-radius-pill`. Components read stops of the scale (`--cui-radius-5`, `--cui-radius-7`), so overriding a stop re-rounds everything that uses it without recompiling.

```scss
$root-token-defaults: map.set($root-token-defaults, --cui-radius, .5rem);
@each $key, $value in $radii {
  $root-token-defaults: map.set($root-token-defaults, --cui-radius-#{$key}, $value);
}
$root-token-defaults: map.set($root-token-defaults, --cui-radius-pill, 50rem);
```

### Sass maps

Each entry is one `--cui-radius-{step}` token as a multiple of `$radius` — override the map to add or retune a step:

```scss
$radii: () !default;
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$radii: defaults(
  (
    0: 0,
    1: calc(var(--cui-radius) * .25),
    2: calc(var(--cui-radius) * .375),
    3: calc(var(--cui-radius) * .5),
    4: calc(var(--cui-radius) * .75),
    5: var(--cui-radius),
    6: calc(var(--cui-radius) * 1.25),
    7: calc(var(--cui-radius) * 1.5),
    8: calc(var(--cui-radius) * 1.75),
    9: calc(var(--cui-radius) * 2),
  ),
  $radii
);
```

### Sass mixins

```scss
@mixin border-radius($radius: var(--cui-radius-5), $fallback-border-radius: false) {
  @if $enable-rounded {
    border-radius: valid-radius($radius);
  }
  @else if $fallback-border-radius != false {
    border-radius: $fallback-border-radius;
  }
}

@mixin border-top-radius($radius: var(--cui-radius-5)) {
  @if $enable-rounded {
    border-top-left-radius: valid-radius($radius);
    border-top-right-radius: valid-radius($radius);
  }
}

@mixin border-end-radius($radius: var(--cui-radius-5)) {
  @if $enable-rounded {
    border-start-end-radius: valid-radius($radius);
    border-end-end-radius: valid-radius($radius);
  }
}

@mixin border-bottom-radius($radius: var(--cui-radius-5)) {
  @if $enable-rounded {
    border-bottom-right-radius: valid-radius($radius);
    border-bottom-left-radius: valid-radius($radius);
  }
}

@mixin border-start-radius($radius: var(--cui-radius-5)) {
  @if $enable-rounded {
    border-start-start-radius: valid-radius($radius);
    border-end-start-radius: valid-radius($radius);
  }
}

@mixin border-top-start-radius($radius: var(--cui-radius-5)) {
  @if $enable-rounded {
    border-start-start-radius: valid-radius($radius);
  }
}

@mixin border-top-end-radius($radius: var(--cui-radius-5)) {
  @if $enable-rounded {
    border-start-end-radius: valid-radius($radius);
  }
}

@mixin border-bottom-end-radius($radius: var(--cui-radius-5)) {
  @if $enable-rounded {
    border-end-end-radius: valid-radius($radius);
  }
}

@mixin border-bottom-start-radius($radius: var(--cui-radius-5)) {
  @if $enable-rounded {
    border-end-start-radius: valid-radius($radius);
  }
}
```

Border radius utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
"rounded": (
  property: (
    --cui-rounded-size: null,
    border-radius: var(--cui-rounded-size)
  ),
  class: rounded,
  values: map.merge(
    $utilities-radii,
    (
      null: var(--cui-radius-5),
      circle: 50%,
      pill: var(--cui-radius-pill)
    )
  )
),
"rounded-size": (
  property: --cui-rounded-size,
  class: rounded-size,
  values: map.merge(
    $utilities-radii,
    (
      null: var(--cui-radius-5),
      circle: 50%,
      pill: var(--cui-radius-pill)
    )
  )
),
"rounded-top": (
  property: border-start-start-radius border-start-end-radius,
  class: rounded-top,
  values: map.merge(
    $utilities-radii,
    (
      null: var(--cui-rounded-size, var(--cui-radius-5)),
      circle: 50%,
      pill: var(--cui-radius-pill)
    )
  )
),
"rounded-end": (
  property: border-start-end-radius border-end-end-radius,
  class: rounded-end,
  values: map.merge(
    $utilities-radii,
    (
      null: var(--cui-rounded-size, var(--cui-radius-5)),
      circle: 50%,
      pill: var(--cui-radius-pill)
    )
```

# Vue Color Scheme Utilities

> Tell the browser which color scheme an element renders in, so form controls, scrollbars and other built-in UI follow it.

## How it works

_Added in 6.0.0._

`.color-scheme-light` and `.color-scheme-dark` set the CSS `color-scheme` property. That property is what the browser reads to paint the parts of the page it draws itself — checkbox and radio ticks, the date and color picker popups, `<select>` menus, scrollbars, and the canvas behind a transparent background.

Our theme classes already set it: `:root` renders in `light`, and the dark theme switches it to `dark`. Reach for these utilities on the exception — a panel that keeps one scheme while the page is in the other.

```html
<div class="color-scheme-light border rounded p-4 mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" for="lightRange">Light scheme</label>
  <CFormRange id="lightRange" />
</div>
<div class="color-scheme-dark border rounded p-4">
  <label class="form-label" for="darkRange">Dark scheme</label>
  <CFormRange id="darkRange" />
</div>
```

## Not a theme

The property changes only the browser's own rendering. It sets no colors of its own, so text and backgrounds stay whatever your CSS says — `.color-scheme-dark` on a white panel leaves the panel white and gives it dark scrollbars.

To flip the colors as well, set the theme with `data-coreui-theme="dark"`, which switches the tokens **and** the color scheme together. See [color modes](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/customize/color-modes/).

## Customizing

### Utilities API

Color scheme utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
"color-scheme": (
  property: color-scheme,
  class: color-scheme,
  values: (
    light: light,
    dark: dark,
  )
)
```


---

# Vue Colors Utilities

> Convey meaning through `color` with a handful of color utility classes. Includes support for styling links with hover states, too.

## Colors

Colorize text with color utilities. To colorize a link, give it a [theme class](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/customize/theme/) instead — Reboot resolves a link's colour from the theme, and the theme slot carries a hover tone with it. See [link utilities](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/link/).

```html
<p class="fg-${c.name}">.fg-${c.name}</p>
<p class="fg-emphasis-${c.name}">.fg-emphasis-${c.name}</p>
<p class="fg-body">.fg-body</p>

<p class="fg-black bg-white">.fg-black</p>
<p class="fg-white bg-black">.fg-white</p>
```

> **Deprecation:** the v5 spellings — `.text-{color}`, `.text-{color}-emphasis`, `.text-body`, `.text-black`, `.text-white`, `.text-reset`, `.text-body-secondary` and `.text-body-tertiary` — still ship and render the same, but are removed in v7. Write `.fg-{color}`, `.fg-emphasis-{color}`, `.fg-body`, `.fg-black`, `.fg-white`, `.fg-reset`, `.fg-2` and `.fg-3`. `.text-muted`, `.text-black-50` and `.text-white-50` are gone, as in Bootstrap 6: write `.fg-2`, `.fg-black.fg-50` and `.fg-white.fg-50`.

> ##### Conveying meaning to assistive technologies
> 
> Relying on color to convey meaning creates a visual cue that assistive technologies, like screen readers, cannot perceive. It's essential that any information represented by color is either apparent from the content itself (e.g., the visible text) or supplemented by alternative methods, such as extra text using the `.visually-hidden` class.

## Foreground ladder

The neutral text hierarchy is a ladder, mirroring the [surface ladder](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/background/#surface-ladder): `.fg-body` is the body text color and the numbers step away from it — `.fg-1` barely, `.fg-4` down to a watermark. The `.fg-{percentage}` opacity utilities compose with all of them.

```html
<p class="fg-body">.fg-body</p>
<p class="fg-1">.fg-1</p>
<p class="fg-2">.fg-2</p>
<p class="fg-3">.fg-3</p>
<p class="fg-4">.fg-4</p>
```

`.fg-2` and `.fg-3` are deprecated names for `.fg-2` and `.fg-3` — they render identically and go away in v7.

## Opacity

Every `.fg-*` utility writes its colour into `--cui-fg` and reads it back, so a companion `.fg-{percentage}` class can mix that colour with `transparent` through `color-mix()`, in the browser, without recompiling Sass.

```css
.fg-primary {
  --cui-fg: var(--cui-primary-fg);
  color: var(--cui-fg);
}

.fg-50 {
  color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-fg) 50%, transparent);
}
```

Override `--cui-fg` to repaint the utility with another colour; the opacity class keeps working, because it reads whatever the token holds.

```html
<div class="fg-primary">This is default primary text</div>
<div class="fg-primary fg-90">This is 90% opacity primary text</div>
<div class="fg-primary fg-80">This is 80% opacity primary text</div>
<div class="fg-primary fg-70">This is 70% opacity primary text</div>
<div class="fg-primary fg-60">This is 60% opacity primary text</div>
<div class="fg-primary fg-50">This is 50% opacity primary text</div>
<div class="fg-primary fg-40">This is 40% opacity primary text</div>
<div class="fg-primary fg-30">This is 30% opacity primary text</div>
<div class="fg-primary fg-20">This is 20% opacity primary text</div>
<div class="fg-primary fg-10">This is 10% opacity primary text</div>
```

`.text-opacity-{25|50|75|100}` are the deprecated v5 names of the same knob and are removed in v7.

## Contrast colors

`.fg-contrast-{color}` sets `--cui-fg` to the theme colour's `contrast` slot — the text colour that reads on the solid colour — so a label on a `.bg-{color}` surface picks the right ink without naming it.

```html
<p class="bg-${c.name} fg-contrast-${c.name} p-3">.fg-contrast-${c.name}</p>
```

These compose with the opacity utilities too.

```html
<p class="bg-primary fg-contrast-primary fg-100 p-3">.fg-contrast-primary .fg-100</p>
<p class="bg-primary fg-contrast-primary fg-70 p-3">.fg-contrast-primary .fg-70</p>
<p class="bg-primary fg-contrast-primary fg-40 p-3">.fg-contrast-primary .fg-40</p>
```

## Reset color

Reset a text or link's color with `.fg-reset`, so that it inherits the color from its parent.

```html
<p class="fg-2">
  Secondary body text with a <a href="#" class="fg-reset">reset link</a>.
</p>
```

## Specificity

Sometimes contextual classes cannot be applied due to the specificity of another selector. In some cases, a sufficient workaround is to wrap your element's content in a `<div>` or more semantic element with the desired class.

## Customizing

In addition to the following Sass functionality, consider reading about our included [CSS custom properties](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/customize/css-variables/) (aka CSS variables) for colors and more.

Do you need a gradient in your custom CSS? Just add `background-image: var(--cui-gradient);`.

### Sass variables

Most `color` utilities are generated by our theme colors, reassigned from our generic color palette variables.

```scss
$primary: oklch(52.945% 0.19103 278.34) !default;
$success: oklch(55.1% 0.173 145) !default;
$info:    oklch(57.4% 0.196 256) !default;
$warning: oklch(84% 0.172 85) !default;
$danger:  oklch(58.7% 0.237 23.81) !default;
$gray:    oklch(60% 0.03948 265.02) !default;
```

### Sass maps

The foreground ladder is one map: each key is one `.fg-{key}` utility and the `--cui-fg-{key}` token behind it, in light and dark mode:

```scss
$theme-fgs: () !default;
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$theme-fgs: defaults(
  (
    "body":        light-dark(var(--cui-gray-900), var(--cui-gray-050)),
    "1":           light-dark(var(--cui-gray-800), var(--cui-gray-200)),
    "2":           light-dark(var(--cui-gray-700), var(--cui-gray-300)),
    "3":           light-dark(var(--cui-gray-600), var(--cui-gray-500)),
    "4":           light-dark(var(--cui-gray-500), var(--cui-gray-600)),
    "bg":          var(--cui-bg-body),
    "white":       var(--cui-white),
    "black":       var(--cui-black),
    "inherit":     inherit,
  ),
  $theme-fgs
);
```

```scss
$utilities-text-emphasis-colors: theme-color-refs("fg-emphasis", "-emphasis") !default;
```

# Vue Container queries Utilities

> Turn an element into a query container so its descendants can respond to its size instead of the viewport.

Use the `.contains-*` utilities to set the `container-type` property, establishing an element as a [query container](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_containment/Container_queries). Once an element is a query container, its descendants can adapt their styles to the container's size rather than to the viewport.

Apply `.contains-inline` to query on inline size (width in horizontal writing modes), or `.contains-size` to query on both inline and block size.

```vue
<div class="contains-inline">
  <CCard>...</CCard>
</div>
```

```scss
// Classes
.contains-inline {
  container-type: inline-size;
}
.contains-size {
  container-type: size;
}
```

> `.contains-size` queries the container's block size as well, so the element needs an explicit height for `size` containment to resolve. When in doubt, reach for `.contains-inline`.

> **`container-type` implies layout containment.** A query container becomes the containing block for absolutely and fixed-positioned descendants, so a `position: fixed` element inside it is positioned against the container rather than the viewport. Keep fixed markup outside your query containers.

Our [CSS Grid](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/layout/css-grid/) uses this: every `.grid` is a query container, which is what makes `.g-col-md-*` respond to the width of the grid instead of the browser window.

Several components read a query container rather than the viewport, and need one on an ancestor to switch at all:

- [`.card-group`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/card/#card-groups) attaches its cards from `sm` up
- [`.list-group-horizontal-*`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/list-group/#horizontal) turns horizontal from its breakpoint up
- [`.hstack-*` and `.vstack-*`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/helpers/stacks/) switch direction at their breakpoint
- [`.table-responsive*`](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/table/#responsive-tables) is itself a query container, so content inside it can respond to its width

## Customizing

### Sass mixins

Write your own container queries with the same breakpoint names the rest of the framework uses. Each mixin takes an optional container name, so you can target one specific container.

```scss
.sidebar {
  @include set-container(); // container-type: inline-size

  .card {
    @include container-breakpoint-up(md) {
      display: flex;
    }
  }
}
```

```scss
// Name a container, then query it by name from anywhere inside it
.layout {
  @include set-container(inline-size, layout);
}

.widget {
  @include container-breakpoint-between(sm, lg, layout) {
    flex-direction: column;
  }
}
```

```scss
// Set an element as a query container.
//
//    @include set-container();                     // container-type: inline-size
//    @include set-container(size);                 // container-type: size
//    @include set-container(inline-size, sidebar); // container: sidebar / inline-size
@mixin set-container($type: inline-size, $name: null) {
  @if $name {
    container: #{$name} / #{$type};
  } @else {
    container-type: #{$type};
  }
}

// Container of at least the minimum breakpoint width. No query for the smallest breakpoint.
// Makes the @content apply to the given breakpoint and wider.
@mixin container-breakpoint-up($name, $container-name: null, $breakpoints: $breakpoints) {
  $min: breakpoint-min($name, $breakpoints);
  @if $min {
    @if $container-name {
      @container #{$container-name} (width >= #{$min}) {
        @content;
      }
    } @else {
      @container (width >= #{$min}) {
        @content;
      }
    }
  } @else {
    @content;
  }
}

// Container of at most the maximum breakpoint width. No query for the largest breakpoint.
// Makes the @content apply to the given breakpoint and narrower.
@mixin container-breakpoint-down($name, $container-name: null, $breakpoints: $breakpoints) {
  $max: breakpoint-max($name, $breakpoints);
  @if $max {
    @if $container-name {
      @container #{$container-name} (width < #{$max}) {
        @content;
      }
    } @else {
      @container (width < #{$max}) {
        @content;
      }
    }
  } @else {
    @content;
  }
}

// Container that spans multiple breakpoint widths.
// Makes the @content apply between the min and max breakpoints.
@mixin container-breakpoint-between($lower, $upper, $container-name: null, $breakpoints: $breakpoints) {
  $min: breakpoint-min($lower, $breakpoints);
  $max: breakpoint-max($upper, $breakpoints);

  @if $min != null and $max != null {
    @if $container-name {
      @container #{$container-name} (width >= #{$min}) and (width < #{$max}) {
        @content;
      }
    } @else {
      @container (width >= #{$min}) and (width < #{$max}) {
        @content;
      }
    }
  } @else if $max == null {
    @include container-breakpoint-up($lower, $container-name, $breakpoints) {
      @content;
    }
  } @else if $min == null {
    @include container-breakpoint-down($upper, $container-name, $breakpoints) {
      @content;
    }
  }
}

// Container between the breakpoint's minimum and maximum widths.
// No minimum for the smallest breakpoint, and no maximum for the largest one.
@mixin container-breakpoint-only($name, $container-name: null, $breakpoints: $breakpoints) {
  $min: breakpoint-min($name, $breakpoints);
  $next: breakpoint-next($name, $breakpoints);
  $max: breakpoint-max($next, $breakpoints);

  @if $min != null and $max != null {
    @if $container-name {
      @container #{$container-name} (width >= #{$min}) and (width < #{$max}) {
        @content;
      }
    } @else {
      @container (width >= #{$min}) and (width < #{$max}) {
        @content;
      }
    }
  } @else if $max == null {
    @include container-breakpoint-up($name, $container-name, $breakpoints) {
      @content;
    }
  } @else if $min == null {
    @include container-breakpoint-down($next, $container-name, $breakpoints) {
      @content;
    }
  }
}
```

### Utilities API

Container utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
"container": (
  property: container-type,
  class: contains,
  values: (
    "inline": inline-size,
    "size": size,
  )
),
```

# Vue Display property Utilities

> Quickly and responsively toggle the display value of components and more with our display utilities. Includes support for some of the more common values, as well as some extras for controlling display when printing.

## How it works

Change the value of the [`display` property](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/display) with our responsive display utility classes. We purposely support only a subset of all possible values for `display`. Classes can be combined for various effects as you need.

## Notation

Display utility classes that apply to all [breakpoints](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/layout/breakpoints/), from `xs` to `2xl`, have no breakpoint abbreviation in them. This is because those classes are applied from `min-width: 0;` and up, and thus are not bound by a media query. The remaining breakpoints, however, do include a breakpoint abbreviation.

As such, the classes are named using the format:

- `.d-{value}` for `xs`
- `.d-{breakpoint}-{value}` for `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, and `2xl`.

Where *value* is one of:

- `none`
- `inline`
- `inline-block`
- `block`
- `grid`
- `inline-grid`
- `table`
- `table-cell`
- `table-row`
- `flex`
- `inline-flex`
- `contents`
- `flow-root`

The display values can be altered by changing the `$displays` variable and recompiling the SCSS.

The media queries affect screen widths with the given breakpoint *or larger*. For example, `.d-lg-none` sets `display: none;` on `lg`, `xl`, and `2xl` screens.

## Examples

```html
<div class="d-inline p-3 text-bg-primary">d-inline</div>
<div class="d-inline p-3 text-bg-inverse">d-inline</div>
```

```html
<span class="d-block p-3 text-bg-primary">d-block</span>
<span class="d-block p-3 text-bg-inverse">d-block</span>
```

## Hiding elements

For faster mobile-friendly development, use responsive display classes for showing and hiding elements by device. Avoid creating entirely different versions of the same site, instead hide elements responsively for each screen size.

To hide elements simply use the `.d-none` class or one of the `.d-{sm,md,lg,xl,2xl}-none` classes for any responsive screen variation.

To show an element only on a given interval of screen sizes you can combine one `.d-*-none` class with a `.d-*-*` class, for example `.d-none .d-md-block .d-xl-none` will hide the element for all screen sizes except on medium and large devices.

| Screen size | Class |
| --- | --- |
| Hidden on all | `.d-none` |
| Hidden only on xs | `.d-none .d-sm-block` |
| Hidden only on sm | `.d-sm-none .d-md-block` |
| Hidden only on md | `.d-md-none .d-lg-block` |
| Hidden only on lg | `.d-lg-none .d-xl-block` |
| Hidden only on xl | `.d-xl-none .d-2xl-block` |
| Hidden only on 2xl | `.d-2xl-none` |
| Visible on all | `.d-block` |
| Visible only on xs | `.d-block .d-sm-none` |
| Visible only on sm | `.d-none .d-sm-block .d-md-none` |
| Visible only on md | `.d-none .d-md-block .d-lg-none` |
| Visible only on lg | `.d-none .d-lg-block .d-xl-none` |
| Visible only on xl | `.d-none .d-xl-block .d-2xl-none` |
| Visible only on 2xl | `.d-none .d-2xl-block` |

```html
<div class="d-lg-none">hide on lg and wider screens</div>
<div class="d-none d-lg-block">hide on screens smaller than lg</div>
```

## Display in print

Change the `display` value of elements when printing with our print display utility classes. Includes support for the same `display` values as our responsive `.d-*` utilities.

- `.d-print-none`
- `.d-print-inline`
- `.d-print-inline-block`
- `.d-print-block`
- `.d-print-grid`
- `.d-print-inline-grid`
- `.d-print-table`
- `.d-print-table-row`
- `.d-print-table-cell`
- `.d-print-flex`
- `.d-print-inline-flex`

The print and display classes can be combined.

```html
<div class="d-print-none">Screen Only (Hide on print only)</div>
<div class="d-none d-print-block">Print Only (Hide on screen only)</div>
<div class="d-none d-lg-block d-print-block">Hide up to large on screen, but always show on print</div>
```

## Customizing

### Utilities API

Display utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
"display": (
  responsive: true,
  print: true,
  property: display,
  class: d,
  values: inline inline-block block grid inline-grid table table-row table-cell flex inline-flex contents flow-root none
),
```

# Vue Divide Utilities

> Draw a border between children without one on the outer edges, for lists of rows and rows of actions.

## Overview

`divide-x` and `divide-y` draw a border *between* children — every child except
the first gets a border on its leading edge — so a list of rows or a row of
actions gets its separators without a border on the outer edges and without
marking up the last item differently.

```html
<div class="divide-y border rounded">
  <div class="p-3">First</div>
  <div class="p-3">Second</div>
  <div class="p-3">Third</div>
</div>
```

`divide-x` separates along the inline axis and follows the writing direction.

```html
<div class="d-flex divide-x border rounded">
  <div class="p-3">First</div>
  <div class="p-3">Second</div>
  <div class="p-3">Third</div>
</div>
```

The dividers take the global `--cui-border-width`, `--cui-border-style`
and `--cui-border-color`, so they follow a theme like every other border.

Both are responsive, which is what makes a list that changes direction work: the
dividers can switch axis at a breakpoint instead of being written twice.

```html
<div class="d-md-flex divide-y divide-y-md-0 divide-x-md border rounded">
  <div class="p-3">First</div>
  <div class="p-3">Second</div>
  <div class="p-3">Third</div>
</div>
```

`divide-y` separates the stacked rows, `divide-y-md-0` removes those separators
once the items line up, and `divide-x-md` draws them between the columns
instead. The `-0` step exists for both axes at every breakpoint, so a divider
can be dropped anywhere it stops making sense.

> The rule is wrapped in `:where()` and therefore adds no specificity — a child
> with its own border wins on its own.

## Customizing

### Sass variables

Divide utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
"divide-x": (
  responsive: true,
  property: border-inline-start,
  class: divide-x,
  child-selector: "> :not(:first-child)",
  values: (
    null: var(--cui-border-width) var(--cui-border-style) var(--cui-border-color),
    0: 0,
  )
),
"divide-y": (
  responsive: true,
  property: border-block-start,
  class: divide-y,
  child-selector: "> :not(:first-child)",
  values: (
    null: var(--cui-border-width) var(--cui-border-style) var(--cui-border-color),
    0: 0,
  )
),
```
