# Vue Shadows Utilities

> Add or remove shadows to elements with box-shadow utilities.

## Examples

While shadows on components are disabled by default in CoreUI for Vue and can be enabled via `$enable-shadows`, you can also quickly add or remove a shadow with our `box-shadow` utility classes. Includes support for `.shadow-none` and three default sizes (which have associated variables to match).

```html
<div class="shadow-none p-4 mb-6 bg-4 rounded">No shadow</div>
<div class="shadow-xs p-4 mb-6 bg-body rounded">Extra small shadow</div>
<div class="shadow-sm p-4 mb-6 bg-body rounded">Small shadow</div>
<div class="shadow p-4 mb-6 bg-body rounded">Regular shadow</div>
<div class="shadow-lg p-4 mb-6 bg-body rounded">Larger shadow</div>
<div class="shadow-xl p-4 mb-6 bg-body rounded">Extra large shadow</div>
```

## Color

_Added in 6.0.0._

A shadow does not have to be grey. Add a `.shadow-{color}` class next to the size class to tint it — the size class supplies the geometry, the colour class supplies the hue.

```html
<div class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-5">
  <div class="shadow shadow-primary p-4 bg-body rounded">Primary</div>
  <div class="shadow shadow-success p-4 bg-body rounded">Success</div>
  <div class="shadow shadow-danger p-4 bg-body rounded">Danger</div>
  <div class="shadow shadow-current p-4 bg-body rounded fg-info">Current color</div>
</div>
```

The tint does not reach nested shadows: an element inside a `.shadow-primary` box draws its own shadow in the default colour, so a tinted card does not silently recolour everything inside it.

```html
<div class="shadow shadow-primary p-6 bg-body rounded">
  <div class="shadow p-4 bg-body rounded">Untinted, inside a tinted parent</div>
</div>
```

## Opacity

_Added in 6.0.0._

`.shadow-opacity-{10…100}`, in steps of ten, scales the shadow without touching its colour or geometry, which is the usual way to soften a shadow on a busy surface. `.shadow-opacity-25` and `-75` are deprecated v5 steps, removed in v7.

```html
<div class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-5">
  <div class="shadow shadow-opacity-30 p-4 bg-body rounded">30%</div>
  <div class="shadow shadow-opacity-50 p-4 bg-body rounded">50%</div>
  <div class="shadow shadow-opacity-70 p-4 bg-body rounded">70%</div>
  <div class="shadow shadow-opacity-100 p-4 bg-body rounded">100%</div>
</div>
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

_Added in 6.0.0._

Every shadow computes its alpha as `base × strength × opacity`, so three separate things can be changed at runtime without rewriting the shadow:

| Variable | Scope | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--cui-shadow-color` | inherits from `:root` | The colour every shadow is mixed from. |
| `--cui-shadow-strength` | inherits from `:root` | Multiplies every shadow's alpha. Dark mode raises it, because the same alpha reads as weaker against a dark surface. |
| `--cui-shadow-tint` | set by `.shadow-{color}`, does not inherit | Overrides the colour for one element. |
| `--cui-shadow-opacity` | set by `.shadow-opacity-*`, does not inherit | Scales one element's shadow. |

Setting `--cui-shadow-color` on the page changes every shadow at once, including the ones components draw:

```css
:root {
  --cui-shadow-color: #1b4b91;
}
```

```scss
@each $key, $value in $shadows {
  // stylelint-disable-next-line scss/at-function-named-arguments
  $name: if(sass($key == null): --cui-box-shadow; else: --cui-box-shadow-#{$key});
  $root-token-defaults: map.set($root-token-defaults, $name, $value);
}
```

### Sass variables

```scss
$shadows: (
  null: #{(
    "0 .125rem .25rem -.0625rem color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-shadow-tint, var(--cui-shadow-color)) calc(4% * var(--cui-shadow-strength) * var(--cui-shadow-opacity, 1)), transparent)",
    "0 .375rem .75rem -.125rem color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-shadow-tint, var(--cui-shadow-color)) calc(5% * var(--cui-shadow-strength) * var(--cui-shadow-opacity, 1)), transparent)",
    "0 .75rem 1.5rem -.25rem color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-shadow-tint, var(--cui-shadow-color)) calc(6% * var(--cui-shadow-strength) * var(--cui-shadow-opacity, 1)), transparent)"
  )},
  xs: 0 .0625rem .125rem color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-shadow-tint, var(--cui-shadow-color)) calc(4% * var(--cui-shadow-strength) * var(--cui-shadow-opacity, 1)), transparent),
  sm: #{(
    "0 .0625rem .125rem color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-shadow-tint, var(--cui-shadow-color)) calc(4% * var(--cui-shadow-strength) * var(--cui-shadow-opacity, 1)), transparent)",
    "0 .125rem .375rem -.0625rem color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-shadow-tint, var(--cui-shadow-color)) calc(5% * var(--cui-shadow-strength) * var(--cui-shadow-opacity, 1)), transparent)"
  )},
  lg: #{(
    "0 .125rem .375rem -.0625rem color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-shadow-tint, var(--cui-shadow-color)) calc(5% * var(--cui-shadow-strength) * var(--cui-shadow-opacity, 1)), transparent)",
    "0 .375rem 1rem -.1875rem color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-shadow-tint, var(--cui-shadow-color)) calc(6% * var(--cui-shadow-strength) * var(--cui-shadow-opacity, 1)), transparent)",
    "0 .75rem 2rem -.375rem color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-shadow-tint, var(--cui-shadow-color)) calc(7% * var(--cui-shadow-strength) * var(--cui-shadow-opacity, 1)), transparent)",
    "0 1.5rem 3.5rem -.75rem color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-shadow-tint, var(--cui-shadow-color)) calc(8% * var(--cui-shadow-strength) * var(--cui-shadow-opacity, 1)), transparent)"
  )},
  xl: #{(
    "0 .1875rem .5rem -.0625rem color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-shadow-tint, var(--cui-shadow-color)) calc(5% * var(--cui-shadow-strength) * var(--cui-shadow-opacity, 1)), transparent)",
    "0 .5rem 1.25rem -.1875rem color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-shadow-tint, var(--cui-shadow-color)) calc(6% * var(--cui-shadow-strength) * var(--cui-shadow-opacity, 1)), transparent)",
    "0 1rem 2.5rem -.375rem color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-shadow-tint, var(--cui-shadow-color)) calc(7% * var(--cui-shadow-strength) * var(--cui-shadow-opacity, 1)), transparent)",
    "0 2rem 5rem -.75rem color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-shadow-tint, var(--cui-shadow-color)) calc(9% * var(--cui-shadow-strength) * var(--cui-shadow-opacity, 1)), transparent)"
  )},
  inset: inset 0 1px 2px light-dark(color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-shadow-tint, var(--cui-shadow-color)) calc(8% * var(--cui-shadow-opacity, 1)), transparent), color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-shadow-tint, var(--cui-shadow-color)) calc(26% * var(--cui-shadow-opacity, 1)), transparent)),
) !default;
```

### Utilities API

Shadow utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
"shadow": (
  property: box-shadow,
  class: shadow,
  // The literal expressions from $shadows, not var(--cui-box-shadow*).
  // A token resolves where it is declared — on :root — so going through one
  // would freeze the tint and the opacity there and leave .shadow-primary
  // and .shadow-opacity-* with nothing to change.
  // `inset` stays out: it is a component's inner shadow, not a utility.
  values: map.merge(map.remove($shadows, inset), (none: none))
),
```

```scss
"shadow-color": (
  property: (--cui-shadow-tint: null),
  class: shadow,
  values: map.merge(
    theme-color-refs("bg"),
    (
      "current": currentcolor,
      "black": var(--cui-black),
      "white": var(--cui-white),
    )
  )
),
```

```scss
"shadow-opacity": (
  property: (--cui-shadow-opacity: null),
  class: shadow-opacity,
  values: map.merge(
    $util-opacity,
    (
      25: .25, // deprecated
      75: .75, // deprecated
    )
  )
),
```

# Vue Space between Utilities

> Space siblings in a plain flow layout, where gap has no container to work from.

## Overview

`gap` needs a flex or grid container. When the layout is plain flow — stacked
blocks, an inline row of links — `space-x-*` and `space-y-*` put the spacing on
the children themselves: every child except the last one gets a margin.

```html
<div class="space-y-4">
  <div class="p-3 border">First</div>
  <div class="p-3 border">Second</div>
  <div class="p-3 border">Third</div>
</div>
```

## Horizontal

`space-x-*` does the same along the inline axis. It reads the writing direction,
so in a right-to-left document the spacing lands on the correct side without
another class.

```html
<div class="space-x-4">
  <a href="#">First</a>
  <a href="#">Second</a>
  <a href="#">Third</a>
</div>
```

## Changing axis across breakpoints

Both are responsive and take the same `0`–`12` steps from the `$spacers` map as
every other spacing utility. Combining the two axes is the usual reason to reach
for them: a stack on small screens that becomes a row further up needs the
spacing to change axis with it.

```html
<div class="d-md-flex space-y-4 space-y-md-0 space-x-md-4">
  <div class="p-3 border">First</div>
  <div class="p-3 border">Second</div>
  <div class="p-3 border">Third</div>
</div>
```

`space-y-4` spaces the stack, `space-y-md-0` drops that spacing once the items
sit in a row, and `space-x-md-4` takes over along the inline axis.

## How it works

> The generated rule is wrapped in `:where()`, so it adds **no specificity**: a
> child that sets its own margin — a utility, or a component that ships with
> one — still wins, and you never need `!important` to escape the container's
> spacing.

## Customizing

### Sass variables

Space utilities are generated from the `$spacers` map.

```scss
$spacer: 1rem !default;
```
```scss
$spacers: () !default;
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$spacers: defaults(
  (
    0: 0,
    1: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * .25),
    2: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * .375),
    3: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * .5),
    4: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * .75),
    5: var(--cui-spacer),
    6: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 1.25),
    7: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 1.5),
    8: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 1.75),
    9: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 2),
    10: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 2.25),
    11: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 2.5),
    12: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 3),
  ),
  $spacers
);
```

Space utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
"space-x": (
  responsive: true,
  property: margin-inline-end,
  class: space-x,
  child-selector: "> :not(:last-child)",
  values: $utilities-spacers
),
"space-y": (
  responsive: true,
  property: margin-block-end,
  class: space-y,
  child-selector: "> :not(:last-child)",
  values: $utilities-spacers
),
```

# Vue Text alignment Utilities

> Realign text with our responsive text alignment utilities.

## Text alignment

Easily realign text to components with text alignment classes. For start, end, and center alignment, responsive classes are available that use the same viewport width breakpoints as the grid system.

```html
<p class="text-start">Start aligned text on all viewport sizes.</p>
<p class="text-center">Center aligned text on all viewport sizes.</p>
<p class="text-end">End aligned text on all viewport sizes.</p>

<p class="text-sm-end">End aligned text on viewports sized SM (small) or wider.</p>
<p class="text-md-end">End aligned text on viewports sized MD (medium) or wider.</p>
<p class="text-lg-end">End aligned text on viewports sized LG (large) or wider.</p>
<p class="text-xl-end">End aligned text on viewports sized XL (extra large) or wider.</p>
<p class="text-2xl-end">End aligned text on viewports sized XXL (extra extra large) or wider.</p>
```

> Note that we don't provide utility classes for justified text. While, aesthetically, justified text might look more appealing, it does make word-spacing more random and therefore harder to read.

## Customizing

### Sass variables

Text alignment utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
"text-align": (
  responsive: true,
  property: text-align,
  class: text,
  values: (
    start: start,
    end: end,
    center: center,
  )
),
```

# Vue Text wrapping Utilities

> Control how text wraps, overflows, and breaks inside its container.

## Wrapping

Wrap text with a `.text-wrap` class.

```html
<div class="badge text-bg-primary text-wrap" style="width: 6rem">
  This text should wrap.
</div>
```

Prevent text from wrapping with a `.text-nowrap` class.

```html
<div class="text-nowrap bg-4 border" style="width: 8rem">
  This text should overflow the parent.
</div>
```

## Balance and pretty

`.text-balance` evens out the line lengths of short runs of text — headings, teasers — so no line is left with a lone word. `.text-pretty` asks the browser for better-looking wrapping of body text, at some rendering cost.

```html
<h4 class="text-balance bg-4 border" style="width: 15rem">A heading balanced across its lines</h4>
<p class="text-pretty bg-4 border" style="width: 15rem">A longer run of body text the browser wraps with fewer awkward line endings than the default.</p>
```

## Word break

Prevent long strings of text from breaking your components' layout by using `.text-break` to set `word-wrap: break-word` and `word-break: break-word`. We use `word-wrap` instead of the more common `overflow-wrap` for wider browser support, and add the deprecated `word-break: break-word` to avoid issues with flex containers.

```html
<p class="text-break">mmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm</p>
```

> Note that [breaking words isn't possible in Arabic](https://rtlstyling.com/posts/rtl-styling#3.-line-break), which is the most used RTL language. Therefore `.text-break` is removed from our RTL compiled CSS.

## Customizing

### Sass variables

Text wrapping utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
"white-space": (
  property: white-space,
  class: text,
  values: (
    wrap: normal,
    nowrap: nowrap,
  )
),
"word-wrap": (
  property: word-wrap word-break,
  class: text,
  values: (break: break-word),
),
"text-wrap": (
  property: text-wrap,
  class: text,
  values: balance pretty,
),
```

# Vue Theme Utilities

> Style utilities that pair a themed surface with the text color that reads on it, so any element can be colored the way component variants are.

## How it works

A [`.theme-{color}` class](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/customize/components/#theme-variants) sets the theme slot tokens — `--cui-theme-bg`, `--cui-theme-fg`, `--cui-theme-bg-subtle` and friends — without painting anything itself. Components read those slots on their own; for arbitrary markup, add one of the style utilities below to pair a themed surface with the text color that reads on it. `.theme-border` additionally draws a border in the theme's border color and composes with any of the three surfaces.

See [Theme](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/customize/theme/) for how the slots resolve and how to add a color of your own.

### Contrast

`.theme-contrast` fills with the solid theme color and sets the text to the color that reads on it — the pairing behind solid component variants:

### Subtle

`.theme-subtle` uses the theme's subtle surface with its readable foreground. The pairing adjusts to the color mode on its own:

And with `.theme-border`:

### Muted

`.theme-muted` uses the theme's muted surface with its emphasis foreground, for the quietest of the three pairings:

## Comparison

All three pairings side by side, per theme color:

## Mixing colors

Each element carries its own `.theme-{color}`, so siblings can differ — the utility reads whichever theme is in scope:

```html
<div class="d-flex gap-3">
  <div class="theme-success theme-contrast p-4 rounded">Success</div>
  <div class="theme-warning theme-contrast p-4 rounded">Warning</div>
  <div class="theme-danger theme-contrast p-4 rounded">Danger</div>
</div>
```

The theme can also come from any element above, so one wrapper themes every pairing inside it:

```html
<div class="theme-primary d-flex gap-3">
  <div class="theme-contrast p-4 rounded">Contrast</div>
  <div class="theme-subtle p-4 rounded">Subtle</div>
  <div class="theme-muted p-4 rounded">Muted</div>
</div>
```

## Reset

_Added in 6.0.0._

`.theme-reset` drops the theme a subtree inherits: it sets every `--cui-theme-*` slot back to `initial`, so components and utilities below it fall back to their defaults.

```html
<div class="theme-primary p-4 rounded">
  <span class="badge">Primary badge</span>
  <span class="badge theme-reset">Default badge</span>
</div>
```

```scss
@mixin theme-reset() {
  $slots: ();

  @each $slots-of-color in map.values($theme-colors) {
    @each $slot in map.keys($slots-of-color) {
      $slots: map.set($slots, $slot, true);
    }
  }

  @each $slot in map.keys(map.merge($slots, ("hover": true, "active": true))) {
    --cui-theme-#{$slot}: initial;
  }
}

@mixin generate-theme-reset() {
  .theme-reset {
    @include theme-reset();
  }
}
```

## Customizing

### Utilities API

Theme utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
// Theme style utilities — pair with .theme-{color} to apply coordinated
// background and text colors
"theme-contrast": (
  property: (
    "background-color": var(--cui-theme-bg),
    "color": var(--cui-theme-contrast)
  ),
  class: theme-contrast,
  values: (null: null)
),
"theme-subtle": (
  property: (
    "background-color": var(--cui-theme-bg-subtle),
    "color": var(--cui-theme-fg)
  ),
  class: theme-subtle,
  values: (null: null)
),
"theme-muted": (
  property: (
    "background-color": var(--cui-theme-bg-muted),
    "color": var(--cui-theme-fg-emphasis)
  ),
  class: theme-muted,
  values: (null: null)
),
"theme-border": (
  property: border,
  class: theme-border,
  values: (null: var(--cui-border-width) solid var(--cui-theme-border))
),
```

# Vue User select Utilities

> Change the way in which the content is selected when the user interacts with it.

## Text selection

Change the way in which the content is selected when the user interacts with it.

```html
<p class="user-select-all">This paragraph will be entirely selected when clicked by the user.</p>
<p class="user-select-auto">This paragraph has default select behavior.</p>
<p class="user-select-text">This paragraph is selectable even where an ancestor disables selection.</p>
<p class="user-select-none">This paragraph will not be selectable when clicked by the user.</p>
```

`.user-select-none` hides the text from the selection, not from the accessibility tree — a screen reader still reads it, and it is still copied when the user selects a surrounding block in some browsers. Use it for decorative or duplicated text, not to protect content.

```scss
"user-select": (
  property: user-select,
  values: all auto text none
),
```

# Vue Vertical alignment Utilities

> Easily change the vertical alignment of inline, inline-block, inline-table, and table cell elements.

Change the alignment of elements with the [`vertical-alignment`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/vertical-align) utilities. Please note that vertical-align only affects inline, inline-block, inline-table, and table cell elements.

Choose from `.align-baseline`, `.align-top`, `.align-middle`, `.align-bottom`, `.align-text-bottom`, and `.align-text-top` as needed.

To vertically center non-inline content (like `<div>`s and more), use our [flex box utilities](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/align-items/).

With inline elements:

```html
<span class="align-baseline">baseline</span>
<span class="align-top">top</span>
<span class="align-middle">middle</span>
<span class="align-bottom">bottom</span>
<span class="align-text-top">text-top</span>
<span class="align-text-bottom">text-bottom</span>
```

With table cells:

```html
<table style="height: 100px">
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td class="align-baseline">baseline</td>
      <td class="align-top">top</td>
      <td class="align-middle">middle</td>
      <td class="align-bottom">bottom</td>
      <td class="align-text-top">text-top</td>
      <td class="align-text-bottom">text-bottom</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

## Customizing

### Utilities API

Vertical align utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
"align": (
  property: vertical-align,
  class: align,
  values: baseline top middle bottom text-bottom text-top
),
```

# Vue Visibility Utilities

> Control the visibility of elements, without modifying their display, with visibility utilities.

Set the `visibility` of elements with our visibility utilities. These utility classes do not modify the `display` value at all and do not affect layout – `.invisible` elements still take up space in the page.

> Elements with the `.invisible` class will be hidden *both* visually and for assistive technology/screen reader users.

Apply `.visible` or `.invisible` as needed.

```vue
<div class="visible">...</div>
<div class="invisible">...</div>
```

```scss
// Class
.visible {
  visibility: visible;
}
.invisible {
  visibility: hidden;
}
```

## Customizing

### Utilities API

Visibility utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
"visibility": (
  property: visibility,
  class: null,
  values: (
    visible: visible,
    invisible: hidden,
  )
),
```

# Vue Width Utilities

> Set an element's width relative to its parent or to the viewport with our width utilities.

## Relative to the parent

Width utilities are generated from the utility API in `_utilities.scss`. Includes support for `25%`, `50%`, `75%`, `100%`, and `auto` by default. Modify those values as you need to generate different utilities here.

```html
<div class="w-25 p-4" style="background-color: #eee">Width 25%</div>
<div class="w-50 p-4" style="background-color: #eee">Width 50%</div>
<div class="w-75 p-4" style="background-color: #eee">Width 75%</div>
<div class="w-100 p-4" style="background-color: #eee">Width 100%</div>
<div class="w-auto p-4" style="background-color: #eee">Width auto</div>
```

## Fixed widths

`.w-1` through `.w-12` set a width from the `$sizes` map, one `$spacer` (1rem) per step, for boxes that should hold their size whatever the parent does — an avatar column, a fixed label, a swatch.

```html
<div class="w-4 p-3 bg-2">.w-4</div>
<div class="w-8 p-3 bg-2">.w-8</div>
<div class="w-12 p-3 bg-2">.w-12</div>
```

## Max width

Use `.max-w-100` to cap an element at the width of its parent — the usual reason to reach for it is an image or an SVG that would otherwise overflow.

```html
<svg class="docs-placeholder-img max-w-100" width="100%" height="100" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Max-width 100%" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice" focusable="false"><title>Max-width 100%</title><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#868e96"></rect><text x="50%" y="50%" fill="#dee2e6" dy=".3em">Max-width 100%</text></svg>
```

## Min width

`.min-w-0` and `.min-w-100` set a floor rather than a cap.

`.min-w-0` is the one you reach for most. A flex or grid child starts at `min-width: auto`, which refuses to shrink below its own content — and a `.text-truncate` child never breaks its line, so its content width is the whole string. The item pushes past its track instead of ellipsizing. Dropping the floor to `0` lets it shrink so the truncation can happen.

```html
<div class="d-flex gap-3 border p-3 mb-3" style="max-width: 320px">
  <div class="text-truncate">Without a floor this line pushes the button out of the box</div>
  <CButton theme="primary" class="flex-shrink-0">Action</CButton>
</div>
<div class="d-flex gap-3 border p-3" style="max-width: 320px">
  <div class="min-w-0 text-truncate">With .min-w-0 the same line truncates instead</div>
  <CButton theme="primary" class="flex-shrink-0">Action</CButton>
</div>
```

## Relative to the viewport

`.vw-100` sets the width to the full viewport, `.min-vw-100` sets it as a floor.

```vue
<div class="min-vw-100">Min-width 100vw</div>
<div class="vw-100">Width 100vw</div>
```

## Dynamic viewport width

A mobile browser resizes the viewport as it shows or hides its URL bar, so `vw` units can end up wider than the visible area. The `dvw` unit tracks that change instead of the largest possible viewport.

```vue
<div class="min-dvw-100">Min-width 100dvw</div>
<div class="dvw-100">Width 100dvw</div>
```

## Intrinsic widths

Size an element from its content instead of its container: `.w-min` (the widest unbreakable word), `.w-max` (the full unwrapped content), `.w-fit` (the content, capped at the container).

```html
<div class="w-min p-3 mb-3 bg-4 border">Min width</div>
<div class="w-max p-3 mb-3 bg-4 border">Max width</div>
<div class="w-fit p-3 bg-4 border">Fit width</div>
```

## Customizing

### Sass maps

Each entry is one `.w-{step}` class and the width it sets. Add a key to define a step, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
$sizes: () !default;
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$sizes: defaults(
  (
    1: var(--cui-spacer),
    2: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 2),
    3: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 3),
    4: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 4),
    5: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 5),
    6: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 6),
    7: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 7),
    8: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 8),
    9: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 9),
    10: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 10),
    11: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 11),
    12: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * 12)
  ),
  $sizes
);
```

### Utilities API

Width utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
"width": (
  property: width,
  class: w,
  values: map.merge(
    $sizes,
    (
      25: 25%,
      50: 50%,
      75: 75%,
      100: 100%,
      auto: auto,
      min: min-content,
      max: max-content,
      fit: fit-content
    )
  )
),
"max-width": (
  property: max-width,
  class: max-w,
  values: (100: 100%)
),
"min-width": (
  property: min-width,
  class: min-w,
  values: (
    0: 0,
    100: 100%,
  )
),
"viewport-width": (
  property: width,
  class: vw,
  values: (100: 100vw)
),
"min-viewport-width": (
  property: min-width,
  class: min-vw,
  values: (100: 100vw)
),
"dynamic-viewport-width": (
  property: width,
  class: dvw,
  values: (100: 100dvw)
),
"min-dynamic-viewport-width": (
  property: min-width,
  class: min-dvw,
  values: (100: 100dvw)
),
```

# Vue Z-index Utilities

> Use our low-level `z-index` utilities to quickly change the stack level of an element or component.

## Example

Use `z-index` utilities to stack elements on top of one another. Requires a `position` value other than `static`, which can be set with custom styles or using our [position utilities](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/position/).

We call these "low-level" `z-index` utilities because of their default values of `-1` through `3`, which we use for the layout of overlapping components. The library's overlay layers are available as utilities too — see [Overlays](#overlays) below.

```html
<div class="z-3 position-absolute p-6 rounded-3"><span>z-3</span></div>
<div class="z-2 position-absolute p-6 rounded-3"><span>z-2</span></div>
<div class="z-1 position-absolute p-6 rounded-3"><span>z-1</span></div>
<div class="z-0 position-absolute p-6 rounded-3"><span>z-0</span></div>
<div class="z-n1 position-absolute p-6 rounded-3"><span>z-n1</span></div>
```

## Overlays

CoreUI overlay components—dropdown, modal, offcanvas, popover, toast, and tooltip—all have their own `z-index` values to ensure a usable experience with competing "layers" of an interface.

_Added in 6.0.0._

Each of those layers has a matching utility, so your own element can join a layer by name instead of repeating the number it happens to have: `.z-dropdown` / `.z-menu`, `.z-sticky`, `.z-fixed`, `.z-sidebar-backdrop`, `.z-sidebar`, `.z-offcanvas` / `.z-drawer`, `.z-modal` / `.z-dialog`, `.z-popover`, `.z-tooltip` and `.z-toast`. The three pairs share a value: the menu, drawer and dialog are the successors of the dropdown, offcanvas and modal, and sit on the same layer.

```html
<div class="position-relative" style="height: 6rem">
  <div class="z-modal position-absolute top-0 start-0 p-4 bg-subtle-primary border rounded">Sits at the modal layer</div>
</div>
```

Read about the values themselves in the [`z-index` layout page](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/layout/z-index/).

## Customizing

### Sass maps

Customize this Sass map to change the available values and generated utilities.

```scss
$zindex-levels: () !default;
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$zindex-levels: defaults(
  (
    n1: -1,
    0: 0,
    1: 1,
    2: 2,
    3: 3,
    dropdown: 1000,
    menu: 1000,
    sticky: 1020,
    fixed: 1030,
    sidebar-backdrop: 1034,
    sidebar: 1035,
    offcanvas: 1045,
    drawer: 1045,
    modal: 1055,
    dialog: 1055,
    popover: 1070,
    tooltip: 1080,
    toast: 1090
  ),
  $zindex-levels
);
```

### Utilities API

Position utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
"z-index": (
  property: z-index,
  class: z,
  values: $zindex-levels,
),
```


---

# Vue Widget Blocks

> Ready-made dashboard statistic blocks built from a Vue card and utilities — copy the markup, keep it, change it.

## How it works

A block is markup you copy into your project, not a component you import. Every block on this page is a [card](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/card/) plus [spacing](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/margin/), [color](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/colors/) and [typography](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/font-size/) utilities, so it ships no CSS of its own and there is no class here that the rest of the library does not already document.

That is the whole point of keeping them as blocks: a statistic card is a layout decision. Once the markup is yours, a widget can grow a second value, lose its chart or change its heading level without waiting for a prop.

The charts are real [chart components](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/chart/) — the same configurations the widget page rendered.

> ##### `CCardBody` lays its children out in a column
> 
> The body is a flex column that packs its children to the start, so anything meant to sit side by side inside one needs `flex-row`, a `CRow` inside it needs `w-100`, and a full-width child needs `w-100` too. Putting the row classes on the body itself does not work: the body's own `flex-direction: column` wins.

            <CIcon :icon="cilChartPie" :height="24" />
          </div>
          <div>
            <div class="fs-6 fw-semibold fg-warning">89.9%</div>
            <div class="fg-2 text-uppercase fw-semibold small">Widget title</div>
          </div>
        </CCardBody>
        <CCardFooter>
          <CLink
            class="fw-semibold small fg-2"
            href="https://coreui.io/"
            rel="noopener noreferrer"
            target="_blank"
          >
            View more
            <CIcon :icon="cilArrowRight" class="float-end" :width="16" />
          </CLink>
        </CCardFooter>
      </CCard>
    </CCol>
  </CRow>
</template>

# Vue templates installation

> Learn how to use CoreUI Vue Admin Dashboard Templates including npm scripts to build templates, compile source code, run tests, and more.

## Tooling setup

CoreUI Vue Admin Templates uses [npm scripts](https://docs.npmjs.com/misc/scripts/) for its build system. Our `package.json` includes convenient methods for working with the framework, including compiling code, running tests, and more.

To use our build system and run our admin template locally, you'll need a copy of source files and Node. Follow these steps and you should be ready to rock:

1. [Download and install Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download/), which we use to manage our dependencies.
2. If you prefer to use Yarn instead of NPM, you have to [download and install it](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/lang/en/docs/install/)
3. [Download CoreUI Vue Admin Template](https://coreui.io/product/free-vue-admin-template/) or [Download CoreUI PRO Vue Admin Template](https://coreui.io/download/).
4. Navigate to the root template directory and run `npm install` or `yarn install` to install our local dependencies listed in `package.json`.

When completed, you'll be able to run the various commands provided from the command line.

## Using npm scripts

Our `package.json` includes numerous tasks for developing the project. Run `npm run` or `yarn run` to see all the npm scripts in your terminal. **Primary tasks include:**

| Task | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run serve` or `yarn serve` | Compiles CSS and JavaScript, builds the documentation, and starts a local server. |
| `npm run build` or `yarn build` | Creates the `dist/` directory with compiled files. Uses [Sass](https://sass-lang.com/), [Autoprefixer](https://github.com/postcss/autoprefixer). |
| `npm test` or `yarn test` | Runs tests locally  |

## Sass

CoreUI uses [Dart Sass](https://sass-lang.com/dart-sass) for compiling our Sass source files into CSS files (included in our build process), and we recommend you do the same if you're compiling Sass using your own asset pipeline.

Dart Sass uses a rounding precision of 10 and for efficiency reasons does not allow adjustment of this value. We don't lower this precision during further processing of our generated CSS, such as during minification, but if you chose to do so we recommend maintaining a precision of at least 6 to prevent issues with browser rounding.

## Autoprefixer

We uses [Autoprefixer][autoprefixer] (included in our build process) to automatically add vendor prefixes to some CSS properties at build time. Doing so saves us time and code by allowing us to write key parts of our CSS a single time while eliminating the need for vendor mixins like those found in v3.

We maintain the list of browsers supported through Autoprefixer in a separate file within our GitHub repository. See `.browserslistrc`.

## Local template

Here's how to get it started:

1. Run through the [tooling setup](#tooling-setup) above to install all dependencies.
2. From the root template directory, run `npm run start` or `yarn start` in the command line.
3. Open `http://localhost:8080` in your browser, and voilà.

## Troubleshooting

Should you encounter problems with installing dependencies, uninstall all previous dependency versions (global and local). Then, rerun `npm install` or `yarn install`.

# Customize Vue templates

> Learn how to theme, customize, and extend CoreUI Vue Templates with Sass, a boatload of global options.

## Overview

There are multiple ways to customize CoreUI for Vue. Your best path can depend on your project, the complexity of your build tools, the version of CoreUI for Vue you're using, browser support, and more.

Our two preferred methods are:

1. You can extend our source files.
2. You can override CoreUI’s styles.

## File structure

Utilize our source Sass files to take advantage of variables, maps, mixins, and functions to help you build faster and customize your project.

Whenever possible, avoid modifying CoreUI's core files. For Sass, that means creating your own stylesheet that imports CoreUI for Vue so you can modify and extend it. Assuming you're using a package manager like npm, you'll have a file structure that looks like this:

```text
your-project/
├── ...
├── node_modules/
│   ├── @coreui/coreui
│   │   ├── scss
│   │   └── ...
│   └── @coreui/vue
│       └── ...
├── src
│   └── scss
│       ├── _custom.scss
│       ├── ...
│       ├── _variables.scss
│       └── ...
└── ...
```

If you use CoreUI PRO version.

```text
your-project/
├── ...
├── node_modules/
│   ├── @coreui/coreui-pro 
│   │   ├── scss
│   │   └── ...
│   └── @coreui/vue-pro
│       └── ...
├── src
│   └── scss
│       ├── _custom.scss
│       ├── ...
│       ├── _variables.scss
│       └── ...
└── ...
```

## Variable defaults

Every Sass variable in CoreUI for Vue includes the `!default` flag allowing you to override the variable's default value in your own Sass without modifying CoreUI's source code. Copy and paste variables as needed, modify their values, and remove the `!default` flag. If a variable has already been assigned, then it won't be re-assigned by the default values in CoreUI.

You will find the complete list of CoreUI's variables in `node_modules/@coreui/coreui/scss/_variables.scss` or in `node_modules/@coreui/coreui-pro/scss/_variables.scss`. Some variables are set to `null`, these variables don't output the property unless they are overridden in your configuration. You can also find a specific component variables list in **Customizing** section ex. [Alerts - Customizing](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/alert/styling/#css-variables)

Here's an example that changes the `background-color` and `color` for the `<body>` when importing and compiling CoreUI for Vue via npm:

```scss
// _variables.scss

// Default variable overrides
$theme-bgs: ("body": #000);
$theme-fgs: ("body": #111);
```

## Custom styles and overrides

In your `custom.scss`, you can put custom code for CoreUI's components or your own styles.

```scss
// _custom.scss

// Additional custom code here
.custom-component {
  border: 2px solid #222;
}
```

# Migration to v5

> Track and review changes to the CoreUI for Vue.js components to help you migrate from v4 to v5.

CoreUI for Vue is the Vue.js version of CoreUI components library, so before read this migration guide, please check also [CoreUI 4 to 5 migration guide](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/migration/v5/).

## Dependencies

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> The `vue` peer dependency changed from `^3.2.21` to `^3.5.0`. Upgrade Vue to 3.5 or newer.
- `@coreui/coreui-pro` is now a dependency of `@coreui/vue-pro`, not a peer dependency. Keep it in your own `package.json` if you import the stylesheet from it.
- `@popperjs/core` is now a dependency of `@coreui/vue-pro`. In v4 it was bundled into the build. You do not need to install it yourself.
- `date-fns` is no longer bundled. v4 used it for the `format` property of the date pickers. Install it yourself if you use it in `inputDateFormat`.
- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> The build files moved. The ES build moved from `dist/index.es.js` to `dist/esm/index.js`, the CommonJS build from `dist/index.js` to `dist/cjs/index.js`, and the types from `dist/index.d.ts` to `dist/esm/index.d.ts`. Import from the package root, `@coreui/vue-pro`, instead of a build file.

## Components

### CAlertHeading

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CAvatar

- Deprecated `textColor` values: `muted`, `high-emphasis`, `medium-emphasis`, `disabled`, `high-emphasis-inverse`, `medium-emphasis-inverse`, `disabled-inverse`. The property validator no longer accepts them, so Vue logs a warning in development. The classes still render.
- New `textColor` values: `primary-emphasis`, `secondary-emphasis`, `success-emphasis`, `danger-emphasis`, `warning-emphasis`, `info-emphasis`, `light-emphasis`, `body`, `body-emphasis`, `body-secondary`, `body-tertiary`, `black`, `black-50`, `white`, `white-50`.

### CBadge

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.
- Deprecated `textColor` values: `muted`, `high-emphasis`, `medium-emphasis`, `disabled`, `high-emphasis-inverse`, `medium-emphasis-inverse`, `disabled-inverse`. The property validator no longer accepts them, so Vue logs a warning in development. The classes still render.
- New `textColor` values: `primary-emphasis`, `secondary-emphasis`, `success-emphasis`, `danger-emphasis`, `warning-emphasis`, `info-emphasis`, `light-emphasis`, `body`, `body-emphasis`, `body-secondary`, `body-tertiary`, `black`, `black-50`, `white`, `white-50`.

### CButton

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CCalendar

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed the `calendar-cell-hover` event to `date-hover`. It still emits the hovered date, or `null` when the pointer leaves.

### CCard

- Deprecated `textColor` values: `muted`, `high-emphasis`, `medium-emphasis`, `disabled`, `high-emphasis-inverse`, `medium-emphasis-inverse`, `disabled-inverse`. The property validator no longer accepts them, so Vue logs a warning in development. The classes still render.
- New `textColor` values: `primary-emphasis`, `secondary-emphasis`, `success-emphasis`, `danger-emphasis`, `warning-emphasis`, `info-emphasis`, `light-emphasis`, `body`, `body-emphasis`, `body-secondary`, `body-tertiary`, `black`, `black-50`, `white`, `white-50`.

### CCardHeader

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CCardImage

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CCardSubtitle

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CCardText

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CCardTitle

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CCloseButton

- Deprecated property `white`, use `dark` instead.

### CDatePicker

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> The `format` property no longer formats the date. Use `inputDateFormat` instead. Without `inputDateFormat`, the date is formatted with the `locale` property.

```vue
// Previous markup
<CDatePicker format="MMMM-dd-yyyy"/>

// New markup
import { format } from 'date-fns'
//...
<CDatePicker :inputDateFormat="(date) => format(new Date(date), 'MMMM-dd-yyyy')" />
```

- `format` still makes the input read-only, as it did in v4. If you remove it and want to keep the input read-only, set `inputReadOnly`.
- Pair a custom `inputDateFormat` with `inputDateParse`, so a typed date is read back with the same pattern.
- The `date-change` event still emits the date object and the formatted string. The formatted string now follows `inputDateFormat`, or the `locale` property, instead of `format`.

### CDateRangePicker

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> The `format` property no longer formats the date. Use `inputDateFormat` instead. Without `inputDateFormat`, the date is formatted with the `locale` property.

```vue
// Previous markup
<CDateRangePicker format="MMMM-dd-yyyy"/>

// New markup
import { format } from 'date-fns'
//...
<CDateRangePicker :inputDateFormat="(date) => format(new Date(date), 'MMMM-dd-yyyy')" />
```

- `format` still makes the inputs read-only, as it did in v4. If you remove it and want to keep the inputs read-only, set `inputReadOnly`.
- Pair a custom `inputDateFormat` with `inputDateParse`, so a typed date is read back with the same pattern.
- The `start-date-change` and `end-date-change` events still emit the date object and the formatted string. The formatted string now follows `inputDateFormat`, or the `locale` property, instead of `format`.
- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Removed the `indicator`, `cleaner` and `separator` slots. The icons come from the stylesheet. The `indicator`, `cleaner` and `separator` properties still show or hide them.

### CDropdown

- The default `variant` changed from `btn-group` to `dropdown`. The wrapper gets the `.dropdown` class instead of `.btn-group`. Set `variant="btn-group"` to keep the v4 markup.

### CDropdownHeader

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CDropdownItem

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CDropdownMenu

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CDropdownToggle

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.
- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Removed property `active`. Add `class="active"` if you need the style.

### CFormFeedback

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CFormRange

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `steps` property to `step`.

### CFormText

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CLoadingButton

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CModalTitle

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CMultiSelect

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Removed key `text` in the options list, use `label` instead.

### CNav

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.
- The `underline` variant has been changed to `underline-border`. Use `variant="underline-border"` to keep the v4 look. `underline` is now a different, simpler style.

### CNavbar

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CNavbarBrand

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CNavbarNav

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CNavItem

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Removed property `component`. In v4 it set the element of the inner link. In v5, `as` sets the element of the wrapper, `li` by default. To change the link element, put a `CNavLink` inside.

```vue
// Previous markup
<CNavItem component="button" href="#">Docs</CNavItem>

// New markup
<CNavItem>
  <CNavLink as="button" href="#">Docs</CNavLink>
</CNavItem>
```

### CProgress

- New `CProgressStacked` component for stacked bars. Put one `CProgress` per segment inside it. Several `CProgressBar` elements inside one `CProgress` still render.

```vue
// Previous markup
<CProgress>
  <CProgressBar :value="15" />
  <CProgressBar color="success" :value="30" />
</CProgress>

// New markup
<CProgressStacked>
  <CProgress :value="15" />
  <CProgress color="success" :value="30" />
</CProgressStacked>
```

### CSidebar

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Sidebar has a light color scheme by default, use `colorScheme="dark"` to make it dark.
- Without the `visible` property, the sidebar is now shown on desktop. In v4 it was hidden. An `overlaid` sidebar still starts hidden.

### CSpinner

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.

### CTimePicker

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Removed the `indicator` and `cleaner` slots. The icons come from the stylesheet. The `indicator` and `cleaner` properties still show or hide them.

### CToastClose

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Renamed `component` property to `as`.
- Deprecated property `white`, use `dark` instead.

### CToastHeader

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> Removed the `close` event. Listen to the `close` event of the parent `CToast` instead.

```vue
// Previous markup
<CToast>
  <CToastHeader closeButton @close="onClose">Title</CToastHeader>
</CToast>

// New markup
<CToast @close="onClose">
  <CToastHeader closeButton>Title</CToastHeader>
</CToast>
```

## Directives

### v-c-popover and v-c-tooltip

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> `content` and `header` are inserted as text, not HTML. Markup in the value shows as literal tags. For HTML content, use `CPopover` or `CTooltip` and the `content` slot (and the `title` slot of `CPopover`).

# Migration to v6

> Track and review changes to the CoreUI for Vue.js components to help you migrate from v5 to v6.

CoreUI for Vue is the Vue.js version of the CoreUI components library, so before reading this
migration guide, please also check the
[CoreUI 5 to 6 migration guide](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/migration/v6/) — it covers the
markup, class names, Sass architecture and design tokens this release is built on. This page covers
what changes in the Vue API.

## Dependencies

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **Popper is gone; positioning runs on
  [Floating UI](https://floating-ui.com/).** `@popperjs/core` is replaced by `@floating-ui/dom`.
  Update your lockfile — nothing else is required for the default configuration.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`popperConfig` is now `floatingConfig`** on
  `CDropdown`, `CPopover` and `CTooltip`, and it takes a Floating UI
  [`ComputePositionConfig`](https://floating-ui.com/docs/computePosition#options) instead of a
  Popper one. The `popper` boolean prop stays and still switches static positioning.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **Positioned elements are stamped with
  `data-coreui-placement`**, not `data-popper-placement`. Custom CSS, tests or scripts keyed on the
  old attribute must be updated. The v6 stylesheet draws tooltip, popover and menu arrows from this
  attribute, so it is not optional.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The exported composables are renamed**:
  `usePopper` → `useFloating`, `useDropdownWithPopper` → `useDropdownWithFloating`.

## New components

- **`CCombobox`** — a `.form-control` toggle over a popup list box: the options are
  `CListBoxOption` children or an `items` array, the selection is single or multiple, the panel
  takes an optional search field with `searchNormalize`, and `name` submits the value through a
  hidden select that takes part in form validation. Ships with the `useCombobox()` composable.
- **`CDateInput`, `CTimeInput`** — section fields: a masked, keyboard-first
  input where every part of the value (day, month, year, hour…) is its own editable section.
  `<CDateInput type="datetime">` carries the time too. The pickers are built on them, and they
  work standalone.
- **`CDialog`** and **`CDrawer`** — the native-`<dialog>` popup and side panel with the Bootstrap 6
  look and the `dialog-*` / `drawer-*` classes. `CDialog` is a centered floating panel over a
  blurred backdrop with optional slide-in variants; `CDrawer` is a floating, inset, rounded panel
  with sheet, translucent, fit-content and fullscreen variants plus responsive breakpoints.
  `CDialog`'s `fullscreen` takes a breakpoint as well as `true`, like `CModal`'s.

  They share their behavior with `CModal` and `COffcanvas`, which keep the classic look and the v5
  vocabulary — and one event vocabulary of their own: `show`, `close` and `close-prevented` on
  both, where the legacy pair says `hide`. **`CModal` and `COffcanvas` are deprecated and may be
  removed in v7** — prefer `CDialog` and `CDrawer` for new work. Pick one per surface; they are
  independent components.
- **`CListBox`** — the ARIA listbox pattern as a component: single, multiple or no selection,
  sections, descriptions, link options, an empty state, typeahead and an `activeDescendant` mode
  that keeps the focus in your own input. Ships with `CListBoxOption`, `CListBoxSection`,
  `CListBoxEmpty`, the header parts (`CListBoxHeader`, `CListBoxSelectAll`, `CListBoxTitle`,
  `CListBoxSubtitle`) and the `useListBox()` composable.
- **`CMenu`** — contextual overlays with submenus, container teleport, responsive placement and
  logical (`start`/`end`) placements. Ships with `CMenuToggle`, `CMenuContent`, `CMenuItem`,
  `CMenuHeader`, `CMenuDivider`, `CMenuText`, `CSubmenu` and the `useMenu()` composable. See the
  [Menu docs](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/components/menu/).
- **`CNumberInput`** — a number field with a stepper you can hit, in place of the browser's own
  spinner (tiny in some engines, absent on iOS). `min`, `max` and `step` stay native.
- **`CTransfer`** — two list boxes and four buttons that move values between them, with a
  select-all header and counter per list, an optional search, a one-way mode and an announcement
  of every move through `announce()`. Ships with the `useTransfer()` composable.

## Field components

`CAutocomplete`, `CMultiSelect`, `CDatePicker`, `CDateRangePicker` and `CTimePicker` are built on
one frame and one panel. These two changes apply to all five; the per-component sections below
cover what is specific to each.

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **A field component *is* the frame.** It carries
  `.form-control-group` on its own root instead of nesting one, so a field is a direct child of an
  `.input-group` like any other control and there is no wrapper level to reach through. Custom CSS
  written as `.date-picker .form-control-group` no longer matches anything. On the pickers, the
  label and the validation feedback also move out of the frame.

  The frame replaces the per-component shells: `.autocomplete-input-group`,
  `.form-multi-select-input-group` and their `-sm`/`-lg` variants are gone, the adornments are
  `.form-control-cleaner` / `.form-control-action` (replacing `.autocomplete-cleaner`,
  `.form-multi-select-cleaner`, `.autocomplete-indicator`, `.form-multi-select-indicator`), and the
  `size` prop puts `.form-control-sm` / `.form-control-lg` on the frame itself.

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The options/picker panel exists only while it
  is open.** It is built when the field opens and removed once the exit transition has played, so a
  closed field carries no panel markup at all — code that queried `.combobox-popup` or
  `.date-picker-popup` up front, or held a ref to it across a close, needs to look it up per open.

## Theme colors

<span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`light` and `dark` are replaced by `inverse`.**
They were theme colors named after a color scheme and neither followed one: `<CButton color="dark">`
stayed near-black on a near-black page. There are seven colors now — `primary`, `secondary`,
`success`, `info`, `warning`, `danger`, `inverse` — and the runtime validator lists them, so
`color="dark"` and `color="light"` warn in the console instead of passing silently.

- **`color="dark"` becomes `theme="inverse"`.** `inverse` resolves to gray-900 in light mode and
  gray-100 in dark, so it stands against the page in both.
- **`color="light"` becomes `theme="secondary"`.** `secondary` is the light neutral now (gray-100 /
  gray-600) rather than the mid gray-blue `#6b7785`, so components already using it change
  appearance.
- **Where the class was painting a plain panel** rather than naming a color, reach for
  `bg-4` or `bg-3`; where it was a fixed dark backdrop, set
  `data-coreui-theme="dark"` on the container.

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`color` on buttons is deprecated in favour of
  `theme`.** A v6 button is a shape plus a colour: `variant` picks the shape (`solid`, `outline`,
  `subtle`, `ghost`) and `theme` picks the colour. `color` renders the v5 spelling `btn-{color}`,
  which fuses the two and cannot inherit a colour from an ancestor; it still works and is removed in
  v7. `` becomes ``, and
  `` becomes
  ``. `color="link"` becomes the
  `link` property — a link button is a shape, not a colour, and it takes its colour from the link
  colour rather than from a theme. `color="transparent"` is gone with the
  `.btn-transparent` class it rendered — use `variant="ghost"`, which shows nothing but the
  button's content until hover and carries the base styling on its own.

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The theme colour tokens finish their rename.**
  `--cui-{color}-text-emphasis` is `--cui-{color}-fg-emphasis` and
  `--cui-{color}-border-subtle` is `--cui-{color}-border`, matching the slot names the
  components already read. Custom CSS naming the old tokens has to follow; the class names
  (`.text-primary-emphasis`, `.border-primary-subtle`) are unchanged.

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The bare theme colour tokens are gone.**
  `--cui-primary`, `--cui-secondary`, `--cui-success`, `--cui-info`, `--cui-warning`,
  `--cui-danger` and `--cui-inverse` no longer exist. A theme colour is its set of slots —
  `-base`, `-bg`, `-fg`, `-fg-emphasis`, `-bg-subtle`, `-bg-muted`, `-border`, `-focus-ring`,
  `-contrast` — and the colour itself is the `-base` slot: `--cui-primary-base` is what
  `--cui-primary` was, the 100–900 scale is mixed from it, and `-bg` (the action background)
  points at it. Rename reads one to one, in custom CSS and in the inline styles the
  examples use to retint a component:

  ```diff
  - 
  + 

  - :root { --cui-primary: #6f42c1; }
  + :root { --cui-primary-500: #6f42c1; }
  ```

  No component prop is affected — `theme="primary"` is unchanged.

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The palette is the theme colours.**
  `$colors` holds `primary`, `success`, `info`, `warning`, `danger` and `gray`; the ten
  hues (`$blue` … `$cyan`) and every `--cui-{hue}` and `--cui-{hue}-{stop}` token are
  gone, as are `$secondary` and `$inverse`. Each `$theme-colors` entry points `base` and
  `bg` at its palette's `500` stop and the other slots at that scale; `secondary` reads
  `--cui-gray-200` and `inverse` `--cui-gray-900`. No palette token is bare: the literal
  sits in `-500`, so `--cui-gray-500` is what `--cui-gray` was, and `--cui-primary-500` is
  the runtime knob for the whole family:

  ```diff
  - :root { --cui-primary-base: #6f42c1; }
  + :root { --cui-primary-500: #6f42c1; }

  - 
  + 
  ```

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **Under a theme the theme wins over a component color token.** A component
  reads the `--cui-theme-*` slot on the property and its own token only as the fallback. In v5 the
  color came from the component's tokens, so a token you set on a colored alert applied; in v6 a
  token set on a themed component, or for the whole page in your CSS or a `$…-tokens` map, changes
  only the components without a theme. To recolor one themed component, set the slot instead:
  `<CAlert theme="danger" :style="{ '--cui-theme-bg-subtle': '#fde2e4' }">`.
- **Variants keep the component token as the override point.** Button variants, `variant="solid"`
  on an alert, `subtle` and `outline` on a badge, `subtle` on an avatar and `outline` on a chip map
  the component tokens to their own slots and paint from the tokens, so there a component token you
  set wins over the theme. Validation states win over a theme too.

## Surface ladder

<span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The neutral surfaces are a numbered ladder.**
`.bg-body-secondary`, `.bg-body-tertiary`, `.text-body-secondary` and `.text-body-tertiary` are
deprecated in favor of ordinal names: `.bg-1` … `.bg-4` for surfaces and `.fg-body`, `.fg-1` …
`.fg-4` for the text hierarchy, with two new rungs (`.bg-1`, `.bg-2`) between the body and the old
surfaces. The deprecated names render identically and are removed in v7. The tokens moved with
them — `--cui-bg-body`, `--cui-bg-1` … and `--cui-fg-body`, `--cui-fg-1` … are canonical, and
`--cui-secondary-bg`, `--cui-tertiary-bg`, `--cui-secondary-color`, `--cui-tertiary-color`,
`--cui-body-bg` and `--cui-body-color` remain as aliases until v7. No component prop is affected.

The deprecated surface names sit two rungs lower than they first did: `.bg-body-secondary`
renders `--cui-bg-3` and `.bg-body-tertiary` `--cui-bg-2`, the v5 stops one rung apart, while
`.text-body-secondary` stays `--cui-fg-2` and `.text-body-tertiary` `--cui-fg-3` — tertiary text
was the lighter of the two in v5 and still is.

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The ladder is three Sass maps, not a row of
  scalars.** `$theme-bgs`, `$theme-fgs` and `$theme-borders` replace `$bg-body`, `$bg-1` …
  `$bg-4`, `$fg-body`, `$fg-1` … `$fg-4`, `$border-subtle`, `$border-muted` and
  `$border-emphasized`. Each map lives in `scss/_theme.scss` in the `defaults()` shape, `:root`
  emits every entry as `--cui-bg-{key}`, `--cui-fg-{key}` or `--cui-border-{key}`, and the
  `.bg-*`, `.fg-*` and `.border-*` utilities are generated from the same maps. `$border-color`
  stays a scalar — it is the default every component reads, not a rung. Override an entry
  instead of a variable:

  ```diff
  - $bg-body: #000;
  - $fg-body: #111;
  + $theme-bgs: ("body": #000);
  + $theme-fgs: ("body": #111);
  ```

## Sass options

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`$enable-important-utilities` is gone with the
  `!important` suffix.** Utilities are emitted in the last cascade layer, so they already beat
  every component and modifier without it, and no switch brings the suffix back. The one case
  it covered is your own **unlayered** CSS, which beats every layer: move that CSS into
  `@layer custom` and utilities win again.
- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`$enable-negative-margins` is gone with the
  `.m*-n*` utilities.** Two negative inline steps ship unconditionally — `.me--1`, `.me--2`,
  `.ms--1` and `.ms--2` — from the `$negative-spacers` map; add a key there to extend the set.
  The block margins have no negative form.

## Breakpoints

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The `xxl` breakpoint prop is `2xl`, and the
  three largest breakpoints move.** `lg` is `1024px` (was 992), `xl` `1280px` (was 1200) and the
  top tier is `2xl` at `1536px` (was `xxl` at 1400); `sm` and `md` are unchanged. A prop whose name
  starts with a digit needs the shorthand or the colon form in a template — `<CCol :2xl="6">`,
  `<CContainer 2xl>` — and a quoted key in an options object.

  | v5 | v6 |
  | --- | --- |
  | `<CCol xxl="6">` | `<CCol :2xl="6">` |
  | `<CRow :xxl="{ cols: 3 }">` | `<CRow :2xl="{ cols: 3 }">` |
  | `<CContainer xxl>` | `<CContainer 2xl>` |
  | `<CPlaceholder :xxl="4">` | `<CPlaceholder :2xl="4">` |
  | `v-c-placeholder="{ xxl: 4 }"` | `v-c-placeholder="{ '2xl': 4 }"` |
  | `<CDropdown :alignment="{ xxl: 'end' }">` | `<CDropdown :alignment="{ '2xl': 'end' }">` |
  | `<CDialog fullscreen="xxl">`, `<CModal fullscreen="xxl">` | `fullscreen="2xl"` |
  | `<CDrawer responsive="xxl">`, `<COffcanvas responsive="xxl">` | `responsive="2xl"` |
  | `<CHeader container="xxl">`, `<CNavbar container="xxl">` | `container="2xl"` |
  | `<CNavbar expand="xxl">` | `expand="2xl"` |
  | `<CListGroup layout="horizontal-xxl">` | `layout="horizontal-2xl"` |
  | `<CTable responsive="xxl">` | `responsive="2xl"` |

- **Responsive placement reads the new scale.** `placement="top 2xl:bottom"` on `CMenu`,
  `CPopover` and `CTooltip` replaces the `xxl:` prefix, and `lg:`/`xl:` switch at 1024px and
  1280px.
- **The exported `Breakpoints` type ends in `'2xl'`** instead of `'xxl'`.
- **Size variants that spell `xxl` are not breakpoints and keep their name** — `CIcon`'s
  `size="xxl"` among them.

## Grid and sizing

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **A denser spacing scale.** `$spacers` has thirteen steps, `0`–`12`: `.25 / .375 / .5 / .75 / 1 / 1.25 / 1.5 / 1.75 / 2 / 2.25 / 2.5 / 3 rem` from `1` (v5: `.25 / .5 / 1 / 1.5 / 3`). Every spacing, gap, space and gutter utility changes value under the same number, and so do the numeric `gutter`, `gutterX` and `gutterY` values of `CRow`; the v5 steps map to v6 as `1`→`1`, `2`→`3`, `3`→`5`, `4`→`7`, `5`→`12`. `p-3` becomes `p-5`, `mb-4` becomes `mb-7`, `<CRow :xs="{ gutter: 3 }">` becomes a gutter of `5`. Components keep their size, cards aside (see `CCard`): their tokens read the stops that carry the v5 values.

- **New: `.w-1` … `.w-12`**, one `$spacer` per step from the `$sizes` map, alongside the
  percentage widths — see the [width utilities](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/utilities/width/).
- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`$grid-gutter-width` is `$grid-gutter-x`, and
  `$grid-gutter-y` joins it.** `make-row()` takes both (`make-row($gutter-x, $gutter-y)`) and
  writes them to `--cui-gutter-x` / `--cui-gutter-y`; the row gutter defaults to `0` as before,
  so nothing moves unless you set it. `$grid-gutter-width` stays as a deprecated alias of
  `$grid-gutter-x` until v7 — set the new name, the alias only reads. `CRow`'s `xs`/`sm`… gutter
  values follow the new spacing scale (see A denser spacing scale).

## Z-index

- **New keys in `$zindex-levels`: `menu`, `drawer`, `dialog`**, on the same values as `dropdown`,
  `offcanvas` and `modal` (1000, 1045, 1055). Each emits a `--cui-z-*` token and a `.z-*` utility,
  and `CMenu`, `CDrawer` and `CDialog` read their own key instead of the legacy component's. The
  legacy keys stay; both spellings of a pair always resolve to one number.

## Typography

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`$font-sizes` sets a line height per stop
  instead of one value for all headings.** `xs` is 1.25, `sm` … `lg` the body leading
  (`--cui-body-line-height`, 1.5), `xl` 2.5⁄1.75, `2xl` 3⁄2.25, `3xl` 1.2, `4xl` and `5xl` 1.1,
  `6xl` 1 — the larger the type, the tighter the leading, and the small stops read at body
  leading instead of 1.2. The sizes are unchanged. Headings follow their stop through
  `--cui-line-height-*`: `h5` (`lg`) and `h4` (`xl`) get taller lines, `h1` (`4xl`) a tighter
  one. `$headings-line-height` still feeds `--cui-heading-line-height` for anything that reads
  it directly.

## Shadows

- <span class="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **Every shadow is a stack of two to four layers
  with a negative spread** instead of one wide blur: a tight layer for contact, wider ones for
  ambient light, each at 4–9 % alpha, so a card reads as lifted rather than smeared.
  `.shadow-xs` and `--cui-box-shadow-xs` are new (one thin layer). The inset shadow reads 8 % in
  the light scheme and 26 % in the dark one, and `--cui-shadow-strength` in the dark scheme is
  `2.4` (was 2.5). The knobs are unchanged: `--cui-shadow-color` and `--cui-shadow-strength` on
  `:root`, `.shadow-{color}` and `.shadow-opacity-*` on the element, `$shadows` in Sass — a
  custom entry is now a comma-separated list of layers.

## Components

### The `visible` family

- **`visible` is deprecated in favour of `show` / `v-model:show`** on `CAlert`, `CDialog`,
  `CDrawer`, `CDropdown`, `CMenu`, `CModal`, `COffcanvas`, `CPopover`, `CSidebar`, `CToast` and
  `CTooltip`. The old prop was semi-controlled: it fed the internal state, but the component still
  closed itself, so the prop and reality desynchronized on the first Escape or backdrop click — a
  confirm-before-close dialog or a pinned tooltip could not be built on it. One prop now covers
  both needs:
  - `show` passed one-way seeds the starting state, and the component keeps managing itself from
    there.
  - `v-model:show` hands the state to your component. Close and trigger gestures (Escape, a
    backdrop or outside click, the dismiss button, hover, the autohide timer) then only emit
    `update:show`, and nothing moves until you flip the value.
  - `update:show` — emitted with the requested state either way.

  `visible` keeps its old behaviour unchanged, is ignored when `show` is set, and is removed in v7.
- **`show` replaces `visible` on the purely controlled components too** — `CCollapse`, `CTabPane`,
  `CTabPanel` and `CBackdrop` take `show`, and `visible` stays as a deprecated alias that loses to
  it. These never owned their state, so nothing changes in behaviour; the library speaks one word
  for the same thing.
- **`CSubmenu` takes `show` / `v-model:show`** in place of its `visible`, which was a seed the
  submenu silently overwrote on hover; a submenu can be controlled now.
- **`CNavGroup` moves to `show` / `v-model:show`.** With a `v-model:show` (or a bare
  `@update:show` listener) the group renders what the prop says and the toggler only emits the
  request; without a listener a bare `show` is the default-open seed and nothing freezes.
  `visible`, `v-model:visible` and `update:visible` stay as deprecated aliases — `update:visible`
  keeps firing alongside `update:show` — and the `togglerContent` slot receives `{ show }` (with
  `visible` still present).

### Controlled value props

<span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The value and state props are fully controlled
when set** — the same contract the `visible` family moved to, applied to the props that hold a
component's value. They used to be semi-controlled: the prop fed the internal state, but the
component still wrote to it, so the prop and reality desynchronized on the first user interaction.
Now the component renders exactly what you pass, an interaction only emits, and nothing moves until
you feed the change back — a bare value prop without its listener freezes the control. Code that
passed one as an initial value migrates to the new `default*` twin, which seeds the state once, on
mount:

| component | controlled prop | initial-value twin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CAutocomplete`, `CMultiSelect` | `value` | `defaultValue` |
| `CButton` (toggle mode) | `active` | `defaultActive` |
| `CChip` | `selected` | `defaultSelected` |

Props that carry a real `v-model` binding need no twin, and none was added: `modelValue` on
`CRangeSlider`, `CRating`, `CStepper` and `COneTimePassword`, `showPassword` on `CPasswordInput`,
`openItemKeys` on `CAccordion`, `show` on the `visible` family, and `date` / `time` /
`startDate` / `endDate` on the pickers and the date-time inputs all seed the starting state when
passed one-way, and hand the state over only once you bind them with `v-model`.

- **A bare `YYYY-MM-DD` string is read in the local timezone.** `Date.parse` treats it as UTC
  midnight, so `` landed on the 13th west of Greenwich and at
  the local offset east of it. Every Vue component that takes a date string is affected —
  `CCalendar`, `CDatePicker`, `CDateRangePicker`, `CDateInput`. The vanilla and React editions
  already read it this way, so this closes a divergence rather than opening one.

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The pickers and the date-time inputs drop
  their `default*` twins** — `defaultDate` on `CDatePicker` and `CDateInput`,
  `defaultTime` on `CTimePicker` and `CTimeInput`, `defaultStartDate` /
  `defaultEndDate` on `CDateRangePicker`, and `defaultValue` on `COneTimePassword`. Pass the value
  prop one-way instead: `` seeds the picker, which keeps managing
  itself. `CDateInput` and `CTimeInput` follow the same rule now — a one-way
  `date` / `time` no longer freezes the field; only a `v-model` binding hands the state over.

- **`CAutocomplete`, `CMultiSelect`: the per-option `selected` flags are a seed**, ignored entirely
  when `value` or `defaultValue` is set, and they no longer re-apply on later renders of the same
  option. In `CAutocomplete` a flag applies once, when its option first appears. In `CMultiSelect`
  it applies only to the options the component starts with: options that arrive later never change
  the selection, and `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange` empties it and takes the marked options when
  the values change. With `value` set the reset only requests the empty selection through
  the `change` event.
- **Form controls answer a native form reset the same way, bound ones included.**
  `CAutocomplete`, `CChipInput`, `CCombobox`, `CDateInput`, `CDatePicker`, `CDateRangeInput`,
  `CDateRangePicker`, `CFormRange`, `CMultiSelect`, `COneTimePassword`, `CRangeSlider`,
  `CRating`, `CTimeInput` and `CTimePicker` with a bound value used to keep it on a reset; they
  now ask for the value they started with through the events that report their value (`change`
  for `CAutocomplete` and `CMultiSelect`, `update:modelValue` for `CFormRange`, the update and
  change events for the rest) and show your
  value until you take it, so a page that resets its own state from the form's `reset` gets that
  request after its handler. A reset brings `CRating`, `CRangeSlider` and `CFormRange` back to the
  value they started with rather than the current prop, `COneTimePassword` emits `change` only
  when the reset changes the code, and `CStepper` keeps the validation marks of a form reset a
  listener cancels.
- **`CButton`: a toggle button's `active` is controlled when set** — a click only emits `click`
  and the pressed state follows your prop; seed an uncontrolled toggle with `defaultActive`.
  Without either prop nothing changes.
- **`CCalendar`: equal re-renders no longer reset the view.** A parent re-rendering with an equal
  `calendarDate`, `startDate` or `endDate` (a fresh `Date` object holding the same value) used to
  yank back the navigated month and cancel an in-progress range selection; only a real value
  change syncs now. Month names also follow `locale` and `monthFormat` changes at runtime.

### Validation state

<span className="badge bg-warning">Deprecated</span> **One `validation-state` prop replaces the
`valid` and `invalid` booleans** on every form control, field and picker, and on `CFormFeedback`.
`validation-state="invalid"` renders `is-invalid` and sets `aria-invalid` on the control,
`"valid"` renders `is-valid`, and any custom state from the `$form-validation-states` Sass map
renders `is-{state}` — two independent flags could neither express a third state nor refuse
`valid` and `invalid` at once. On the components that had them in v5 the booleans keep working as
deprecated aliases (with both set, `invalid` wins, where they used to stack), and are ignored
whenever `validation-state` is set; `CCheckbox`, `CChipInput`, `CCombobox`, `CDateInput`,
`CDateRangeInput`, `CNumberInput`, `CRadio`, `CSwitch` and `CTimeInput` take `validation-state`
only. Four side effects worth knowing:

- `feedback` follows the state: it renders only while `validation-state` is set, styled after it,
  and describes the control in every state, not only the invalid one.
- Every control that reads `validation-state="invalid"` now sets `aria-invalid="true"`, except
  `CCombobox`, whose toggle is a button and takes only the message in `aria-describedby`; a control
  without a validation state still sets none.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> `validation-state="invalid"` (or the deprecated
  `invalid`) blocks the submit on `CFormInput`, `CFormSelect`, `CFormTextarea`, `CNumberInput`,
  `CPasswordInput`, `CCheckbox`, `CRadio`, `CSwitch`, `CFormCheck` and `CFormSwitch`, with the text
  of the invalid feedback as the browser's message, the way it already did on the fields that
  build their own markup. Each control emits `update:validationState` with `undefined` when the
  user changes its value or the form is reset; bind it with `v-model:validation-state` (with the
  deprecated `invalid`, set it to `false` on that event instead), or a form you gave an invalid
  state stays blocked until you clear it yourself. See
  [Validation](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/validation/#custom-validation).
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> `CMultiSelect`, `CChipInput`, `CCombobox`,
  `COneTimePassword`, the date and time fields, the pickers and `CAutocomplete` take and show their
  validation state the same way, described under
  [Form components](https://coreui.io/vue/docs/forms/validation/#form-components). A field a validation reports shows the
  state on the component's frame, and `<CForm>` and `CStepper` leave the field that carries the
  value to the component. After taking the result over with `preventDefault()` in a `validate`
  listener, keep `event.isValid` rather than calling `checkValidity()`: the call reports every
  invalid field again, and the components then show their error.

### Help text and feedback ids

**`text` and the feedback get ids of their own.** A form control used to hand its
`aria-describedby` to the `text` and to the feedback as their id, so the help text and the error
shared one id: the control read the help text and never the error, a valid control with
`feedback-invalid` was described by the hidden error, and an `aria-describedby` that pointed at an
element of the page gave that id to a second element. Now `text`, `feedback`, `feedback-invalid` and
`feedback-valid` get generated ids, and the control lists them in its own `aria-describedby` after
the one you pass: the text always, `feedback` while `validation-state` is set, `feedback-invalid`
only while the control is invalid and `feedback-valid` only while it is valid, whether that state
comes from `validation-state` or, in a `data-coreui-validate` form, from the browser's `:user-invalid`
and `:user-valid` (the date and time fields and the pickers use the field's own verdict instead). A
`validation-state` you set takes precedence. Pass
`aria-describedby` only to point at elements of your own; a value you passed so that the `text`
would carry it is no longer needed, and CSS or scripts that found the text by that id need another
hook. `CFormControlWrapper` and `CFormControlValidation` replace their undocumented `describedby`
prop with `description-id`, the prefix the ids are built from (`<description-id>-label`, `-text`,
`-feedback`, `-feedback-invalid` and `-feedback-valid`).

### CAccordion

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The accordion is built on the native
  `<details>` and `<summary>` elements.** `CAccordionItem` renders a `<details class="accordion-item">`
  and `CAccordionHeader` its `<summary>`, so the browser owns opening, closing, keyboard
  interaction and the disclosure semantics — none of it depends on the component being mounted.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`CAccordionButton` is removed**, together
  with `.accordion-button`, `.accordion-collapse` and `.collapsed`. The trigger is the `<summary>`
  itself and the panel is the element's own content, revealed through `::details-content`.
  `CAccordionHeader` already rendered the button for you, so markup written against the components
  needs no change; custom CSS keyed on those classes does. Style the open state with
  `.accordion-item[open] > .accordion-header`.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`CAccordionHeader` renders a `<summary>`,
  not an `<h2>`.** A `<summary>` is not a heading — where the accordion divides a page into
  sections, wrap the label in an `<h2>`–`<h6>` inside the header. The heading inherits the
  summary's typography, so nothing looks different.
- **Grouping is the `name` attribute.** Without `alwaysOpen` the items of one accordion share a
  generated `name`, and the browser keeps a single one open.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The open items follow the controlled /
  uncontrolled split the rest of the library uses.** `activeItemKey` fed the initial state, so it
  read like a controlled prop and behaved like a default: changing it after mount did nothing, and
  nothing reported back when the user opened an item. It is deprecated in favour of three props
  that say which is which:
  - `openItemKeys` passed one-way is the initial value, where `activeItemKey` maps — the accordion
    manages the open items from there.
  - `v-model:open-item-keys` hands them to your component, which then has to feed each `change`
    back.
  - `change` — emitted with the new list either way.

  They are named for what an accordion holds. `active` is the vocabulary of a selection — one
  item out of a set, which is what tabs have — while a `<details>` element is open or closed,
  and that is what `CAccordionItem` calls its own prop.
